status_note: active, maintained by Frappe (powers frappe.io); requires Frappe Framework v15-17 bench; recently added a full server-side AI agent ('Bob') via litellm
core_problem: A Figma-like visual website builder inside the Frappe framework that stores pages as a JSON block tree, renders them server-side to lean HTML/CSS (Lighthouse-friendly), supports components with version pinning, data-bound/repeater blocks, per-breakpoint styles, one-click publish with snapshots, and (new) an AI agent that edits the same block tree through validated tool calls.
architecture: Python app (builder/) + Vue 3 frontend (frontend/). DATA MODEL: a Builder Page doctype (builder/builder/doctype/builder_page/builder_page.json) holds `blocks` (Long Text JSON, the published tree) and `draft_blocks` (working tree), plus route, published/staging flags, page_data_script (Python), dynamic_route, client_scripts, head/body HTML, meta fields, is_standard/app for export-to-app. Each block (frontend/src/block.ts class Block, ~1.1k lines) is a DOM-like node: blockId, element (semantic tag), children[], baseStyles / mobileStyles / tabletStyles (camelCase CSS maps), attributes, customAttributes, classes[], innerHTML, dataKey + dynamicValues (bindings to page data), isRepeaterBlock, visibilityCondition, props (typed, with isStandard/isPassedDown/isDynamic/comesFrom), clientScript, extendedFromComponent + componentVersion + isChildOfComponent + referenceBlockId (component instances resolve their reference block through componentStore, pinned to a frozen version snapshot when set). Components are Builder Component docs; builder/builder/component_versions.py pins versions at drag-drop and pin_components_in_page_data() pins the rest at publish. RENDER/PUBLISH: builder_page.publish() sets published=1, staging=0, calls promote_draft_blocks() which take_snapshot()s draft_blocks + page_data_script (snapshot_type Publish, pruned to KEEP_PUBLISH_SNAPSHOTS), copies draft_blocks -> blocks, saves, and enqueues a preview image; publish_to_staging/mark_as_staging serve the route but disable indexing; restore_snapshot restores into the draft. get_context() (Frappe website generator hook) runs the page data script, picks draft_blocks in preview mode, and calls get_block_html(blocks) -> BeautifulSoup tree: per block extend_block_with_component(), process_block_props() (standard props stack, dynamic props become Jinja refs), build_tag() creates the tag with CSS classes emitted into one <style> (base + tablet/mobile media queries, font registration, italic tracking), render_repeater_children() for data-bound loops, attach_client_script(); the resulting HTML + style are rendered through Jinja against page data, then meta tags, favicon, language, fonts (Google font URLs or user fonts) and global/page client scripts are attached; on_update() clears route caches and, in developer mode, exports standard pages/templates to an app as files. EDITOR: Pinia stores (pageStore, canvasStore, componentStore, blockTemplateStore, builderStore); frontend/src/utils/useCanvasHistory.ts implements undo/redo with @vueuse watchIgnorable + debounceFilter(100 ms) on the root Block: each record is the serialized whole tree (getBlockString) + selected ids; CAPACITY 500 entries, MAX_BYTES 20 MB with MIN_ENTRIES 10, reference-counted pause()/resume() during drag/resize, batch(), silentSetSource() for snapshot preview without recording, enable/disable for read-only. AI AGENT (builder/ai/): agent/loop.py AgentRunner drives a litellm tool-calling loop (MAX_ROUNDS 40, stream retries, Anthropic cache markers on system/turn, FULL_CONTEXT_LIMIT 45k chars above which the page is sent as a compact outline and read_block pulls detail); the server-side WorkingTree (agent/tree.py) is authoritative: every block op is applied there first, persisted to draft_blocks after each round, and only accepted ops are mirrored to the canvas (a live view); ops are rejected with honest messages for bad refs, non-plain bind keys (BIND_KEY_RE), repeater-via-bind, and moustache/Jinja text in content (which would crash the published route). agent/registry.py: each Tool has a side 'client' (block ops), 'server' (handler returns text) or 'terminal' (ends turn: present_ui, request_confirmation), optionally an 'artifact' + generator (generate_page streams page YAML from a heavier model, page_writer.py expands YAML -> Block JSON with style normalization). block_codec.py compresses Block JSON to a compact YAML vocabulary (el, ref, name, style, m_style, t_style, attrs, text, c, classes, icon) so the model never sees raw SVG or editor fields. Tools: generate_page, add_block/update_block/update_blocks/remove_block/move_block, query_blocks/read_block(show_image), preview_page (screenshot at viewport/colour scheme), set_page_script/update_script, set_design_token, query_records, run_python, connect_form, search_images, read_url/research, present_ui, memory. agent/pending.py confirm-gates sensitive kinds (home_page, global_settings, create_doctype, seed_sample_data, connect_form): the tool persists a pending action and ends the turn; only the user's Apply runs it. snapshots.py saves a revert snapshot before any turn that uses SNAPSHOT_TOOLS so every AI turn is revertable. prompts.py encodes hard rules: style on blocks or Builder Tokens only (never :root CSS), tokens referenced by document id, colours are facts to be read not guessed, never invent facts about a real business (delegate to research/read_url), no emoji icons (Lucide), summaries may claim only what preview_page showed, banned self-praise words.
core_innovation: A server-authoritative working tree that validates and applies every AI block operation before mirroring it to the editor, combined with a lossy-but-round-trippable codec that shows the model a compact YAML view of the same block JSON the visual editor and server renderer use.
strengths: One block tree is the contract for editor (Vue Block class), server renderer (get_block_html via BeautifulSoup + one generated stylesheet), publish snapshots, and the AI agent (via BlockCodec); no second renderer, and published pages are lean static HTML that scores well on Lighthouse.

WorkingTree rejects invalid ops deterministically (bad ref, expression bind keys, moustache text, repeater misuse) and returns honest tool results, so the model self-corrects; canvas and server cannot diverge because only accepted ops are mirrored.
Confirm-gating (pending.py): sensitive writes are proposals persisted as pending actions and applied only by user action; every mutating turn gets a pre-turn revert snapshot.

Publish pipeline is a real state machine: draft_blocks vs blocks, staging vs published, Publish/Manual snapshots with pruning, component version pinning at drag-drop and at publish, route-cache invalidation on any relevant field change.
Component versioning: instances carry componentVersion and resolve against frozen version snapshots, so editing a component cannot silently change a published page.
Undo/redo is production-grade: debounced deep watcher, byte-capped stack, reference-counted pause for gestures, silent source swap for previewing snapshots.

Prompt rules that align with our philosophy: tokens are Builder Token records (never raw :root CSS), colours are read not guessed, facts about real businesses are never invented (research/read_url), summaries claim only what preview_page showed, self-praise vocabulary banned.
Context management: compact YAML codec, outline mode above 45k chars, Anthropic cache markers, streamed artifact from a heavier model separate from the conversational model.
Large test suite (builder_page tests 2k lines, ai/test_* for codec, tree apply, page writer, read_page, locks, web).
weaknesses: Element-level, Webflow-style model (div/section/h1 with camelCase style maps per breakpoint): no notion of section variants, arrangements, composition or archetypes; design quality is whatever the user or the model composes from raw CSS.

Hard dependency on Frappe Framework (bench, MariaDB/Postgres, Redis, Python website generator, Jinja): cannot be used inside an Astro/TS pipeline; the renderer emits HTML via BeautifulSoup + Jinja, not components.

The AI agent still lets the model author raw CSS values and layout (style maps in YAML) and search stock images; grounding is by prompt rules plus a few regex guards, not by a typed eligibility system.
Published output is one generated <style> block with generated class names; no design-token file surface comparable to our visual_dna, only Builder Token records referenced by uuid.
AI subsystem is new (2026) and coupled to Frappe realtime events, doctypes and Desk; loop.py is 1.5k lines with product-specific event contracts.
Snapshots serialise the whole tree per record (undo stack and publish snapshots), which the code itself notes gets heavy for large pages.
patterns_to_steal: Server-authoritative WorkingTree with op-level validation and mirror-only-accepted-ops -> Assembly and post-V1 editor: the canonical SiteDefinition lives in Postgres; model or editor proposals are ops validated by Zod + predicate rules server-side, and the UI only reflects accepted ops.

Deterministic op guards that encode 'this will crash the published page' knowledge (BIND_KEY_RE, MOUSTACHE_RE, repeater-via-bind) -> Anti-slop tier 1 / Launch QA: pure regex and structural bans on model output that cannot render (unknown variant ids, template syntax in copy, facts not in the FactRegistry).

BlockCodec: a compact, documented model-facing vocabulary generated from the same data model, with FIELD_DOCS as the single source for the prompt's field list -> agent orchestration: derive the model-visible catalogue of eligible ids/fields from the Zod schemas, never hand-type it.

Confirm-gated terminal tools (pending.py KINDS) -> orchestration: publish, positioning changes and anything owner-declared are proposals that end the turn and require explicit approval; the model can only propose.
Pre-turn revert snapshot for any mutating tool set -> Decision Manifest/telemetry: snapshot SiteDefinition before each pipeline stage so every change is revertable and diffable.

Publish state machine (draft vs published, staging, snapshot + prune, version pinning at publish, cache invalidation on field change) -> CMS/publish stage for Astro output: pin design_system and section library versions into the published manifest.
Outline-above-threshold context strategy (FULL_CONTEXT_LIMIT + read_block on demand) -> agent orchestration for large SiteDefinitions.

Prompt rules worth keeping as code checks: 'summary claims only what preview showed', 'never invent facts about a real business', 'colours are facts to be read' -> map to Launch QA screenshot verification, FactRegistry provenance and design-system token lookup.
patterns_to_avoid: Free-form element/CSS block model (element + style maps) -> we deliberately constrain to section variants x arrangements; letting the model author CSS values violates 'model selects, never emits a token'.
Frappe-coupled runtime (doctypes, Jinja website generator, realtime events) -> not portable to Astro/TS; take the mechanisms, not the code.
Stock-image search tool (search_images) as the imagery path -> our art direction requires real owner photos with asset constraints.
Whole-tree snapshot per undo record -> for large SiteDefinitions prefer op logs or structural sharing; keep the byte cap idea.
Prompt-only enforcement of design rules where a check is possible (e.g. 'no :root CSS') -> encode as validators.
reusable_patterns: AuthoritativeWorkingTree: apply proposed ops to a server-side model first, persist, then mirror only accepted ops to any live view.
ModelFacingCodec: a compact, documented projection of the canonical schema shown to the model, with the field list generated from one table.
ConfirmGatedTerminalTool: sensitive actions end the turn as persisted proposals that only a human can apply.
PreTurnRevertSnapshot: snapshot the artefact before any mutating tool set so a whole turn can be reverted.
DraftPublishStateMachine: draft/published/staging fields with snapshot-on-publish, pruning and dependency version pinning.
OutlineOnOverflow: send a structural outline above a size threshold and let the model fetch detail on demand.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not run Frappe; the block model is element-level and the runtime is Python/Jinja. Port five mechanisms into TypeScript: the authoritative working-tree op pipeline (Zod + predicate validation before mirroring), deterministic 'this cannot render' guards into the anti-slop gate, a generated model-facing codec/catalogue derived from the Zod schemas, confirm-gated terminal tools plus pre-turn snapshots for the orchestration loop, and the draft/staging/publish state machine with version pinning for the publish stage. Its prompt rules about facts, colours and self-praise are a useful checklist to convert into code checks. This is the most architecturally mature repo in the category and the best reference for the post-V1 visual editor's undo and component-version design.

license: No LICENSE file (README shows an MIT badge but the repo ships no license; GitHub reports none)
status_note: active but low-frequency; the original TubeGuruji-style 'Bolt clone' tutorial codebase that SamTerces/AI-first-Builder forked
core_problem: Prompt-to-React-project generator: Gemini returns a JSON map of Vite/React files, Sandpack renders them in the browser, Convex stores the chat and files, JSZip exports the project.
architecture: Next.js 15 App Router in plain JS. configs/AiModel.jsx creates one GoogleGenerativeAI client (model 'gemini-flash-lite-latest', key from NEXT_PUBLIC_GEMINI_API_KEY) and exports three module-level `model.startChat(...)` singletons: chatSession (text/plain, temperature 1), GenAiCode (responseMimeType 'application/json', temperature 1, maxOutputTokens 8192, seeded with a two-turn few-shot history showing a to-do app in the exact output shape) and enhancePromptSession. app/api/gen-ai-code/route.jsx calls GenAiCode.sendMessageStream(prompt), relays chunks as SSE, then JSON.parse(fullText) at the end and emits {final, done} or {error:'Invalid JSON response'}; there is no schema validation. app/api/enhance-prompt/route.jsx reuses chatSession (not enhancePromptSession) so enhancement turns pollute the shared chat history. data/Prompt.jsx holds CODE_GEN_PROMPT (JSON schema {projectTitle, explanation, files:{path:{code}}, generatedFiles}), which visibly contains a leaked editing artifact ('Here's the reformatted and improved version of your prompt:') and the whole schema twice, plus contradictory image rules ('use Unsplash API', 'Do not use images from unsplash.com', 'use images from the internet'). components/custom/CodeView.jsx composes the prompt client-side (JSON.stringify(messages) + CODE_GEN_PROMPT), merges returned files over Lookup.DEFAULT_FILE and renders with SandpackProvider (template 'react', externalResources cdn.tailwindcss.com, dependencies from Lookup.DEPENDANCY). Convex schema: users {name,email,picture,uid}, workspace {messages: v.any(), fileData: v.optional(v.any())}; convex/workspace.js exposes CreateWorkspace/GetWorkspace/UpdateWorkspace/UpdateFiles with v.any() args.
core_innovation: None beyond the field baseline; the one cheap trick is anchoring the output shape with responseMimeType='application/json' plus a few-shot exemplar turn in the chat history.
strengths: Format anchoring: GenAiCode is started with a canned user/model exchange that demonstrates the exact JSON envelope, plus Gemini's application/json response mime type; this is the lowest-cost structured-output trick and works reasonably on small models.
Server route separates the streaming relay from the final parse, so the UI can show progress while the parse decides success or failure.
203 stars and 111 forks make it the reference implementation of this tutorial family; useful only as a baseline of what 'AI website builder' means to hobbyists.
weaknesses: Module-level chat singletons (chatSession, GenAiCode) are shared across every request and user: conversation history leaks between users and grows unbounded until the context window overflows.
Gemini key is read from NEXT_PUBLIC_GEMINI_API_KEY; the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix inlines it into the client bundle.
No output validation: JSON.parse only; no check that /App.js exists, that files compile, that imports are installed; failure surfaces as a Sandpack red overlay.
temperature 1 / topP 0.95 for code generation and 'Add as many functional features as possible' guarantee non-reproducible, bloated output.
Prompt is internally contradictory and contains leaked scaffolding text; image guidance leads to hallucinated URLs and broken images.
Generated project package.json is told to include firebase, @google/generative-ai, MUI, react-icons and framer-motion for a static site; exported bundles are heavy by construction.
No license file despite the MIT badge; legally unusable as code without asking the author (not that any code is worth taking).
Persistence is v.any() blobs with no generation lineage, versioning, or telemetry.
patterns_to_steal: FewShotEnvelopeAnchor: prime the model with a minimal exemplar of the exact typed envelope before the real request → creative_direction / beat selection prompts: show one valid SiteDefinition selection object as an exemplar, then parse with Zod (the Zod parse is what this repo is missing).
Stream-then-parse split: relay chunks for UX, but only accept the final parsed object → renderer/assembly boundary: nothing partial ever enters state.
patterns_to_avoid: Shared LLM session singletons across requests → cross-user state leakage and unbounded context; every generation in our pipeline must be a fresh, fully specified call with a recorded predicate snapshot.
Client-composed system prompt with serialised history → prompt injection and cost abuse; keep prompts server-side and let the model only choose ids.
JSON without schema validation → cannot detect truncation, missing files or drift; SiteDefinition must be Zod-parsed and rejected on failure.
Temperature 1 for structured selection → non-reproducible outputs, incompatible with Decision Manifest and telemetry-driven priors.
Model-chosen image URLs of any kind → asset_constraints require owner-provided or licensed photos with provenance; anything else is a broken-image or licensing incident.
Prescribing a heavy dependency list to the generated site → violates the 180 kB JS budget and near-zero-JS Astro target.
reusable_patterns: FewShotEnvelopeAnchor: one exemplar turn demonstrating the exact output envelope, paired with a JSON response mime type.
StreamThenParse: stream tokens for feedback, commit only the fully parsed final object.
ScaffoldMergeDefaults: deterministic default files merged under model output (weak: model can overwrite scaffold).
adoption_strategy: Ignore. This is the canonical tutorial Bolt clone: raw JSON files map, no validation, shared model sessions, client-side prompt assembly, and a prompt that mandates the generic look. Its only transferable idea, few-shot envelope anchoring plus JSON mime type, is a two-line trick we would pair with Zod anyway. Treat its output ('Well Designed UI' Tailwind card grids with hallucinated image URLs) as a negative reference for what the anti-slop gate must reject.

status_note: active but early (v1.0.0, ~9k LOC, single-org, last push Mar 2026); tests cover only export-html and deploy-security
core_problem: A self-hosted website builder where one JSON document (SiteConfig) is the source of truth that a visual editor, an AI generator and a static exporter all read and write, so AI output is structured data rather than fragile generated code.
architecture: Vite + React 19 SPA. Contract: src/blocks/types.ts defines BlockConfig {id, type: BlockType (19-string union), variant: string, props: Record<string, unknown>}, PageConfig {id,name,path,blocks[]}, SiteConfig {name, pages?, blocks (legacy first-page mirror), theme?: Partial<ThemeConfig>} and ThemeConfig (6 bg + 4 text + accent/accentDim + 3 border hex tokens, 3 font names, 2 radii). There is NO Zod or runtime schema; props is untyped. The block catalog is declared in five parallel hand-maintained places: (1) the BlockType union, (2) src/lib/block-metadata.ts (label, category, variants[], defaultProps), (3) each block's local props interface + a switch(block.variant) inside e.g. HeroBlock.tsx that picks HeroCentered/HeroSplit/HeroGradient/HeroMinimal (default -> centered), (4) src/editor/PropertiesPanel.tsx blockFields (per-type FieldDef list driving the sidebar inputs), and (5) the LLM system prompt which lists all 19 types/variants/props as prose, duplicated in src/lib/generation-prompt.ts and api/generate.ts (already drifted: the API copy has no pages and adds a testimonials.company field). Registration: src/blocks/registry.tsx is a plain Record<string, ComponentType<{block}>> plus a per-block React error boundary and a PlaceholderBlock fallback for unknown types; RenderBlock(block) = registry[block.type] || Placeholder. Rendering: src/editor/Canvas.tsx maps active page blocks through BlockWrapper (selection, hover, move/dup/delete) and RenderBlock inside a Tailwind @container div whose inline style is themeToCSS(resolveTheme(theme)) -> --color-* CSS variables; viewport switching just changes max-width (880/768/375) and block styles use @md:/@2xl: container queries, so no iframe is needed. State: src/store/configStore.ts (Zustand + immer + persist). Undo/redo is a whole-config snapshot stack: pushUndo() deep-clones {pages, blocks, theme} via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) with a label + timestamp, MAX_UNDO=50, redoStack cleared on every push; undo() pops and pushes the current snapshot onto redo; previewTheme() and renamePage() intentionally bypass the stack (transient hover previews); stacks are excluded from persistence (partialize) and VersionHistory.tsx just lists undoStack labels reversed; persist has a version:2 migrate that wraps legacy blocks[] into pages[]. AI flow: src/lib/generate-site.ts is a three-rung ladder: (1) client-side BYOK Gemini (gemini-3-flash-preview, responseMimeType application/json, temperature 0.8, key in localStorage), (2) POST /api/generate Vercel function with the same call server-side, (3) getTemplateForPrompt() keyword-matched hard-coded templates (portfolio/restaurant/agency/...). All AI output passes validateSiteConfig(): unknown block types are dropped, an invalid variant is coerced to variants[0], props = {...defaultProps, ...raw.props} with no shape check, theme hex values regex-validated and radii clamped, empty results fall back to a template. The AgentPanel 'JSON patch' chat is a regex demo (change headline / add X / remove X / make X variant / switch theme) with a random 800-1400 ms fake typing delay; no LLM. Export: src/lib/export-html.ts is a second, hand-written string-template renderer (1.4k lines) covering only 13 of 19 types and only config.blocks (first page); the other six types emit an HTML comment. JsonDrawer.tsx applies pasted JSON via setConfig(JSON.parse(text)) with no validation.
core_innovation: A flat {type, variant, props} block document shared verbatim by editor, AI generator and renderer, with the AI catalogue expressed as a prose copy of the same block metadata and a coercing validator that repairs rather than rejects model output.
strengths: The shared-contract shape is minimal and legible: BlockConfig {id,type,variant,props} + PageConfig + ThemeConfig; every mutation path (editor, AI, JSON drawer) converges on one Zustand store so the canvas re-renders from one document.

Coercing validator (validateSiteConfig/validateBlock): unknown types dropped, invalid variant -> first variant, defaultProps merged under model props, hex/radius range checks, template fallback on empty output. Cheap and keeps the canvas from ever crashing on bad AI JSON.
Three-rung generation ladder (BYOK client -> server key -> deterministic keyword template) so the product always produces a page; the template rung is instant and honest ('source: template').
Container-query canvas (@container + @md:/@2xl: block styles + inline --color-* vars) gives responsive preview and per-site theming without an iframe or a second stylesheet.
Undo/redo as labelled whole-document snapshots with transient-mutation bypass (previewTheme) is trivially correct and doubles as the version-history UI.
Per-block React error boundary in the registry isolates a broken block from the rest of the page.
weaknesses: 'Typed JSON' is nominal: props is Record<string, unknown>, no Zod/JSON Schema anywhere; the block catalogue lives in five hand-synced declarations (types.ts, block-metadata.ts, per-block props interface + variant switch, PropertiesPanel blockFields, two prompt copies) and has already drifted.

Model emits raw design tokens (20 hex colours, font names, radii) and copy in one shot at temperature 0.8; theme quality is whatever the LLM guesses. Exactly the 'model emits a token' pattern the architect rejected.

Blocks are generic 'Hero 1/2/3' presets: variants are a string switch inside the component with no requires/enhanced_by/compat metadata, no composition or asset constraints, no notion of arrangement or signature move.
Double renderer: React components for the editor and a separate 1.4k-line string-template exporter that covers only 13/19 types and only the first page, so export and canvas diverge by construction.

AgentPanel 'AI agent with JSON patches' is regex pattern matching with a fake typing delay; the README's 'JSON schema enforces validity' claim only holds on the AI path (JsonDrawer.setConfig is unvalidated).
Prompt is aspirational/one-shot ('write compelling copy', 'pick a theme that fits the vibe'); no fact grounding, no placeholder scan beyond 'do not use Lorem ipsum', no QA loop.
Tiny community (79 stars, one org), dark-theme-only editor, localStorage persistence, no tests for the store or validator.
patterns_to_steal: Coerce-then-validate on model output (drop unknown type, snap invalid variant to a known one, merge defaults under props, clamp numeric ranges) -> our Assembly stage: run it as a pre-pass before the Zod parse of SiteDefinition so a single bad field degrades to a default instead of failing the whole build, and log every coercion into the Decision Manifest.

Deterministic fallback rung (keyword template returns a complete SiteConfig with source:'template') -> our pipeline's fail-safe: when Creative Direction or Beat selection yields no eligible variant, fall back to the service_clarity archetype deterministically and mark it in the Gap Report.

Labelled whole-document snapshot undo stack with an explicit transient bypass (previewTheme) -> post-V1 visual editor: snapshot SiteDefinition per committed edit, bypass for hover previews, expose the stack as version history.

Container-query canvas with inline CSS-variable theme injection -> visual editor / renderer preview: render Astro section HTML inside a @container root with the design system's token file injected as --vars, so viewport emulation is a max-width change and design-system swaps are a variable swap.

Registry = Record<type, component> + per-block error boundary + placeholder fallback -> renderer: resolve variant x arrangement ids to Astro components through one table, with an explicit 'unknown variant' placeholder that fails the Launch QA placeholder scan rather than crashing the build.
patterns_to_avoid: Model-emitted theme tokens (raw hex, font names, radii in the generation prompt) -> violates 'model selects an id, never emits a token'; our design systems are authored token files.

Prose copy of the block catalogue inside the prompt, hand-synced with the TS types -> drift is already visible in this repo; our Zod schemas must be the single source and the prompt-visible catalogue must be generated from them (or use structured outputs / tool schemas).

Generic Hero/Features/CTA 'variant = string switch' blocks with no metadata -> the architect already rejected extending this schema; our section variants need requires/compat/composition/motion/a11y/priors and arrangements.
Separate string-template exporter duplicating the React renderer -> two renderers guarantee divergence; Astro components must be the only renderer for both preview and publish.
Regex 'agent' that fakes LLM latency -> misleading; if an edit agent exists it must be a real, reviewable patch with a diff, applied through the same validator.
One-shot 'write compelling copy for this business' generation -> fabricates claims; every sentence in our pages must trace to the FactRegistry.
reusable_patterns: CoerceThenValidate: repair model JSON toward known enums/defaults before strict parsing, recording every coercion.
FallbackLadder: ordered generation strategies (BYOK -> server -> deterministic template) each returning the same contract type plus a provenance tag.
SnapshotUndoStack: labelled deep-clone snapshots of the whole document with a transient-bypass channel for preview-only mutations.
ContainerQueryCanvas: preview root as a CSS container with tokens injected as custom properties, so viewport and theme are pure style changes.
TypeVariantRegistry: single Record<type, renderer> resolution with error boundary and placeholder fallback.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (narrowly). Do not adopt the codebase or its SiteConfig; the architect has already ruled that out and the code confirms why (untyped props, five drifting catalogue copies, generic variants, double renderer, fake agent). Lift three mechanisms into our own stack: the coerce-then-validate pre-pass in front of Zod, the deterministic fallback rung with provenance tagging, and the container-query preview root with token injection. Keep the snapshot-undo design on file for the post-V1 editor. Treat the prompt-catalogue drift as a concrete cautionary example: generate any model-visible catalogue from the Zod schemas.

Every capability goes through src/lib/vcaas.ts (vcaasApi catalog: projects.list/get/create/launch, agent runs, files, deploy, versions, secrets, domains, github, figma, db) -> same-origin proxy routes src/app/api/vcaas/[...path] -> src/lib/vcaas-server.ts adds the TOTALUM_VCAAS_API_KEY header -> https://api-accounts.totalum.app/api/v1/vcaas. The agent is fully remote and opaque: per src/lib/agent-progress.ts 'The agent reports init or done and nothing in between', so the UI derives progress from elapsed time via RUN_ESTIMATE_MS (10 min), a RUN_ESTIMATE_LADDER of 12 rungs that extends the estimate as the run outlives it, PROGRESS_CEILING 0.97 and strictly increasing interpolation so the bar never moves backwards. What is implemented locally: (1) the visual editor, ~6.6k lines across src/lib/visual-edit*.ts and src/app/api/visual-edit/[projectId]/apply/route.ts: the preview is a production next start build proxied same-origin by src/app/api/preview/[projectId]; an in-page agent posts an ElementSignature (route, tag, decoded text, source-stripped className, parent/sibling text, nthOfType, id/ancestorId, src with proxy prefix stripped, selectionId) and the matcher resolves it to exact character spans in three tiers: build tag data-tlm-loc="file:line:col" from a template loader, then structural matching over a TypeScript-AST source model (visual-edit-source.ts parses TSX with the typescript compiler: every JSX element, static class tokens with spans, entity-decoded/collapsed text, parent/siblings, whether inside .map(); it never evaluates expressions), then data-array matching for copy that lives in const arrays rendered by .map(); ambiguity or low confidence refuses instead of guessing. (2) src/lib/preview-health.ts classifies fetched preview HTML into ok / placeholder (<4 KB sandbox page) / assets-missing / scripts-dead (document 200 but several /_next/static chunks 503), requiring several independent signals because false positives destroy trust. (4) Database CMS (DatabasePanel + lib/totalum-schema/query/join-filter) copied verbatim from the platform, always server-side querying. data-tlm-loc build tag (file:line:col injected by a loader) as the exact tier: cheap, deterministic element-to-source provenance.
preview-health.ts: multi-signal verdicts with an explicit 'false positive is worse than false negative' policy and a reproduced failure case (scripts-dead) documented in code.
agent-progress.ts: honest progress UX under an opaque agent (extending estimate ladder, ceiling below 100%, never-backwards interpolation), pure and unit-testable.

AGENTS.md as a precise, invariant-focused map for AI coding agents (commands, where features live, non-obvious rules).

Very large components (1.7k-line workspace page, 2.3k-line DatabasePanel, 5.2k-line i18n dictionary copied from the platform); no tests (verification is 'typecheck + build + click through with a real key').
Runs take 4-10 minutes with no intermediate signal, so the UI is built around guessing.

patterns_to_steal: Build-time source location tag (data-tlm-loc=file:line:col via a loader) -> post-V1 visual editor: emit data-section-id/data-field-path attributes from Astro components so a clicked element maps directly to a SiteDefinition path, no inference needed.

AST-based structural source model with refusal on ambiguity -> visual editor fallback only if we ever allow editing hand-authored section code; the principle 'refuse rather than guess' applies to any model-proposed patch that cannot be located uniquely.

Multi-signal preview health verdicts (placeholder / assets-missing / scripts-dead) with a false-positive-averse threshold -> Launch QA gate: classify a crawled page as healthy only when document, stylesheet and script chunks all resolve; flag hydration-dead pages.
Extending-estimate progress ladder with a ceiling and monotone interpolation -> owner-facing job status for our multi-minute pipeline runs.
Server-authoritative operation locks with self-expiry mirrored by the client -> pipeline job state: one persisted operation slot per site (build/audit/publish), server timestamps, stale-lock expiry.
patterns_to_avoid: Opaque remote agent with init/done-only status -> our Decision Manifest and telemetry require every stage to emit structured events; never accept a black-box generator.
Full-stack code generation as the deliverable -> we ship a constrained SiteDefinition rendered by Astro.
No-auth operator-key architecture -> even though accounts are cut from V1, any exposed endpoint must not spend credits on behalf of strangers.
Copying a vendor's 5k-line i18n dictionary and CMS verbatim -> avoid importing platform surface area we do not need.
reusable_patterns: SourceLocationTag: stamp rendered elements with a build-time file:line:col (or schema path) so editor selections resolve without inference.
RefuseOnAmbiguity: a matcher returns not-found / low-confidence / ambiguous as first-class outcomes instead of a best guess.
MultiSignalHealthVerdict: require several independent failure signals before declaring a preview broken.
ExtendingEstimateLadder: progress estimates that lengthen as a job runs, capped below completion, never moving backwards.
ServerAuthoritativeOperationLock: a single persisted in-flight operation with server-issued timestamps and self-expiry.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for the pipeline; Adapt two ideas for later. The repository cannot inform agent orchestration because its agent is closed-source, and its product model (hosted Next.js apps on a metered API) is orthogonal to a constrained site pipeline. Two mechanisms are worth noting for the post-V1 visual editor and the QA gate: build-time source/schema location tags (trivial with Astro components) and the false-positive-averse preview-health classifier. Do not depend on the Totalum API.

license: MIT (stated in README; no LICENSE file in the repo)
status_note: active, single developer (Thomas Tschinkel), package still named 'bloom'; vite.log / dev.verify logs and a Remotion ad project are committed
core_problem: A browser-based, bring-your-own-key AI website builder: a multi-provider tool-calling agent writes a React/TS/CSS project into a virtual filesystem, bundles it in the browser with esbuild-wasm, executes it in a hidden iframe to catch runtime errors, and deploys the result to Cloudflare Pages without any server-side code execution.
architecture: React 19 + Vite SPA; Supabase for auth/Postgres/Realtime; Vercel functions in api/ (deploy, provider-keys, admin, supabase-oauth) sharing api/_shared.ts (JWT check, rate limit, AES-256-GCM key encryption) and re-implemented as dev middleware shims in vite.config.ts. The product core is src/lib/agent.ts (3.8k lines): runOpenThornAgent() drives a tool loop (MAX_TOOL_TURNS=30) over 12 providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama) with per-call retry/backoff/Retry-After, a circuit breaker (3 failures, 30 s cooldown), mid-run provider failover (max 2), context compaction (estimateMessageTokens, KEEP_RECENT_TURNS=6, summary every 6 turns), and a LoopDetector that fingerprints only FAILING tool calls (3 repeats of an action or error -> loopBreakPrompt nudge). Tools (src/lib/agent-prompt.ts AGENT_TOOLS, alphabetically sorted for byte-identical cache prefixes): think, set_title, load_skill, list_files, read_file, search_files, write_file, edit_file, multi_edit, delete_file, set_schema, compile, done; selectToolsForRun() picks a core / small-refine / expanded tool set once per run. The system prompt is byte-identical across calls (dynamic state goes in <system-reminder> user messages) and skills (SKILL_BLOCKS: ui-ux-pro-max, frontend-design, react-best-practices, motion-dev-animations, performance, core-web-vitals, shadcn, karpathy-guidelines) are loaded on demand via load_skill. Write path: write_file runs agent-lint.normalizeWrittenCode (strip unused react imports, whitespace) and shouldRejectWholeFileRewrite() (refine mode, file >=160 lines, new >=65% of old size, preservedLineFraction >= 0.55 or small-refine prompt -> reject and demand multi_edit unless the prompt says rebuild/redesign). compile tool: preview-bundle.buildPreview() bundles the virtual FS via esbuild-wasm + virtualFsPlugin, with an import map that pins React 18.2 from esm.sh, a data-URL hash router replacing react-router-dom, and only packages in allowed-packages.ts (framer-motion, lucide-react, recharts, clsx, date-fns, nanoid, supabase-js; the same list is rendered into the prompt); then preview-runtime-check.runtimeSmokeTest() injects a capture script into the HTML, runs it in a sandboxed iframe (1.4 s settle, 8 s hard timeout) and reports uncaught errors, console.error, whether #root rendered, route 404s and NaN canvas draws; a passing compile sets runCtx.lastCompileOk and clears dirtySinceCompile. done tool: runDoneVerificationGate() rejects with a structured DONE_REJECTED error if (1) files changed since the last passing compile, (2) findOrphanedStylesheets() finds a .css with rules that nothing imports, (3) findDisallowedImageSources() finds remote images outside an allowlist of free hosts (unsplash/picsum/placehold.co), or (4) interactiveSmokeTest() (clicks interactive elements, checks DOM changed, no handler errors) fails; inconclusive checks never block. agent-memory.ts persists lessons.md (FIX/PATTERN/GOTCHA/TRIED/WORKS) and a CHANGELOG.md across sessions; pending error lessons are promoted only after a subsequent passing compile. set_schema declares Supabase tables (access: owner/public_read/authenticated) and api/_schema.ts generates RLS-enabled migrations. Templates (src/lib/templates.ts, 2.4k lines) are nine hand-written starter projects as file arrays. Visual click-to-edit swaps the jsx-dev-runtime for a shim that stamps data-oeid on host elements (preview-edit.ts / preview-inspect.ts).
core_innovation: A deterministic 'done' verification gate that refuses the model's completion claim unless the exact current files have passed an in-browser build, a runtime execution smoke test, an interactive smoke test, and cross-file lint checks (orphaned stylesheet, image licensing).
strengths: runDoneVerificationGate is exactly the 'gate before generator' posture: stale-compile, orphaned stylesheet, image-host licensing and interactive smoke test are all pure, reproducible checks that reject the model's 'done' with a structured, retryable error and a concrete suggestion.

compile = build AND execute: esbuild only transpiles, so the bundle is actually run in a sandboxed iframe with error/console/#root/route/canvas-NaN capture; 'build succeeded but crashes at runtime' is treated as failure.
allowed-packages.ts is a single dependency-free source of truth consumed by both the bundler's import map and the prompt; the model literally cannot import anything else.

Prompt-cache discipline: byte-identical system prompt, alphabetically sorted tool schemas, tool set chosen once per run, dynamic state only in <system-reminder> messages; skills loaded on demand by id.

Whole-file-rewrite guard (preservedLineFraction) and write-time lint hooks bind hygiene to the harness rather than the model's memory; LoopDetector counts only failing calls to avoid false positives on healthy edit/compile rhythms.
Robust provider layer: retry with Retry-After, circuit breaker, mid-run failover, malformed tool JSON returned to the model as structured errors, per-run token/cache telemetry.
Cross-session memory with a promotion rule (error lessons only become 'recovered lessons' after a passing compile) and a TRIED/FAILED changelog to avoid dead ends.
Good test coverage for the deterministic parts (agent-lint, preview-bundle, preview-edit/inspect, edit-fuzzy-match, virtualFsPlugin, schema-compiler).
weaknesses: It is a code generator (React + CSS in a virtual FS), the exact fragile paradigm we are avoiding; quality depends on the model writing good CSS, and the design 'skills' are aspirational prompting ('BOLD aesthetic direction', 'UNFORGETTABLE', 'NEVER use Inter') that the brief explicitly rejects.
No structured site model, no section library, no design-system tokens as data; 'design language' is whatever the skill prose induces. Output is not reviewable as a contract.
Image licensing gate is host-allowlist only (Unsplash/Picsum/placeholders), i.e. it steers toward generic stock, and there is no real-photo/art-direction layer at all.
In-browser esbuild-wasm preview pins React 18.2 from esm.sh and replaces react-router-dom with a hash router: the preview environment is not the deploy environment.
Single developer, 23 stars, no LICENSE file, package still named bloom, logs and a Remotion ad committed; the 3.8k-line agent.ts and 3k-line ProjectBuilderPage.tsx are hard to extract from.

Runtime checks are heuristic (1.4 s settle, click-everything smoke test) and 'inconclusive never blocks', so the gate can pass a page that is visually broken; there is no axe/Lighthouse/schema validation.
Sensitive product concerns for us: Adsterra ad banners, admin panel, blog CMS, community page: most of the repo is product surface unrelated to generation.
patterns_to_steal: Deterministic done-gate with structured retryable rejections (code, message, suggestion) -> our Launch QA gate: the agent's 'ship' call is refused unless the current SiteDefinition hash matches the last passing Playwright/axe/Lighthouse/placeholder run; rejection payload names the failing check and the fix.
Stale-compile tracking (dirtySinceCompile + lastCompileOk + cached last preview) -> Assembly/QA: hash the SiteDefinition and reuse the last QA report when unchanged; any mutation invalidates it.

Cross-file deterministic lints that pass the compiler but break the page (orphaned stylesheet, disallowed image hosts) -> Anti-slop tier 1 and Launch QA: unreferenced assets, images not from the FactRegistry/asset store, sections referencing missing facts.

Single-source allowlist consumed by both the runtime resolver and the model-visible catalogue (allowed-packages.ts) -> Eligibility/Creative Direction: the eligible design_system_ids, art_direction_ids and variants shown to the model must be the same objects the renderer accepts; generate the prompt catalogue from them.
Prompt-cache discipline (static system prompt, sorted tool schemas, per-run tool set, dynamic state in reminders) -> agent orchestration for every model call in the pipeline.
LoopDetector that fingerprints only failing actions and injects a nudge -> agent orchestration for the audit/fix loop.
Whole-file-rewrite guard (preservedLineFraction) -> visual editor / fix loop: reject a model 'fix' that rewrites most of a section when the prompt was a small refine; require a targeted patch.
Lessons promoted only after a passing verification -> Telemetry -> priors promotion: a prior only moves when a later gate confirms the fix.
patterns_to_avoid: Skill prompts like frontend-design.ts ('pick an extreme tone', 'never use Inter', 'unexpected layouts') -> aspirational prompting is rejected; taste must be encoded in authored design systems and section variants, not adjectives.
Generating React/CSS source as the artefact -> our artefact is SiteDefinition JSON rendered by Astro; the model never writes markup.
Stock-photo host allowlist as the image policy -> we need real owner photos with asset_constraints and art direction; stock URLs would fail our 'real photos' rule.
In-browser bundling with pinned esm.sh React and a hash-router shim -> preview must be the real Astro build, not an approximation.
Karpathy/ui-ux-pro-max style mega-prompts (hundreds of rules) -> rules that can be checked should be code (axe, regex, budgets), not prompt text.
reusable_patterns: DoneVerificationGate: the completion tool is refused unless the current artefact hash has passed all deterministic checks; rejection is structured and retryable.
BuildThenExecute: treat 'compiles' as insufficient; run the artefact in a sandbox and capture runtime/console/render signals.
SharedAllowlist: one dependency-free module defines what the model may reference and what the runtime will resolve.
StaticPromptDynamicReminder: keep system prompt and tool schemas byte-stable; move per-turn state into reminder messages.
FailingCallLoopDetector: fingerprint only errored tool calls and repeated error messages; nudge after N repeats.
PreservedLineFractionGuard: reject wholesale rewrites when most of the original survives verbatim.
VerifiedLessonPromotion: memory entries derived from errors are promoted only after a later passing check.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Ignore the product and the code-generation paradigm, but port the verification harness ideas into our QA gate and agent loop: a structured done/ship gate keyed to the artefact hash, build-then-execute smoke tests (our equivalent is the Astro build plus Playwright crawl), cross-file deterministic lints, the shared allowlist pattern for eligible ids, and the prompt-cache/loop-detection discipline. These are 100-300 line mechanisms each and map cleanly onto TypeScript. Explicitly do not port the skill prompts or the image-host policy.

core_problem: Chat-to-React-site tutorial clone: user types a prompt, the model returns a JSON map of Vite/React files, Sandpack renders them in the browser, JSZip exports them. In this fork the actual model calls have been removed.
architecture: Next.js 15 App Router (JS, not TS). data/Prompt.jsx holds three string prompts (CHAT_PROMPT persona, CODE_GEN_PROMPT, ENHANCE_PROMPT_RULES). components/custom/CodeView.jsx builds the request as `JSON.stringify(messages) + Prompt.CODE_GEN_PROMPT` (entire chat history serialised as a JSON string and concatenated to the instructions, composed on the client) and POSTs to app/api/gen-ai-code/route.jsx, which now returns 503. The expected contract is a JSON object {projectTitle, explanation, files:{'/App.js':{code}}, generatedFiles[]}; the client reads SSE 'data:' lines, takes `finalData.files`, runs preprocessFiles (coerces strings/objects into {code}) and shallow-merges over Lookup.DEFAULT_FILE (public/index.html with cdn.tailwindcss.com, App.css, tailwind.config.js, postcss.config.js) with no validation. Preview is @codesandbox/sandpack-react template 'react' with externalResources ['https://cdn.tailwindcss.com'] and a customSetup.dependencies list (Lookup.DEPENDANCY) that includes firebase, @google/generative-ai, MUI, react-toastify, three uuid packages. Persistence is Convex with schema `workspace: {messages: v.any(), fileData: v.optional(v.any())}` (untyped blobs). Export writes the same files plus a synthesized package.json into a zip. Repo also commits .omc/ agent state, a vexp AGENTS.md, and a PERFORMANCE_IMPROVEMENTS.md about useCallback/dynamic imports.
core_innovation: None; it is a de-wired copy of a YouTube-tutorial Bolt clone whose only distinguishing artifact is a prompt that spells out the canonical AI-slop aesthetic as requirements.
strengths: The CODE_GEN_PROMPT is an unusually explicit written specification of the generic AI look (indigo-500/purple-500/pink-500 gradients, backdrop-blur glassmorphism, rounded-2xl, shadow-xl, hover:scale-105 / -translate-y-1, gradient text headlines, lucide icons, framer-motion) and therefore a useful seed corpus for a tier-1 token ban list.

ENHANCE_PROMPT_RULES example output ('deep purple (#1a1a2e) backgrounds and vibrant gradient accents (indigo to pink)... glassmorphism cards... glowing input focus states... subtle particle effects') is a second, copy-level list of clichés to ban.
Sandpack-in-browser preview with a fixed dependency allowlist is a cheap, working preview mechanism for React output (mechanism is Sandpack's, not the repo's).
weaknesses: AI generation is disabled: every API route returns 503, so the repo cannot be run as described; README tells users to restore configs/AiModel.jsx from git history, which the shallow default branch no longer contains.

Output contract is an untyped JSON files map parsed on the client with no schema, no dependency check, no build check; any model drift (App.jsx vs App.js, missing files) reaches Sandpack as a red error overlay.
System prompt is assembled client-side and the whole message history is stringified into the prompt, so any user can rewrite the instructions and cost is unbounded by history length.

Prompt hardcodes the slop aesthetic as mandatory ('Use gradient backgrounds (e.g., from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500)', 'Add subtle glassmorphism effects', 'Card hover lift effects'), and instructs the model to use 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-[id]?w=800' URLs, which yields hallucinated photo ids and broken images.
Convex schema stores messages and files as v.any(); no versioning, no lineage, no telemetry.
Dependency hygiene: jszip and jzip, uuid + uuidv4 + uuid4, MUI alongside Tailwind, firebase and @google/generative-ai injected into every exported project's package.json.
Committed tooling residue (.omc state, .vscode/mcp.json, vexp AGENTS.md) indicates an agent-edited repo with no review; 11 stars, single author.
patterns_to_steal: Prompt text as ban-list corpus: harvest the literal class tokens and phrases from CODE_GEN_PROMPT and the ENHANCE example ('from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500', 'backdrop-blur', 'glassmorphism', 'hover:scale-105', 'hover:-translate-y-1', 'gradient text', 'particle effects', 'glowing', 'floating geometric shapes') → anti_slop tier-1 regex/token bans and tier-3 n-gram seed list.

Fixed dependency allowlist passed to the sandbox (Lookup.DEPENDANCY → Sandpack customSetup) → qa_gate: our Astro build should fail on any import outside a pinned allowlist, which is the deterministic version of this idea.
patterns_to_avoid: Client-composed system prompt with serialised chat history appended → prompt injection, unbounded token cost, and no server-side control of what the model is told; our pipeline keeps prompts server-side and the model only selects ids.
Untyped JSON files map as the AI-to-renderer contract → no Zod validation possible, no way to detect truncation or missing files; contradicts SiteDefinition typed contract.
Aspirational and aesthetic-prescriptive prompting ('visually stunning', 'impress users immediately', mandatory gradients/glassmorphism) → already rejected; this repo shows exactly what it produces.
Model-invented image URLs (unsplash photo-[id]) → violates asset_constraints on real photos; hallucinated ids render as broken images in front of a client.
v.any() persistence with no generation lineage → no telemetry, no priors promotion, no reproducibility.
reusable_patterns: SlopLexiconHarvest: mine tutorial-grade generation prompts for the literal utility classes and adjectives they mandate and turn them into a ban list.
SandboxDependencyAllowlist: preview environment is given a fixed, pinned dependency set so anything the model imports outside it fails loudly at preview time.
ScaffoldMergeDefaults: deterministic scaffold files are shallow-merged under model output so boilerplate never depends on the model (weak here because model files can still overwrite scaffold).

status_note: active hobby project; a TubeGuruji-course-derived builder (frames/projects/chats schema, WebsiteDesign and ElementSettingSection components) re-skinned with an NVIDIA NIM provider layer and a three.js liquid-glass landing page; 880 KB of the repo is a committed .graphify code-graph viewer, not templates
core_problem: Prompt-to-single-page-HTML generator: streams a Tailwind HTML document from NVIDIA NIM (gpt-oss-120b/20b) token-by-token into an iframe, lets the user click elements to edit text/styles in place, and exports the HTML.
architecture: Next.js 15.5 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript, Clerk auth, Neon Postgres via Drizzle. config/schema.ts: users {credits, maxCredits}, projects, frames {frameId, designCode text}, chats {chatMessage json}, generations {generationId, provider, modelId, canonicalModelId, prompt, output, reasoning, status, durationMs, promptTokens, completionTokens, finishReason, error}. lib/ai/: types.ts (BloomModel with capability flags, ChatRequest, ChatChunk, AIProvider interface), registry.ts, router.ts (AIRouter.executeStream with same-provider fallback to 'bloom-reason' when the selected model errors), providers/nvidia (OpenAI-compatible client against integrate.api.nvidia.com), providers/openrouter stub. app/api/ai-model/route.ts inserts a 'started' generations row, streams raw text/plain chunks (X-Bloom-Generation-Id header), caps max_tokens at 6000 with a comment explaining truncated HTML is worse than a shorter page, temperature 0.6, then updates the row with output/reasoning/tokens/duration. The prompt lives in the client: app/playground/[projectId]/PlayGroundContent.tsx const Prompt ('expert web designer... visually stunning... single-page HTML... Tailwind CDN... Google Fonts Inter... Lucide via unpkg... images ONLY from picsum.photos... subtle gradients, rounded corners, soft shadows'); a keyword regex (/create|build|design|generate|.../) decides whether to wrap the user text in that prompt, otherwise it is passed raw; modifications send the full current HTML plus the request and expect a full rewrite. The client watches the stream for a ```html fence, then rAF-batches setGeneratedCode. app/playground/_components/WebsiteDesign.tsx writes a fixed shell into the iframe with document.write, extracts the <body> contents of the generated document (discarding its <head>), sets root.innerHTML, re-creates <script> nodes so they execute, re-runs lucide.createIcons/initFlowbite on timers, and attaches mouseover/click handlers that outline elements and set contenteditable=true; ElementSettingSection.tsx mutates style and className directly; saving clones documentElement, strips outlines and persists outerHTML to frames.designCode. The iframe is sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin". .claude/CLAUDE.md wires an Astryx design-system CLI (148 components, tokens) for the builder's own UI; generated output does not use it.
core_innovation: None; the closest thing to a mechanism is a per-generation audit row (prompt, output, reasoning, tokens, duration, finish reason) and a body-only injection into a fixed iframe shell.
strengths: generations table records provider, canonical model id, prompt, output, reasoning, token counts, duration, finishReason and status for every call; that is the right minimum telemetry row.
Provider abstraction (AIProvider interface, BloomModel capability flags, AIRouter with same-provider fallback) is cleanly separated from the route handler.
Explicit max_tokens cap with a written rationale (truncated HTML is worse than a shorter page) acknowledges the truncation failure mode of raw-HTML output.
Body-only injection into a fixed shell means the model never controls the document head; conceptually close to 'renderer owns the shell'.
rAF-batched streaming render is a small, correct fix for setState storms during token streaming.
weaknesses: iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" defeats the sandbox: generated scripts run same-origin with the app and can reach the parent document and Clerk session.
Output is a raw HTML string with no schema, no validation, no QA of any kind; the only structural check is finding a ```html fence.
Generated <head> is discarded, so the Google Fonts link the prompt demands is dropped unless the shell already has it; the prompt and the renderer disagree.

Prompt mandates the generic look verbatim ('Inter' as the only font, 'subtle gradients, rounded corners, soft shadows') and random picsum.photos images that have no relationship to the business; the result is polite, uniform slop.
Prompt is composed on the client and intent is detected by a keyword regex, so non-matching requests are sent raw and matching ones can rewrite the instructions.
Every modification is a full-document rewrite of the entire HTML; no diffing, no lineage between frames beyond overwriting designCode.
Direct-DOM editing (contenteditable, style/className mutation) with outerHTML persistence has no source of truth; edits and regenerations diverge and outlines/attributes can leak into saved output.
CDN scripts pinned to @latest (lucide via unpkg) in generated pages; Tailwind Play CDN in production output.
No license file; 6 stars; committed .graphify cache and studio HTML inflate the repo.
patterns_to_steal: GenerationAuditRow (provider, canonical model, prompt, output, reasoning, tokens, duration, finishReason, status, error) → telemetry: mirror this as the per-call record attached to each Decision Manifest, keyed by predicate-snapshot hash.

Shell-owns-head: the renderer supplies the document shell and the model output is only ever inserted into a designated region → renderer: already our model (Astro layout owns head, fonts, meta, schema.org); Bloom shows what breaks when the prompt still asks the model for head content.

Truncation as a first-class failure: cap and detect finishReason=length → qa_gate: any selection call that ends on length is a hard failure, and typed JSON makes truncation detectable rather than guessable.
patterns_to_avoid: allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin on an iframe that runs model-generated markup → sandbox escape into the builder session; our preview is a static Astro build served from an isolated origin.
Raw HTML string as the AI contract with fence-sniffing as the parser → no Zod validation, no section typing, no diffs; contradicts SiteDefinition.
contenteditable/direct-DOM editing persisted as outerHTML → no source of truth; the post-V1 visual editor must edit SiteDefinition JSON and re-render.
Hardcoded single font ('Inter') and random stock photos (picsum) in the prompt → the exact 'AI template' tell our tier-1 gate bans; photos must be owner assets with art-direction constraints.
Keyword-regex intent routing and client-side prompt assembly → fragile and injectable; orchestration decides turn types server-side.
Full-document rewrite for every edit → non-deterministic drift and cost; edits are patches to typed state.
reusable_patterns: GenerationAuditRow: one durable record per model call with model identity, prompt, output, reasoning, usage, duration, finish reason and status.
ShellOwnsHead: the renderer controls the document shell; model output is confined to a designated content region.
StreamBatchRender: buffer streamed tokens and flush to UI state at most once per animation frame.
SameProviderFallback: on model-specific errors, retry with a known-good default model from the same provider before surfacing the error.
adoption_strategy: Ignore. Bloom is a raw-HTML, single-page, prompt-in-the-client builder whose preview iframe is effectively unsandboxed and whose editor mutates the DOM with no source of truth; its prompt hardcodes Inter, soft shadows, rounded corners and random picsum photos, which is precisely the uniform look the anti-slop gate exists to reject. The one thing worth keeping is the shape of its generations audit row, which we replicate in telemetry alongside the Decision Manifest. Nothing else maps onto an Astro/Zod pipeline.

status_note: personal derivative of mendableai/open-lovable (Firecrawl); not a GitHub fork; adds a Crawl4AI FastAPI microservice + Docker; commits .omc/ agent-state files and __pycache__; single contributor
core_problem: Clone or re-imagine an existing website: scrape a URL to markdown + screenshot, hand it to an LLM that emits a full Vite/React project as <file> tags, write those files into a remote sandbox (E2B or Vercel Sandbox) running Vite, and iterate with targeted edits.
architecture: Next.js app router with ~25 API routes under app/api/*. The fork's own delta (CHANGES.md) is small: five routes that called Firecrawl now call crawl4ai-service/main.py, a 165-line FastAPI wrapper exposing GET /scrape (AsyncWebCrawler with BrowserConfig(enable_stealth) + CrawlerRunConfig(magic=True, wait_until=networkidle, delay_before_return_html=3.0), returns {markdown}) and GET /screenshot (base64 PNG); optional residential proxy and a commented-out CapSolver Turnstile solver. /api/search is stubbed to [] and /api/extract-brand-styles now returns raw markdown because Firecrawl's branding format has no equivalent. Upstream architecture retained: app/api/scrape-url-enhanced/route.ts fetches markdown+screenshot in parallel, sanitizes smart quotes and returns {content, screenshot, structured}. app/api/generate-ai-code-stream/route.ts (2k lines) is a single streaming Vercel AI SDK call: builds a ~400-line system prompt of shouted rules ('CRITICAL RULE - VIOLATION WILL RESULT IN FAILURE'), appends conversation context from global.conversationState (scraped websites, recently created files 'DO NOT RECREATE'), for edits fetches sandbox files, builds a FileManifest (types/file-manifest.ts: FileInfo with imports/exports/componentInfo, routes, componentTree) via lib/file-parser.ts regexes, classifies the prompt with lib/edit-intent-analyzer.ts (regex table -> EditType UPDATE_COMPONENT/ADD_FEATURE/FIX_ISSUE/REFACTOR/FULL_REBUILD/UPDATE_STYLE/ADD_DEPENDENCY plus a fileResolver per type) and lib/context-selector.ts (primary files to edit + App/tailwind/index.css/package.json always in context), then asks for complete files in <file path="...">...</file> tags (or <edit> blocks when MORPH_API_KEY enables lib/morph-fast-apply.ts). app/api/apply-ai-code-stream/route.ts parseAIResponse() regex-extracts <file>, <package(s)>, <command> tags, normalizes paths under /home/user/app/src, writes via the SandboxProvider abstraction (lib/sandbox/types.ts abstract class with e2b-provider.ts / vercel-provider.ts; factory.ts picks by env) and installs detected packages. lib/build-validator.ts validateBuild() waits 3 s, fetches the sandbox URL, and decides success by string checks (not the default Vite page, contains id="root", no 'vite-error-overlay'); classifyError() maps messages to missing-package/syntax/timeout/not-rendered and calculateRetryDelay() picks backoff. State is process-global (global.activeSandbox, global.conversationState, global.sandboxState: ~66 references across three routes), i.e. single-tenant. app/generation/page.tsx (4.1k lines) orchestrates the UI: scrape-screenshot -> extract-brand-styles -> scrape-url-enhanced -> generate-ai-code-stream -> apply-ai-code-stream -> sandbox iframe, plus inject-inspector for click-to-select.
core_innovation: Nothing new in the fork itself; upstream's idea is a FileManifest + regex edit-intent classifier that narrows an LLM edit to predicted target files, with generated code exchanged as <file> tags and validated by probing the live Vite sandbox.
strengths: SandboxProvider abstract class (createSandbox/runCommand/writeFile/readFile/listFiles/installPackages/getSandboxUrl/terminate) cleanly separates E2B from Vercel Sandbox behind one interface.
FileManifest data model (imports/exports/componentInfo/routes/componentTree/styleFiles) is a reasonable minimal project index for targeted edits, and EditIntent carries confidence + suggestedContext.
The Crawl4AI service keeps a stable {markdown} contract so callers did not change; docker-compose wires health checks between the two containers.
build-validator's error taxonomy (missing-package, syntax-error, sandbox-timeout, not-rendered, vite-error) with per-type retry delays is a small, reusable classification.
extractMissingPackages() parses three import-failure message shapes and feeds auto-install: a concrete self-heal loop.
weaknesses: The fork adds almost nothing architecturally; it degrades upstream (search stubbed, brand extraction reduced to raw markdown) and commits tool state (.omc/, __pycache__, .replit-tasks).

Website-cloning is the pipeline the architect already rejected for V1; the Cloudflare/anti-bot bypass layers (stealth driver, residential proxy, CAPTCHA solving) are a legal and ethical liability for an agency product.

Generation is one streaming shot with a prompt built from shouted imperatives and emoji; there is no plan, no schema, no structured output; correctness relies on regex-parsing <file> tags from free text.
Validation is string-sniffing the sandbox HTML after a fixed 3 s sleep (no 'vite-error-overlay', has id=root); no axe, Lighthouse, or runtime execution checks.
Process-global mutable state (global.activeSandbox etc.) makes it single-user by construction; 4.1k-line page component and 2k-line route file.
Regex file parser and regex intent classifier are brittle (upstream comments admit fallbacks); brand extraction is now 'the AI can infer brand styles from markdown'.
1 star, one contributor, last push May 2026; upstream mendableai/open-lovable is the maintained lineage.
patterns_to_steal: Error taxonomy + per-class retry policy (classifyError/calculateRetryDelay) -> QA/fix loop: classify Playwright/Lighthouse/axe failures into fixed categories with distinct retry or escalation rules.

Provider abstraction for the execution environment (SandboxProvider abstract class) -> agent orchestration: one interface for local build vs remote preview runner so Astro builds can run in CI, locally, or a sandbox without touching the pipeline.

Edit-intent -> target-file narrowing (FileManifest + EditIntent.targetFiles/suggestedContext) -> post-V1 visual editor and fix loop: map a fix request to the specific SiteDefinition sections and design tokens it may touch, and pass only those to the model.
Scrape contract {markdown, screenshot} with quote sanitization -> research stage only as an input to the FactRegistry (owner-supplied URLs), never as a design corpus.
patterns_to_avoid: Crawl -> screenshot -> 'clone this site' generation -> rejected website-cloner pipeline; trade-dress and copyright exposure.
Cloudflare bypass / residential proxy / CAPTCHA solving -> not acceptable for an agency product; if we crawl, we crawl owner-authorized sources politely.
Free-text <file> tag output parsed by regex -> our model output is Zod-validated JSON selections, never source code.
Prompt engineering by shouting (dozens of 'CRITICAL ... VIOLATION = FAILURE' lines) -> replace with schema constraints and deterministic gates.
Validation by sniffing HTML strings after a sleep -> use real Playwright crawl + axe + Lighthouse budgets.
Process-global state for sandbox/conversation -> pipeline state must be persisted per job (Postgres) and snapshotted.
reusable_patterns: ErrorClassRetryPolicy: map failure messages to a small enum and attach a distinct backoff/escalation per class.
ExecutionProviderInterface: abstract create/run/write/read/list/install/url/terminate over interchangeable sandboxes.
IntentToTargetNarrowing: classify an edit request and resolve it to the minimal set of artefacts the model may modify.
StableScrapeContract: swap scraping backends behind a fixed {markdown, screenshot} shape.
adoption_strategy: Ignore. The fork's contribution is a thin Crawl4AI wrapper plus anti-bot bypasses on top of a cloning pipeline the architect has already excluded; its generation and validation are weaker than OpenThorn's and structurally incompatible with a typed SiteDefinition. The only things worth keeping are two small generalizable patterns (error-class retry policy, execution-provider interface), which we can write from scratch in an afternoon. If crawling is ever needed for FactRegistry ingestion, evaluate upstream Crawl4AI directly (Tier-1 elsewhere), not this wrapper.
