license: FSL-1.1-ALv2 (Functional Source License 1.1 with Apache-2.0 future license): source-available, forbids use in a competing product for two years per release, then converts to Apache-2.0. Our product is a competing use; code cannot be reused, only clean-room patterns.
status_note: active, pre-1.0, single author, heavily agent-authored (every file carries 'W1 PR-1 byte-identical to legacy monolith' style commentary); multi-tenant SaaS scaffolding (Supabase auth/RLS, Stripe, Upstash) is more complete than the generation core
core_problem: BYOK/local-LLM website generator: streams a whole HTML site or a Vite+React project as marker-delimited text from Ollama or OpenRouter, parses it into files, repairs the scaffold, previews in a sandboxed iframe or Sandpack, supports delta edits and one-click Vercel deploy.
architecture: Next.js 16 + React 19 + Zustand stores; Supabase Postgres with users, projects, generations (parent_generation_id lineage), project_files per generation, messages, usage_events, api_key_health, plus RLS and AES-256-GCM encrypted stored keys; Stripe subscriptions and metered premium model SKUs; Upstash sliding-window rate limits. lib/llm.ts is a provider-agnostic streaming helper (Ollama NDJSON vs OpenRouter SSE, browser-direct BYOK or the authenticated /api/openrouter proxy). components/Builder.tsx (about 1300 lines) is the orchestrator: buildSystemPrompt (HTML) or buildReactSystemPrompt (React) → stream → lib/generation/parser.ts (HTML markers '<!-- FILE: x -->', '// FILE:', '/* FILE: */'; with no markers it sniffs doctype/function/braces to guess index.html vs script.js vs styles.css; trimToHtmlBounds strips prose outside <!doctype..</html>) or lib/generation/project-parser.ts (line-based '===AIWP:FILE path="..."===' / '===AIWP:END===' / '===AIWP:DELETE path===' with sanitizeProjectPath rejecting absolute paths, '..', backslashes, >200 chars, non [A-Za-z0-9._-/+@]) → lib/generation/react-scaffold.ts ensureReactScaffold/normalizeTailwindSetup (inject pinned package.json, vite.config.js, index.html; delete tailwind/postcss config; strip @tailwind directives; force cdn.tailwindcss.com) → lib/generation/import-validator.ts findForbiddenImports (regex scan of import/require/dynamic import against ALLOWED_PACKAGES; detection only, posts a chat warning) → lib/generation/slot-renumber.ts (rewrites every data-aiwp-slot to a site-wide sequential number) → silent second LLM call with IMAGE_PASS_PROMPT asking for an Unsplash URL per slot alt text → applyImageUrls. Delta edits: modify prompt returns changed files only, mergeProjectFiles keeps the rest; scoped-modify prompt edits exactly one file; plan-mode prompt is a read-only turn that must not claim changes and emits a ```aiwp-plan checklist. Preview: HTML via srcDoc iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" (no same-origin) with external <link>/<script src> stripped and lib/preview/slot-badges.ts injecting a numbered overlay per data-aiwp-slot; React via Sandpack. lib/prompts/templates.ts holds 31 long-form prompt templates with named fictional businesses and explicit 'avoid centered-heading-plus-3-card-grid; use asymmetric split, bleed image, horizontal strip, bento, masonry, diagonal divider, oversized pull-quote' instructions. Repo root also contains tattoo-parlor-builder-prompt.md (a hand-written design anti-pattern list and {{PLACEHOLDER: ...}} convention) and wedding-intake.md (client intake questionnaire).
core_innovation: A numbered image-slot contract (data-aiwp-slot) that survives regeneration, is renumbered deterministically, is visualised as badges in the preview, and lets a user say 'put my logo in spot 3'; everything else is a conventional stream-parse-repair loop.
strengths: Deterministic post-parse canonicalisation: normalizeTailwindSetup/ensureReactScaffold overwrite boilerplate the model should never own (package.json, vite.config, index.html), delete config files it was told not to emit, and strip @tailwind directives; this is 'never trust the model for scaffolding' done in code.
sanitizeProjectPath is a small, correct path-traversal guard for model-emitted file paths (rejects absolute, '..', backslashes, empty segments, long paths, unusual characters).
Import whitelist scan (import/require/dynamic import regexes, scoped-package aware, config files exempt) catches the most common React-preview failure before the bundler does.

Image-slot contract: data-aiwp-slot attributes, client-side renumbering to site-wide uniqueness, overlay badges injected into the preview, and edit prompts that address slots by number; a clean addressing scheme for owner-provided assets.
Delta-edit semantics: AIWP:DELETE markers plus mergeProjectFiles, and a scoped single-file edit prompt that sends only the target file plus a path listing.
Plan mode is an explicit read-only turn ('you are NOT generating... Do NOT claim to have changed anything') with a fenced aiwp-plan checklist; separates discussion from mutation.
srcDoc iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts" only (no allow-same-origin) and stripping of external stylesheet/script links is the correct sandbox posture for untrusted generated HTML.

tattoo-parlor-builder-prompt.md contains a concrete, human-authored anti-pattern list (multi-hue gradient bleed, centered hero with gradient blob, pill buttons by default, Inter/Poppins/Roboto as display font, emoji icons, three identical icon cards, stock 'smiling person at laptop', pastel drop shadows on every card) and a {{PLACEHOLDER: description}} convention for business facts.
Generation lineage in Postgres (generations.parent_generation_id, project_files per generation, usage_events) is a sensible telemetry substrate.
weaknesses: FSL-1.1 license: any use in a competing website-generation product is prohibited; only clean-room reimplementation of ideas is possible.

System prompts are pure aspirational slop prompting: 'elite web developer with 15+ years', 'Fortune 500 client with a $50,000 budget', 'look like it cost $10,000', 'glassmorphism, gradients, or modern design trends', 'Always add 2-3 features beyond what was explicitly requested', 'Generate realistic data, names, descriptions' (mandated fabrication of facts and testimonials).

The React prompt pins and actively pushes a heavy client stack ('USE IT' for framer-motion, react-query, zustand, react-hook-form, zod, dnd-kit, recharts, react-markdown) into marketing sites, uses HashRouter, and ships Tailwind Play CDN in production output; incompatible with a 180 kB JS budget and with Lighthouse budgets.

Image pass asks the model to invent 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-[ID]' URLs from alt text; ids are hallucinated, so the pass swaps working placehold.co boxes for broken images, and it is a licensing/provenance hole.
Validation is warn-only: forbidden imports produce a chat message but the files are still saved and previewed; there is no gate.

Output contract is raw text with comment/marker delimiters; the no-marker fallback guesses file type by substring sniffing; nothing is typed or schema-validated; truncation is undetectable except via the missing closing marker.
The parser accepts the model's own claims about structure (FILE markers) with no HTML parse, no a11y, no performance, no placeholder scan.

Design quality lives in prose templates ('avoid centered-heading-plus-3-card-grid', 'named business Wavelength') rather than in code; the templates admit that phrasing changes alter parser success rates, i.e. the whole pipeline is prompt-fragile.

1300-line client component orchestrates generation, billing, integrations and image passes; temperature is user-tunable; hosted quota logic is bypassable by the 'silent: true' flag semantics being client-supplied.
One star, single author, agent-written commentary about byte-identical legacy templates; no tests (acknowledged 'unit-test gap').
patterns_to_steal: ScaffoldCanonicalizer (normalizeTailwindSetup/ensureReactScaffold) → assembly: after the model's selections are applied, deterministically overwrite every non-selectable artifact (layout shell, head, config, fonts) from the design system; never accept model-emitted boilerplate.

sanitizeProjectPath → fact_registry / assets ingestion: any model- or owner-provided path (asset filename, slug, route) passes the same allowlist regex and traversal check before touching object storage.
Import/host allowlist regex scan → anti_slop tier-1 and qa_gate: ban any <script src>, <link href>, import specifier or image host outside the pinned allowlist; unlike here, make it a hard failure.

data-aiwp-slot numbered asset slots with deterministic renumbering and preview badges → visual_editor (post-V1) for 'replace photo in slot N', and gap_report: enumerate unfilled slots per selected arrangement to tell the owner exactly which photos would unlock better variants.
AIWP:DELETE + mergeProjectFiles delta semantics → visual_editor / agent_orchestration: edits are patches against a known snapshot, never whole regenerations.
Plan-mode read-only turn contract → agent_orchestration: a 'discuss' turn type that is structurally unable to mutate SiteDefinition and must not claim it did.
tattoo-parlor anti-pattern list and {{PLACEHOLDER: ...}} convention → anti_slop tier-1 ban list seed and qa_gate placeholder scan (grep for {{PLACEHOLDER, TODO, Lorem, 'Company Name').

templates.ts named alternate compositions (asymmetric split, bleed image, horizontally scrollable strip, bento with mismatched cells, masonry, diagonal divider, oversized pull-quote) → section library arrangement vocabulary and signature_move naming, authored as arrangements rather than prose.
patterns_to_avoid: Aspirational and monetary-quality prompting ('$50,000 budget', 'cost $10,000 to build', 'visually stunning') → already rejected; produces the exact generic output the templates then try to talk the model out of.

'Add 2-3 features beyond what was asked' and 'generate realistic data, names, descriptions' → fabricates claims, testimonials and stats; every claim in our sites must come from FactRegistry with provenance.
LLM image-resolution pass inventing Unsplash ids → broken images and unknown licensing; asset_constraints require real, owned or licensed photos with provenance.
Warn-only validation → a gate that does not block is telemetry, not a gate; our tier-1 checks must fail the build.
Marker-delimited raw text as the model output contract → cannot be Zod-validated, truncation-detected, or diffed; SiteDefinition typed JSON stays the contract.
Pushing a heavy client dependency stack and Tailwind Play CDN into generated sites → violates JS budget, motion budget and Lighthouse CI budgets.
User-tunable temperature and client-driven 'silent' quota flags → non-reproducible outputs and trust-boundary bugs; generation parameters are pipeline constants recorded in the Decision Manifest.
Any direct code reuse → FSL-1.1 prohibits competing use; clean-room only.
reusable_patterns: ScaffoldCanonicalizer: after parsing model output, deterministically replace all boilerplate/config artifacts with pinned versions and delete artifacts the model was forbidden to emit.
PathSanitizer: allowlist regex plus traversal and length checks for any externally supplied file path before it reaches storage or a bundler.
NumberedAssetSlots: stable, deterministically renumbered slot ids on every image element, visualised in preview and addressable in edit commands.

status_note: active, single author, pnpm monorepo (frontend on Cloudflare Pages, Hono server in Docker, Supabase Postgres); credit-pack billing, Cloudflare Pages deploy and custom domains are wired; depends on @earendil-works/pi-agent-core and pi-ai pinned to 'latest'
core_problem: Pay-per-generation static site builder for semi-technical users: a tool-calling agent plans a typed site spec, writes each HTML page through a validating write tool, edits with exact-once search/replace, self-validates, and the result is deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
architecture: server/src/lib/generation/agent.ts exports generateWebsite(), an async generator that builds an Agent from @earendil-works/pi-agent-core with model getModel('openai','gpt-5.6-terra'), thinkingLevel 'low', a system prompt from system-prompt.ts, and tools from tools.ts, then relays AgentEvents (tool_execution_start/end, message_end usage) as GenerationEvents over SSE from routes/generate.ts after reserving credits. tools.ts (TypeBox schemas): plan_site fills a typed SiteSpec (type enum landing|portfolio|business|saas|restaurant|agency|blog|ecommerce, tone enum, siteComplexity enum minimal|fun|standard|premium, colorPalette of five hex strings, typography enums, pages[] with sections[] {type, headline, subheadline, content, layout, elements}, features[]); write_page runs validateHtml() and refuses to store the page when hard issues exist, returning the issue list to the agent; read_page; edit_page applies search/replace where each 'old' must occur exactly once (0 or >1 occurrences fail with a corrective message), re-validates, but saves even with issues; validate_site is a model self-report (overallQuality enum, per-page issues/suggestions). agent-interface.ts validateHtml: hard issues = missing DOCTYPE/html/head/body, missing tailwindcss or alpinejs CDN, any image src or css url() outside the allowlist (illustrations.popsy.co, data:); quality warnings = duplicate consecutive section types (class-name sniffing), hero without link/button, adjacent section py-N ratio > 3, same-tone text/background Tailwind class pairs, Popsy URL validity, accessibility heuristics, missing AOS/Lucide. system-prompt.ts = senior-designer persona + workflow (plan_site → write_page per page with <!-- SECTION: name --> markers → validate_site → edit_page fixes) + a DESIGN ANTI-PATTERNS list ('Welcome to [Business]', generic testimonials, dark gradient + floating orbs for every site, same section order every time) + text-forward image policy (no Unsplash/Pexels/picsum/placehold; Popsy SVGs, inline SVG, CSS shapes, gradient orbs) + microinteraction and inline Heroicon snippets + prompts.ts DESIGN_SYSTEM_PROMPT (industry-specific intuition, FONT_PAIRINGS) + design-seeds.ts generateDesignSeed(seed, complexity) (mulberry32 PRNG picks one layout strategy, two signature motifs, hero constraint, CTA style, section-order twist, typography twist, spacing personality, visual texture; fun/minimal variants with emoji directives) + components.ts selectComponentExamples(sectionTypes, seed) (about 1400 lines of HTML exemplars over 19 section types, one per needed type plus two extras, seeded shuffle). interpreter.ts is a separate generateObject/Zod SiteSpecSchema planner on gpt-5.4-mini (appears to be a pre-agent path). skills.ts holds post-hoc whole-HTML rewrite prompts (seo, accessibility, performance, darkMode). lib/analytics/html-quality.ts computes hasSingleH1, ordered headings, CTA above fold, and palette consistency (declared hex palette vs hex values used). Frontend renders pages and shows an AgentActivityLog from tool events.
core_innovation: The write tool is the gate: page output is validated by deterministic code inside the tool call and rejected back to the agent with structured issues, while a seeded design-directive bundle and seeded exemplar selection make each generation's creative constraints reproducible from an integer seed.
strengths: ValidatingWriteTool: write_page refuses invalid HTML and returns the issue list, so the agent's self-repair loop is driven by code checks rather than by its own judgement; toolMetrics counts pagesFailedValidation and fixAttemptsPerPage.

Typed plan before generation: plan_site's TypeBox schema forces the model to commit to enums (site type, tone, complexity, heading style, body font), a five-colour palette and a page/section outline before any HTML is written; the spec is emitted as an event and stored.

Seeded design directive: generateDesignSeed derives layout strategy, motifs, hero constraint, CTA style, section-order twist, typography twist, spacing and texture from a mulberry32 PRNG, so variety is reproducible and loggable rather than left to temperature.
Seeded exemplar selection: selectComponentExamples picks reference HTML per needed section type from the same seed, with an explicit instruction not to copy verbatim.
Image-source allowlist enforced in code over both and css url(); the 'no stock photos' rule is a hard validation failure, not advice.
Exact-once search/replace edits with corrective error messages for zero or multiple matches; read_page-before-edit discipline in the prompt.
html-quality.ts palette-consistency metric compares the declared palette to hex values actually used; a cheap 'did the output honour the plan' check.
Honest text-forward fallback: when no real photos exist, the design leans on typography, colour blocks and inline SVG instead of stock imagery (matches the idea of a no_photo_fallback).
Complexity-aware scope (minimal/fun modes cap sections and forbid forced testimonials/pricing) prevents corporate-ifying a party invite.
weaknesses: GPL-3.0: no code can be reused in our product; patterns only.

Output contract is still raw HTML strings per page; sections are HTML comments, not typed nodes, so validation is substring and regex sniffing over class names with no DOM parse, no axe-core, no Lighthouse.
Generated pages load Tailwind Play CDN, Alpine.js, AOS and Lucide from CDNs at runtime; four render-blocking or layout-shifting scripts in production output, no budgets.
validate_site is an LLM self-assessment with an 'excellent|good|needs_improvement' enum, the rejected design-critic pattern; it does not gate anything and the agent decides when it is done.

The seed vocabulary contains the very clichés the prompt bans: 'bold gradient background with floating geometric shapes', 'dark section with glowing accent elements', 'gradient orbs', 'glassmorphism with frosted elements', 'pill-shaped buttons', 'gradient text highlights'; and write_page's own description says 'follow modern design patterns with gradients, glassmorphism'.

plan_site makes the model infer positioning, palette, tone and industry; our rule is that positioning is owner-declared and design system ids are selected from eligible sets, never invented as hex values.
Prompt explicitly asks for fabricated social proof ('Testimonials with specific details (names, companies, concrete results)'), a trust and legal hazard for a real client.
Popsy/undraw illustrations are a recognisable startup-template tell; the allowlist swaps one cliché for another.
edit_page saves pages that fail validation; only write_page is a true gate.
Model id 'gpt-5.6-terra' and all server deps pinned to 'latest'; pi-agent-core comes from a tiny org with unknown maintenance; interpreter.ts and plan_site duplicate the planning role.
One star, single author, no tests in the generation package visible.
patterns_to_steal: ValidatingWriteTool → anti_slop tier-1 and assembly: the model's selection call is accepted only if the deterministic gate passes; on failure return structured issues and re-prompt with a bounded attempt counter (fixAttemptsPerPage) that feeds telemetry.

SeededDirectiveBundle → creative_direction and decision_manifest: derive the set of eligible arrangement choices offered to the model from a recorded integer seed so a generation is reproducible and the seed appears in the manifest; the vocabulary must be our authored arrangements, not prose adjectives.
ImageSourceAllowlist (extractImageUrls over src and css url()) → qa_gate placeholder/asset scan: fail on any host outside owned object storage; extend to <script src> and <link href>.
PaletteConsistencyCheck (declared palette vs used colours) → anti_slop tier-1: assert that only the selected design system's tokens appear in rendered CSS, zero foreign hex values.
ToolCallMetrics (writePageCalls, pagesFailedValidation, fixAttemptsPerPage, usage) → telemetry: per-generation counters that become evidence for priors promotion (which arrangements fail gates most).
ExactOnceEdit → visual_editor / agent patch semantics post-V1: an edit must address exactly one node (by id), and ambiguity is an error returned to the caller.

ComplexityTier (minimal|fun|standard|premium capping sections) → page_archetype selection: archetype choice should bound section count and forbid inapplicable beats, computed in code from owner inputs.
TextForwardFallback → art_direction no_photo_fallback: typographic and colour-block arrangements when no eligible real photos exist, but with illustration packs banned.
patterns_to_avoid: LLM validate_site self-report with a quality enum → the rejected design-critic gate; keep tier-2 LLM judge warning-only and never let the model decide it is done.
Model-invented palette, tone and positioning in plan_site → violates owner-declared positioning and 'model selects ids, never emits tokens'.
Fabricated testimonials with names and companies → every claim must be in FactRegistry with provenance and a quotable flag.
Seed vocabulary that includes gradient orbs, glassmorphism, glowing accents → the directive bundle must draw only from the human-authored section library.
Raw HTML per page with comment section markers → not Zod-typed, not diffable; keep SiteDefinition JSON.
Four CDN runtimes (Tailwind Play, Alpine, AOS, Lucide) in shipped pages → breaks the 180 kB JS budget and Lighthouse budgets; Astro islands with near-zero JS instead.
Popsy/undraw illustration allowlist → a different template tell; art direction forbids generic illustration packs as well as ai_generated_person.
Any GPL code reuse → clean-room only.
reusable_patterns: ValidatingWriteTool: the tool that persists output runs deterministic checks and rejects with structured issues; invalid output never enters state.
SeededDirectiveBundle: creative constraints sampled from a recorded seed via a fixed PRNG so variety is reproducible and auditable.
ImageSourceAllowlist: extract every image and css url() reference and fail on any host not on the allowlist.
ExactOnceEdit: search/replace or node edits must match exactly one location; zero or many is an error returned to the caller.
PaletteConsistencyCheck: compare colours declared in the plan or design system to colours present in the output.
ToolCallMetrics: count tool invocations, validation failures and fix attempts per artifact as telemetry.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (patterns only, clean-room; GPL forbids code reuse). Reimplement the validating-write-tool loop as our tier-1 gate boundary: the model's SiteDefinition selection is accepted only after Zod plus deterministic checks pass, failures return structured issues with a bounded retry counter that is logged. Take the seeded directive idea but bind the seed to our authored arrangement library and record it in the Decision Manifest. Port the image/host allowlist and palette-consistency checks into launch QA and tier-1. Reject the LLM validate_site self-score, the model-inferred palette and positioning, the fabricated testimonials instruction, the CDN runtime stack and the illustration-pack allowlist.

status_note: active but strategically superseded: README now says 'This is the open-source visual editor that started Onlook (Next.js + Tailwind). The hosted product we're building next ... is in early access via the waitlist' — the OSS web app is the legacy product, 382 open issues, last substantive commit in clone 2026-07-21. Fully open (Apache-2.0) but operationally dependent on external services: CodeSandbox SDK (sandboxes), Supabase (auth/db), OpenRouter (LLMs), Morph/Relace (fast-apply), Freestyle (hosting), PostHog, Langfuse. Self-hosting docs exist (docker-compose). apps/admin is a git submodule to a separate repo. Next.js + Tailwind projects only.
core_problem: Let designers edit a real Next.js codebase visually: every DOM edit in a live preview (style, text, insert, move, group) is translated into an AST edit of the exact JSX source that produced that element, with an AI chat that has the same code access.
architecture: Monorepo (Bun). apps/web/client is a Next.js app whose state is a MobX EditorEngine (components/store/editor/engine.ts) composed of managers: branches (each branch = its own sandbox + history + CodeFileSystem), frames (iframes on an infinite canvas), elements/overlay/snap (selection UI), action, history, code, ast, style, text, insert, move, group, copy, image, font, theme, pages, chat, git, sandbox, screenshot, ide. The user's project runs inside a CodeSandbox VM (packages/code-provider: CodesandboxProvider | NodeFsProvider) and is mirrored into a browser-side CodeFileSystem (packages/file-system) by a sync engine. DOM<->source mapping ('sourcemap for JSX'): CodeFileSystem.writeFile -> processJsxFile parses with @babel/parser (ts+jsx), addOidsToAst (packages/parser/src/ids.ts) stamps data-oid="" on every JSXOpeningElement except Fragments, deduping against per-file/global/branch OID sets (conflicts or duplicates get fresh ids), regenerates with retainLines:true, prettier-formats, and rebuilds an index oid -> JsxElementMetadata { path, branchId, startTag/endTag {line,column}, component (enclosing function/class/variable name via a componentStack), dynamicType: array|conditional (detected from .map() callbacks, ternaries, &&/||), coreElementType: component-root|body-tag, code (exact source slice) } via createTemplateNodeMap + getContentFromTemplateNode (packages/parser/src/template-node/map.ts); the index is persisted and rebuildIndex batches all JSX files. The root layout additionally gets injectPreloadScript (a
core_innovation: A write-time 'source map for JSX' (stable data-oid stamped into source, indexed to file/line/column/enclosing-component/dynamic-context) that lets non-destructive DOM edits be replayed as inverse-safe serializable actions which are compiled into AST edits of the originating source.
strengths: Cleanest open implementation of DOM->source mapping: stable ids injected at write time (not build time), a persisted oid index with exact ranges and enclosing component, and explicit handling of dynamic contexts (.map, ternaries) and component-instance vs definition.

Serializable inverse actions with transactions (packages/models/src/actions, store/editor/history): every edit is data, undo is computed not snapshotted, continuous edits coalesce, and the docs state the intent that 'an agent generate actions'.

Non-destructive live preview: style edits live in an injected stylesheet keyed by DOM ids (css-tree AST) and text edits in an overlay, so nothing in the app is mutated until the action is committed to code.
Typed RPC boundary between editor and page (penpal; PenpalChildMethods = typeof preloadMethods) with reconnect logic — a small, reviewable contract instead of ad-hoc postMessage.

Layer tree is derived from the real DOM (buildLayerTree) then enriched from source metadata (component name, dynamic/conditional flags) — the editor tells users when an element is one of many rendered by a loop.
Tool-call repair via a small model constrained to the tool's Zod schema; ASK/EDIT/CREATE/FIX modes with distinct prompts and models; summary-mode context compaction.
Apache-2.0, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md present (repo is agent-friendly), branches-as-sandboxes and git checkpoints give cheap experiment/rollback semantics.
weaknesses: Product pivot: the OSS repo is now the predecessor of a hosted product; expect slowing maintenance (382 open issues) and no roadmap for non-Next.js/non-Tailwind support.
Heavy external-service coupling (CodeSandbox SDK, Supabase, OpenRouter, Morph/Relace, Freestyle, PostHog, Langfuse); the web app is not a library you can embed — it is a whole SaaS clone.

data-oid attributes are written into the user's source files and shipped to production DOM unless stripped (removeIdsFromAst exists but is opt-in); LLM prompts must be told not to touch them; regenerate+prettier can produce noisy diffs.
Style edits are lossy: CSS deltas are translated to Tailwind classes (CssToTailwindTranslator) — anything Tailwind cannot express is dropped or approximated; non-Tailwind projects unsupported.

Instance resolution is a heuristic (N-th same-named child in the parent's source slice) that degrades under conditionals/maps; real-time insert is disabled as buggy; undo requires a code write + HMR round trip (slow, and a failed write desynchronises DOM and source).
Babel-specific pipeline (JSX AST, retainLines codegen) — no path to .astro templates without a different parser/serializer.
The editing model is 'edit arbitrary source' — the opposite of a typed SiteDefinition; there is no schema, no catalogue, no constraints on what the designer or AI may change.
Security posture of the preload channel is permissive (allowedOrigins '*', TODO in source).
patterns_to_steal: Inverse serializable Action union with Change<T>{original, updated} and transactions -> visual_editor over SiteDefinition: define SiteEditAction (set-copy, swap-asset, reorder-section, toggle-section) with computed inverses and coalescing; history is the action log, which doubles as telemetry input.

Write-time stable node ids + persisted id index (oid -> file/range/component/dynamic flags) -> renderer/visual_editor: stamp data-section-id / data-node-path from the SiteDefinition into rendered Astro output so the preview can map any click back to a Zod path; Astro dev mode already emits data-astro-source-file/loc for the code-first case (verify).

Non-destructive preview stylesheet keyed on DOM ids (css-tree managed) -> visual_editor: preview owner edits (e.g. design_system swap, copy) as an overlay before committing a new SiteDefinition version.
Typed penpal RPC contract between editor and preview iframe -> visual_editor: one exported preloadMethods object whose type is the contract; keep the page-side script dependency-free.

Layer tree from DOM enriched with source metadata (dynamic/conditional markers) -> visual_editor: show owners which elements are repeated from data (fact lists, testimonials) so they edit the source record, not one instance.

Tool-call repair with a schema-constrained small model -> agent_orchestration: when the selection model emits an invalid design_system_id/arrangement payload, repair against the Zod schema instead of retrying the big model.
Branch = sandbox + git checkpoints -> agent_orchestration/qa_gate: run alternative arrangements as branches with checkpoints so the QA gate can compare and roll back deterministically.
Separate CREATE/EDIT/ASK/FIX prompt+model routing with stepCountIs limits -> agent_orchestration: bound tool loops per stage.
patterns_to_avoid: Editing arbitrary source AST as the owner-facing model -> owners edit typed fields of SiteDefinition; sections are human-authored and immutable to owners; only the agency pipeline (and only via section variants) changes layout.
CSS -> Tailwind class translation of free-form style edits -> styles come from selected design tokens; there is no free style editing to translate.
Injecting editor ids into committed source files -> ids belong to the rendered output/SiteDefinition, never to the authored section templates.
CREATE-from-prompt page generation and fast-apply file rewriting -> rejected generation path; our model selects ids, it does not write section code.
Depending on a hosted sandbox (CodeSandbox) for preview -> Astro dev server or a static build in a local worker is sufficient and deterministic.
reusable_patterns: SourceIdSourcemap: stamp a stable id attribute on every authored element at write time and keep an index id -> {file, range, enclosing component, dynamic context} so any rendered node maps back to its source.
InverseActionHistory: edits are serializable actions with a pure inverse function; undo/redo re-dispatch computed inverses; transactions coalesce continuous edits.
OverlayStylesheetPreview: preview changes as rules in a dedicated injected stylesheet keyed by per-node ids, leaving the application's own styles untouched until commit.
InstanceVsDefinitionResolution: when a source element renders multiple DOM nodes, resolve each node to the usage site (instance id) by walking to the nearest component boundary.
TypedIframeRPC: a single exported methods object on the page side whose TypeScript type is the contract, bridged with a promise-based messenger with reconnect.
SchemaConstrainedToolRepair: on invalid tool arguments, ask a small model to regenerate them against the tool's schema before failing.
adoption_strategy: Adapt — Onlook is the wrong product shape for owners (arbitrary source editing, Next.js/Tailwind only, SaaS-tethered, pivoting) but the right mechanics for a code-aware editor and for the agent loop. Immediately: define SiteDefinition edits as an inverse-action union with transactions (their HistoryManager/helpers are ~300 lines and portable), and stamp SiteDefinition node ids into Astro output so the future editor can map DOM->Zod path without any Babel machinery. Post-V1 editor: reuse the penpal-style typed RPC + overlay-stylesheet preview over an Astro dev iframe; skip CodeSandbox, Tailwind translation and AST rewriting. For the agency's internal code-first loop (agent fixes a section arrangement), Astro's dev-mode source-location attributes replace data-oid; only if we need programmatic .astro rewrites would we build an @astrojs/compiler-based equivalent of packages/parser (difficulty ~6). Do not run the app itself.

status_note: active - v0.23.6 (2026-08-26), 58 commits since 2026-03, but effectively a one-person project: artf has 5462 contributions vs the next human contributor ~70. pnpm monorepo: packages/core (the library), packages/cli, docs.
core_problem: A framework-agnostic, embeddable HTML/CSS web-builder runtime: an iframe canvas where a Backbone model tree of DOM-like 'Components' plus a separate CSS-rule model is edited via drag/drop, traits and a style manager, then exported back to HTML+CSS or a JSON project.
architecture: Backbone 1.4 + underscore runtime (packages/core/src). editor/model/Editor.ts instantiates a fixed module list (`deps`) and a `storableDeps` list [DataSourceManager, AssetManager, CssComposer, PageManager, ComponentManager, SelectorManager]; `storeData()` merges each module's `store()` slice keyed by `storageKey` ('pages','styles','assets','dataSources',...) into ProjectData and `loadData()` clears and reloads each slice in order. ProjectData is typed `{[key:string]: any}` (storage_manager/model/IStorage.ts) - there is no schema. The document is Pages -> Frames -> a root 'wrapper' Component -> recursive `components`. Component (dom_components/model/Component.ts, 2262 lines) is a Backbone Model whose defaults are DOM-ish (tagName, type, attributes, content, style, classes, script) plus ~20 editor-permission flags (draggable, droppable, stylable, editable, removable, copyable, locked, unstylable[], propagate[], delegate{}) and undo flags (`_undo`, `_undoexc`); `toJSON()` strips runtime keys (toolbar, traits, status, open) and optionally only-changed props (`avoidDefaults`). `ComponentDefinition` is open-ended (`[key:string]: unknown`). New types are registered with `Components.addType(id, {model, view, isComponent, isParsedNode, extend, extendView, extendFn})`, which builds a prototype-extension stack; ParserHtml runs each type's `isComponent(node)` recogniser to reverse-parse arbitrary HTML into typed components. Styles are NOT on the component: CssComposer holds CssRule {selectors, style, mediaText, state, atRuleType}; `component.setStyle()` writes an `#id` rule (or inline when configured). Canvas: canvas/view/FrameView.ts renders one `<iframe>` per Frame; `renderBody()` injects editor CSS and each ComponentView mounts DOM with `$el.data('model', model)` and `el.__gjsv = view` (utils/mixins getModel/getViewEl) - the DOM->model map is a per-element pointer, not an id lookup. Inline text: ComponentTextView toggles a pluggable RTE on the element and on blur reparses innerHTML back into child components ('sync:content'). Undo: undo_manager/index.ts wraps backbone-undo, registers models/collections, custom undo types for change/add/remove/reset; `_undo` (boolean or list of attribute keys) and `_undoexc` decide which attribute changes are recorded. Traits (trait_manager/types.ts: type, name, label, changeProp, getValue/setValue, min, max, unit, options) are per-component property editors. StyleManager = Sectors -> Property models (Number/Select/Radio/Slider/Composite/Stack) with `buildProps`. Blocks = {label, media, content: html | ComponentDefinition, category}. Symbols (dom_components/model/SymbolUtils.ts) link a main component to instances with change propagation and per-instance overrides. DataSources (added 2025-26) contribute `data-variable`, `data-condition`, `data-collection` component types that resolve paths into DataRecords with `transformers`; the 'dataSources' slice loads before the others. Plugins are `(editor, opts) => void` functions resolved by id in PluginManager with config from `pluginsOpts`. Export: `component.toHTML({withProps})` emits `data-gjs-*` attributes so HTML can be re-imported.
core_innovation: A DOM-shaped Backbone component tree with a real CSS-rule model, rendered live in an iframe, plus a recogniser stack (`isComponent`) that lets arbitrary HTML round-trip back into typed components.
strengths: Complete, battle-tested editor runtime: pages/frames, layers, selectors/states/media queries, RTE, device previews, keymaps, i18n, storage, undo - all as swappable modules on one EditorModel.
Per-component permission flags (draggable/droppable/stylable/editable/locked/unstylable[]/propagate[]) are a real constraint vocabulary for locking an editor down.
Symbols (main/instance with propagation + overrides) solve shared header/footer editing correctly.
DataSources with data-variable / data-condition / data-collection components give declarative data binding that keeps a reference to source id and path.
Traits and Style-manager Properties are declarative UI descriptors rendered generically, not bespoke forms.
128 test files under packages/core/test; docs/modules/*.md document each subsystem; BSD-3 is permissive.
weaknesses: ProjectData is untyped `Record<string, any>` and ComponentDefinition is open-ended: there is no contract, so validation must be bolted on outside the editor.

The document is a DOM with metadata (tagName/attributes/style), not a semantic section tree; there is no place for `requires`, `design_compat`, `arrangement`, `intensity` except untyped custom props the editor ignores.

Defaults are all-permissive (every component draggable, droppable, stylable) and the Style Manager writes arbitrary CSS rules - the opposite of 'model selects a design_system_id, never emits a token'. Locking it down means fighting every default.
Backbone/underscore/cash runtime, a 2.2k-line Component god-class, prototype-extension `addType` stack; heavy bundle, not tree-shakeable, no TypeScript generics for component props.

The editor's own DOM render is the editing surface. Server-rendered Astro output can only enter via ParserHtml reverse-parsing, which makes the HTML the source of truth and SiteDefinition a derived artifact (double source of truth, lossy).
Bus factor 1 (single maintainer), 0.x versioning since 2017.
patterns_to_steal: Storable module slices (`storageKey` + `store()`/`load()` composed into one project doc, dataSources loaded first) -> SiteDefinition as named Zod sub-documents (site, pages, assets, facts) each with its own load order and migration.

Per-component permission flags with `propagate[]` inheritance and `unstylable[]` allow-lists -> per-section-variant and per-field `editable` / `locked` / `allowed_ops` metadata in the Zod schema so the post-V1 editor is constrained by the same contract the generator obeys.
`_undo` / `_undoexc` attribute-level undo eligibility -> declare which SiteDefinition fields are undoable vs ephemeral (selection, ui state) in the schema, not in editor code.

`toHTML({withProps})` emitting `data-gjs-*` attributes + `isComponent` recogniser -> the Astro renderer emits `data-sd-path` (JSON pointer into SiteDefinition) and `data-sd-variant` on every section/field root so an overlay editor maps DOM -> data node by attribute, never by re-parsing HTML.

DataSources data-variable {path, defaultValue} + record `transformers` -> FactRegistry binding: a section field holds a fact reference; the renderer resolves it and keeps provenance/quotable flags for the QA gate.
Symbols main/instance with override map -> shared blocks (header/footer/CTA) referenced by id in SiteDefinition with per-page overrides.
Trait descriptors (type/label/min/max/options/changeProp) -> derive editor property panels from Zod field metadata instead of hand-written forms.
patterns_to_avoid: DOM-as-document (tagName/attributes/style on every node) -> our unit is a section variant with typed fields; exposing tagName/classes to an editor destroys the arrangement genome and lets humans generate slop.

Free-form Style Manager writing CSS rules -> violates 'design system = token files, model/human selects an id'. Any editor over our stack must only offer enumerated variants/arrangements, never CSS properties.
Embedding the GrapesJS runtime and reverse-parsing Astro HTML via ParserHtml -> two sources of truth and a Backbone+iframe render pipeline that duplicates the Astro renderer.
Prototype-extension `addType` with `extendFn` method chaining -> untyped and order-dependent; use discriminated Zod unions per section family instead.
Untyped ProjectData `Record<string, any>` -> never let the editor persist anything that is not the Zod SiteDefinition.
reusable_patterns: StorableSlices: a project document assembled from independently loadable/serialisable module slices with a declared load order.
PermissionFlagsWithPropagation: node-level capability flags (draggable/droppable/stylable/locked) that children inherit via an explicit propagate list.
AttributeAnnotatedRoundTrip: emit machine-readable data-* attributes on rendered HTML so a recogniser can map DOM back to typed nodes.
UndoEligibilityOnModel: undo participation declared per attribute on the data model (_undo / _undoexc) rather than per action in the editor.
SymbolInstancePropagation: a main node whose instances receive changes unless a per-instance override map says otherwise.
DeclarativeTraitDescriptors: property editors described as data (type/options/min/max) and rendered generically.
adoption_strategy: Adapt - do not embed GrapesJS. Its document is a DOM-with-metadata and its defaults make everything draggable and stylable, which fights a typed Zod SiteDefinition made of enumerated section variants; the integration would be spent locking every flag and would still end with an untyped ProjectData. Take five mechanisms instead: storable slices for the SiteDefinition sub-documents, permission flags + propagate as Zod field metadata, attribute-annotated HTML (`data-sd-path`) emitted by the Astro renderer so a post-V1 overlay editor can map DOM to data node, data-variable style fact binding for the FactRegistry, and symbol/instance for shared blocks. Undo should be a patch log over SiteDefinition (see craft.js), not Backbone model tracking.

status_note: active (v0.23.0, 2026-08). GitHub org redirected measuredco -> puckeditor; npm package renamed @measured/puck -> @puckeditor/core. Core editor + renderer are MIT and fully in-repo. 'Puck AI' (@puckeditor/plugin-ai + @puckeditor/cloud-client) is NOT in the repo: it is a closed npm client that proxies to cloud.puckeditor.com and needs a PUCK_API_KEY (SaaS boundary).
core_problem: A React-only, config-driven page editor: you describe a component catalogue (Config) with typed fields per component, and Puck gives you a drag-and-drop editor that emits/consumes a plain JSON document (Data) which a separate <Render> turns back into React. You own the data; no backend.
architecture: Two artefacts. (1) Config (packages/core/types/Config.tsx): components[name] = { render, label, defaultProps, fields, permissions, inline, resolveFields, resolveData, resolvePermissions, metadata } plus root and categories. Fields (types/Fields.ts) are a discriminated union: text, textarea, number, select, radio, richtext (tiptap), array (arrayFields, min/max), object (objectFields), external (fetchList/mapProp — async pickers), custom (render), slot (allow/disallow component lists). (2) Data (types/Data.tsx): { root: { props }, content: ComponentData[], zones?: Record<'parentId:zone', ComponentData[]> } with ComponentData = { type, props: { id, ...fields }, readOnly? }. Nested content now lives inside props via slot fields (WithDeepSlots<T> recursively rewrites Slot -> SlotComponent at render time); 'zones' (DropZone) is deprecated and lib/migrate.ts carries an ordered migrations array (root->root.props, zones->slots) with a migrateDynamicZonesForComponent escape hatch. Runtime: zustand store (store/index.ts) with slices for history, permissions, fields, nodes; a reducer (reducer/actions/*) with insert/move/reorder/remove/duplicate/replace/replaceRoot/set/setData/setUi/registerZone; a derived flat index PrivateAppState.indexes { nodes[id] -> { data, parentId, zone, path }, zones['parentId:zone'] -> { contentIds, type } } that every operation reads. Editor canvas is an iframe (AutoFrame, iframe.enabled/syncHostStyles); DraggableComponent stamps data-puck-component={id} on the rendered element and DropZone stamps data-puck-dropzone={zoneCompound}; lib/dom-selectors.ts and lib/get-selector-for-id.ts map DOM<->node. DnD is @dnd-kit 0.4 with a custom NestedDroppablePlugin, dynamic/directional collision detectors and 'fluid|static' behaviours. Inline editing: fields with contentEditable:true are swapped at render by field-transforms (lib/field-transforms/default-transforms/inline-text-transform.tsx) for an <InlineTextField> (contentEditable='plaintext-only') that writes back with setDeep(props, propPath, value) + resolveAndReplaceData. Resolvers: resolveData(data, { changed, lastData, trigger: insert|replace|load|force|move, parent, root, metadata }) -> { props, readOnly } cached per id (lib/resolve-component-data.ts); resolveAllData (lib/resolve-all-data.ts, RSC-safe) walks root, content, slots and zones concurrently with a per-call cache; resolveFields for dynamic field sets; resolvePermissions (store/slices/permissions.ts) layers global -> component -> per-instance async permissions {drag, duplicate, delete, edit, insert, ...custom}. Rendering: components/Render (client) and components/ServerRender (exported at @puckeditor/core/rsc) are pure functions of (config, data) — no editor code — resolving slots via useSlots/SlotRenderPure. Extension: Plugin = { name, label, icon, render, overrides, fieldTransforms }; overrides (types/API/Overrides.ts: header, headerActions, fields, fieldLabel, fieldTypes, drawer, drawerItem, componentOverlay, outline, preview, iframe, actionBar, puck) are curried across plugins by lib/load-overrides.ts; usePuck/createUsePuck exposes appState, dispatch, history, getPermissions. History (store/slices/history.ts): debounced (250 ms) whole-AppState snapshots in histories[] with an index; back/forward dispatch {type:'set'}; InitialHistory prop seeds it; onAction(action, appState, prevAppState) hook. AI: recipes/next-ai wires createAiPlugin() in the browser to puckHandler() from @puckeditor/cloud-client on the server; 'assembly mode' only composes components from Config, 'design mode' lets the cloud generate new components which withDynamicConfig(config, data) merges into Config at render time.
core_innovation: Treating the component catalogue as a typed Config where nested layout is just another field type (slot with allow/disallow), so the document stays a plain {type, props} tree that a stateless <Render> can rebuild anywhere, with async resolvers (data/fields/permissions) as the only side-effect surface.
strengths: Config is a real 'catalogue the editor is constrained to': the palette, the fields, and per-slot allow/disallow lists (lib/data/is-component-allowed.ts, resolve-zone-constraints.ts) are all declared in one object; nothing outside Config can be inserted.

Data is minimal and renderer-agnostic in shape ({type, props{id}} tree) and the renderer is a pure function of (config, data) with an RSC-safe export (bundle/rsc.tsx) — it can be run at build time with no client JS.

Three-layer permissions (global -> component -> resolvePermissions per instance, async, cached on changed props) plus per-prop readOnly returned by resolveData: enough to lock structure and expose only copy/asset fields.

resolveData contract is well designed: 'changed' diff, 'trigger' enum, parent/root context, id-keyed cache, and an offline resolveAllData for publish-time hydration — a clean seam for a FactRegistry lookup.

Plugin/overrides API is composable (curried overrides across plugins) and already ships a heading-analyzer plugin (packages/plugin-heading-analyzer) that audits h1-h6 hierarchy inside the iframe — a template for QA-in-editor plugins.
Explicit data migration mechanism (lib/migrate.ts) with ordered migrations, and the 'assembly mode' concept in Puck AI proves the market wants AI constrained to a catalogue.
MIT, active, small core (5.4 MB clone), strong TypeScript generics (Config<Props>, UserGenerics) giving end-to-end prop typing from Config to render.
weaknesses: Types only, no runtime schema: Config components is deliberately Record<string, any> (types/Config.tsx comment 'This _deliberately_ casts as any'); Data is never validated against Config at load; no version/$schema field on Data (migrations are inferred from shape).

React-only for both editor and renderer; sections must be React components for the canvas to render them. Our sections are Astro — the editor canvas cannot show them without either a React twin of every section or replacing the preview via overrides.preview/iframe (which loses DnD, since DnD relies on DraggableComponent wrapping each render).
Undo/redo is full-state snapshots debounced at 250 ms — coarse, memory-heavy for large documents, no operation semantics, cannot be replayed as an audit log.
Editor bundle is heavy: tiptap 3 (~20 packages), @dnd-kit, zustand, radix, happy-dom, object-hash, deep-diff — fine on an /edit route, unacceptable anywhere near the public page.
Fields are UI widgets, not constraints: 'text' has no maxLength/regex, 'select' options are untyped, no cross-field rules; resolveFields can implement them but imperatively.
Ongoing model churn (DropZone -> slot, root -> root.props) and an overrides API documented as 'highly experimental and likely to experience breaking changes'.
Puck AI (the interesting constrained-assembly part) is closed SaaS; the open repo only contains the plumbing to call it.
resolveData runs inside the editor on every prop change, encouraging network side-effects from field edits.
patterns_to_steal: Config-as-catalogue with per-slot allow/disallow -> our section library's design_compat / Compat filter: generate a Puck-style Config from the Zod section variants so the post-V1 editor can only insert eligible variants into eligible slots.

Three-layer permissions + readOnly-per-prop -> visual_editor: lock drag/insert/delete globally, expose only copy, CTA text, image slot and alt text as editable; everything from the layout genome stays readOnly.

resolveData(changed, trigger, parent, root) with resolveAllData at publish -> cms/fact_registry: hydrate quotable facts and asset metadata from FactRegistry at publish time, mark them readOnly, and skip work unless 'changed' touches the fact reference.
Ordered migrations array (lib/migrate.ts) -> SiteDefinition versioning: keep a migrations[] keyed on schema version so playbook/section schema changes never strand stored sites.

Flat node/zone index derived from the tree (PrivateAppState.indexes) -> renderer/visual_editor: compute an id -> {parentId, slot, path} index once per SiteDefinition load; all editor ops address nodes by id, never by array position.
onAction(action, state, prevState) hook -> telemetry: emit typed editor actions as telemetry events for priors promotion (which variants owners keep vs. replace).

Heading-analyzer plugin pattern (query the preview iframe DOM, build outline, link back to node) -> qa_gate: run cheap DOM audits (heading order, missing alt, placeholder text) live in the editor before the Playwright/axe gate.
Field transforms (swap a prop value for an inline-editable node only in edit mode) -> visual_editor: inline copy editing over server-rendered output without changing section components.
patterns_to_avoid: 'Design mode' (AI generates new components on the fly, merged via withDynamicConfig) -> violates 'innovation is constraint, not generation'; only 'assembly mode' semantics are acceptable, and we implement them ourselves against the Zod catalogue.
Whole-state snapshot history -> we want inverse, serializable operations over SiteDefinition (see Onlook) so edits are auditable and replayable.

Free-form component render + free-form fields as the contract -> our sections carry requires/composition/motion/a11y metadata that Puck's ComponentConfig has no slot for; do not flatten SiteDefinition into a Puck Data document as the source of truth — project into it for the editor only.
Running the Puck editor as the site's runtime -> React + tiptap + dnd-kit would blow the 180 kB JS budget; the editor must live on a separate route and the public site must stay Astro static output.
TypeScript-only Data contract with no runtime validation -> keep Zod as the single validated contract; Puck types can be derived from it, never the reverse.
reusable_patterns: CatalogueConfig: a single declarative object listing every insertable component, its typed fields, defaults and per-slot allow-lists, from which palette, forms and validation are all derived.
SlotAsField: nested content is a typed field of the parent node (props.children: Node[]) rather than a side table, so the document is one tree and the renderer needs no zone lookup.
LayeredPermissions: global -> per-type -> per-instance (async, cached on changed props) boolean capabilities resolved to a single Permissions object per node.
ChangedDiffResolver: async resolver receives (data, { changed, lastData, trigger }) and returns partial props + readOnly, cached by node id so expensive lookups run only when referenced props change.
OrderedDataMigrations: an array of pure (data, config) -> data migrations applied in sequence on load, each detecting the legacy shape it fixes.
EditModeFieldTransform: at render time in edit mode, substitute a prop value with an editable widget bound to the prop path; production render is untouched.
adoption_strategy: Adapt — Do not adopt Puck as the runtime or as the source of truth, but it is the closest existing shape to 'a component catalogue the AI and the owner are constrained to'. Post-V1: generate a Puck Config from the Zod section library (zod -> Puck fields mapping; slot allow-lists from design_compat; permissions drag/insert/delete=false, readOnly on every genome prop) and project SiteDefinition into Puck Data for a copy/asset-editing session, then map edits back through Zod. For the canvas, evaluate overrides.preview pointing at an Astro dev-server iframe with our own data-section-id attributes (accept losing DnD, which we do not want owners to have anyway); if that proves awkward, keep only Puck's Fields/Outline plugins and write our own preview. Independently of the editor, copy the resolveData/resolveAllData, layered permissions and migrations patterns into the SiteDefinition tooling now.

status_note: maintenance mode: v5.4.6 (2026-07-28) is a dependency/security-hygiene release (ajv 8, yarn 4, drop coveralls; one PR from a 'claude/' branch); previous release v5.4.5 was 2024-11-05 and v5.4.4 2023-04. 7 commits since 2025-01-01, all tooling. 11 open issues. Lerna monorepo: packages/editor (@react-page/editor), packages/plugins/{content,layout}, packages/react-admin.
core_problem: A React content editor where a page is a recursive 12-column grid of rows and cells, each cell owned by a versioned 'cell plugin' that renders its own data, with i18n, migrations and a static renderer for read-only output.
architecture: packages/editor/src. Document (core/types/node.ts): `Value {id, rows: Row[], version}`; `Row {id, cells: Cell[]}`; `Cell {id, rows?: Row[], plugin?: {id, version}, dataI18n?: {[lang]: Record<string, unknown>}, size?: 1..12 twelfths, inline?: 'left'|'right', isDraft?, isDraftI18n?, hasInlineNeighbour?, isRoot?}`. Cells either carry a plugin (leaf) or nested rows (layout). Plugin data is untyped in the document (`Record<string, unknown>`); typing exists only at the plugin level: `CellPlugin<DataT> = {id, version, migrations: Migration[], Renderer, Provider?, controls: {type:'autoform', schema: JsonSchema<DataT>} | {type:'custom', Component} | SubControlsDef[], createInitialData, serialize/unserialize, childConstraints {maxChildren}, cellPlugins (allowed child plugins, static or fn(data)), isInlineable, allowInlineNeighbours, allowNeighbour(item), cellStyle/cellClassName/cellSpacing (static or fn(data)), getTextContents(data), handle*HotKey}` (core/types/plugins.ts). Autoform controls are rendered by uniforms from a JSON-Schema-like TS type (core/types/jsonSchema.ts) with `showIf`, enum and per-field `uniforms` props; ajv validates. Versioning: `Migration({fromVersion, toVersion, migrate(state, {cellPlugins, lang})})` (core/migrations/Migration.ts); core/migrations/migrate.ts `migrateValue()` upgrades the Value envelope through EDITABLE_MIGRATIONS and, per cell, runs the plugin's migration chain when `cell.plugin.version !== plugin.version`; this runs both on editor load and inside renderer/HTMLRenderer.tsx. State: redux 4 + redux-thunk; core/reducer/values/index.ts wraps the value reducer in redux-undo `undoable(value, {filter: whitelist of action types [UPDATE_VALUE, CELL_UPDATE_DATA, CELL_REMOVE, CELL_RESIZE, CELL_INSERT_*], notUndoable flag on actions, neverSkipReducer, syncFilter})` giving `ValueWithHistory {past, present, future}` full snapshots. Selection/hover: redux `focus`/`hover` slices keyed by cell id; hover position computed by react-dnd drop targets into `Levels {left,right,above,below}` for the 12-col insert logic; no DOM->data mapping is needed because each cell is rendered by a Cell component that already knows its nodeId and calls `onChange(data, {lang, notUndoable})`. Static output: renderer/HTMLRenderer.tsx renders rows/cells with the same plugins' `Renderer` in readOnly mode with a NoopProvider, after `migrateValue`, `optimizeRows`, `setAllSizesAndOptimize` - usable for SSR without the editor bundle. Editor chrome is MUI 5 with react-dnd 15 and react-draggable.
core_innovation: Per-plugin content versioning with an explicit migration chain that runs at load and at render, so stored documents never break when a cell plugin's data shape changes.
strengths: Versioned cell plugins with `Migration` chains applied in both the editor and the static renderer - the most complete schema-evolution story in this batch.
Clean split between the document (Value) and a dependency-light static HTMLRenderer that reuses plugin Renderers read-only.
Plugin-level structural constraints: `cellPlugins` allowed-children (static or data-dependent), `childConstraints.maxChildren`, `allowNeighbour`, `isInlineable`.
Data-level i18n (`dataI18n` per lang) with per-lang draft flags; `getTextContents` gives a text-extraction hook per plugin.
Undo whitelist by action type plus a `notUndoable` escape hatch keeps UI state out of history.
MIT; TypeScript throughout; 11 open issues.
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: content releases stopped in 2024; 2026 activity is dependency hygiene only.

The document primitive is a recursive 12-column row/cell grid - free-form layout that produces generic pages and has no concept of section archetype, arrangement or rhythm; directly contradicts the layout-genome approach.
Plugin data is `Record<string, unknown>` in the document; typing is per-plugin generics plus a bespoke JSON-Schema-ish TS type validated by ajv - not a single typed contract for the whole page.
Full-snapshot redux-undo (`past[]`, `future[]` copies of the whole Value) rather than patches; scales poorly and cannot be persisted cheaply.
Heavy editor runtime: MUI 5, redux, react-dnd, react-draggable, uniforms; rendering is React-only so it cannot overlay Astro output.
Cell sizing in twelfths and `inline` float hacks encode a Bootstrap-era grid model into the data.
patterns_to_steal: Per-plugin `version` + `Migration({fromVersion,toVersion,migrate})` chain run by `migrateValue()` on load AND inside the static renderer -> every section variant in the human-authored library carries `schema_version` and a migration list; the Astro renderer and the CMS loader both upgrade stored SiteDefinitions before Zod validation, so the section library can evolve without breaking shipped sites.

Static HTMLRenderer reusing plugin Renderers read-only, with no editor deps -> confirms the intended split: Astro is the only renderer; the post-V1 editor is a separate app that renders through Astro, never a second render path.

Plugin-declared allowed children (`cellPlugins` as fn(data)) and `childConstraints` -> express `design_compat` / allowed-parent / slot-content rules in the section variant definition so Compat filter and editor share them.
`getTextContents(data)` per plugin -> a `extractText(sectionProps)` hook per section variant feeding the anti-slop n-gram detector and the placeholder scan.
`notUndoable` flag on actions + action-type whitelist -> label SiteDefinition mutations as document vs ephemeral in the editor's patch log.
`dataI18n` with per-language draft flags -> if multilingual sites arrive, keep locale variants at the field level of SiteDefinition with a draft marker, not as duplicated pages.
patterns_to_avoid: Recursive 12-column row/cell grid as the document primitive -> free-form layout is exactly the slop generator we are designing against; layout must come from arrangement ids, not column sizes.
Full-snapshot undo (`past/present/future` Value copies) -> use patch pairs.
JSON-Schema-driven uniforms autoforms with ajv -> Zod is our schema source; derive forms from Zod, do not maintain a parallel JSON Schema.
MUI + redux + react-dnd editor stack -> far heavier than an overlay editor needs; irrelevant to the 180 kB site budget but a maintenance burden.
Untyped plugin data in the document -> the page contract must be one discriminated Zod union, not per-plugin generics.
reusable_patterns: VersionedPluginMigrations: each content type carries a version and a migration chain applied on load and on render.
RendererEditorSplit: a dependency-light static renderer that consumes the same document and component set as the editor.
PluginDeclaredChildConstraints: allowed child types and counts declared on the content type, optionally as a function of its data.
TextContentExtractor: a per-content-type hook that returns plain text for search, QA and slop detection.
UndoActionWhitelist: history participation decided by an action-type whitelist plus a per-action notUndoable flag.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (narrow) - do not use @react-page/editor; its grid model and React-only rendering are incompatible with an Astro-rendered, arrangement-driven page. Copy exactly one mechanism now, because it affects V1: per-section-variant `schema_version` with a migration chain that runs before Zod parsing in both the loader and the renderer (core/migrations/migrate.ts is a 140-line reference). Copy `getTextContents` as a per-variant text extractor for the anti-slop and placeholder gates. Note the `cellPlugins(data)` idea when writing `design_compat`.

status_note: active, but this repo is only the client SDKs (packages/core, packages/react gen1, packages/sdks gen2 generated by Mitosis for React/Vue/Svelte/Solid/Qwik/Angular/React-Native), examples, starters and editor plugins. The visual editor, content API/CDN, Figma import and 'Visual Copilot' AI are closed SaaS at builder.io; the editor cannot be self-hosted.
core_problem: A headless visual CMS: marketers assemble pages in a SaaS editor from registered code components plus free-form styled boxes, and the resulting JSON is fetched and rendered by an SDK in the host app's framework.
architecture: Content model (packages/core/src/types/content.ts, element.ts): BuilderContent { id, name, published: 'published'|'draft'|'archived', modelId, '@version', data: { blocks: BuilderElement[], inputs, state, ... }, variations: { [id]: { data, name, testRatio } }, startDate/endDate }. BuilderElement { '@type': '@builder.io/sdk:Element', '@version', id, tagName, layerName, children: BuilderElement[], responsiveStyles: { large|medium|small|xsmall: Partial<CSSStyleDeclaration> }, component?: { name, options }, bindings: { [path]: jsExpressionString }, properties (HTML attrs), actions: { [event]: jsString }, code: { bindings, actions } (user-authored source that transpiles into bindings), repeat: { collection, itemName }, animations, meta, groupLocked/layerLocked }. Every element is a styled DOM box; a component is an optional annotation on the box, and dynamic behaviour is string JS evaluated at render (packages/react/src/functions/string-to-function.ts; isolated-vm on the server for gen2 SDKs). Registration (packages/core/src/builder.class.ts): Builder.registerComponent(Component, { name, inputs: Input[], defaultStyles, canHaveChildren, noWrap, defaultChildren, defaults, childRequirements: { message, component | query (sift.js Mongo-style) }, requiresParent: { message, component | query }, models, group, hideFromInsertMenu, requiredPermissions, isRSC, meta }). Input { name, type: string (open string: 'text','longText','richText','number','boolean','color','file','object','list','reference','code'...), required, defaultValue, enum, regex: { pattern, options, message }, subFields, showIf (fn|string), localized, advanced, broadcast, bubble, helperText, model, meta }. Registration side-effect: window.parent.postMessage({ type: 'builder.registerComponent', data: spec }) so the SaaS editor learns the catalogue from the running page. Visual editing: the host page is loaded in an iframe inside builder.io; packages/react/src/scripts/init-editing.ts announces { type: 'builder.isReactSdk', supportsPatchUpdates: 'v4', supportsCustomBreakpoints, supportsGlobalSymbols, blockLevelPersonalization } as a capability handshake; the editor pushes 'builder.updateContent' / JSON patches that BuilderBlock applies with apply-patch-with-mutation.ts; each block renders with class 'builder-block' and builder-id attributes, responsiveStyles compiled to emotion CSS with max-width media queries (builder-block.component.tsx emotionCss). Rendering: <BuilderComponent model=... content=...> -> BuilderBlocks -> BuilderBlock (class component) -> registered component or raw tag; gen2 SDKs reimplement the same in Mitosis .lite.tsx blocks (packages/sdks/src/blocks/*) with component-info.ts descriptors. Undo/redo, versioning, scheduling, A/B, personalization live server-side in the SaaS.
core_innovation: Compile one editor-agnostic block JSON (styled boxes + component annotations + string bindings) to many frameworks via Mitosis, and let the running page register its own component catalogue into the editor through postMessage.
strengths: Declarative structural constraints on the catalogue: childRequirements and requiresParent accept either a component name or a sift.js query over the element JSON, with a human-readable violation message.
Capability negotiation between page SDK and editor (init-editing.ts flags) so the editor can degrade features per SDK version — a clean pattern for editor/preview version skew.
Content-level A/B variations with testRatio, schedules (startDate/endDate) and published state are first-class on the document, not bolted on.
Every element is self-describing ('@type', '@version'), which makes the JSON safe to migrate and to validate per node.
Input schema has practical validation affordances (regex with message, enum, required, showIf, localized) and 'reference' inputs to other content models.
Multi-framework output from one source (Mitosis) proves a block model can stay framework-neutral if the renderer is a pure function of JSON.
weaknesses: The core unit is a free-form styled box with per-breakpoint arbitrary CSS in the content JSON — exactly the 'Hero 1/2/3 with free styling' model we rejected; design quality is left to the marketer.

Dynamic behaviour is string-evaluated JavaScript (stringToFunction / new Function / isolated-vm) inside content — a security surface and a runtime-JS requirement that conflicts with a near-zero-JS Astro output.
The editor, content API, CDN, versioning, undo/redo and AI are closed SaaS; the repo gives no editor to adapt and no DOM->data mapping code beyond builder-id attributes.
No Astro SDK; gen1 React SDK is class components + emotion; gen2 SDKs still need a client runtime for bindings, state and personalization.
Input.type is an open string, Component.inputs are runtime arrays, not a discriminated union or Zod schema — weak compile-time typing of the catalogue.
Repo is a 340 MB monorepo with generated SDK outputs checked in; heavy to read and irrelevant to our stack.
Content model mixes concerns (layout, styling, data binding, behaviour, personalization) in one element type, so no gate can reason about layout separately from copy.
patterns_to_steal: childRequirements/requiresParent with a query predicate + message -> Compat filter / section library: declare parent/child compatibility as data (e.g. testimonial_grid requires_parent: proof_first archetype beats) and reuse the message in the Gap Report.

SDK<->editor capability handshake -> visual_editor: when the Astro preview iframe boots, it should announce which edit affordances it supports (inline text, image swap, section reorder) so the editor UI enables only those.
Per-node '@type'/'@version' tags -> SiteDefinition: version each section node so migrations and validators can target individual node kinds.
Document-level variations { testRatio } + schedule -> telemetry/priors: keep the shape in mind for future variant experiments over arrangements, computed server-side, never in client JS.
Input.regex { pattern, message } and localized flags -> Zod field schemas for owner-editable copy (length/regex bounds with human messages surfaced in the editor).
patterns_to_avoid: responsiveStyles per element in content JSON -> design tokens must come from the selected design_system_id; styles never live in the document.
String JS bindings/actions evaluated at render -> violates JS budget and determinism; all data binding happens at build time from FactRegistry.

Registering the catalogue from the running page via postMessage -> our catalogue is a versioned, human-reviewed artefact; the editor must load it from the same Zod source as the renderer, not discover it from a live page.
Depending on a SaaS editor for the owner-facing surface -> the post-V1 editor must be self-hosted over our own SiteDefinition.
reusable_patterns: StructuralPredicateConstraint: a component declares requiresParent/childRequirements as a data query plus a user-facing message; the editor and validators both enforce it.
CapabilityHandshake: the embedded preview announces a feature-flag object on boot so the host editor enables only supported affordances.
TaggedVersionedNode: each node carries '@type' and '@version' so per-node migration and validation are possible.
VariationEnvelope: a document carries named variations with ratios and schedules alongside the default payload.
BindingIndirection: dynamic values are stored as expressions in a separate 'bindings' map keyed by target path rather than inline in props (pattern only; we would bind to FactRegistry ids, not JS).
adoption_strategy: Ignore — The open-source part is only delivery SDKs for a closed editor, and the content model (free-form responsive CSS per box + string-evaluated JS bindings) is the antithesis of a constrained, token-driven, near-zero-JS site. Nothing here renders to Astro. Lift two small ideas into our own schemas: the requiresParent/childRequirements predicate-with-message shape for section compatibility, and the preview capability handshake for the post-V1 editor. Do not spend further time on the monorepo.
