status_note: maintenance-mode / effectively dormant: last release @craftjs/core 0.2.12 on 2025-02-14, 10 commits in the 24 months before that, 227 open issues and 15 open PRs; issues filed in 2026 (#752 perf, #753 setProp) have no maintainer response. Not archived.
core_problem: A headless-ish React framework for building drag-and-drop page editors: user-supplied React components become editable nodes in a normalized tree, with serialization, rules and undo provided by the library while the UI is entirely yours.
architecture: packages/core/src. Data model (interfaces/nodes.ts): flat normalized map `Nodes: Record<NodeId, Node>`; each Node = {id, data: NodeData, rules, related, events, dom: HTMLElement|null, _hydrationTimestamp}; NodeData = {type: string | React.ElementType, props: Record<string, any>, name, displayName, isCanvas, parent, nodes: NodeId[], linkedNodes: Record<string, NodeId>, hidden, custom}. `nodes` = ordered children of a canvas; `linkedNodes` = named slots owned by a component (via `<Element id="x" is={...} canvas>`), so a parent addresses sub-canvases by key not index. Serialization (utils/serializeNode.tsx, deserializeNode.tsx): `SerializedNodes = Record<NodeId, SerializedNode>` where type becomes `string | {resolvedName}`; the `resolver: Record<string, ElementType>` (interfaces/editor.ts) is the only link between JSON and code, with a cached reverse Map (utils/resolveComponent.ts) and an invariant if a component is missing. Props are arbitrary JSON; functions are dropped; React elements inside props are serialized recursively. No schema validation of props exists. State: editor/store.tsx uses @craftjs/utils `useMethods` (the use-methods pattern) over immer `produceWithPatches`; ActionMethodsWithConfig declares `ignoreHistoryForActions: ['setDOM','setNodeEvent','selectNode','clearEvents','setOptions','setIndicator']` and a `normalizeHistory` that prunes events pointing at deleted nodes after undo/redo. History (@craftjs/utils/src/History.ts) is a timeline of {patches, inversePatches, timestamp} with a pointer; `throttleAdd` merges entries within 500 ms, `merge` folds into the last entry, `undo/redo` are `applyPatches`. Actions (editor/actions.ts): add/addNodeTree/addLinkedNodeFromTree/delete/deserialize/move/replaceNodes/setProp/setHidden/setCustom/setDOM/selectNode/setState. DOM mapping: `useNode()` (hooks/useNode.ts -> nodes/useInternalNode.ts) exposes `connectors.connect(el)` and `connectors.drag(el)`; DefaultEventHandlers.connect calls `store.actions.setDOM(id, el)` so the node record holds its live element and event listeners are attached to it; drop placement is computed from getBoundingClientRect in events/findPosition.ts. Rules live on the component: `Component.craft = {rules: {canDrag, canDrop, canMoveIn, canMoveOut}, props, related: {settings: SettingsComponent}, isCanvas}` (UserComponentConfig). `Frame data={json}` (render/Frame.tsx) deserializes once with `history.ignore()`, or parses JSX children via `query.parseReactElement().toNodeTree()`; `Editor onNodesChange(query)` fires with `query.serialize()` on every change (full-tree serialization each time; issue #752). Rendering is React only: NodeElement -> RenderNode -> the user component; no static/headless renderer is shipped.
core_innovation: A normalized node map with named `linkedNodes` slots where undo/redo is an immer patch timeline over the whole editor state, and the only JSON-to-code coupling is a string resolver map.
strengths: Flat normalized tree (id -> node, parent pointers, ordered `nodes`, keyed `linkedNodes`) is the cleanest editor data model in this batch and maps directly onto a section tree with named slots.
Immer patch-based history: cheap, serialisable, throttled merge of rapid edits, explicit `ignoreHistoryForActions` list and `history.ignore()/throttle()/merge()` modifiers.
Resolver pattern keeps the persisted JSON independent of component identity; a missing resolver entry fails loudly with an invariant.
Rules (`canDrag/canDrop/canMoveIn/canMoveOut`) are declared on the component and receive query helpers, so structural constraints live with the component definition.
Headless UI: the library supplies no panels or styling, so an editor's chrome can be minimal.
MIT; React 16.8-19 peer range.
weaknesses: Dormant: no release since Feb 2025, 227 open issues, unanswered 2026 bug reports; adopting means forking.
Props are `Record<string, any>` with no validation; SerializedNodes is a typed shape but not a typed contract for content.

Hard React runtime coupling: nodes render only through React and the node holds a live `dom` pointer; there is no way to sit over server-rendered Astro HTML, and no static renderer exists (you would write a React twin of every Astro section).
Full-tree `query.serialize()` on every change and a global module-level resolver cache (resolveComponent.ts CACHED_RESOLVER_DATA) - known perf and multi-editor footguns.
HTML5 drag-and-drop with placement from bounding rects inside the page (no iframe isolation); editor CSS and page CSS collide.
Undo history is in-memory React state only; no persistence format for the patch log.
patterns_to_steal: Immer `produceWithPatches` timeline (patches + inversePatches, pointer, throttled merge, ignore/merge modifiers) -> the post-V1 editor's undo/redo as a JSON-Patch log over the Zod SiteDefinition, persisted per session and replayable; also gives the Telemetry stage an exact edit trail.

Normalized `Record<id, node>` with `parent`, ordered `nodes` and keyed `linkedNodes` -> SiteDefinition page tree: sections by id with named slots (e.g. `hero.media`, `footer.legal`) instead of anonymous children arrays.

Resolver map `resolvedName -> component` with reverse lookup and invariant on miss -> section variant registry: SiteDefinition stores `variant_id`, the Astro renderer resolves it to a component and fails the build (not silently) on an unknown id.

Rules declared on the component (`craft.rules`) with query helpers -> `requires` / `design_compat` / allowed-parent predicates evaluated by the Compat filter and re-used by the editor to reject invalid drops.

`ignoreHistoryForActions` + `normalizeHistory` -> separate ephemeral editor state (selection, hover, dom refs) from the document so undo never touches UI state and dangling references are pruned after undo.
patterns_to_avoid: Live `dom: HTMLElement` stored on the data node and `connectors.connect(ref)` -> couples the document to a React runtime; over Astro output the mapping must be attribute-based (`data-sd-path`) from the rendered HTML, not a ref registry.
Untyped `props: any` on nodes -> every section's props must be a Zod-validated variant schema; do not accept the library's open props bag.
Rendering the editable page with the editor's React tree -> forces a React implementation of every section; Astro must remain the single renderer, with the editor as an overlay.
Full-tree serialization on every change (`onNodesChange`) -> emit patches, not snapshots.
reusable_patterns: PatchTimelineUndo: history as immer/JSON-Patch forward+inverse patch pairs with a pointer, throttled merging and an ignore list of non-document actions.
NormalizedNodeMapWithNamedSlots: id-keyed nodes, parent pointers, ordered children plus keyed `linkedNodes` slots.
StringResolverRegistry: persisted documents reference components by name; a resolver map restores them and fails loudly on unknown names.
ComponentDeclaredRules: canDrag/canDrop/canMoveIn/canMoveOut predicates attached to the component definition and evaluated with tree query helpers.
EphemeralStateSeparation: selection/hover/dom refs are excluded from history and normalized after undo/redo.
adoption_strategy: Adapt - do not depend on @craftjs/core (dormant, untyped props, React-render-bound). Re-implement its two good ideas in ~300 lines on our stack: (1) a `history.ts` using immer `produceWithPatches` over the Zod SiteDefinition with throttle/merge/ignore semantics and a persisted patch log; (2) a normalized node map with keyed slots as the in-editor working form of the page tree, converted to/from the SiteDefinition. Keep the section-variant registry as a string resolver that the Astro renderer and the editor share. The architectural fork this repo exposes: if sections are authored as .astro files, no React editor (craft, Puck, react-page) can render them, so the post-V1 editor must be an overlay on Astro dev-server output; if sections were authored as React and SSR'd by Astro without hydration they become editable by React editors but lose Astro-native features. Decide this before the section library is built.

status_note: active (daily pushes). Split-licence monorepo: the SDKs (host, loader-*, react-web, cli, data-sources) are MIT; the actual visual editor and its backend (platform/wab, platform/react-renderer, canvas-packages, live-frame) are AGPL-3.0 and heavy to self-host (Postgres + typeorm migrations, pnpm setup-all, Jenkins release). Default loaders talk to the SaaS codegen/CDN (codegen.plasmic.app). GitHub issues are disabled (has_issues=false); support is forum-only.
core_problem: A Figma-grade visual design tool that produces real React components: designers build pages/components with variants, slots, tokens and data bindings in Studio, and the output is either fetched as compiled React bundles at runtime (loader) or synced as generated .tsx into the codebase (codegen); code components from the host app are registered into Studio with a rich prop-meta schema.
architecture: Three layers. (1) Host registration (packages/host, MIT): registerComponent(Component, CodeComponentMeta) pushes { component, meta } into window.__PlasmicComponentRegistry; CodeComponentMeta (packages/host/src/registerComponent.ts) = { name, displayName, importPath, importName/isDefaultExport, props: { [p]: PropType }, states, componentHelpers, actions, styleSections, isRepeatable, defaultStyles, templates (ComponentTemplates keyed by name with previewImg), parentComponentName, isAttachment, providesData, figmaMappings/figmaPropsTransform, alwaysAutoName, hideFromContentCreators, refActions, treeLabel, defaultDisplay, trapsFocus, variants: { [name]: { cssSelector, displayName } } }. PropType (packages/host/src/types/component-types.ts) is a large union — string/href/color/class/richText/code/cardPicker, boolean, number/slider, object/array (nested fields), choice (single/multi, options may be context functions), slot ({ allowedComponents, allowRootWrapper, isRepeated, mergeWithParent, renderPropParams, unstable__isMainContentSlot, defaultValue: PlasmicElement }), imageUrl, dataSource, dataPicker, exprEditor, eventHandler(argTypes), custom (React control with studioOps), dynamic, dateString/dateRangeStrings — each with context-dependent hidden(ctx), readOnly(ctx), validator(value, ctx) -> string|true, defaultValue/defaultExpr, invariantable, editOnly/uncontrolledProp. Sibling registrars: registerToken (style tokens from code), registerGlobalContext, registerFunction, registerTrait. PlasmicElement (packages/host/src/element-types.ts) is a small declarative template DSL: { type: 'box'|'vbox'|'hbox'|'page-section'|'text'|'img'|'button'|'input'|'textarea'|'component'|'default-component'|'json', tag, value, styles: CSSProperties & { layout }, attrs (whitelisted keys), children } used for slot defaults and component templates. (2) Canvas host (packages/host/src/canvas-host.tsx): the app exposes a route rendering <PlasmicCanvasHost/>; Studio loads that URL in an iframe with #canvas=true (or live=true), the host injects studio.js from staticBaseUrl and portals whatever root node Studio hands it (setPlasmicRootNode) into #plasmic-app.__wab_user-body — so Studio is the renderer and the host only supplies registered code components and React runtime; PlasmicCanvasContext tells components they are on canvas. (3) Delivery: loader-fetcher fetches LoaderBundleOutput { modules: { browser, server }: CodeModule { fileName, code, imports } | AssetModule, components: ComponentMeta[] { id, name, path, isPage, cssFile, entry, isCode, pageMetadata, serverQueriesExecFuncFileName }, globalGroups, projects: ProjectMeta { remoteFonts, styleTokensProviderFileName, globalContextsProviderFileName }, activeSplits: (experiment|segment) Split[], deferChunksByDefault }; loader-core Registry.load compiles each CodeModule with new Function('require','exports', code) (browser or Node) and resolves imports against registered host modules; loader-react renders via PlasmicRootProvider/PlasmicComponent with renderToString/hydrateFromElement and @plasmicapp/prepass to extract query data for SSR. Codegen path: packages/cli 'plasmic sync' writes Plasmic*.tsx presentational components + wrappers and style tokens into the repo (actions/sync*.ts, migrations/ for generated-code format changes). The Studio document model lives in platform/wab/src/wab/shared/model/model-schema.ts as a custom DSL: Site { components, arenas/pageArenas/componentArenas, globalVariantGroups, styleTokens (Color|Spacing|Opacity|LineHeight|FontFamily|FontSize with variantedValues), styleTokenOverrides, mixins, themes, imageAssets, splits, globalContexts, defaultComponents, pageWrapper } with @WeakRef annotations enforcing a single strong-reference tree (cycles only via weak refs) — this underpins bundling, undo logs and cross-project imports. Undo/redo, multiplayer, branching and Figma import are inside platform/wab (AGPL). No Astro loader exists; loader-vue/svelte/angular wrap the React runtime.
core_innovation: A design-tool-fidelity editor whose native document is a strongly-typed component/variant/token tree that compiles to real React code, with a registration meta-schema rich enough (context-dependent visibility, validators, slot allow-lists, templates) to make arbitrary host components first-class design primitives.
strengths: The richest component registration schema in the field: per-prop hidden/readOnly/validator as functions of (props, contextData), slot allowedComponents, hideFromContentCreators, templates with preview images, variants exposed by cssSelector — a superset of what a constrained owner editor needs.

First-class design tokens in the model (StyleToken type enum with variantedValues) and registerToken from code, plus global variant groups (screen, theme) — mirrors our design_system token layer and the idea that tokens are selected, not typed.
PlasmicElement is a tiny, whitelisted declarative element DSL (types, tags, attr keys) — a good reference for how small a 'default content template' language can be.
@WeakRef tree discipline in model-schema.ts: one strong-ownership path per node, everything else weak — a principled rule for serializable documents, bundling and undo.
Loader bundle carries page metadata, fonts, tokens provider, splits and server-query exec hooks per component, i.e. a complete 'publish artefact' contract.
SSR story is thought through (prepass query extraction, renderToString/hydrate, server/browser module sets).
MIT SDK layer is substantial and separable from the AGPL Studio.
weaknesses: The editor is AGPL-3.0 and enormous (platform/wab; repo languages show 33 MB of TypeScript); self-hosting means running Studio, codegen and Postgres and accepting copyleft on modifications.

Design freedom is the product: arbitrary CSS, free-form boxes, Figma import — precisely the slop vector our pipeline exists to remove; 'content creator mode' guardrails are Studio-side config, not a schema-level contract.
React everywhere: generated code, runtime, loaders; Vue/Svelte/Angular loaders embed React; no Astro target. Runtime loader executes fetched code via new Function — acceptable at build time only.
Default delivery depends on SaaS codegen/CDN (codegen.plasmic.app); packages require exact-version lockstep and window globals (__PlasmicComponentRegistry) that break with duplicate installs.
The document model (Site/Component/TplNode/variants/vsettings) is a design-tool model, not a section contract; nothing encodes narrative beats, evidence requirements or asset constraints.
GitHub issues disabled; roadmap and support live in a proprietary forum — weak open-source governance signal despite the code being public.
Registration meta is TypeScript interfaces validated at Studio runtime, not a portable schema (no JSON Schema/Zod export).
patterns_to_steal: Context-dependent prop meta (hidden/readOnly/validator as functions of current props + context) -> visual_editor: owner-editable fields whose visibility and bounds depend on the selected arrangement (e.g. quote length limit tightens when arrangement is 'pull_quote_large').

Slot allowedComponents + hideFromContentCreators -> Compat filter and editor palette: a per-slot eligible set computed from design_compat, and section variants hidden from owners but available to the agent.
StyleToken enum with variantedValues -> design_system: token values per variant (dark mode, reduced motion) declared in the token file, selected by id, never emitted by the model.
@WeakRef single-ownership tree rule -> SiteDefinition Zod schema: sections own their nodes; cross-references (facts, assets, design ids) are ids only, so undo logs and diffs stay tree-local.

Component templates with previewImg (ComponentTemplates) -> section library: each arrangement ships an authored preview image and a default props template, used by the editor palette and the Gap Report.

LoaderBundleOutput as publish artefact (components meta + page metadata + fonts + splits) -> Decision Manifest/renderer: publish one manifest listing pages, section ids, fonts, tokens provider and QA results.
PlasmicElement whitelisted element DSL -> anti_slop tier-1: a closed vocabulary of allowed tags/attrs for any agent-authored micro-content (e.g. rich text inside a section).
patterns_to_avoid: Free-form Figma-style canvas editing of layout and CSS -> owners must only edit copy/assets within a fixed genome; any drag-anything canvas reintroduces slop.
Runtime code loading (Registry.load via new Function of CDN bundles) -> build-time only; the public site ships static Astro output with no dynamic module loading.
Registering the catalogue via side-effectful window globals -> our catalogue is the versioned Zod library imported by both renderer and editor.
Adopting the AGPL platform for the post-V1 editor -> licence contagion plus a design-tool UX we do not want; only patterns cross over.
Figma import / vector-to-DOM translation -> rejected 'cloner'/mining direction; no value for a constraint-first pipeline.
reusable_patterns: ContextDependentFieldMeta: a field's hidden/readOnly/validator are pure functions of the node's current props and editor context, evaluated on every change.
SlotAllowList: a slot declares the set of component ids it accepts and whether wrapper roots are allowed; validators and the palette share it.
VariantedToken: a design token holds a base value plus per-variant overrides, resolved by the active variant set at render time.
WeakRefTreeModel: document nodes form a strict ownership tree; all other references are weak ids, guaranteeing serializability and local undo.
PublishBundleManifest: a publish emits a manifest listing every component/page with metadata, assets, fonts and experiment splits, consumed by the renderer without touching the editor.
WhitelistedElementDSL: a closed set of element types/tags/attr keys for declarative default content.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a tool, Adapt its schemas — Plasmic's Studio is AGPL, React-only, SaaS-tethered by default and built for design freedom, so it cannot be our editor or renderer. Its registration and model schemas, however, are the most complete reference for how to express editing constraints as data: copy context-dependent field meta, slot allow-lists, varianted tokens, component templates with previews, and the weak-ref ownership rule into the Zod SiteDefinition and section-library schemas now (difficulty ~3 for the patterns). Do not attempt to run platform/.
evidence: README.md 'License' section and LICENSE.md (MIT) vs LICENSE.platform.md (AGPL-3.0): 'All content outside of platform/ is licensed under the MIT license... platform/ is licensed under the AGPL'

status_note: abandoned alpha. master's last commit is 2020-06-26; the 2026 pushed_at comes only from renovate bot branches (renovate/babel-monorepo, renovate/eslint-7.x, ...). README says 'very early alpha ... not yet fully functional'. Stack is Gatsby 2, React 16.13, theme-ui 0.3, Babel 7.10.
core_problem: A WYSIWYG page builder whose document is literally a JSX source string: every visual edit is a Babel AST transform on that string, so the output is always real, exportable React/MDX code.
architecture: Yarn workspaces: packages/blocks-ui (the editor), packages/property-controls (Framer-style control descriptors), packages/react (@blocks/react: a small section library of headers/footers/quotes/taglines built on theme-ui `sx` and `variant`), packages/gatsby-plugin-blocks. Source of truth: a JSX code string held in React state (providers/code.js `useState`). Rendering: transforms.js `toTransformedJSX` runs @babel/standalone in the browser with a plugin chain [set-default-export-to-container, drag-and-drop, inject-blocks-root, remove-named-exports, remove-imports, transform-react-jsx with pragma 'jsx'] and inline-render.js evaluates the result with `new Function('React', ...scopeKeys, code + '; return React.createElement(BLOCKS_Container)')` - eval in the editor page, no iframe. Identity: babel-plugins/add-tuid-prop.js injects a `___uuid` string-literal attribute (constants.js `uuidName`) on every JSXOpeningElement (skipping BLOCKS_* internals); pragma.js is a custom jsx pragma that strips `___uuid`, wraps every element with onClick -> `setCurrentElementId(id)` and onMouseEnter/Leave hover, and paints selection/hover as an inset boxShadow. Selection -> data: babel-plugins/get-current-element.js is a query plugin that walks the AST for the element whose `___uuid` matches `elementId` and fills {id, name, props (parsed from JSX attributes incl. the `sx` object), parentId, children | text}; get-element-tree.js and get-blocks-usage.js are similar AST queries. Mutations are one Babel plugin each (~20 in babel-plugins/, each with snapshot tests): apply-prop, apply-sx-prop, remove-sx-prop, replace-text, insert-before/after, insert-block, clone, remove, reorder-blocks, drag-and-drop; transforms.js exposes them as pure `(code, options) => code` functions. Property panel: property-controls/src/index.js defines ControlType {Boolean, Enum, Number, String, FusedNumber, Color, Image, File, ComponentInstance, Array, EventHandler, Style, Object} and `applyPropertyControls(Component, controls)` sets a static `Component.propertyControls`; @blocks/react components (e.g. headers/basic.js HeaderBasic with HeaderBasic.Logo/.Nav/.Link compound parts) declare their controls this way and the editor renders a form per control type and writes back via applyProp. Export: `toRawJSX` strips uuids (remove-tuid) and re-adds imports (add-block-imports). Undo/redo: none - code state is a plain useState; there is no history module.
core_innovation: Code-as-document: the JSX source string is the canonical document and every editor operation is a pure, unit-testable Babel AST transform that preserves it as real code.
strengths: Every operation is a pure `(code, options) => code` transform with snapshot tests - operations are composable, replayable and testable without a browser.
Stable element identity via an injected `___uuid` attribute survives re-renders and gives a trivial DOM-event -> source-node mapping through a custom jsx pragma.
Property controls as static, co-located component metadata (`Component.propertyControls`) with a small closed enum of control types.
@blocks/react shows a compact section library shaped as compound components (Header.Logo, Header.Nav) driven by theme-ui variants - a slot vocabulary rather than free-form children.
Output is human-readable JSX/MDX, so there is no lock-in format.
weaknesses: Abandoned since mid-2020 at alpha quality; Gatsby 2 / React 16 / Babel 7.10 / theme-ui 0.3 toolchain.
The document is an untyped code string: no schema, no validation, props parsed heuristically from JSX attributes (get-current-element.js only handles string literals and flat object expressions).
In-page `new Function` evaluation of transformed code (inline-render.js) - CSP-hostile, no iframe isolation, editor styles and page styles collide.
Every interaction re-parses and re-transforms the whole file with @babel/standalone in the browser - O(file) per click.
No undo/redo at all; no persistence layer; theme editing mutates theme-ui theme objects (free-form tokens).
Layout expressed via `sx` style props (free-form CSS) - a token-emitting surface, which our constraints forbid.
patterns_to_steal: Stable-id injection pass (`___uuid` on every element at transform time) -> the Astro renderer stamps `data-sd-path` / `data-sd-id` on every section and editable field root from the SiteDefinition at build time, so a post-V1 overlay editor maps a click to a Zod path without runtime registries.

Operations as pure transforms over the canonical document, each with snapshot tests (babel-plugins/*.test.js) -> define editor and generator mutations as `(SiteDefinition, params) => SiteDefinition` pure functions with fixture tests; the same functions serve the Assembly stage and the future editor.

Static co-located property controls with a closed control-type enum -> attach UI hints to Zod fields (control type, options, min/max) via a small meta registry so panels are generated, never hand-built.
Compound-component slot vocabulary (Header.Logo/Nav/Link) -> section variants expose named slots with typed allowed content instead of arbitrary children.
patterns_to_avoid: Code string as the document -> untyped, unvalidatable, and the model or human could write anything; SiteDefinition must stay typed JSON that a renderer turns into code, never the reverse.
In-page eval of transformed code -> use an iframe/dev-server preview of the real Astro output.
Re-parsing the entire document per interaction -> operate on the JSON tree with patches.
`sx` / theme editing as the styling surface -> exposes raw tokens; only design_system_id and variant/arrangement ids are selectable.
reusable_patterns: IdentityInjectionPass: a build-time pass that stamps every renderable node with a stable id attribute for DOM-to-source mapping.
PureDocumentTransforms: each edit is a pure function over the canonical document with snapshot-tested fixtures.
StaticPropertyControls: component-attached, enum-typed control descriptors that drive generated property panels.
CompoundSlotComponents: sections expose named sub-components as the only extension points.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a codebase - it is a 2020 alpha with no undo, no types, in-page eval and a dead toolchain. The two ideas worth keeping are already cheap to implement natively: stamp `data-sd-path` ids in the Astro renderer (the `___uuid` idea done at the right layer) and write every SiteDefinition mutation as a snapshot-tested pure function (the babel-plugin-per-operation idea without Babel). Nothing here should influence the section library beyond the reminder that compound slot components beat free-form children.

status_note: active; CLI at shadcn@4.21.0; registry v4 now generates base x style combinations (radix|base|aria x nova|vega|maia|lyra|mira|luma|sera|rhea) and ships an Astro template
core_problem: Distribute UI components as source code copied into the consumer's repo (ownership, no runtime dependency) while still giving them a dependency graph, install-time theming, and a versioned, addressable registry so that agents and humans can compose from many registries.
architecture: Monorepo: packages/shadcn (the CLI, published as `shadcn`) and apps/v4 (docs site + the authored registry). The registry contract is a Zod schema in packages/shadcn/src/registry/schema.ts: `registryItemSchema` is a discriminated union on `type` (registry:ui|component|block|page|file|lib|hook|theme|style|base|font|item) with `name`, `files[] {path,type,target?,content?}`, `dependencies` (npm), `devDependencies`, `registryDependencies` (item addresses), `cssVars {theme,light,dark}`, `css` (recursive rule tree), `tailwind.config`, `envVars`, `meta`, `docs`, `extends`, `categories`; `registry:base` carries a partial components.json `config`, `registry:font` a `font` block. Item addresses (registry/address.ts) have five schemes: bare `button` (official), `@ns/item` (configured registry with url/params/headers in components.json), `https://.../x.json`, `./x.json`, and `owner/repo/item#ref` (GitHub source registry, ref resolved to a commit SHA via `git ls-remote` in github-ref.ts before any file is read, so installs are snapshot-consistent). The `add` flow (commands/add.ts -> registry/add.ts `addRegistryItems` -> registry/resolver.ts `resolveRegistryTree`) fetches items, recursively resolves `registryDependencies` with a visited set, topologically sorts them (`topologicalSortRegistryItems`), floats `registry:theme` items first, deep-merges `tailwind`/`cssVars`/`css`/`envVars`, dedupes files by resolved target, then utils/add-components.ts runs updaters: update-dependencies (npm install), update-css-vars.ts (a PostCSS plugin chain that inserts/updates `:root`/`.dark` vars inside `@layer base` for TW3 or `@theme inline` + `@custom-variant dark` for TW4), update-css.ts, update-fonts.ts, update-files.ts which runs a ts-morph transformer pipeline per file (transform-import rewrites `@/registry/...` to the project's aliases, transform-css-vars, transform-tw-prefix, transform-icons swaps `IconPlaceholder` for the chosen icon library, transform-menu, transform-aschild, transform-rtl, transform-rsc, transform-font, transform-cleanup) and skips files whose content is unchanged (`isContentSame`). Theming: colors are plain CSS custom properties in oklch (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--destructive`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--chart-1..5`, `--sidebar-*`, `--radius`) declared on `:root`/`.dark` and re-exposed to Tailwind through `@theme inline { --color-primary: var(--primary) ... --radius-lg: var(--radius); --radius-sm: calc(var(--radius)*0.6) }` (apps/v4/app/globals.css); themes are data in apps/v4/registry/themes.ts (`type: registry:theme`, cssVars light/dark). The v4 registry build (apps/v4/scripts/build-registry.mts) is a matrix generator: authored headless bases in registry/bases/{base,radix} (components use semantic `cn-*` class hooks + `data-slot` attributes, e.g. bases/base/ui/accordion.tsx) are crossed with style token files registry/styles/style-*.css (each style redefines `.cn-accordion-trigger`, `.cn-badge` etc. via @apply) and compiled by `transformStyle`/`createStyleMap` from shadcn/utils into flat Tailwind class strings per combination (base-nova, radix-sera, ...), emitting public/r/styles/<style>/*.json for the CLI. A full design-system choice (base, style, baseColor, theme, chartColor, font, fontHeading, iconLibrary, radius, menuColor, menuAccent) is bit-packed into a base62 preset code with a version prefix (packages/shadcn/src/preset/preset.ts; PRESET_FIELDS_V2 = 51 bits) and consumed by `init`/`preset` commands. Blocks (registry/new-york-v4/blocks/_registry.ts) are `registry:block` items bundling a `registry:page` with `target` plus `registry:component` files and a long `registryDependencies` list (dashboard-01 pulls 19 ui items + dnd-kit + tanstack-table); the catalogue is dashboards/sidebars/login/signup, not marketing sections. Extension points: `include` to split registries, `registries` map in components.json with auth headers, `shadcn build`/`registry validate` to compile a source registry, an MCP server (commands/mcp.ts) and an agent SKILL.md with composition/styling rules (skills/shadcn/rules/*.md). templates/astro-app shows the official Astro story: `@astrojs/react` + Tailwind v4 + React 19, i.e. every interactive component is a React island.
core_innovation: A registry item is a typed, addressable, dependency-graphed bundle of source files plus install-time side effects (css vars, tailwind theme, deps, env), and a design system is a bit-packed id over enumerated axes (base x style x theme x font x radius x icons) rather than free-form tokens.
strengths: Registry item schema is a clean, Zod-typed distribution contract: files + npm deps + registry deps + cssVars/css/tailwind/env side effects, discriminated by `type`; already mirrored as a public JSON Schema (apps/v4/public/schema/registry-item.json).

Dependency graph resolution is real: recursive `registryDependencies` with cycle guard, topological sort, theme-first ordering, deep-merge of token side effects, target-path dedup (registry/resolver.ts).

Pinned, snapshot-consistent versioning for GitHub registries: `owner/repo/item#v1.2.0` is resolved to a 40-char SHA once per command and every include/file is read from that SHA (registry/github-ref.ts); refs are explicitly not inherited by dependencies.

Token contract is CSS custom properties, framework-agnostic: components only reference semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`), never raw palette; styling rules in skills/shadcn/rules/styling.md forbid raw colors and manual dark: overrides.

Separation of three orthogonal axes: headless behaviour base (radix|base-ui|react-aria), visual style (style-*.css `cn-*` hooks), colour theme (cssVars) plus font/radius/icon axes, each enumerated and combinable at build time.

Install is idempotent and drift-aware: unchanged files are skipped (`isContentSame`), `add --diff` shows upstream drift, transformers rewrite imports/icons/prefixes so the copied code is native to the target repo.
Universal items (`registry:file`, `registry:item`) can ship any project file (rules, MCP config, docs) without a framework, bypassing transformers.
Agent-facing surface is first-class: MCP server, SKILL.md with hard composition rules (e.g. Dialog must have Title, TabsTrigger inside TabsList) that read like lintable constraints.
weaknesses: React-only at the component layer: the ui/ and blocks/ catalogue and all three bases (Radix, Base UI, React Aria) are React; in Astro every interactive section becomes a React island (React 19 runtime ~45 kB gz before any primitive), which is hostile to a 180 kB total JS budget if more than 2-3 sections hydrate.
The `blocks` catalogue is app-shell UI (dashboard, sidebar, login, signup, calendar) with zero marketing sections; nothing to reuse as section families.

The style axis is expressed as Tailwind @apply utility soup inside style-*.css; it captures micro-styling (radius, padding, ring width) but has no notion of composition, density, rhythm, motion budget, or art direction, so it cannot express our section-variant metadata.

The CLI's transformer pipeline (ts-morph/babel, PostCSS, tsconfig-paths, execa git) is heavyweight Node tooling tuned to Next/Vite React projects; `registry:page` targets assume `app/` routing conventions.

No provenance or integrity fields on items: no content hash, no semver on items themselves, no signature; version pinning exists only for the GitHub address scheme, while the official registry is `latest`.
Theming is colour-centric (~35 colour vars + one radius); typography scale, spacing scale, motion tokens and breakpoints are not part of the theme item contract.
Very high churn: 4.x rewrote the registry into base x style combinations, added presets, bases, fonts, GitHub addressing within months; pinning to a CLI version is mandatory.
patterns_to_steal: Registry item schema (name, type, files[{path,type,target}], dependencies, registryDependencies, cssVars, css, meta) → SectionLibrary manifest: each section variant is an item whose `registryDependencies` point to primitives/islands and whose `cssVars`/`css` declare the tokens it consumes; keep it Zod-typed exactly like packages/shadcn/src/registry/schema.ts.

resolveRegistryTree (recursive dep resolution with visited set + topological sort + deep-merge of token side effects + target-path dedup) → Assembly stage: compute the closed set of islands/CSS for a SiteDefinition deterministically and emit one CSS/JS bundle list.

SHA-pinned GitHub addressing (`owner/repo/item#ref` resolved to commit SHA before reading any file) → versioned, pinned section library: every SiteDefinition records the library commit SHA; the Decision Manifest cites it; rebuilds are reproducible.

Bit-packed base62 preset code over enumerated axes (preset/preset.ts, append-only arrays, version prefix char) → design_system_id / art_direction_id encoding: the model selects an id; the id decodes deterministically into token files; backward-compat rules (never reorder, defaults at index 0) are exactly what versioned priors need.

Three-axis separation base x style x theme, compiled at build time by crossing authored bases with style token files → our design-system token files: keep behaviour (a11y island), skin (style css), and palette (oklch cssVars) as separate, independently versioned layers so eligibility can gate each axis.

Semantic-only colour contract (`--primary`/`--primary-foreground` pairs, `--muted`, `--ring`, `--radius` with derived radius-sm/md/lg via calc) → design_system token file baseline; the foreground pairing guarantees contrast pairs exist for axe-core.

Content-identical skip + `add --diff` drift detection (utils/compare.ts isContentSame, commands/diff.ts) → section library upgrade path post-V1: detect which client sites have drifted from a pinned variant before applying a library bump.

Agent rule files as lintable constraints (skills/shadcn/rules/composition.md: 'Dialog always needs a Title', 'TabsTrigger must be inside TabsList') → anti-slop tier-1 / QA gate: convert composition rules into deterministic AST or DOM checks rather than prompt text.
patterns_to_avoid: Using shadcn components (React + Radix/Base UI) as the runtime for marketing sections → each interactive section becomes a React island; 3+ islands blow the 180 kB JS budget and main-thread 120 ms motion budget on mobile; use Astro components + vanilla TS or a single small island runtime instead.
Adopting the `blocks` catalogue → it is dashboards/sidebars/auth forms, not marketing; and 'Hero 1/2/3'-style generic blocks were already rejected.

Encoding visual style as Tailwind @apply utility strings (style-*.css) → not queryable by the eligibility/compat filter; our design systems need typed tokens (spacing scale, type scale, density, motion) not class soup.

Running the shadcn CLI transformer pipeline (ts-morph, PostCSS mutation of the user's globals.css) inside our build → we own both sides of the contract, so a plain file copy + generated CSS from typed tokens is simpler and deterministic.
Letting `registryDependencies` reference `latest` (the official registry has no item versions) → every dependency in our library must be pinned to a library SHA/semver; no floating refs.
Colour-only theme items → our design_system files must carry typography, spacing, motion and breakpoint tokens too, otherwise the anti-slop and rhythm rules have nothing to reason over.
reusable_patterns: RegistryItemContract: a typed manifest (files + deps + registryDeps + token side effects + meta) that makes a copied-source component addressable and composable.
SnapshotPinnedAddress: resolve any human ref (tag/branch) to an immutable content id (commit SHA) before reading a single file, and never inherit refs across dependencies.
AxisMatrixBuild: author behaviour bases and style token files separately, then generate every base x style combination at build time from a single source of truth.
BitPackedPresetId: enumerate every design axis as an append-only array and encode the selection as a versioned integer id, giving a stable, decodable 'design_system_id'.
TokenSideEffectMerge: install-time deep-merge of cssVars/css/tailwind across the resolved dependency tree, theme items ordered first.
DriftAwareInstall: skip byte-identical files, expose a diff against the pinned upstream before overwriting owned code.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not take the React components or the CLI; take the contract. Write our SectionLibrary manifest as a Zod schema modelled on registryItemSchema (name, type, files, registryDependencies, cssVars, meta) and add our own fields (requires, enhanced_by, design_compat, composition, motion, a11y, arrangements). Pin the library by commit SHA exactly as github-ref.ts does and record it in the Decision Manifest. Encode design_system_id and art_direction_id as bit-packed, versioned preset ids over enumerated axes so the model can only select. Reuse the semantic oklch cssVars naming (`--primary`/`--primary-foreground`, `--radius` with derived sizes) as the floor of our token files, then extend with typography/spacing/motion tokens. Steal the composition rules from skills/shadcn/rules as deterministic lint checks for the anti-slop and QA gates.

status_note: active; v9.6.2 monorepo (13 packages), React 19 peer, Node >=22, very high release cadence
core_problem: A full React component library (161 core components + 87 hooks) whose single JS theme object is compiled into a stable set of CSS custom properties, so every component is styled by plain CSS modules that only read variables, and theming/dark mode/scaling never require CSS-in-JS at runtime.
architecture: Data model: `MantineTheme` (packages/@mantine/core/src/core/MantineProvider/theme.types.ts) is a typed object of scalar tokens (fontSizes/spacing/radius/shadows/lineHeights/fontWeights/breakpoints as xs..xl records, headings.sizes h1..h6, colors as 10-shade tuples, `primaryColor`, `primaryShade: number | {light,dark}`, `scale`, `autoContrast`, `luminanceThreshold`, `variantColorResolver`, `components` (per-component classNames/styles/vars/defaultProps overrides) and an untyped `other` bag). `createTheme` is an identity function used purely for typing; `mergeMantineTheme` deep-merges the override onto DEFAULT_THEME and `validateMantineTheme` throws on an invalid primaryColor/primaryShade. Token -> CSS-var compilation is a pure function: `defaultCssVariablesResolver(theme)` (MantineCssVariables/default-css-variables-resolver.ts) returns `{variables, light, dark}` maps; `getCSSColorVariables` derives, per color and per scheme, the 10 raw shade vars plus semantic aliases (`--mantine-color-X-filled`, `-filled-hover`, `-light`, `-light-hover`, `-light-color`, `-outline`, `-outline-hover`, `-text`) from `primaryShade`; `convertCssVariables` serializes to `:root, :host{...}` and `:root[data-mantine-color-scheme=dark|light]{...}` strings. It runs at BOTH build time and runtime: scripts/codegen/generate-default-css-variables.ts writes `default-css-variables.css` (27 kB raw / 3.9 kB gz) which MantineProvider imports statically, and at runtime `<MantineCssVariables>` runs the resolver on the merged theme, diffs against the default output (`removeDefaultVariables`, `deduplicateCssVariables=true`) and injects only the delta in a `<style data-mantine-styles>` tag. The `cssVariablesResolver` provider prop is a user function `(theme) => {variables, light, dark}` deep-merged over the default output, i.e. an extension point to add project-specific vars. Colour scheme: `ColorSchemeScript` emits an inline pre-paint script that reads localStorage and sets `data-mantine-color-scheme` on `<html>`; `useProviderColorScheme` keeps it in sync with `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`. Virtual colors (`virtualColor({name, light, dark})`) are tuples of `var(--mantine-color-name-i)` with hidden props, so one token name resolves to different palettes per scheme. `luminance.ts` computes WCAG relative luminance (gamma-corrected sRGB, oklch fast path) and `isLightColor(color, luminanceThreshold)` drives `getContrastColor`/`autoContrast` to pick black or white text for filled variants; `defaultVariantColorsResolver` maps (variant x color) -> {background, hover, color, border} and is replaceable via `theme.variantColorResolver`. Component layer: `Box` (core/Box/Box.tsx) is the polymorphic base; `extractStyleProps`/`parseStyleProps` turn shorthand props (m, p, bg, c, fz, w, pos...) into inline styles via typed resolvers (spacing/color/fontSize/radius...), and responsive object values into a hashed class + runtime `<InlineStyles>` tag with `(min-width: theme.breakpoints[bp])` media queries. Each component declares a `createVarsResolver<Factory>((theme, props, ctx) => ({root: {'--button-bg': ...}}))` (Button.tsx) whose output is set as inline CSS variables on the root; `Button.module.css` consumes them with fallbacks (`background: var(--button-bg, var(--mantine-primary-color-filled))`) and encodes size scales as CSS vars (`--button-height-xs..xl`), modifiers as `data-*` attributes (`mod` prop -> `getBoxMod`) and all selectors wrapped in `:where()` for zero specificity. `useStyles` (styles-api/use-styles) merges static classes (`mantine-Button-root`, `classNamesPrefix`), CSS-module classes, per-instance `classNames/styles/vars`, and `theme.components[name]` overrides; `unstyled` and `HeadlessMantineProvider` disable the styles. `rem()` (utils/units-converters/rem.ts) emits `calc(Xrem * var(--mantine-scale))` and `postcss-preset-mantine` with `autoRem` rewrites px in CSS modules to that form at build time. CSS distribution (scripts/build/generate-css.ts): each `*.module.css` is compiled to `styles/<Component>.css` and `styles/<Component>.layer.css` (`@layer mantine {...}`), plus the bundle `styles.css` (277 kB raw / 39 kB gz); three globals (`baseline.css`, `default-css-variables.css`, `global.css`) are mandatory and per-component files must be imported in dependency order (UnstyledButton before Button). No AI wiring anywhere. Dependencies of @mantine/core: @floating-ui/react, clsx, react-number-format, react-remove-scroll, type-fest; peer @mantine/hooks + react/react-dom ^19.2. Bundlephobia for the whole barrel: 552 kB min / 162 kB gz (`sideEffects: ['*.css']` so ESM tree-shakes per component). @mantine/hooks: 87 hooks, zero runtime deps, `sideEffects: false`.
core_innovation: A typed theme object compiled by one pure resolver into a namespaced CSS-custom-property contract, emitted at build time for defaults and as a runtime diff for overrides, with per-component vars resolvers so components are styled by static CSS that only reads variables.
strengths: Theme -> CSS-var compilation is a pure, testable function (`defaultCssVariablesResolver` -> `convertCssVariables`) with a snapshot test; the same function powers build-time codegen (`generate-default-css-variables.ts`) and runtime delta injection (`removeDefaultVariables`).

Semantic colour aliases are derived, not authored: from a 10-shade tuple + `primaryShade {light, dark}` it emits `-filled/-filled-hover/-light/-light-hover/-outline/-text` per scheme, so a design system author only supplies palettes and one shade index.
`autoContrast` + `luminanceThreshold` compute foreground (black/white) from WCAG relative luminance (`luminance.ts`, oklch aware) at compile time of the vars, giving deterministic contrast decisions.
Virtual colours (`virtualColor`) let one token name resolve to different palettes in light/dark without touching consumers.
`scale` token + `rem()` = `calc(Xrem * var(--mantine-scale))` + PostCSS `autoRem` gives global proportional scaling from a single variable.

Component CSS discipline worth copying: `:where()` zero-specificity selectors, `data-*` modifier attributes, size scales expressed as CSS vars, instance overrides via inline CSS vars with `var(--x, fallback)`; components remain plain CSS modules with no runtime style generation for the non-responsive path.
`ColorSchemeScript` pre-paint inline script + `data-mantine-color-scheme` attribute is the correct FOUC-free dark-mode pattern and is framework-free.
CSS ships per component (`styles/Button.css`, 8 kB raw / 1.6 kB gz) and as `@layer mantine` variants, so cascade order against host CSS is controllable.

@mantine/hooks is dependency-free; `use-media-query`, `use-in-viewport`, `use-intersection`, `use-reduced-motion` are thin wrappers over matchMedia/IntersectionObserver; `use-focus-trap` (with `tabbable.ts`/`scope-tab.ts`) and `use-scroll-into-view` (rAF easing, reduced-motion aware, cancel on user scroll) contain reusable browser logic.
MIT, 31.7k stars, single dominant maintainer but extremely active (pushed the day before analysis), strong typing (`MantineThemeSizesOverride`/`MantineThemeColorsOverride` module augmentation).
weaknesses: Hard React 19 dependency: every component needs `MantineProvider` context (theme, colour scheme, classNamesPrefix) so any Astro island using a Mantine component pulls React runtime (~45 kB gz) + provider + `@floating-ui/react` + `react-remove-scroll`; incompatible with our 180 kB total JS budget and near-zero-JS islands.

Global CSS is mandatory: `baseline.css` + `default-css-variables.css` + `global.css` before any component CSS; full `styles.css` is 277 kB raw / 39 kB gz and per-component imports must be hand-ordered by dependency (docs page css-files-list.mdx).

Runtime style generation still exists: responsive style props (`{base, sm, md}`) create a random/hashed class and a `<style>` tag per Box (`InlineStyles`), and the theme delta is injected via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` at runtime; not SSG-static by default.

`isLightColor` returns false for any `var(...)` value, so autoContrast silently yields white text whenever a colour is expressed as a CSS variable; the contrast decision is luminance-thresholded (0.3), not a WCAG ratio, so it does not guarantee AA.

Design language is a generic app/dashboard aesthetic (system fonts, blue primary, xs..xl scales); zero support for editorial/marketing `visual_dna` (type scales, rhythm, art direction) -> would fight our design-system-as-token-file model.
Theme is untyped where it matters for us: `other: Record<string, any>`, `components.*: any`; no schema validation beyond primaryColor/primaryShade (`validateMantineTheme`).
`createTheme` is an identity function; there is no serialisable token format (DTCG/JSON) - the theme is JS with functions (`variantColorResolver`), so it cannot be a data file selected by id.

Breakpoints are consumed by JS (`parseStyleProps` builds media queries from `theme.breakpoints`) and by PostCSS (`postcss-simple-vars` duplicates them in postcss.config.cjs), so the same tokens live in two places.

Monorepo is 340 MB with docs apps; upgrade churn is high (v7 -> v8 -> v9 in ~2 years with breaking style API changes), and CSS class hashing (`hash-css-selector`) makes visual-editor targeting brittle.
patterns_to_steal: Pure `theme -> {variables, light, dark}` resolver + `convertCssVariables` serializer -> our design_system stage: `compileTokens(designSystem.json) -> tokens.css` emitted at build time by Astro integration, snapshot-tested per design_system_id, with `[data-color-scheme]` selector scoping.

Build-time default + runtime delta (`removeDefaultVariables`) -> our renderer: emit base `tokens.css` per design system once; page-level overrides (e.g. section-scoped accent) become a tiny inline delta on the section root, never a whole theme.

Derived semantic colour aliases from palette + `primaryShade {light, dark}` (`getCSSColorVariables`) -> design_system token compiler: author only 10-shade palettes and a shade index; compiler emits `--ds-color-primary-filled/-hover/-subtle/-outline/-text` deterministically.

`luminance.ts` + `getContrastColor` -> design_system compiler AND qa_gate: compute on-colour text at compile time, but replace the luminance threshold with a WCAG 2.x contrast-ratio check (>= 4.5) and fail the build (not the runtime) when a palette shade cannot host readable text.
`virtualColor` -> design_system: a scheme-dependent alias token (`surface`, `accent`) resolving to different palettes for light/dark without consumers knowing.
`ColorSchemeScript` inline pre-paint script (framework-free, ~10 lines) -> renderer `<head>` partial for FOUC-free colour scheme; `useProviderColorScheme` matchMedia sync -> a 1 kB vanilla island.

`createVarsResolver` per component + CSS module with `var(--x, fallback)` -> section library: each section variant/arrangement declares a typed `vars` contract (e.g. `--section-density`, `--focal-weight`) resolved from `composition` fields in deterministic TS, consumed by static CSS.

`:where()` zero-specificity selectors + `data-*` modifiers (`mod` -> `getBoxMod`) + `@layer` output (`generate-css.ts`) -> renderer CSS conventions so art_direction and design_system layers can override section CSS predictably.
`scale` token + `rem()` = `calc(Xrem * var(--scale))` + PostCSS autoRem -> design_system: one `--ds-scale` var for density presets (compact/comfortable/editorial) without regenerating tokens.

`use-focus-trap` (`tabbable.ts`, `scope-tab.ts`), `use-scroll-into-view` easing/cancel logic, `use-in-viewport` -> motion/islands: port as framework-free TS utilities for the <=1 interactive island per section (mobile nav, dialog, in-view reveal), all respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` like `useScrollIntoView` does.
patterns_to_avoid: Adopting `@mantine/core` components in Astro islands -> requires React 19 runtime + `MantineProvider` context + mandatory global CSS (baseline/default-css-variables/global) per island; blows the 180 kB JS budget and the near-zero-JS rule, and drags in @floating-ui/react and react-remove-scroll.

Runtime theme injection via `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML>` (`MantineCssVariables`) and per-Box `InlineStyles` for responsive props -> our pages are static; all tokens and responsive CSS must be emitted at build time so Lighthouse CI budgets and the anti-slop/QA gates see the final CSS.

Style props system (`m`, `p`, `bg`, `fz`... on every element) -> invites ad-hoc per-element values that bypass the token contract; our model selects ids, never emits tokens, so sections must consume only named vars.

`theme.other: any` / `components: any` escape hatches and function-valued theme fields (`variantColorResolver`) -> our design systems must be pure JSON validated by Zod so they can be versioned, diffed and selected by id.
Luminance-threshold contrast (0.3) as the accessibility decision -> not a WCAG ratio; our qa_gate uses axe-core; the compiler should use a real contrast ratio and hard-fail.

Generic xs..xl size scale and system-font dashboard aesthetic as the token vocabulary -> our design systems need `visual_dna` (type scale ratios, rhythm, texture, depth) that Mantine's theme shape cannot express; do not inherit its token taxonomy wholesale.
Hashed CSS-module class names (`hash-css-selector`) -> brittle targets for the post-V1 visual editor and for Playwright QA selectors; prefer stable `data-section`/`data-variant` attributes.
reusable_patterns: TokenResolverCompiler: a pure function `(typedTheme) -> {shared, light, dark}` CSS-variable maps, serialised to scoped selectors, run at build time for defaults and diffed at runtime/pagetime for overrides.
DerivedSemanticAliases: raw N-shade palettes + a per-scheme primary shade index generate all semantic role variables (filled/hover/subtle/outline/text) deterministically.
VirtualColorToken: a token name whose value is `var(--name-i)` and resolves to different palettes per colour scheme.
ComputedContrastForeground: compile-time luminance/contrast computation selecting foreground colour and stored as a variable, never decided in the browser.

ComponentVarsContract: each component/section declares a typed set of CSS variables, resolved from props by a pure resolver and consumed by static CSS with `var(--x, fallback)`; instance overrides never touch selectors.
PrePaintSchemeScript: an inline `<head>` script sets a `data-color-scheme` attribute from storage/matchMedia before first paint; all scheme-dependent vars hang off that attribute.
ScaleVariable: every rem value is `calc(Xrem * var(--scale))` so global density is one variable.
adoption_strategy: Adapt - do not install @mantine/core (React runtime, provider requirement, 39 kB gz global CSS and a dashboard token vocabulary all conflict with Astro islands, the 180 kB JS budget and design-systems-as-JSON). Port the pattern: write a ~200-line TS `compileDesignSystem(tokens.json) -> tokens.css` modelled on `default-css-variables-resolver.ts` + `convert-css-variables.ts`, including derived semantic colour aliases from palette + primaryShade, virtual (scheme-dependent) tokens, compile-time contrast computation (upgraded to a WCAG ratio check that fails the build), and the `--scale` multiplier; snapshot-test its output per design_system_id. Adopt the CSS conventions (`:where()`, `data-*` modifiers, `@layer`, per-component vars with fallbacks) for the section library, and copy the framework-free pieces verbatim: the ColorSchemeScript inline script and the focus-trap/tabbable, scroll-into-view and in-viewport logic from @mantine/hooks as vanilla TS for islands.

status_note: active (turbo/pnpm monorepo; apps/www is a Next 15 + Tailwind v4 + fumadocs site that doubles as the shadcn-format registry host; 78 registry:ui items + 170 registry:example items; 1 open issue, AGENTS.md present for LLM contributors)
core_problem: Gives design-engineers ~80 copy-paste React/Tailwind 'marketing effect' components (shimmer buttons, marquees, bento grids, orbiting icons, globes, beams, text reveals) distributed through the shadcn registry protocol so `npx shadcn add @magicui/<name>` drops source into the consumer's repo instead of installing a package.
architecture: Monorepo (turbo, pnpm) with a single app `apps/www`. Components live as plain source files in `apps/www/registry/magicui/*.tsx` (78 files) and demos in `registry/example/*.tsx` (170). The registry manifest is hand-authored TypeScript: `registry/registry-ui.ts`, `registry-examples.ts`, `registry-lib.ts`, merged in `registry/index.ts` and validated with `registryIndexSchema` from `shadcn/schema` (Zod). Each item is a shadcn RegistryItem: `{name, type: 'registry:ui'|'registry:example'|'registry:lib'|'registry:style', title, description, dependencies (npm, with optional pins like 'cobe@^0.6.4'), registryDependencies (e.g. bento-grid -> ['button'] from shadcn's registry), files:[{path,type,target}], cssVars:{theme:{'animate-x': 'x 8s linear infinite'}}, css:{'@keyframes x': {...}}}`. The build script `apps/www/scripts/build-registry.mts` (1) runs `sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts`, a ts-morph pass that parses example files' imports of `@/registry/magicui/*` and rewrites `registryDependencies` in `registry-examples.ts` so the manifest can never drift from the code; (2) codegens `registry/__index__.tsx` (a `Record<string, {name,type,files,component: React.lazy(() => import(...))}>` used by the docs site's live previews); (3) writes `registry.json` and copies it to `public/r/registry.json`; (4) emits `public/llms.txt` and `public/llms-full.txt` (the full source of every component + examples concatenated, 660 kB) for LLM consumption; (5) shells out to `npx shadcn build registry.json --output public/r` which produces one `public/r/<name>.json` per item with `files[].content` inlined plus `cssVars`/`css`. `lib/registry.ts` serves items to the docs pages: it reads file content, strips `export default`, and rewrites `@/registry/.../(components|ui|hooks|lib)/x` imports into consumer alias paths via `fixImport`. Runtime deps: `motion` ^12.23 (32 of 78 UI components import `motion/react`), `cobe` (globe, WebGL), `canvas-confetti`, `rough-notation` (highlighter), `svg-dotted-map`, `react-tweet`, `shiki` (code-comparison), Radix icons/button. Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` in `styles/globals.css` declares `--animate-*` tokens and 22 `@keyframes` (gradient, meteor, marquee, marquee-vertical, spin-around, shimmer-slide, shiny-text, orbit, shine, ripple, rippling, rainbow, line-shadow, aurora, pulse, pulse-ripple, blink-cursor, background-position-spin, line, ping, accordion-*). No AI is wired in; AGENTS.md is a contributor prompt for coding agents (naming, hook deps, 'subsecond performance' aspiration) and llms-full.txt is the AI-facing distribution surface.
core_innovation: Nothing mechanically new: it is the shadcn registry protocol applied to animated marketing effects, with the one genuinely useful build-time idea being a ts-morph import scan that auto-syncs `registryDependencies` from real imports so the manifest cannot lie.
strengths: Registry item shape is a clean, Zod-validated (`shadcn/schema`) contract that separates npm `dependencies`, cross-registry `registryDependencies`, files with `target` paths, and CSS side-effects (`cssVars.theme` + `css['@keyframes ...']`) — exactly the granularity a section-variant `requires`/asset manifest needs.

`scripts/sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts` (ts-morph) derives dependency lists from actual import statements and fails CI (`registry-deps:check`) on drift — manifest-from-code, not code-from-manifest.

Roughly 20 of the 78 effects are pure CSS keyframes on `transform`/`background-position`/`opacity` with zero runtime JS: marquee, orbiting-circles, animated-gradient-text, animated-shiny-text, shimmer-button, shine-border, rainbow-button, pulsating-button, ripple, meteors (styles randomised once), aurora-text, line-shadow-text, neon-gradient-card, grid-pattern/hexagon-pattern/dot-pattern(static). These use `transform-gpu`, container-query units (`100cqw`, `@container-[size]`), and `offset-path` — compositor-friendly and portable to Astro with no island.

Consistent parameterisation via CSS custom properties set inline (`--duration`, `--gap`, `--radius`, `--spread`, `--shiny-width`, `--angle`) so the keyframes stay static and only per-instance vars change — the right pattern for token-driven design systems.
Emits `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` from the same registry build, so the machine-readable catalogue and the human docs cannot diverge.
MIT, active (pushed 2026-09-20), 22k stars, lockstep with shadcn CLI 3.x and Tailwind v4 — low licensing and abandonment risk.

Some newer components show real engineering: `retro-grid.tsx` is a WebGL fragment shader with a CSS-keyframe fallback, DPR cap of 2, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` media rule; `floating-3d-particles` and `icon-cloud` poll `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.
weaknesses: Accessibility is not systemic: only 5 of 78 UI components (dia-text-reveal, floating-3d-particles, icon-cloud, retro-grid, scroll-based-velocity) reference `prefers-reduced-motion`; `styles/globals.css` has no global reduced-motion rule; infinite CSS animations (marquee, orbit, gradient, meteor, shimmer, shine, rainbow) run forever with no pause affordance (marquee only pauses on hover, opt-in). Fails WCAG 2.2.2 out of the box.

32 of 78 components hard-depend on `motion` (framer-motion successor, ^12.23). `motion/react` with `motion.div` + `AnimatePresence` + `useSpring` is ~35-45 kB gzip; a single BlurFade or NumberTicker island therefore costs a quarter of our 180 kB page budget and requires a React island in Astro. Blur-fade additionally animates `filter: blur()` which is not compositor-only.

12 components run their own `requestAnimationFrame` loops (particles, flickering-grid, glyph-matrix, icon-cloud, floating-3d-particles, hyper-text, morphing-text, cool-mode, retro-grid, smooth-cursor, pulsating-button, confetti); particles.tsx redraws N arcs per frame on a 2D canvas with a global `mousemove` listener that triggers React state updates per event — main-thread cost is unbounded and there is no IntersectionObserver gating on most of them, so off-screen sections keep burning frames.

globe.tsx: cobe WebGL at `devicePixelRatio: 2`, 16k map samples, `phi` advanced every frame forever, no visibility pause, no reduced-motion handling, no static poster. It alone would consume our '<=1 WebGL section' allowance and violate the poster-fallback rule.

Meteors, particles, dot-pattern(glow) and animated-grid-pattern use `Math.random()` in effects/render → non-deterministic output; breaks visual-regression snapshots and our 'everything computed deterministically' principle unless seeded.

Bento-grid is not a layout engine: it is `grid-cols-3 auto-rows-[22rem]` plus a card whose hover translates text 40px and reveals a CTA; the CTA is `opacity-0`/`hidden lg:flex` and only appears on hover on desktop → discoverability and keyboard-focus problem.

The library is the single largest source of what the public now recognises as AI-generated landing-page aesthetics (every v0/Lovable/Bolt default draws on it). Adopting its signature effects directly would undermine the positioning-driven design DNA we are building.

Everything is React 19 + Tailwind v4 + `cn()` from shadcn; class strings use Tailwind v4 arbitrary syntax (`inset-(--cut)`, `bg-size-[...]`, `mask-intersect`) that must be either kept in a Tailwind pipeline or hand-expanded to CSS for Astro.

AI-slop cliché signatures this library popularised — anti-slop tier-1 should BAN (in default/local_trust/premium positionings) or hard rate-limit (max 1 per site, challenger/leader only): shimmer-button, animated-gradient-text (orange→purple `#ffaa40/#9c40ff` default), animated-shiny-text badge ('✨ Introducing …' pill), marquee logo cloud (horizontal infinite), bento-grid feature section, orbiting-circles integration ring, border-beam / shine-border / neon-gradient-card glowing card borders, meteors, globe (cobe), particles / floating-3d-particles hero backgrounds, dot-pattern / grid-pattern / animated-grid-pattern / interactive-grid-pattern / flickering-grid / retro-grid / hexagon-pattern backgrounds with radial-mask fade, rainbow-button, aurora-text, light-rays, warp-background, ripple concentric circles, animated-beam 'integrations' diagrams, iphone/safari/android device mockups around screenshots, hero-video-dialog with blurred thumbnail, dock (macOS dock on a marketing site), typing-animation / word-rotate / morphing-text hero headlines, sparkles-text, text-reveal (scroll-driven opacity words), cool-mode/confetti on CTA click.

Still legitimately usable when constrained: number-ticker (counts once on in-view; must respect reduced-motion and render the final value server-side), blur-fade / text-animate 'blurIn' as a one-shot reveal (as CSS `@keyframes` + IntersectionObserver `class` toggle, not motion), CSS-only marquee for genuine content (testimonials, press quotes) with pause control and reduced-motion off, static (non-glow) dot/grid SVG pattern at very low contrast as texture, highlighter (rough-notation underline) for one word, scroll-progress bar, avatar-circles social-proof stack, progressive-blur on image edges, noise-texture as art-direction grain, animated-circular-progress-bar for a single stat, and pulsating-button only for a single live/status indicator.
patterns_to_steal: Registry item contract (`shadcn/schema` RegistryItem: name/type/dependencies/registryDependencies/files[{path,type,target}]/cssVars/css) → section library manifest: model each Section Variant/Arrangement as a registry-style item whose `css` field carries the exact keyframes it needs, so the Astro assembler only injects keyframes that the selected variants actually use (per-page CSS budget stays computable).

ts-morph import-scan → manifest sync (`scripts/sync-example-registry-dependencies.mts`, `--check` in CI) → build-time validator for our section library: derive each variant's `requires` for lib/components/islands from real imports of the .astro/.ts file and fail CI on drift, so `requires` is never hand-maintained.

CSS-custom-property parameterisation with static keyframes (`--duration`, `--gap`, `--radius`, `--shiny-width`, `--angle`, orbit uses `calc(var(--angle) * 1deg)`) → design_system motion tokens: keyframes live once in the design-system CSS; variants only set vars, which keeps the motion budget a static function of (variant, tokens).

Zero-JS keyframe ports: marquee (translateX(calc(-100% - var(--gap))) with N repeated tracks), orbit, shimmer-slide + spin-around (conic-gradient spark, `100cqw` container units), shiny-text (background-position sweep), meteor, shine/rainbow (background-position) → renderer: implement as `.astro` components with inline `<style>` + `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none }` and a `data-motion="decor"` attribute the motion-budget checker can count.

In-view one-shot reveal pattern (blur-fade/number-ticker use `useInView(once:true, margin:'-50px')`) → motion layer: a single ~600-byte IntersectionObserver script that toggles `[data-reveal]` classes, replacing framer-motion for entrance animations; number-ticker reimplemented with `requestAnimationFrame` + `Intl.NumberFormat` and SSR-rendered final value for no-JS/poster fallback.

llms-full.txt generated from the registry build → Decision Manifest / Gap Report tooling: emit one machine-readable catalogue of section variants (with `requires`, `signature_move`, motion cost) from the same build that produces the runtime library, so the model's eligible-set prompt is generated, never hand-written.

retro-grid.tsx WebGL-with-CSS-fallback structure (shader path, `MAX_DEVICE_PIXEL_RATIO=2`, injected fallback keyframes, reduced-motion media rule) → the template for our single allowed WebGL section: render poster/CSS fallback first, upgrade to WebGL only if `matchMedia` allows motion and the island is in view.
patterns_to_avoid: Adopting `motion` (framer-motion) as the animation runtime → 35-45 kB gzip per page for effects our budget says must be CSS; 32/78 components would pull it in; blur filters and spring-driven `offsetDistance` (border-beam) are JS-driven per frame and count against the 120 ms main-thread budget.

Canvas/rAF ambient backgrounds (particles, flickering-grid, glyph-matrix, floating-3d-particles, icon-cloud) → unbounded per-frame main-thread cost, global mousemove listeners, no in-view gating, `Math.random()` layouts; incompatible with static poster fallback and deterministic QA snapshots.

globe (cobe) as a hero decoration → uses the entire WebGL allowance for a decorative element with no content value, DPR 2 render every frame forever, no poster; only conceivable for a 'leader' positioning with real geographic claims from the FactRegistry, and even then must be poster-first.
Hover-only CTA reveal in bento-grid cards (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, `hidden lg:flex`) → hides primary links from keyboard and touch users; violates our a11y gate.

Shipping the library's default palette values (`#ffaa40` → `#9c40ff`, white shimmer on black) or its component names as-is → these are the literal n-gram/visual signatures the tier-3 self-cliché detector should catch; design systems must supply tokens, components must never carry colour defaults.
Copying the shadcn `React.lazy` `__index__.tsx` runtime and docs-site plumbing → irrelevant to an Astro renderer; only the manifest shape and build validation matter.

Treating llms-full.txt as an eligible-set prompt → it is a flat dump of 660 kB of source; our catalogue must be structured (Zod) and pre-filtered by eligibility predicates, never a raw corpus for the model to browse.
reusable_patterns: RegistryItemContract: a Zod-validated component manifest that lists npm deps, cross-registry deps, files with install targets, and CSS side-effects (theme vars + keyframes) as first-class fields.
ManifestFromImports: derive a component's dependency list at build time by AST-scanning its imports (ts-morph) and fail CI when the hand-written manifest disagrees.
VarParameterisedKeyframes: keep `@keyframes` static in the design-system stylesheet and parameterise per instance only through CSS custom properties set on the element.
OnceInViewReveal: IntersectionObserver with `once:true` and negative root margin toggles a class; the entrance animation itself is CSS; SSR renders the final state for no-JS.
ContainerUnitAnimation: use `100cqw`/`100cqh` container-query units inside keyframes so an effect scales with its host element without JS measurement (shimmer-button).
PosterFirstWebGL: render a CSS/static fallback by default, inject shader/WebGL only after checking reduced-motion, DPR cap, and visibility (retro-grid).
adoption_strategy: Adapt — narrowly. Do not add magicui or `motion` as dependencies. Port 6-8 CSS-keyframe effects (marquee, orbit, shimmer/shine sweep, shiny-text sweep, gradient text, meteor, reveal/blur-in, number-ticker) to zero-JS `.astro` components in the design-system layer with tokenised colours, mandatory `prefers-reduced-motion` rules, pause controls, and SSR final states, and register each with a motion cost so the assembler can sum against the 120 ms/180 kB budgets. Copy the registry-item manifest shape and the ts-morph import-sync validator for the section library's `requires` field. Feed the full effect list into the anti-slop tier-1 ban/rate-limit tables and add its default colour pairs and component idioms to the tier-3 cliché n-grams; whatever survives (number-ticker, one-shot blur-fade, content marquee, static low-contrast pattern texture, highlighter) is only permitted when a variant's `motion` budget and `design_compat` explicitly allow it.
