status_note: active — maintained by WorkOS (Chance Strickland is the sole recent committer, last commit 2026-07-31); npm: radix-ui 1.6.7 / @radix-ui/react-accordion 1.2.20 / react-dialog 1.1.23 / react-tabs 1.1.21 all published 2026-07-24; 205 open issues + 151 open PRs (GitHub reports 356 combined); React-only, peer React 16.8–19.
core_problem: Provides unstyled, WAI-ARIA-correct React widget primitives (accordion, tabs, dialog, menus, popover, navigation-menu, etc.) so design systems get keyboard handling, focus management, layering and mount/unmount animation semantics right without owning that logic; styling is delegated entirely to consumer CSS via data-* attributes and CSS custom properties.
architecture: pnpm monorepo: packages/core (framework-free: primitive/composeEventHandlers, rect, number) and packages/react/* — ~60 packages, one per primitive or hook, plus packages/react/radix-ui which is the unified `radix-ui` package re-exporting every primitive as a namespace (`export * as Accordion from '@radix-ui/react-accordion'`). Every widget is built from the same ~10 building blocks: (1) packages/react/primitive/src/primitive.tsx — a factory over 17 tag names (`Primitive.div`, `Primitive.button`, `Primitive.h3`...) each accepting `asChild`, which swaps the tag for a Slot; (2) packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx — `createSlot` clones the single child and `mergeProps` composes `on[A-Z]` handlers (child first, then slot), shallow-merges `style`, joins `className`, unions `aria-describedby`; `Slottable` marks which child receives slotted props; (3) packages/react/context/src/create-context.tsx — `createContextScope(name, deps)` creates per-instance React contexts passed as a hidden `__scope<Name>` prop, and `composeContextScopes` lets Accordion compose the Collection + Collapsible scopes so nested primitives don't collide; (4) packages/react/use-controllable-state — `{prop, defaultProp, onChange, caller}` controlled/uncontrolled dual mode with a dev warning on mode switch and onChange only firing on actual change; (5) packages/react/presence/src/presence.tsx — a 3-state reducer machine (mounted / unmountSuspended / unmounted, use-state-machine.tsx) that keeps a node mounted through its CSS exit animation; (6) packages/react/collection — item registration; index.ts exports collection-legacy.tsx as `createCollection` (ref-based, `getItems()` reads `data-radix-collection-item` nodes) and collection.tsx as `unstable_createCollection` (an `OrderedDict` keyed by element, re-sorted with `compareDocumentPosition`, MutationObserver hook stubbed); (7) packages/react/roving-focus — `MAP_KEY_TO_FOCUS_INTENT` (Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown → prev/next/first/last), orientation filtering, RTL key swap, `wrapArray` for loop, `focusFirst` that tries candidates until `document.activeElement` changes, single tab stop (`tabIndex={isCurrentTabStop ? 0 : -1}`); (8) packages/react/focus-scope — `getTabbableCandidates` via TreeWalker on `node.tabIndex >= 0`, document `focusin`/`focusout` listeners + MutationObserver to re-trap, a global `focusScopesStack` that pauses the previous scope, cancelable `focusScope.autoFocusOnMount/Unmount` custom events; (9) packages/react/dismissable-layer — module-level `Set`s (`layers`, `layersWithOutsidePointerEventsDisabled`, `branches`); a layer's index in `layers` decides `isHighestLayer` (only it handles Escape), any layer with `disableOutsidePointerEvents` sets `body.style.pointerEvents='none'`, outside-dismiss is detected pointerdown→click, and a `dismissableLayer.update` CustomEvent re-renders all layers; (10) packages/react/portal — `ReactDOM.createPortal` into `document.body` after hydration. Widgets: accordion.tsx = Collection + Collapsible per item (`AccordionItem` maps `value` into Collapsible `open`), `AccordionImpl.onKeyDown` handles Home/End/Arrow with orientation+dir, `AccordionContent` sets `role=region aria-labelledby=triggerId` and aliases `--radix-collapsible-content-height` → `--radix-accordion-content-height`; collapsible.tsx measures content by zeroing `transitionDuration`/`animationName`, calling `getBoundingClientRect`, then restoring, and blocks the mount animation with a rAF-cleared `isMountAnimationPreventedRef`. tabs.tsx = RovingFocusGroup with `role=tablist/tab/tabpanel`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, deterministic ids `${baseId}-trigger-${value}` / `-content-`, `activationMode` automatic|manual, focus-before-activate on mousedown, `hidden={!present}` + `tabIndex=0` on panels. dialog.tsx = Portal + Presence + FocusScope(trapped) + DismissableLayer(disableOutsidePointerEvents) + `react-remove-scroll` + `aria-hidden`'s `hideOthers` (used instead of aria-modal) + dev-only Title/Description warnings. navigation-menu.tsx (1403 lines) adds `delayDuration`/`skipDelayDuration` hover intent, `data-motion` (from-start/to-end...) and `--radix-navigation-menu-viewport-width/height` + indicator translate vars. Styling contract: `data-state` (open/closed, active/inactive, ~143 uses), `data-orientation`, `data-disabled`, `data-side`/`data-align`/`data-highlighted`, and ~58 `--radix-*` custom properties (popper: anchor/available width/height + transform-origin; collapsible/accordion content size; toast swipe; scroll-area). No AI wiring. Tooling: vitest + vitest-axe (16 test files run axe), Playwright e2e for popper/dialog/menus, Storybook + Chromatic visual regression, an SSR test app.
core_innovation: A composable, framework-encoded accessibility contract — every widget is `Primitive.<tag>` + scoped context + controllable state + Presence + a data-state/CSS-variable styling surface — so ARIA, keyboard and layering semantics are reused across ~35 widgets from ~10 tiny mechanisms.
strengths: Reference-grade ARIA/keyboard behaviour for accordion (Home/End/Arrow with orientation+dir, aria-disabled when non-collapsible single), tabs (automatic/manual activation, tablist roving focus, deterministic trigger/content ids) and dialog (focus trap, hideOthers, Escape only on highest layer) — each mechanism is small, readable and unit-tested with axe.

Presence solves the hard part of CSS exit animations correctly: detects an exit animation by diffing computed `animation-name` before/after the `present` flip (because there is no `animationrun` event and `animationstart` fires after delay), waits for `animationend`/`animationcancel` filtered by `CSS.escape(event.animationName)`, and pins `animation-fill-mode: forwards` to avoid a flash on unmount.

Styling surface is entirely declarative and framework-agnostic: `data-state`, `data-orientation`, `data-side`, and measured CSS custom properties (`--radix-accordion-content-height`, `--radix-popper-available-height`) — our design-system token files and section CSS can target exactly this contract.

Scoped contexts (`createContextScope` + `__scope<Name>`) let primitives nest without collisions (Accordion composes Collection and Collapsible scopes) — a clean solution to the 'primitive inside same primitive' problem.
Dismissable-layer stack and focus-scope stack are correct for nested overlays (popover inside dialog): highest layer owns Escape, body pointer-events gating, `branches` exempt from outside-dismiss.

MIT, 19k stars, still actively released (July 2026) by a funded maintainer (WorkOS); unified `radix-ui` package removes per-package version drift; is the base of shadcn/ui so the ecosystem knowledge is huge.

Bundle cost per widget is modest for React: accordion 24.1 kB min / 8.1 kB gz (9 deps), tabs 24.5 / 8.4 kB gz, dialog 37.9 / 12.6 kB gz (15 deps incl. react-remove-scroll 4.2 kB gz + aria-hidden), navigation-menu 37.7 / 11.9 kB gz.
weaknesses: React-only. In Astro every interactive section becomes a React island: the first island pays React + ReactDOM (~45 kB gz) before any primitive; a FAQ accordion island therefore costs ~53 kB gz, roughly 30% of our 180 kB total JS budget, for behaviour native `<details name>` gives for 0 kB.

Bus factor: essentially one active committer (Chance Strickland) in the last year; 205 open issues / 151 open PRs; the newer `unstable_createCollection` still has its MutationObserver re-sort commented out — signs of slow-moving maintenance.

Heavy reliance on React internals and workarounds (`getElementRef` probing `isReactWarning` getters, `dispatchDiscreteCustomEvent` via `flushSync`, `useInsertionEffect` aliasing to dodge bundlers, `window[Symbol.for('radix-ui')]` global) — none of this is portable and it churns with React releases.

Presence and Collapsible measure layout synchronously (`getComputedStyle`, `getBoundingClientRect`, temporary style mutation) which forces style/layout recalcs; the source cites issue #1634 about expensive style recalcs — relevant to our ≤120 ms main-thread motion budget.

Dialog pulls `react-remove-scroll` (tslib, react-remove-scroll-bar, use-sidecar) and `aria-hidden`; modern native `<dialog>` + `closedby` + `overscroll-behavior` make most of that redundant for a marketing site.

No SSR-time output of state: `data-state`/`hidden` are computed in React render, so without an island the static HTML has no styling hooks — we would have to emit the same attributes from our own Astro components anyway.
Zero relevance to research/positioning/anti-slop/QA stages; only touches renderer, motion, and the post-V1 visual editor.
patterns_to_steal: data-state / data-orientation / data-disabled attribute contract (`open|closed`, `active|inactive`, `vertical|horizontal`) → make it the required attribute vocabulary in SiteDefinition section-variant `a11y` specs and in design-system CSS; Astro components emit it statically and the vanilla enhancer only flips it — renderer + design_system.

Presence exit-animation protocol (diff computed `animation-name` on state flip, wait `animationend`/`animationcancel` filtered by `CSS.escape(event.animationName)`, `animation-fill-mode: forwards` pin) → port as a ~40-line vanilla TS `waitForExitAnimation(el)` used by mobile nav, dialogs and any section whose `motion` budget declares an exit keyframe; falls back to instant when `animation-name === 'none'` or reduced-motion — motion.

Collapsible measurement trick (zero `transitionDuration`/`animationName`, read `getBoundingClientRect`, restore, expose `--content-height`; rAF-guarded `isMountAnimationPrevented` to skip animating the initial state) → vanilla accordion height transition when `<details>` is not enough; measured once, gated by the section motion budget — motion + renderer.

Tabs ARIA/keyboard spec verbatim (`role=tablist/tab/tabpanel`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, ids `${base}-trigger-${value}`/`${base}-content-${value}`, `hidden` on inactive panels, `tabIndex=0` on panels, automatic vs manual activation, focus-before-activate on pointerdown) and roving-focus `MAP_KEY_TO_FOCUS_INTENT` + orientation filter + RTL swap + `wrapArray` loop + `focusFirst`-until-activeElement-changes → a ~1 kB vanilla TS `tabs.ts`/`rovingFocus.ts` shared by tabs, pricing toggles, testimonial carousels; these exact attributes become assertions in the Playwright/axe QA gate — renderer + qa_gate.

Accordion keyboard spec (Home/End/ArrowUp/ArrowDown with orientation, RTL-aware ArrowLeft/Right, wrap, skip disabled triggers, `aria-disabled` on the open item when single+non-collapsible, `role=region aria-labelledby=triggerId` on content) → applied on top of native `<details name="faq">` (exclusive accordion, no JS for open/close) with a small keydown enhancer for arrow navigation — renderer.

DismissableLayer stacking rules (only the highest layer handles Escape; outside-dismiss detected pointerdown→click; `branches` exempt; body pointer-events gated while a modal layer is open) → encode as the behaviour spec for the mobile-nav drawer + any modal, implemented with native `<dialog>` (`closedby`, `showModal` gives the focus trap and inertness `hideOthers` emulates) — renderer.

Test-tooling recipe (`vitest-axe` per widget + `@axe-core/playwright` e2e + Chromatic visual regression) → our section library's per-arrangement Playwright + axe tests; every arrangement gets an axe test the way every Radix primitive does — qa_gate.

Scoped composition idea (`createContextScope` / `__scope<Name>`) → only if the post-V1 visual editor is React (Puck-style); then Radix/shadcn is the natural editor chrome and the scope pattern matters — visual_editor.
patterns_to_avoid: Shipping Radix as React islands for marketing sections (FAQ accordion, feature tabs, nav) → React runtime ~45 kB gz + 8–13 kB per primitive against a 180 kB total budget and a near-zero-JS Astro stack; native `<details name>`, `<dialog>` and a ~1–2 kB vanilla enhancer cover the same a11y for marketing pages.

`asChild`/Slot prop-merging → a React-render-tree mechanism with no meaning in Astro's static HTML; our section variants should own their markup, and composition happens in the arrangement layer, not by cloning children.

`createContextScope` and controlled/uncontrolled `useControllableState` → React state plumbing; our site has no framework state; state lives in DOM attributes (`data-state`, `open`) which is what the CSS targets anyway.

`react-remove-scroll` + `aria-hidden`/`hideOthers` for modals → replaced by native `<dialog>` `showModal()` (top layer, inert background) and `overscroll-behavior: contain`; adds ~6 kB gz and a sidecar for behaviour the platform now provides.

Synchronous `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect` on every open/close inside sections that also run scroll-linked animations → conflicts with the ≤120 ms main-thread motion budget; prefer `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` where supported, with the Presence protocol only as the fallback path.

Adopting the whole primitive taxonomy (Menubar, ContextMenu, Toolbar, Select, Slider, OTP field) → app-UI components with no place in a marketing-site section library; would tempt over-decomposition into many packages before shipping (already rejected).
reusable_patterns: DataStateStylingContract: interactive state is exposed only as `data-state`/`data-orientation`/`data-*` attributes plus measured CSS custom properties, so styling and animation are 100% CSS and framework-independent.

AnimationAwarePresence: keep a node in the DOM after its logical close until the CSS exit animation (detected by animation-name diff) ends, via a 3-state machine mounted → unmountSuspended → unmounted.
MeasuredCollapse: temporarily disable transitions/animations, measure full content size, restore, and expose the size as a CSS variable so height can transition from 0 to a real value.

RovingTabStop: a group has exactly one `tabIndex=0` item; Arrow/Home/End keys map to prev/next/first/last intents filtered by orientation and reading direction, with wrap-around and focus-until-activeElement-changes.

LayerStackDismissal: a global ordered set of overlay layers where only the topmost handles Escape/outside-pointer dismissal, branches are exempt, and body pointer-events is gated when any modal layer exists.
ScopedComposition: nested instances of the same primitive get isolated contexts through a hidden per-instance scope object, letting a higher-level widget compose lower-level ones without collisions.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not add React islands for marketing-page accordion/tabs/nav; instead (1) build our FAQ/accordion arrangements on native `<details name="…">` with Radix's ARIA attributes and Home/End/Arrow keyboard handling ported as a ~1 kB vanilla TS enhancer, (2) port tabs.tsx's role/id/aria scheme + roving-focus's key-intent table into a shared `rovingFocus.ts`/`tabs.ts`, (3) port Presence's animation-name-diff + animationend wait as `waitForExitAnimation()` for the mobile-nav drawer and any section with an exit keyframe, with `@starting-style`/`allow-discrete` as the primary path, and (4) adopt the `data-state` vocabulary as the mandatory attribute contract in section-variant `a11y`/`motion` specs and as Playwright+axe assertions in the QA gate. Only Adopt Radix (via shadcn/ui) inside the post-V1 React visual editor, where a React runtime is already paid for.

architecture: Turborepo/Bun monorepo: apps/www (coss.com marketing), apps/ui (coss ui docs + registry.json, 577 items: 56 registry:ui, 508 registry:block 'particles' named p-<component>-<n>, 6 registry:lib, 3 registry:font, 2 registry:style, 2 registry:hook), apps/origin (the frozen Origin UI app + registry.json with 646 items: 600 registry:component demos, 40 registry:ui, 5 hooks, 1 lib), packages/ui (@coss/ui, version 0.0.0, private-ish workspace package exporting ./components/*, ./base-ui/*, ./hooks/*, ./lib/*, ./fonts, ./globals.css; deps: @base-ui/react 1.8.0, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, lucide-react, @hugeicons, next-themes, shiki; peer next ^16, react ^19, tailwindcss 4). Primitive base is Base UI (MUI's headless library), not Radix: components/button.tsx uses `useRender`/`mergeProps` from @base-ui/react and CVA variants with `data-pressed`, `data-loading`, `pointer-coarse:after:min-h-11` hit-target enlargement. Token contract is pure CSS custom properties in packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css: Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` maps `--color-*` to semantic vars (background/foreground/card/popover/primary/secondary/muted/accent/destructive/info/success/warning + foreground pairs, border/input/ring, chart-1..5, sidebar-*, code-*), `--radius-sm/md/lg/xl` derived from `--radius` by +-px, `--font-sans/--font-heading/--font-mono`, and a small motion set (`--animate-skeleton`, `--animate-caret-blink`, toast keyframes) with an explicit `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that disables the toast animations. Light values are Tailwind palette references (`var(--color-neutral-800)`), dark values use `color-mix()` and `--alpha()` against neutral-950. The registry `registry:style` items ship the same cssVars plus a `css` block (`@layer base { * { @apply border-border outline-ring/50 } body { @apply bg-background text-foreground } }`), and `registry:font` items declare Google-provider fonts (Inter for sans and heading, Geist Mono) with `--font-*` variables. Distribution is a namespaced registry `@coss/<item>` (live at https://coss.com/ui/r/<name>.json with $schema ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry-item.json and inlined file content) consumed by `npx shadcn add @coss/button`; particles depend on ui items via `registryDependencies: ['@coss/accordion']`. The legacy apps/origin registry is Radix (`radix-ui` 27 items) + React Aria (`react-aria-components` 14) based, with tailwind keyframes for accordion in the item `tailwind.config`, and is explicitly marked 'support and maintenance are limited'. core_innovation: Nothing mechanically new: a shadcn-style registry whose headless base is Base UI instead of Radix, with a 'particles' layer of 508 pre-composed usage patterns per primitive and an unusually careful CSS-only token file (color-mix dark mode, reduced-motion opt-out, coarse-pointer hit targets).
strengths: Token file is a good reference for CSS-only theming on Tailwind v4: semantic pairs plus info/success/warning roles, `--radius` derivation, fonts as `--font-*` vars, and reduced-motion handled in CSS rather than JS (packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css).

Registry usage is idiomatic and complete: registry:style carries cssVars + css, registry:font items declare font provider/variable/dependency, particles express `registryDependencies` on `@coss/*` items, so the whole design system is installable and dependency-graphed.

Base UI (`useRender` + `mergeProps`) instead of Radix `asChild` is a lighter, actively developed headless base; components use `data-*` state attributes (`data-pressed`, `data-loading`, `data-slot`) as the styling hooks.
Accessibility details baked into CSS: `pointer-coarse:after:min-h-11 min-w-11` enlarges touch targets to 44px without changing layout; focus-visible rings on tokens.
The legacy Origin UI catalogue (646 items, MIT) remains readable as a corpus of form/input/select/slider patterns and is served from coss.com/origin.
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 on the active code (root LICENSE, @coss/ui package.json). For a commercial agency product, copying coss ui component source into generated client sites makes each site a derivative work distributed under AGPL: the client site source must be offered under AGPL, and if the pipeline itself is a hosted service that incorporates coss code, the network-use clause (AGPL s.13) applies to the pipeline too. There is no dual/commercial license offered in the repo. Only apps/origin (legacy, MIT) is safe to copy.
Entirely app-UI oriented: inputs, selects, combobox, calendar, availability editor, sidebars, tables. Zero marketing sections, no motion/layout vocabulary; irrelevant to the section library.

React 19 + Next 16 peer dependencies and `'use client'` on every component; in Astro every interactive piece is a React island (React runtime ~45 kB gz + @base-ui/react), incompatible with the 180 kB budget for more than a couple of islands.
Design direction is a single Cal.com brand voice (neutral palette, Inter, Cal Sans); it is one design system, not a token system that can host many.
Legacy Origin UI snapshot is frozen ('maintenance limited'), still on Radix + React Aria mix, so the surviving MIT corpus will bit-rot.
Registry items are unversioned (`latest` only); no changelog per item, no content hashes.
patterns_to_steal: CSS-only reduced-motion opt-out inside the token file (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { :where(.animate-*) { animation: none } }`) → motion layer: every design_system token file must ship the same block covering all `--animate-*` tokens so the QA gate can assert it statically.
Coarse-pointer hit-target enlargement via pseudo-element (`pointer-coarse:after:min-h-11 min-w-11`) → renderer button/link primitives; satisfies WCAG 2.5.8 target size without layout changes.

Dark-mode values derived with `color-mix()`/`--alpha()` from a single neutral base rather than a second hand-authored palette → design_system token compiler: derive dark scheme from light tokens deterministically where art direction allows.

registry:font items with provider/import/variable/dependency → SectionLibrary manifest: model fonts as first-class items with a `--font-*` variable contract so eligibility can gate typography by design system.

Particles naming (`p-<primitive>-<n>` with `categories` and `registryDependencies`) → arrangements: a section variant's arrangements are exactly this shape, keep the flat numbered naming plus human-authored `signature_move`.
patterns_to_avoid: Copying any coss ui (@coss/*) component source into client sites → AGPL-3.0 contamination of client deliverables and potentially of the hosted pipeline; no commercial license available.
Using the React/Base UI components as the runtime for sections → React island per component, `'use client'` everywhere, Next 16 peer dep; violates the near-zero-JS Astro constraint.
Adopting a single-brand token set (Cal.com neutral/Inter) as our default design system → it is one aesthetic; our design systems must be many, with visual_dna, and selected by id.
Building on the legacy apps/origin corpus → frozen Radix + React Aria mix with limited maintenance; MIT but bit-rotting and still app-UI only.
reusable_patterns: ReducedMotionInTokens: declare motion tokens and their reduced-motion kill switch in the same CSS file so the rule is static and auditable.
CoarsePointerHitTarget: enlarge touch targets with an absolutely positioned pseudo-element under `pointer: coarse` instead of changing box size.
DerivedDarkScheme: compute dark tokens from light tokens with color-mix/alpha rather than authoring two palettes.
NumberedPatternRegistry: pre-composed usage patterns per primitive as numbered registry blocks with categories and registryDependencies.
LicenseFenceByDirectory: keep a legacy MIT snapshot in a separate app with its own LICENSE.md inside an otherwise AGPL monorepo (a warning to check license per path, not per repo).
adoption_strategy: Ignore. Nothing here is marketing-oriented, the active code is AGPL-3.0 with no commercial option, and the runtime is React 19 + Base UI + Next 16. Do not copy any @coss/* source into the pipeline or into client sites. Lift only the license-free CSS ideas (reduced-motion block in the token file, coarse-pointer hit targets, color-mix dark derivation, font items as registry entries) and re-author them in our own token compiler; if a form-heavy client page ever needs a reference for input/select/combobox patterns, consult the MIT apps/origin snapshot at coss.com/origin, not the coss ui package.

status_note: active; @ark-ui/react|vue|solid 5.39.2 and @ark-ui/svelte 5.24.2 released 2026-09-13 on Zag 1.44.0; 15 open issues
core_problem: Provide one accessible, headless behaviour implementation per widget (accordion, tabs, carousel, dialog, menu, combobox, ...) that works identically in React, Vue, Solid and Svelte by moving all logic into framework-agnostic Zag.js state machines and keeping the framework layer to prop plumbing.
architecture: Two repos. chakra-ui/zag holds the logic: `@zag-js/core` (create-machine.ts, types.ts) defines a machine as `{ props(), initialState(), context() of bindable values, computed, refs, watch(track), on, states: { <state>: { entry, exit, effects, on: { EVENT: Transition | Transition[] } } }, implementations: { guards, actions, effects } }` with `createGuards()` (and/or/not) and string-keyed actions/guards so the machine is declarative data. Each widget lives in `packages/machines/<name>/src/` as five files: `<name>.machine.ts` (states/transitions, e.g. accordion has `idle` and `focused` with events TRIGGER.FOCUS/BLUR/CLICK, GOTO.NEXT/PREV/FIRST/LAST, VALUE.SET and guards `isExpanded`, `canToggle`), `<name>.connect.ts` (pure function `connect(service, normalizeProps)` that projects state into per-part prop bags: `getRootProps/getItemProps/getItemTriggerProps/getItemContentProps/getItemIndicatorProps` emitting `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `hidden`, `data-state=open|closed`, `data-orientation`, `data-focus`, `data-disabled`, plus keyboard maps ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right/Home/End via `getEventKey` with dir/orientation awareness), `<name>.anatomy.ts` (`createAnatomy('accordion').parts('root','item','itemTrigger','itemContent','itemIndicator')` producing `data-scope`/`data-part` attributes), `<name>.dom.ts` (id scheme and element queries through a `Scope` with getRootNode for shadow DOM) and `<name>.types.ts`. The framework adapters in `packages/frameworks/{react,vue,solid,svelte,preact,vanilla}` each implement the same `useMachine` interpreter (react/src/machine.ts uses useRef/flushSync/useSyncExternalStore; svelte/src/machine.svelte.ts uses $derived/$effect runes; vanilla/src/machine.ts is a `VanillaMachine` class with `subscribe`, `send`, `updateProps`, `start/stop`) plus `normalizeProps` (framework prop naming) and, for vanilla, `spreadProps(node, attrs, machineId)` which diff-applies attributes, inline styles (property by property so popper `--x/--y` vars survive) and event listeners onto existing DOM nodes. Carousel machine (carousel.machine.ts, 582 lines) is built on native CSS scroll-snap (`@zag-js/scroll-snap` computes snap positions, `scrollSnapType` set in connect), has `idle`/`dragging`/`autoplay` states, IntersectionObserver-tracked `slidesInView` (inViewThreshold 0.6), ResizeObserver, pauses autoplay on `visibilitychange`, and connect emits `role=region` + `aria-roledescription=carousel`, `aria-live` polite/off depending on autoplay, slides as `role=group aria-roledescription=slide` with `aria-hidden` when out of view, prev/next `aria-controls`, and an autoplay toggle with start/stop labels. chakra-ui/ark is the thin component layer: `packages/react/src/components/accordion/use-accordion.ts` is 15 lines (`useMachine(accordion.machine, {id, dir, getRootNode, ...props})` then `accordion.connect(service, normalizeProps)`), `accordion-root.tsx` splits machine props from DOM props with `createSplitProps`, merges `getRootProps()` via `mergeProps` and renders `ark.div` (polymorphic factory with `asChild`); `accordion-item-content.tsx` delegates to `Collapsible.Content`, whose `use-presence.ts` wraps `@zag-js/presence` for animation-aware mount/unmount with `lazyMount`, `unmountOnExit`, `hideMode: 'display-none' | 'activity'` (React Activity when supported) and `skipAnimationOnMount`. The Svelte layer (`packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion-root.svelte`, `use-accordion.svelte.ts`) is the same shape with `$bindable` value and `$derived` props, confirming that ~95% of behaviour is in Zag. Extension points: `EnvironmentProvider` (root node), `LocaleProvider` (dir), `ids` overrides, `translations` per machine, `data-scope/data-part` for styling recipes (Park UI). Bundle (esm.sh bundled, gzip): @zag-js/vanilla 6.7 kB, @zag-js/accordion 3.3 kB, @zag-js/tabs 6.5 kB, @zag-js/carousel 9.8 kB, @zag-js/collapsible 4.4 kB, @zag-js/presence 2.5 kB, @zag-js/dom-query 11.2 kB (shared, partially tree-shaken per machine), @zag-js/react 4.4 kB + React; @ark-ui/react full barrel 290 kB gz with 69 deps (not tree-shake-safe: sideEffects false is not set).
core_innovation: One declarative state machine plus one pure connect() projection per widget serves every framework, including vanilla DOM, so accessibility semantics and keyboard behaviour are written once as data and the framework adapter is only an interpreter plus prop normaliser.
strengths: Framework-free path exists and is real: `@zag-js/vanilla` (VanillaMachine + spreadProps + normalizeProps) can run an accordion/tabs/carousel machine against server-rendered Astro HTML with no React/Vue/Svelte runtime, ~10-17 kB gz per widget including core.

A11y is baked into connect(): role/aria-* wiring, `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` id contracts, orientation- and RTL-aware key maps, `hidden` on collapsed panels, `aria-roledescription` carousel/slide, `aria-live` handling, autoplay pause on document hidden.
Machine spec is declarative and inspectable: states, events, guards, actions are strings resolved in `implementations`, so the behaviour graph can be validated, tested, or even snapshotted as data.
Anatomy contract (`data-scope`, `data-part`, `data-state`) decouples styling completely from behaviour; CSS can target parts without classes.
Carousel is built on native CSS scroll-snap rather than transform math, so it degrades to a plain scrollable list without JS and respects browser scroll physics.
Presence machine handles enter/exit animation waits (animationend) generically, with lazy mount / unmount-on-exit / display-none vs Activity hide modes.
Large surface (60+ machines) with monthly releases across four frameworks; MIT.
weaknesses: Zag machines run entirely client-side and require the DOM ids/attributes to be applied by the adapter; with SSR'd Astro HTML you must either pre-render the exact same attribute set (ids, aria, data-state) or accept a hydration flash while spreadProps rewrites them.

Per-widget cost is not trivial relative to native HTML: an accordion via vanilla Zag is ~10 kB gz where `<details name>` with a few lines of CSS is 0 kB; tabs ~13 kB; carousel ~17 kB. Fine within 180 kB, but each island adds up.
Full `@ark-ui/react` is 290 kB gz / 69 deps and does not declare `sideEffects: false`; only per-machine `@zag-js/*` imports are budget-safe.
The vanilla adapter has no docs beyond source (README missing), only a jsdom test suite; API stability of `spreadProps`/`VanillaMachine` is less proven than the React/Vue adapters.
Machines do not read `prefers-reduced-motion`: carousel autoplay and presence animations are left to CSS; the caller must gate autoplay and keyframes.
Some machines pull heavy shared utilities (`dom-query` 11 kB, `interact-outside`, `focus-visible`) into dialog/menu/popover, so overlays cost 20-30 kB gz even in vanilla.
Maintained by a small team (Segun Adebayo's Chakra org); breaking changes between Zag majors (v0 -> v1 rewrote the machine API in 2025).
patterns_to_steal: Machine-per-widget as declarative data (`states`, `on`, `guards`, `actions` as string keys resolved in `implementations`) → section variant `a11y` contract: express each interactive section's allowed states/events (accordion: idle/focused; carousel: idle/dragging/autoplay) so the QA gate can assert keyboard paths from the spec, not from prose.

connect() prop-bag projection with anatomy parts (`data-scope`, `data-part`, `data-state`, `data-orientation`) → renderer: Astro section templates render exactly these attributes server-side so styling and Playwright/axe assertions target parts, and a vanilla machine can attach without rewriting markup.

`@zag-js/vanilla` VanillaMachine + spreadProps on existing DOM → islands runtime: for FAQ accordion, feature tabs and testimonial carousel, hydrate SSR'd HTML with the machine (10-17 kB gz each) instead of shipping a framework island; keep native `<details>` for the cheapest accordion arrangements.

Carousel on CSS scroll-snap with IntersectionObserver `slidesInView`, `aria-roledescription`, autoplay pause on `visibilitychange` → testimonial/logo carousel arrangements: base markup must scroll-snap natively (JS-off fallback), autoplay only when eligibility allows and never under reduced motion.
Presence machine's animationend-aware unmount with lazyMount/unmountOnExit → motion layer: reuse for any expand/collapse so exit animations complete before `hidden` is applied.

Id scheme through a `Scope` (`getById`, `getRootNode`) with overridable `ids` → SiteDefinition: assign deterministic section-scoped ids at assembly time so aria-controls/labelledby pairs are stable across rebuilds and diffable.
patterns_to_avoid: Importing `@ark-ui/react` (or vue/solid/svelte) into Astro islands → framework runtime per island plus a 290 kB gz barrel with 69 deps; use `@zag-js/<machine>` + `@zag-js/vanilla` directly, or native HTML.

Using Zag for content that native HTML already handles (single-open accordion via `<details name>`, simple disclosure, static tabs that can be links) → 0 kB beats 10 kB; reserve machines for roving-focus tabs, carousels with autoplay/indicators, and overlays.
Relying on the machines for reduced-motion or motion budget → they do not consult `prefers-reduced-motion`; motion gating must live in our token CSS and in the section's `motion` budget.

Overlay machines (dialog, menu, popover, combobox) in marketing sections → 20-30 kB gz each with focus-trap/interact-outside/dom-query; marketing pages should avoid overlays except a single mobile nav drawer, which native `<dialog>` covers.
Client-only attribute application (letting spreadProps add aria/ids after hydration) → hydration flash and axe failures on the SSR snapshot; render the connect() attribute set at build time.
reusable_patterns: DeclarativeWidgetMachine: widget behaviour as a serialisable state chart with string-keyed guards/actions and separate implementations.
ConnectProjection: a pure function from machine state to per-part attribute/handler bags, framework-agnostic via a normalizeProps shim.
AnatomyPartsContract: `data-scope`/`data-part`/`data-state` attributes as the only coupling between behaviour and styling.
VanillaHydrateExistingDOM: attach a machine to server-rendered markup by diff-spreading attributes, styles and listeners rather than re-rendering.
ScrollSnapCarousel: native scroll-snap as the base with JS only for indicators, autoplay and aria-live.
AnimationAwarePresence: wait for animationend before hiding/unmounting, with lazy mount and unmount-on-exit options.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (Adopt the Zag machines selectively, not Ark). Yes, state-machine-per-widget is the right a11y base for interactive sections, but consume it as `@zag-js/accordion|tabs|carousel` + `@zag-js/vanilla` inside Astro `<script>` islands attached to SSR'd markup, never as an Ark framework island. Encode the connect() attribute set (role, aria-*, data-part, data-state, ids) into the Astro section templates at build time so the static HTML already passes axe and the machine only takes over interactivity; budget roughly 10 kB gz for accordion, 13 kB tabs, 17 kB carousel and prefer native `<details>`/scroll-snap-only arrangements when the variant's `motion`/`a11y` spec allows. Reuse the machine vocabulary (states, events, guards) as the schema for our section `a11y` contract, and gate carousel autoplay and presence animations with our reduced-motion tokens since Zag does not.

status_note: Effectively frozen. Vercel acquired Tremor on 2025-01-22; co-founder stated on the Vercel community forum (quoted in issue #140) that net-new development happens in shadcn/ui. Last substantive commit 2025-04-12 (Tailwind v4); the two Oct-2025 commits only delete CI (chromatic.yml, storybook publish). One maintainer (severinlandolt: 79 of 84 commits). 9 open PRs unmerged including #166 (React 19 / Recharts 3 upgrade, June 2026) and #121 (jsrepo CLI). Legacy npm package @tremor/react is at 3.18.7 (published 2025-01-13, Tailwind v3 + headlessui, repo tremor-npm not archived, not npm-deprecated, 63 open issues, no commits since).
core_problem: Gives dashboard builders copy-and-paste React source for 35 Tailwind v4 + Radix components, of which six are Recharts wrappers (Area/Bar/Line/Combo/Donut/Spark) that expose a fixed 9-colour category palette and a uniform props API so charts look consistent without touching Recharts directly.
architecture: Not a package: package.json is `tremor-raw`, private, version 0.0.0, and there is no registry.json, components.json, CLI or exports map. Distribution is `scripts/component-folder.js`, which copies every `src/components/<Name>/<Name>.tsx` into `src/components-folder/` and regex-rewrites `../../utils/*` imports to a single `@/lib/utils` import so the file can be pasted into a Next.js app. Each component file carries a header version (`// Tremor AreaChart [v1.0.0]`) and sits beside its own `changelog.md`, `*.stories.tsx` and a Playwright `*.spec.ts` that drives Storybook on :6006 (three browsers; vitest covers only `src/utils/utils.spec.ts`). Styling is 100% literal Tailwind palette classes with inline `dark:` variants; `src/globals.css` defines only animation keyframes under `@theme`, no colour, spacing or radius tokens, and Card hardcodes `dark:bg-[#090E1A]`. Variants use tailwind-variants `tv()` with slots (ProgressBar: background/bar slots x default|neutral|warning|error|success). The chart layer is Recharts 2.15.2 (`ResponsiveContainer` + `Area/Bar/Line/Pie` + `XAxis/YAxis/Tooltip/Legend/CartesianGrid`), all `use client`. Colour mapping lives in `src/utils/chartColors.ts`: a `chartColors` const of 9 keys (blue, emerald, violet, amber, gray, cyan, pink, lime, fuchsia) each holding a 4-tuple of Tailwind classes `{bg, stroke, fill, text}` (e.g. `fill-blue-500`); `constructCategoryColors` assigns colours to series by index modulo palette length; `getColorClassName(color, utility)` falls back to gray. Charts pass empty `fill`/`stroke` props to Recharts and inject the class instead; the area gradient uses `<linearGradient className="text-blue-500"><stop stopColor="currentColor">` so colour flows through CSS `currentColor`. The tooltip cursor is a hardcoded `#d1d5db` hex in all four cartesian charts. Every root element carries a `tremor-id="tremor-raw"` DOM attribute (76 files). Dashboard blocks (KPI cards, tables, 300 blocks) are not in this repo; they live in `tremorlabs/tremor-blocks` (MIT after acquisition, last push 2025-01-22) and the `template-*` repos (pushed Dec 2025 to Jan 2026). No AI wiring of any kind.
core_innovation: A per-semantic-colour utility tuple ({bg, stroke, fill, text}) that lets one colour key drive SVG series, legend swatches and tooltip dots consistently through Tailwind classes and currentColor, instead of hex values passed to Recharts.
strengths: Colour-tuple contract in src/utils/chartColors.ts is tiny, typed (`as const satisfies`), and gives every chart, legend and tooltip the same colour source; `constructCategoryColors` is a pure, deterministic series-to-colour assignment.
Every component is a self-contained file with a header version and a per-component changelog.md, so vendored copies can be diffed against upstream without a package manager.

Uniform chart props API across Area/Bar/Line/Combo (index, categories, colors, valueFormatter, showLegend, startEndOnly, autoMinValue, customTooltip, tooltipCallback, onValueChange) hides Recharts entirely from the consumer.
Series animation is off by default (`isAnimationActive={false}`) and legend overflow is handled with an arrow-key scrollable slider (`enableLegendSlider`), a rare detail.
Storybook + Playwright per component across chromium/firefox/webkit, with `@storybook/addon-a11y` installed.
Apache-2.0 with clear provenance; ProgressBar (role=progressbar, aria-valuenow/max) and CategoryBar (aria-valuenow) got an explicit a11y fix in PR #100.
weaknesses: Maintenance is over: single maintainer absorbed into Vercel, no substantive commit since 2025-04, unmerged React 19/Recharts 3 PR, and the founders point users to shadcn/ui charts (which also wrap Recharts).

Bundle cost is incompatible with our 180 kB JS budget: Recharts 2.15 is 4.6 MB unpacked and drags lodash, victory-vendor (d3-scale/shape/array/interpolate), react-smooth and eventemitter3; a single chart island would ship the React runtime plus roughly 90-110 kB gzipped of Recharts before any page code. Recharts 3 is larger (7.4 MB unpacked).

Chart accessibility is decorative only: the only aria in AreaChart/BarChart/LineChart/DonutChart is `aria-hidden` on colour swatches; no role=img, no aria-label, no data-table or text fallback, no keyboard access to data points, no `prefers-reduced-motion`, and Recharts 2's `accessibilityLayer` prop is not used. Playwright specs check visibility and CSS classes, not axe results.

No token layer: colours are literal Tailwind palette classes with inline dark: variants, a hardcoded `#d1d5db` cursor and `dark:bg-[#090E1A]` on Card; re-theming means find-and-replace across files (that is literally how the 'Feat/blue theme' PR #88 worked). This contradicts our rule that design systems are concrete token files the model selects by id.
All charts are client components; nothing renders server-side or as static SVG, so charts cannot be pre-rendered to a poster for the static fallback.
Copy-paste distribution without a manifest means no dependency graph, no `requires`/`design_compat` metadata, no install verification; the import-rewrite script assumes an `@/lib/utils` alias.
The 9-colour palette is unordered by perceptual contrast and cycles modulo length, so a 10th series silently reuses blue; no colour-blind-safe ordering.
patterns_to_steal: Colour utility tuple {bg, stroke, fill, text} per semantic colour key (src/utils/chartColors.ts) -> design_system: add a `chart_series` block to each design-system token file that maps `series-1..n` to CSS variables and pre-resolved class names, so a post-V1 analytics section can colour SVG marks from the same token file as the page.

Deterministic series-to-colour assignment `constructCategoryColors(categories, colors)` -> renderer: pure function computed at assembly time, not by the model; snapshot the mapping into the Decision Manifest.

Per-file header version + sibling changelog.md -> section library: stamp every human-authored section variant/arrangement file with a version header so telemetry and priors can be keyed to an exact variant revision.

`scripts/component-folder.js` import-rewrite step -> renderer build: an export script that rewrites internal import paths when vendoring a section into a client repo, if we ever hand off source to clients.

currentColor gradient trick (`<linearGradient className=text-x><stop stopColor=currentColor>`) -> renderer: lets static SVG charts inherit colour from CSS variables with zero JS, useful for the static poster fallback of any data section.
patterns_to_avoid: Recharts-based client charts -> violates the 180 kB total JS budget and the Astro near-zero-JS stack; any V2 analytics page should render charts as server-generated static SVG (or a tiny island) rather than adopt Recharts wrappers.

Literal Tailwind palette classes with inline dark: variants as the theming mechanism -> our design systems must be token files with CSS variables; hardcoded `bg-blue-500` and `#d1d5db` cannot be swapped by selecting a design_system_id.
Copy-paste distribution without a registry/manifest -> we need `requires`, `design_compat` and `a11y` metadata on every section; a bare .tsx file carries none of it.
Charts with aria-hidden swatches and no text fallback -> would fail our axe-core gate and offers no screen-reader path; do not treat Tremor's chart a11y as a baseline.
Modulo colour cycling without a contrast-ordered palette -> pick a fixed perceptually ordered series palette per design system and cap series count in the section's `requires`.
reusable_patterns: ColorUtilityTuple: one semantic colour key resolves to a fixed set of per-utility class names or variables (bg/stroke/fill/text) so markup, SVG and text share a single colour source.
DeterministicSeriesPalette: series names are mapped to palette slots by index in a pure function, producing a snapshotable mapping rather than per-render randomness.
FileLevelVersionStamp: each vendored source file carries its own version header and changelog so copies can be diffed against upstream without a package registry.
ImportRewriteVendoring: a build script copies components and rewrites internal relative imports to a consumer alias, turning a monorepo folder into paste-ready files.
CurrentColorSVGTheming: SVG fills and gradients read `currentColor` from a CSS class on the element, decoupling chart colours from JS props.
SlotVariants: tailwind-variants `tv({slots})` gives named sub-parts (background/bar) per semantic variant (success/warning/error) in one typed object.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for V1 and for the marketing-site generator: nothing here touches sections, layout, positioning, art direction or QA, and the chart layer is a frozen Recharts wrapper whose bundle cost alone breaks the JS budget. The only durable value is the colour-tuple shape in src/utils/chartColors.ts; when post-V1 client analytics pages are designed, lift that shape into each design-system token file as CSS variables (`--series-1..n` plus bg/stroke/fill/text resolutions) and render charts as static SVG via the currentColor trick, without pulling Recharts or the Tremor components. If a React chart island is ever justified, shadcn/ui charts are the maintained successor and use the same Recharts base, so nothing is lost by skipping Tremor.

license: Proprietary (free tier: copy-paste, no OSS license file; Pro 'End Product' license: commercial/client use allowed, no redistribution/marketplace resale of components or derivative component products)
status_note: closed-source; analyzed from public catalogue (https://ui.aceternity.com/components) and the public shadcn-format registry at https://ui.aceternity.com/registry/{name}.json; the listed GitHub repo shadcnblocks/aceternity-ui is a 404 and no official source repo exists
core_problem: Sells 'landing pages that look 100x better' by packaging eye-catching hero/background/text effects (beams, sparkles, lamp, aurora, 3D tilt) as copy-paste React + Tailwind + Motion components, monetised through a Pro block/template library.
architecture: Distribution is a public shadcn-compatible registry: `https://ui.aceternity.com/registry.json` lists 284 items (112 `registry:ui`, 172 `registry:block`), each item JSON at `/registry/{name}.json` inlines `files[].content` (Pro blocks such as `github-globe` return HTTP 401). Items carry only `dependencies` and `files`; across 284 items there are zero `cssVars`, zero `tailwind` extensions and zero `css` blocks, so effects that rely on custom keyframes (`animate-aurora`, `animate-meteor-effect`, `animate-scroll`, `animate-spotlight`) ship without their keyframes and require the user to hand-paste Tailwind config from the docs page. Dependency profile: `motion` (framer-motion) in 169/284 items, `@tabler/icons-react` 69, `react-fast-marquee` 6, `three`/`@react-three/fiber`/`@react-three/drei` 3, `cobe` 2, `@tsparticles/*` 1, `simplex-noise` 2. Component anatomy from the sampled sources: `background-beams.tsx` is a `<motion.path>` over ~50 SVG path strings with `repeat: Infinity` and `duration: Math.random()*10+10` per path; `lamp.tsx` stacks two `conic-gradient` `motion.div`s plus four blurred layers (`blur-2xl`, `blur-md`, `blur-3xl`, `blur-2xl`) driven by five `whileInView` animations on hard-coded cyan; `aurora-background.tsx` layers six `repeating-linear-gradient`s with `blur-[10px]` and an `animate-aurora` class whose 60 s `background-position` keyframe is not in the item; `meteors.tsx` renders 20 absolutely positioned spans with `animate-meteor-effect`; `3d-card.tsx` uses React context + `onMouseMove` to set `rotateY(${x}deg) rotateX(${y}deg)` under `perspective: 1000px` with no touch or keyboard path; `sparkles.tsx` boots the tsparticles engine (`initParticlesEngine` + `loadSlim`, `fpsLimit: 120`) on a canvas; `vortex.tsx` runs its own `requestAnimationFrame` canvas loop with simplex noise; `infinite-moving-cards.tsx` clones the DOM list (`cloneNode`) and relies on an `animate-scroll` keyframe; `text-generate-effect.tsx` staggers per-word `filter: blur` with `stagger(0.2)`; `hero-highlight.tsx` tracks the pointer with `useMotionValue` into a radial `mask-image`. None of the 16 sampled items references `prefers-reduced-motion` or `useReducedMotion`. There is no theming layer: colours are literal Tailwind palette classes and hex stops (cyan-500, indigo-500, `#ffaa40`), not semantic tokens. The Pro tier (Annual $169, Lifetime $199, Team $1,590) adds 200+ blocks: hero, logo cloud, bento, CTA, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, navbar, footer, team, stats, and 'shaders' (dither, cloud, spotlight WebGL).
core_innovation: None mechanically; its innovation is commercial: it productised a catalogue of hero-section spectacle effects and, by being the default 'make it look premium' library for AI builders, became the visual fingerprint of AI-generated landing pages.
strengths: Registry-format distribution means the item list, dependency profile and source of every free effect are machine-readable, which makes building a slop-signature corpus trivial (284 item names + class/keyframe names).

A few effects are honest CSS: `aurora-background` (gradient + keyframe, 0 JS), `meteors` (spans + keyframe), `spotlight` (one SVG + keyframe), `bento-grid` (plain grid), `infinite-moving-cards` (CSS marquee) can be ported to zero-JS Astro if the visual is ever eligible.

The Pro block taxonomy (hero, logo cloud, CTA, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, stats, team, footer) is a reasonable checklist of marketing section families, useful only as a naming cross-check for our 8 families.
Consistent component anatomy (Container/Body/Item compound components, `className` passthrough, `cn()`) so effects compose with shadcn.
weaknesses: Closed-source with a proprietary license: free items have no license file at all, and the Pro license forbids distributing the components or derivative component products; an agency pipeline that emits these components into many client sites is at best a grey area and cannot redistribute them in a versioned section library.

Motion/JS cost violates our budgets by construction: 169/284 items require `motion` (~40 kB gz), `sparkles` pulls tsparticles engine at 120 fps, `vortex`/`canvas-reveal`/`pixelated-canvas` run rAF canvas loops, `globe`/`3d-globe` need three.js + cobe/three-globe (WebGL), `background-beams` animates ~50 SVG paths forever on the main thread.

No reduced-motion handling in any sampled component (0/16), no poster/static fallback, no `visibility`-based pause when off-screen; hover-only interactions (3D card, direction-aware hover, glare) have no touch or keyboard equivalent.

Registry items omit `cssVars`/`tailwind`/`css`, so installs are incomplete (keyframes missing) and there is no token contract: colours are hard-coded palette classes and hex values, incompatible with design-system token selection.
Heavy blur stacking (`blur-3xl` layers, `backdrop-blur`, `mix-blend`) is GPU-expensive on mobile and is itself a slop signature.

The look is the AI-slop canon: beams, sparkles, lamp, aurora, meteors, spotlight, glowing borders, bento with skeletons, animated gradient text, typewriter/flip-words headlines, macbook-scroll mockups, globe; every one is a tier-1 ban candidate.
No versioning of items, no changelog per item, no semver; registry URL is `latest` only.
patterns_to_steal: Machine-readable slop-signature corpus from the public registry (item names, `animate-*` class names, `motion`/`three`/`tsparticles` dependency fingerprints, `conic-gradient`+`blur-3xl` stacks, `#ffaa40`/`#9c40ff` style gradient stops) → anti_slop tier-1 regex/token bans and tier-3 n-gram detector training negatives.

Pro block taxonomy (hero, logo cloud, bento, CTA, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, stats, team, footer, navbar) → sanity cross-check that our 8 section families cover the commercially expected set; nothing else.

CSS-only mechanisms behind `aurora-background`, `meteors`, `spotlight`, marquee (keyframe on `background-position`/`transform`, DOM duplication for seamless loops) → motion layer: if a texture/ambient background arrangement is ever eligible, implement it as a zero-JS Astro component with `prefers-reduced-motion` gating and a static poster, never import the item.
Compound-component anatomy with `className` passthrough (CardContainer/CardBody/CardItem) → renderer: our section arrangements should expose the same slot-based composition to the editor post-V1.
patterns_to_avoid: Installing any Aceternity item into generated client sites → proprietary license, no versioning, missing keyframes in registry items, and the visuals are the exact signatures the anti-slop gate exists to reject.

Ambient infinite animations (beams, sparkles, vortex, shooting stars, meteors, aurora) → permanent main-thread/GPU cost, no off-screen pause, no reduced-motion; breaks the 120 ms main-thread motion budget and the 'static poster fallback' rule.
WebGL/three.js decor (globe, 3d-globe, dither/cloud/spotlight shaders, 3D marquee) → we allow at most one WebGL section and only with a poster fallback; decorative globes are also a slop signature.
Pointer-tracked effects (3D card tilt, hero-highlight mask, wobble, glare, magnetic button, following pointer) → hover-only, no touch/keyboard parity, fail a11y expectations for marketing sites.

Headline gimmicks (typewriter, flip-words, text-generate blur-in per word, encrypted text, colourful text) → cliché and harmful to LCP/readability; our narrative/rhythm rules should forbid animated headlines entirely.
Hard-coded palette colours (cyan-500, indigo-500, hex stops) inside components → violates 'model selects a design_system_id, never emits a token'.
reusable_patterns: SlopSignatureCorpus: derive ban lists from the machine-readable catalogue of the most-copied effect library rather than from taste.
KeyframeOnlyAmbient: an ambient background as a single CSS keyframe on transform/background-position, gated by prefers-reduced-motion, with a static poster as the default.
SeamlessLoopByDuplication: duplicate the item list once and translate -50% for infinite marquees without JS timing.
SlotCompoundAnatomy: Container/Body/Item compound components with className passthrough for editor-friendly composition.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a dependency; use as a negative corpus. Do not install or port any item into the section library: the license is proprietary and forbids redistribution, items lack tokens/keyframes/versioning, 169/284 need framer-motion, and 0/16 sampled components honour reduced motion. Instead, scrape the public registry index once, and feed the item names, `animate-*` classes, dependency fingerprints and layered-blur/conic-gradient patterns into the anti-slop tier-1 ban list; ban outright: background beams, sparkles, lamp effect, aurora background, meteors, shooting stars, vortex, spotlight, glowing/moving/hover-border-gradient, 3D card/comet/glare tilt, globe (both), bento grid with skeletons, typewriter/flip-words/text-generate headlines, infinite moving cards logo clouds, macbook/iphone/ipad mockups, tracing beam, canvas reveal. Where a client design system legitimately calls for an ambient texture, author our own CSS-only arrangement with poster fallback.

status_note: active; motion@13.4.1 (Framer Motion renamed; `motion/react` = Framer Motion, `motion` = vanilla)
core_problem: One animation engine for React (declarative motion components, layout/shared-element animations, gestures) and vanilla JS (animate/scroll/inView), using a hybrid of WAAPI, native ScrollTimeline and a JS frameloop.
architecture: Yarn/Lerna/Turbo monorepo, packages: framer-motion (React code, re-exported as motion/react), motion (thin re-exports: src/index.ts = `export * from 'framer-motion/dom'`, src/mini.ts = 'framer-motion/dom/mini', plus react, react-m, react-mini, three, vgpu, animate-view entries), motion-dom (vanilla engine: animation/{JSAnimation, NativeAnimation, GroupAnimation}, waapi/supports, generators/{spring,keyframes}, frameloop batcher, gestures/{hover,press}, view/ (View Transitions API wrapper), resize/), motion-utils (easings, pure helpers). Vanilla API (framer-motion/src/dom.ts): animate() (animation/animate/index.ts: createScopedAnimate with {scope, reduceMotion, skipAnimations}; picks NativeAnimation (WAAPI) when supportsWaapi and keyframes are compositor-friendly, else JSAnimation), animateMini (waapi/animate-style.ts, pure WAAPI, exported as animate from motion/mini), scroll() (render/dom/scroll/index.ts: attachToFunction or attachToAnimation; uses native ScrollTimeline/ViewTimeline when can-use-native-timeline.ts says supportsScrollTimeline(), else a rAF-driven scrollInfo tracker with offset presets), inView() (render/dom/viewport/index.ts: IntersectionObserver wrapper with amount:'some'|'all'|number and margin, onStart may return onEnd), stagger, spring generator. React-only: motion.* components, layout/shared-element animation via projection tree (projection/, MeasureLayout.tsx), AnimatePresence, useReducedMotion (utils/reduced-motion/use-reduced-motion.ts: lazily initialises a matchMedia listener from motion-dom's prefersReducedMotion, returns a snapshot state) and MotionConfig reducedMotion:'user'|'always'|'never' (use-reduced-motion-config.ts). Size discipline: framer-motion/package.json bundlesize gates (motion component 34.9 kB, m 6 kB, dom-animation 17.85 kB, dom-max 29.8 kB, animate 19.1 kB, scroll 5.2 kB, waapi-animate 2.26 kB gz) enforced by dev/inc/bundlesize.mjs and rollup.size.config.mjs; motion-dom gates style-effect 2.9 kB, motion-value 1.9 kB. Repo has AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules and a plans/ folder (e.g. 035-bundle-size-budget-enforcement.md).
core_innovation: A hybrid engine that transparently chooses WAAPI/ScrollTimeline (compositor/off-main-thread) when the browser can, and falls back to a JS frameloop only when it must, behind one API for both vanilla and React.
strengths: Vanilla entry needs no React: measured esbuild tree-shaken (min/gz) inView 1.0 kB/0.6 kB, scroll 17.7 kB/7.2 kB, motion/mini animate 10.9 kB/4.4 kB, full animate 59.5 kB/22.1 kB, animate+inView+scroll+stagger 67.7 kB/25.1 kB, mini+inView+scroll 26.9 kB/10.5 kB - the cheapest credible motion stack for Astro islands.
scroll() uses native CSS ScrollTimeline where supported, so scroll-linked effects cost ~0 main-thread; inView is a 0.6 kB IntersectionObserver wrapper.
createScopedAnimate({reduceMotion, skipAnimations}) is a build-time hook: a reduced-motion profile can be compiled as a scoped animate whose reduceMotion:true collapses transforms to opacity-only.
Per-entry gzipped bundlesize budgets enforced in CI; the repo even has a written plan for budget enforcement.
MIT, very active (pushed 2026-09-22), used by Framer, Cursor, Linear, Figma sites.
View Transitions wrapper (motion-dom/src/view) offers a standards-based route for page/section transitions with no React.
weaknesses: Everything distinctive (layout animations, shared-element, AnimatePresence, drag, useReducedMotion hook, MotionConfig) is React-only (motion/react measured 126 kB/41.7 kB gz) - irrelevant for an Astro-first renderer that avoids React islands.

Full vanilla animate() is 22 kB gz because it pulls the JS keyframe resolver/spring; only motion/mini stays tiny, and mini cannot animate non-compositor values or independent transforms in older browsers.
No scroll pinning, scrub timeline with labels, text splitting, or FLIP for vanilla - the GSAP feature set that section arrangements (e.g. pinned comparison, line reveals) need is absent.
useReducedMotion snapshots on first render and does not update live (TODO in source); vanilla users must call initPrefersReducedMotion/prefersReducedMotion themselves.
Commercial Motion+ layer (examples, Cursor/Ticker APIs, 'AI skills') means the most polished patterns are paywalled and not in the repo; the vanilla docs are thinner than the React docs.
1.6 GB repo (yarn cache and dev fixtures committed); reading source requires targeted API reads.
patterns_to_steal: inView(el, onStart->onEnd, {amount, margin}) -> the single reveal primitive for the section library: assembly emits one inView per section with amount from composition.focal_weight; effect callbacks come from the effect registry -> motion / renderer.

can-use-native-timeline -> gate scroll-linked patterns on supportsScrollTimeline() at runtime and prefer CSS animation-timeline:scroll() emitted statically by Astro; JS scroll() only as fallback -> motion / renderer.
createScopedAnimate({reduceMotion, skipAnimations}) -> compile motion profile.reduced_motion_fallback in {'opacity_only','none'} to a scoped animate instance per page -> motion.
bundlesize per entry + rollup.size.config 'size-rollup-*' entries -> mirror for our effect registry: each pattern id declares max gz bytes; CI fails the anti-slop/QA gate if exceeded -> qa_gate.
MotionConfig reducedMotion:'user'|'always'|'never' tri-state -> adopt the same enum in the SiteDefinition motion profile (never 'never' for launch QA) -> design_system / a11y.
patterns_to_avoid: motion/react layout/shared-element animations -> require React islands and a projection tree; cost 40+ kB gz and hydrate whole sections; contradicts near-zero JS Astro.
AnimatePresence-style exit animations for marketing sections -> nothing exits on a static page; pure decoration.
Full `animate` from 'motion' for simple reveals -> 22 kB gz where motion/mini (4.4 kB) or CSS does the same.
Motion+ 'AI skills' / prompt-driven animation authoring -> model-written animation code violates 'selection not generation'.
reusable_patterns: HybridEngineSelection: pick native (WAAPI/ScrollTimeline) vs JS animation per keyframe set at runtime via feature detection.
ScopedAnimateFactory: an animate() factory closed over policy flags (reduceMotion, skipAnimations, scope) so callers cannot bypass them.
IntersectionRevealPrimitive: inView returning an optional onEnd, enabling enter/exit symmetry without state.
EntrySizeBudgetCI: rollup 'size-*' entries measured gzipped and compared to package.json maxSize.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (adopt the vanilla subset). Use `motion/mini` + `inView` (+ `scroll` only when a section needs JS scroll-linking) as the default lightweight tier (~10.5 kB gz measured) for the majority of section families whose motion is 'reveal once' or 'scroll-linked opacity/transform'; reserve GSAP for the small set of arrangements that need pinning, timelines or SplitText. Never ship motion/react. Copy the scoped-animate-with-policy and per-entry size-budget mechanisms into our effect registry.

status_note: maintenance mode: last version 5.13.0 (commit 2024-11-19), 857 open issues, no GitHub releases; the format's momentum moved to LottieFiles' dotLottie (@lottiefiles/dotlottie-web, Rust/WASM ThorVG renderer)
core_problem: Play Adobe After Effects compositions exported as Bodymovin JSON in the browser via SVG, canvas or hybrid HTML renderers, so designers ship motion without hand-coding it.
architecture: Rollup builds from player/js/modules/*.js entry files that register renderers/modifiers/effects into a singleton (renderersManager.registerRenderer, ShapeModifiers.registerModifier, registerEffect): full.js registers svg+canvas+html renderers, all shape modifiers, the expressions engine and SVG effects (lottie.min.js 305.7 kB / 76.6 kB gz); svg_light.js registers only SVGRenderer + shape modifiers, no expressions/effects (lottie_light.min.js 168.4 kB / 46.7 kB gz; esbuild import measured 49.1 kB gz); also lottie_svg, lottie_canvas, lottie_light_canvas, lottie_light_html and lottie_worker/canvas_worker builds (OffscreenCanvas in a worker). Runtime: AnimationManager keeps one requestAnimationFrame loop for all AnimationItems (resume() re-schedules while playingAnimationsNum>0 and not frozen); AnimationItem parses the JSON (dataManager.loadAnimation, optional autoloadSegments/progressiveLoad), builds an element tree (elements/, mask.js, EffectsManager) and renders per frame; SVGRendererBase creates the <svg> with preserveAspectRatio and clipPath; rendererSettings expose title/description (index.d.ts lines 105-108) which are written as <title>/<desc> for basic a11y. No prefers-reduced-motion handling anywhere in player/js; no IntersectionObserver pausing (offscreen animations keep ticking unless the page calls pause()). JSON schema is Bodymovin's; `.lottie` (dotLottie = zip of JSON + assets + manifest) is not supported by this repo - it needs @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web (0.80.0, MIT, WASM: measured index.js 165 kB/33 kB gz plus a WASM binary).
core_innovation: A faithful runtime reimplementation of After Effects' layer/shape/mask/expression model in JS so a designer-authored composition renders as live vector DOM.
strengths: Lets a curated, human-made illustration/icon system carry motion (authored in AE, checked into the asset library) - consistent with 'illustration systems are selected, not generated'.
SVG renderer output is real DOM: it scales, can be styled, and can carry <title>/<desc> via rendererSettings.
lottie_light removes expressions and effects (the parts that are slow and eval-like) and halves the size.
MIT; the Bodymovin JSON format is a de-facto standard with an open ecosystem (LottieFiles, dotLottie, ThorVG, Rive as a competitor).
weaknesses: Bundle cost: even lottie_light is ~47 kB gz (26% of the 180 kB budget) plus the JSON payloads (tens to hundreds of kB each) for what are usually decorative icon loops; dotlottie-web trades JS for a WASM binary and canvas (no DOM).

Main-thread cost: JS re-computes every layer every frame and mutates hundreds of SVG nodes; complex AE files (masks, mattes, repeaters) routinely blow a 120 ms budget and cause layout/paint storms - the worker build only helps canvas.
No reduced-motion support and no offscreen pausing built in; the pipeline must wrap it (matchMedia -> autoplay:false + goToAndStop, IntersectionObserver -> pause/play).
Maintenance risk: last code change 2024-11, 857 open issues, Airbnb's own attention is on native Lottie; the web ecosystem is moving to LottieFiles' dotLottie/ThorVG.

Lottie assets are the archetypal 'stock animated illustration' slop (generic blob people, floating icons, checkmark loops); free LottieFiles marketplace assets are exactly the generated/AI-ish look the art-direction layer forbids.
Expressions engine in the full build evaluates AE expression code (JS strings) at runtime - a security/perf smell for third-party JSON.
patterns_to_steal: Renderer/modifier/effect registration split into build entries (full vs svg_light) -> same idea for our effect registry: a 'light' motion runtime entry that excludes anything not in the pattern_allowlist -> motion / renderer.

rendererSettings.title/description a11y hooks -> if any Lottie asset is allowed, the art_direction asset record must carry alt text that is injected as <title>/<desc> and validated by the placeholder scan -> art_direction / qa_gate.
Single shared rAF loop with playingAnimationsNum gating (AnimationManager) -> our runtime should stop its ticker when no allowlisted animation is active -> motion.
patterns_to_avoid: Shipping lottie-web for hero illustrations or icon micro-animations -> 47-77 kB gz + JSON + per-frame DOM mutation for decoration; violates JS and main-thread budgets and reads as stock.
Full build with expressions -> runtime evaluation of AE expression code and largest bundle; never.
Autoplaying infinite loops (the LottieFiles default) -> infinite decorative motion is a WCAG 2.2.2 pause/stop issue and a slop idiom.
Sourcing assets from LottieFiles marketplace -> generic illustration style is precisely what the art-direction rule excludes; assets must be commissioned per illustration system.
reusable_patterns: BuildEntryFeatureRegistration: features registered into a singleton by separate entry modules so bundles are composed by entry, not flags.
SharedTickerWithActiveCount: one rAF loop that self-stops when the count of playing items reaches zero.
DesignerAuthoredMotionAsset: motion authored in a design tool and shipped as data, selected by id rather than generated.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for V1. Nothing in the eight section families requires AE-authored motion, and the cost (>=47 kB gz + JSON + main-thread SVG mutation, no reduced-motion support) fails both budgets. If an illustration system later includes authored micro-motion, prefer (a) static SVG with CSS keyframes on <=3 compositor properties, or (b) a pre-rendered poster + short WebM/AVIF sequence, or (c) dotlottie-web canvas in a client:visible island with matchMedia-gated autoplay - as an art-direction asset selected by id, never a stock LottieFiles file.

status_note: active but slow; npm latest 10.1.2, 11.0.0-beta.0 published 2026-06-21; default branch 'next'; 76 open issues
core_problem: Spring-physics-first animation for React (and react-three-fiber) where values are driven by mass/tension/friction rather than durations, with interruptible, velocity-preserving transitions.
architecture: pnpm/Turbo monorepo. packages/core (Controller, SpringValue, FrameValue, Interpolation, hooks useSpring/useSprings/useTrail/useTransition/useChain, SpringContext), packages/animated (animated() HOC wrapping host elements and applying values without React re-renders), packages/shared (globals.ts with assign({skipAnimation, frameLoop, requestAnimationFrame, onDemand}), fluids, hooks/useReducedMotion.ts), packages/rafz (frameloop scheduler with demand mode), packages/parallax, packages/types; targets/web (@react-spring/web 11.0.0-beta.0, ESM-only, peer react 16.8-19) and targets/three. useReducedMotion (shared/src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts) listens to matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion)') and calls Globals.assign({skipAnimation: matches}) so every Controller/SpringValue jumps to goal values. All animation runs in a JS frameloop (rafz) on the main thread - no WAAPI path. Repo carries .specify/specs (spec-kit) and CLAUDE.md.
core_innovation: Springs as the default primitive with velocity carry-over between interruptions, and an animated() binding that writes styles outside React's render cycle.
strengths: Best-in-class spring semantics (interruptible, velocity-preserving) for stateful UI interactions.
Global skipAnimation switch wired to prefers-reduced-motion is a clean single point of control (Globals.assign).
rafz 'onDemand' frameloop lets a host drive frames (r3f) - a good pattern for a single shared ticker.
MIT; @react-spring/web measured 42.7 kB/17.2 kB gz (esbuild, React external).
weaknesses: React-only (hooks + animated components); no vanilla entry - unusable from Astro without hydrating a React island per animated section.
Pure JS frameloop on the main thread (no WAAPI), so cost scales with number of springs and directly eats the 120 ms main-thread budget.

Springs target interaction-heavy app UI (drawers, drag, lists); marketing-site motion is mostly scroll-reveal and timeline choreography, which react-spring handles poorly (no scroll trigger/pin, no timeline labels).
Slow cadence: v10 took 7 months from 9.7.5 (2024-10) to 10.0.0 (2025-05); v11 has been in beta since 2026-06.
useReducedMotion returns null on first render (SSR), so reduced-motion is only honoured after hydration.
patterns_to_steal: Globals.assign({skipAnimation}) wired to prefers-reduced-motion -> a single process-wide 'motion kill switch' flag in our runtime that every allowlisted effect must consult; test it in the Playwright QA run by emulating reduced motion -> motion / qa_gate.
Spring config presets (default/gentle/wobbly/stiff/slow/molasses named configs) -> if any spring is ever allowlisted, expose only named presets, never raw tension/friction -> design_system / motion.
patterns_to_avoid: React-hook-driven animation for static marketing sections -> forces React islands, hydration cost, and per-section JS; contradicts near-zero-JS Astro.
useTrail/useTransition list choreography -> the 'staggered cards springing in' idiom is generic AI/SaaS-template slop.
@react-spring/three for hero 3D -> violates the <=1 WebGL section / poster-fallback rule unless strictly gated.
reusable_patterns: GlobalSkipAnimation: one mutable global consulted by every animation controller to jump to goal state.
OutOfRenderStyleWrite: animated() applies interpolated values directly to DOM nodes, bypassing React reconciliation.
DemandFrameloop: frameloop that only schedules rAF when work is pending and can defer to a host clock.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for V1. The stack is Astro with near-zero JS; react-spring requires React islands and a main-thread frameloop and offers nothing for scroll choreography. Revisit only for the post-V1 visual editor UI (React app chrome), where spring interactions are appropriate - not for shipped sites.
