status_note: active; v3.15.0; owned by Webflow since fall 2024; all plugins free since 2025-04-30
core_problem: Framework-agnostic, high-precision property tweening with a robust timeline/sequencing model plus a plugin ecosystem (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip, ScrollSmoother) that papers over browser inconsistencies.
architecture: Single ESM/UMD package with no runtime deps. src/gsap-core.js (3,255 lines) holds the Animation base class, Tween, Timeline (nested timelines, position parameters, labels), the rAF _ticker with lagSmoothing(threshold=500ms, adjustedLag=33ms), PropTween linked lists, ease parser, utils (interpolate, mapRange, snap, pipe) and the plugin registry. Plugins are objects passed to gsap.registerPlugin() and normalized by _createPlugin into {init, render, add, kill, modifier, rawVars} + statics {targetTest, get, getSetter, aliases, register}; Tween init consults _plugins[property] for every vars key so a plugin is just a property handler (CSSPlugin is itself a plugin registered in esm/index.js). gsap.registerEffect({name, effect, plugins, defaults, extendTimeline}) registers reusable named effects that become Timeline methods. Context (gsap.context) records every tween/ScrollTrigger created inside a function so it can be revert()ed; MatchMedia extends Context: mm.add({key:'(min-width: 800px)', reduce:'(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'}, (ctx)=>{...}) creates a Context per condition set, registers MediaQueryList change listeners, and on change kill(revert=true) reverts all recorded tweens in reverse globalTime order then re-runs the setup. ScrollTrigger.js (1,790 lines): per-trigger start/end computed on refresh(), scroll position cached via Observer's _scrollCacheFunc (reads scrollTop only after a scroll event to avoid layout thrash), update() clamps progress and drives either toggleActions (play/pause/resume/reverse/restart/reset/complete/none for enter/leave/enterBack/leaveBack) or a scrub tween; pin via position:fixed or transform with pinSpacing; ScrollTrigger.batch() groups triggers (the classic stagger-reveal API); ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll() intercepts wheel/touch to drive scroll from JS; ScrollTrigger.matchMedia is deprecated in favour of gsap.matchMedia. SplitText.ts (517 lines, rewritten 2025, TypeScript): splits with Intl.Segmenter, options aria:'auto'|'hidden'|'none' (auto sets aria-label on parent and aria-hidden on fragments, reverting on revert()), deepSlice for nested inline elements, autoSplit on resize/font load, mask:'lines'|'words'|'chars', propIndex CSS vars. Flip.js: getState() snapshots bounds/props, from()/to() compute FLIP deltas, absolute/nested/scale modes. ScrollSmoother.js: wraps content in .ScrollSmoother-wrapper and sets matrix3d transform on content each tick (native scrollbar preserved), data-speed/data-lag parallax effects via _transformPosition. Observer.js normalizes wheel/touch/pointer/scroll. TypeScript types shipped in types/.
core_innovation: A property-agnostic tweening core where every animatable key is resolved through a plugin registry, plus gsap.matchMedia()/Context giving deterministic create-and-revert of whole animation sets keyed on media queries (including prefers-reduced-motion).
strengths: Framework-agnostic ESM with sideEffects:false and per-plugin entry points (gsap/ScrollTrigger etc.) - fits Astro <script> islands or plain module scripts with zero React.

Measured tree-shaken cost (esbuild, min/gzip): core+CSSPlugin 71.7 kB/28.5 kB; core+ScrollTrigger 116.7 kB/46.5 kB; +SplitText 124.2 kB/49.5 kB. Individual dist mins: ScrollTrigger 18.0 kB gz, SplitText 3.7 kB gz, Flip 9.7 kB gz, ScrollSmoother 5.6 kB gz.

gsap.matchMedia() is exactly the shape of a compiled 'motion profile': a map of named media conditions to setup functions with automatic revert - reduced-motion becomes a first-class branch, not an afterthought.
ScrollTrigger is the most battle-tested scroll model (pinning, scrub, snap, batch, containerAnimation, refresh on resize/font load, limitCallbacks on startup).
SplitText 2025 rewrite bakes in a11y (aria-label/aria-hidden handling), Intl.Segmenter grapheme splitting, and autoSplit responsive reflow - solves the most common text-reveal accessibility bug.
gsap.registerEffect() is a native mechanism for a fixed, named, parameter-constrained effect vocabulary - maps directly to a pattern_allowlist.
Now free for commercial use including all former Club plugins; AI-generated GSAP code explicitly permitted.
weaknesses: Not open source: proprietary no-charge license controlled by Webflow; no LICENSE file in the repo; terms can change. Our product (an autonomous agency that emits sites) is a 'Permitted Use' as long as it is not marketed as a visual/no-code animation builder - but the planned post-V1 visual editor must not become a Webflow-Interactions-like animation builder or it risks the 'Prohibited Uses' clause.

Heavy for our 180 kB total JS budget: core+ScrollTrigger alone is ~46.5 kB gz (~26% of budget) before any page code; there is no WAAPI/compositor path - every tween runs on the main thread via rAF, so density must be capped.
Core is a single 3,255-line JS file with a custom object model (linked lists, _gsap cache on elements); not hackable, no source-level type safety (types are hand-maintained .d.ts).

ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll and ScrollSmoother hijack native scroll (wheel/touch interception, transform-based scroll) - conflicts with the a11y stance and with position:sticky/anchors; ScrollSmoother is the AI-slop 'luxury scroll' signature.
The library is what powers the generic 'everything reveals on scroll' aesthetic; the defaults (ScrollTrigger.batch + fade-up) are the slop pattern unless the vocabulary is constrained upstream.
Effects/plugins register globally (gsap.registerPlugin mutates a module singleton) - multiple islands must share one bundle instance.
patterns_to_steal: gsap.matchMedia({reduce:'(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)', motion:'(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)'}) + Context.revert -> the compile target for motion profile.reduced_motion_fallback: assembly emits one mm.add() block per profile branch; static-poster fallback lives in the 'reduce' branch -> motion / renderer.

registerEffect({name, effect, defaults, plugins}) -> implement the motion profile's pattern_allowlist as a fixed registry of ~10 named effects (e.g. 'reveal-lines', 'counter', 'flip-reorder') whose parameter ranges are validated by Zod at build time; the model only selects effect ids -> motion / anti_slop.
ScrollTrigger toggleActions string grammar ('play none none reverse') -> a 4-slot enum in the section variant motion schema instead of free-form callbacks -> design_system / motion.

SplitText aria:'auto' semantics (aria-label on parent, aria-hidden fragments, revert restores) -> make this a hard requirement in the a11y gate for any text-split arrangement; axe-core check that split headings still expose text -> qa_gate.
ScrollTrigger.batch(interval, batchMax) -> derive density from the section's composition.density: batchMax bounds simultaneous tweens, which is how budget_ms compiles to a concrete cap -> motion.
_ticker.lagSmoothing(500, 33) -> in the Lighthouse/Playwright QA run, record long tasks during scroll and fail if main-thread animation time exceeds the 120 ms budget -> qa_gate.
patterns_to_avoid: ScrollSmoother / ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll -> scroll hijacking: breaks native scroll semantics, sticky, iframe, keyboard expectations; also the canonical agency-slop signature. Never in the allowlist.

gsap.matchMedia as the only reduced-motion mechanism -> still requires JS to load; the CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion) poster fallback must be in the Astro-rendered HTML so a11y holds if JS fails.
MorphSVG / MotionPath / Physics plugins -> decorative motion that inflates budget and reads as generated; no section family needs them.
Loading gsap/all (833 kB, 186 kB gz) or the CDN UMD bundle -> destroys the 180 kB budget; always per-plugin ESM imports.
Letting the model write GSAP code -> violates 'model selects, code computes'; GSAP calls must be generated from a typed effect registry.
reusable_patterns: MediaQueryScopedContext: an animation context created per media condition set that records all created animations and can revert them deterministically when the condition changes.
PropertyPluginRegistry: every animatable key resolved via a registry of {init, render, kill} handlers, so new targets extend the engine without touching the core loop.
NamedEffectRegistry: registerEffect(name, defaults, requiredPlugins) turns ad-hoc tweens into a closed, parameterized vocabulary.
ToggleActionGrammar: a 4-slot enter/leave/enterBack/leaveBack action string as the entire behaviour spec for a scroll-bound animation.
CachedScrollRead: read scrollTop only after a scroll event fires (cache id bump) to avoid forced layout on every tick.
AccessibleTextSplit: keep aria-label on the container, aria-hidden on fragments, and restore DOM on revert.
adoption_strategy: Adopt (as the vanilla motion runtime, wrapped). Use gsap core + ScrollTrigger + SplitText (~49.5 kB gz measured) behind a tiny typed 'effect registry' module of our own; the SiteDefinition motion block carries only effect ids and bounded params, and assembly compiles them to gsap.registerEffect calls inside a gsap.matchMedia() block whose 'reduce' branch renders the static poster state. Load it as one Astro client:visible island script so pages with no motion ship zero GSAP. Explicitly exclude ScrollSmoother, normalizeScroll, MorphSVG and Physics plugins from the allowlist. Legal note for the manifest: proprietary no-charge license, Webflow-owned; permitted for site output, but the post-V1 visual editor must not expose a no-code animation builder on top of GSAP.

status_note: active; v1.3.26; V2-ROADMAP.md published (defaults flip to 'bulletproof by default')
core_problem: Smooth (lerped) scrolling that stays on the native scroll position so WebGL/DOM scroll scenes can be synchronised from one loop - smooth scroll itself was, per MANIFESTO.md, a side effect.
architecture: Bun workspace; packages/core/src: lenis.ts (1,211 lines, class Lenis), virtual-scroll.ts (wheel/touch listeners registered with {passive:false}; deltaMode line/page multipliers; touch delta tracking), animate.ts (Animate.advance(dt): duration+easing or exponential damp(value, to, lerp*60, dt)), dimensions.ts (ResizeObserver or naive scrollHeight), emitter.ts; packages/react (ReactLenis provider creating the instance in useEffect with its own rAF when autoRaf, useLenis(callback, deps, priority) via a Store fallback), packages/vue (+nuxt module), packages/snap. Runtime: VirtualScroll emits deltas -> onVirtualScroll (lenis.ts 437-600) walks event.composedPath() for data-lenis-prevent*/prevent()/allowNestedScroll, then event.preventDefault()s the wheel/touch event and calls scrollTo(targetScroll+delta,{programmatic:false, lerp|duration/easing}); raf(time) advances Animate and setScroll() writes wrapper.scrollTo({behavior:'instant'}) so the real scroll position (and therefore sticky, anchors, scrollbar, find-in-page) remains native. Keyboard, scrollbar drag and browser-initiated scrolls are NOT intercepted: onNativeScroll (614-646) detects them, syncs animatedScroll=targetScroll=actualScroll and marks isScrolling='native'. Reduced motion: reducedMotionMediaQuery = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') read live at scroll time; in scrollTo(), if prefersReducedMotion then programmatic scrolls become immediate and gesture scrolls get lerp=1 (1:1 tracking) - respectReducedMotion:true by default (lines 39, 755-764, 1177-1180). Anchors: with anchors:true a click handler intercepts <a href='#'> and calls scrollTo honouring scroll-margin/scroll-padding CSS. lenis.css sets overscroll-behavior:contain on prevent regions and pointer-events:none on iframes while smooth. Build: tsdown ESM + IIFE; measured lenis.min.js 18.7 kB/5.4 kB gz, lenis-react.mjs 1.7 kB gz, esbuild tree-shaken 5.6 kB gz.
core_innovation: Lerp the wheel/touch input into the native scroll position (not a transformed container), so smooth scroll and WebGL sync coexist with native sticky/anchors/scrollbar/keyboard behaviour.
strengths: Tiny (5.4 kB gz) and dependency-free; framework-agnostic core with thin React/Vue bindings.

Correct architectural choice versus ScrollSmoother/Locomotive: writes to the real scroll position, so position:sticky, keyboard scrolling, scrollbar dragging, find-in-page and anchors keep working (keyboard/scrollbar are never intercepted - onNativeScroll just re-syncs).

Reduced motion honoured by default and read live (no listener needed): programmatic scrolls jump, gesture scrolls track 1:1, while the raf loop keeps running so any WebGL sync remains consistent - this is the most careful reduced-motion implementation of the six repos.
scrollTo respects CSS scroll-margin/scroll-padding on targets; data-lenis-prevent attributes and prevent() give escape hatches for modals/nested scroll.
V2 roadmap makes safe behaviour default (autoToggle, anchors, allowNestedScroll, stopInertiaOnNavigate) and acknowledges AI/no-code users as the main audience.
weaknesses: It is still scroll hijacking: wheel and touch events are preventDefault()ed on non-passive listeners (virtual-scroll.ts listenerOptions {passive:false}), which is a Lighthouse best-practice hit, adds per-event main-thread work, breaks iframe scrolling, disables CSS scroll-snap (needs lenis/snap), caps at 60fps on Safari, and can fight OS-level inertia on trackpads.
The lag between input and viewport is a vestibular/WCAG 2.3.3 concern for users who have not set prefers-reduced-motion; the a11y guarantee depends on the OS flag.
Requires a permanent rAF loop (autoRaf) even when idle - Animate.advance is cheap but non-zero; with ScrollTrigger integration it also forces gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0).

Smooth scroll is now a recognised 'awwwards-agency / AI-generated portfolio' signature in 2025-26; it signals template motion rather than brand identity and is the opposite of the constraint principle.
allowNestedScroll walks the DOM on every gesture (README warns of perf cost); syncTouch on iOS <16 is flaky; touch smoothing is off by default so mobile and desktop feel different.
No tests directory in the repo; behaviour is validated via playground apps.
patterns_to_steal: Live-read prefersReducedMotion with a tri-mode policy (programmatic->immediate, gesture->1:1, loop keeps running) -> adopt as the semantic definition of reduced_motion_fallback for any scroll-linked effect in the motion profile -> motion / a11y.

onNativeScroll re-sync (never intercept keyboard/scrollbar; reconcile state from actualScroll) -> any custom scroll-linked runtime we ship must treat native scroll as the source of truth -> renderer / motion.

scroll-margin/scroll-padding-aware scrollTo -> our anchor navigation (sticky header offsets) should read CSS scroll-margin-top instead of hardcoded offsets, and ideally use native scroll-behavior:smooth -> renderer.
data-lenis-prevent attribute grammar -> an attribute-level opt-out convention for motion (e.g. data-motion='none') that arrangements can set on scroll regions/modals -> design_system.
V2 'bulletproof defaults' table -> our motion profile should ship with the conservative branch as default and require explicit opt-in for anything denser -> motion / anti_slop.
patterns_to_avoid: Smooth/lerped scrolling on the whole page -> wheel/touch preventDefault, main-thread per-event work, iframe/scroll-snap breakage, and a slop signature; put 'smooth_scroll' on the tier-1 anti-slop ban list unless a niche playbook explicitly allows it for a <=1-WebGL-section luxury archetype.
lenis/snap -> re-implements CSS scroll-snap in JS; use native scroll-snap.
ReactLenis provider wrapping the whole page -> forces a React root around all content; incompatible with Astro islands.
GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis coupling (lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update) + lagSmoothing(0)) -> two scroll models fighting; if we ship GSAP, native scroll is enough.
reusable_patterns: NativePositionSmoothing: interpolate input into the real scroll position rather than transforming a container, preserving native scroll semantics.
LiveReducedMotionPolicy: read matchMedia.matches at action time and map (programmatic->instant, gesture->1:1, loop->keep running).
NativeScrollReconcile: treat un-intercepted native scroll events as truth and re-sync internal targets from them.
AttributeOptOutGrammar: data-* attributes on subtree roots to exclude regions from a global behaviour.
SafeDefaultsFlip: version-major that inverts opt-in safety flags to opt-out.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a shipped dependency; adapt its reduced-motion policy. Smooth scroll fails the architect's a11y stance (non-passive wheel/touch interception, vestibular risk) and is itself a slop signature in 2026, so 'smooth_scroll' goes on the anti-slop ban list. If a luxury archetype ever needs WebGL-DOM sync, Lenis (5 kB, MIT) is the only defensible option and its reduced-motion behaviour should be required verbatim - but that is a post-V1 playbook decision, gated by budget_ms.

status_note: ARCHIVED (read-only). Motion One (motion@10.x) was merged into motiondivision/motion; the vanilla `motion` package (v11+, now v13.4.1) and `motion/mini` are its successors.
core_problem: A tiny animation library that drives the browser's Web Animations API (WAAPI) directly so transforms/opacity run off the main thread, with a minimal polyfill for what WAAPI lacks.
architecture: Lerna/Turbo monorepo: @motionone/animation (minimal WAAPI polyfill/JS fallback), @motionone/dom (animate, timeline, scroll, inView, resize, spring/glide via @motionone/generators), @motionone/easing, @motionone/types, @motionone/utils, and the umbrella `motion` package (v10.18.0) that re-exports dom + animation. packages/dom/package.json carried a bundlesize gate: animate 4.1 kB, animateStyle 3.4 kB, timeline 4.82 kB, spring 1.5 kB, inView 0.45 kB, scroll 2.51 kB (gzipped). inView() wrapped IntersectionObserver; scroll() tracked scroll position with a lightweight rAF-on-scroll approach. Thin @motionone/react/solid/vue wrappers existed and were later dropped.
core_innovation: Treat WAAPI as the engine and ship only the delta the browser is missing, giving a ~4 kB animate() with compositor-thread transforms.
strengths: Proved the WAAPI-first approach (compositor-run opacity/transform, near-zero main-thread cost) at ~4 kB - the model that `motion/mini` (measured 4.4 kB gz) still implements.
Per-feature bundlesize budgets in package.json as a CI gate - the same discipline our 180 kB budget needs.
MIT.
weaknesses: Archived; no fixes since 2024-11; 66 open issues frozen.

Its successor's default `animate()` (from 'motion') is no longer tiny (measured 22 kB gz) because the hybrid engine merged in Framer Motion's JS spring/keyframe resolver; only `motion/mini` keeps the Motion One footprint.
WAAPI cannot animate layout, SVG path data or non-CSS values natively; the JS fallback was limited.
patterns_to_steal: Per-entry bundlesize maxSize map in package.json -> add a size-limit gate per motion effect bundle in our CI so each allowlisted pattern has a declared byte cost -> qa_gate / motion.

WAAPI-first: only animate opacity/transform/clip-path so animations are compositor-threaded -> hard rule in the motion profile: allowlisted patterns may only touch compositor properties -> anti_slop / motion.
patterns_to_avoid: Depending on the archived motion@10 packages -> unmaintained; use `motion/mini` instead.
reusable_patterns: PlatformFirstPolyfill: use the native API (WAAPI) as the engine and ship only the missing capabilities.
SizeBudgetPerEntry: each public entry point has a gzipped byte ceiling enforced in CI.
adoption_strategy: Ignore (archived). Its ideas survive in `motion/mini`; evaluate that under motiondivision/motion. Keep the per-entry bundlesize gate idea.

status_note: active; r186 (0.186.0), monthly releases, dev branch; WebGPU renderer shipped as a parallel entry point
core_problem: General-purpose 3D scene graph, materials, loaders and renderers (WebGL2 and WebGPU) for the browser.
architecture: ESM source under src/ (core, math, materials, geometries, lights, loaders, textures, objects, renderers/{webgl,webgpu,common,webxr,shaders}, nodes/ with 239 files for the TSL node material system). Build entries in utils/build/rollup.config.js produce build/three.module.js (src/Three.js, classic WebGL), build/three.webgpu.js (src/Three.WebGPU.js), build/three.tsl.js and three.core.js; package.json exports map '.', './webgpu', './tsl', './addons/*' (= examples/jsm/*, 560 files: controls, loaders, postprocessing, environments, etc.), './src/*'. sideEffects is limited to ./src/nodes/**/* so the classic path is tree-shakeable in principle, but WebGLRenderer transitively imports the entire shader-chunk library, program cache, state, extensions, shadow map, cube/PMREM machinery and all built-in materials' uniforms, so the practical floor is large. src/renderers/webgpu/WebGPURenderer.js extends a common Renderer and picks WebGPUBackend when navigator.gpu exists or WebGLBackend (webgl-fallback) otherwise, with a forceWebGL parameter; materials on that path are Node materials (TSL). Addons model: examples/jsm is published but not part of the core API contract; three-stdlib exists because addons are not typed/tree-shaken as carefully. A repo-root llms.txt points to https://threejs.org/docs/llms.txt. AI wiring: none beyond llms.txt.
core_innovation: A single scene-graph/material model that now compiles to both WebGL2 and WebGPU through a node-based shader language (TSL), while keeping the classic renderer as the default entry.
strengths: De-facto standard: every loader, exporter and tool (Blender glTF, gltfjsx, Spline, Theatre r3f) targets it; skills are abundant.
Exports map cleanly separates classic ('three'), WebGPU ('three/webgpu') and TSL ('three/tsl') entry points, and addons are opt-in per file.
WebGPURenderer has an automatic WebGL2 backend fallback so one code path covers both APIs.
Excellent for build-time use: headless rendering (puppeteer/playwright) can bake posters, sprite sheets or WebM loops from a scene with zero runtime cost.
MIT, monthly releases, huge test/example corpus; PMREM/RoomEnvironment give studio lighting without external HDR files.
weaknesses: Measured floor for a one-mesh WebGL scene: esbuild 519.5 kB min / 130.4 kB gzip / 107.8 kB brotli; rollup+terser with aggressive treeshake 508.4 kB min / 122.9 kB gzip / 100.3 kB brotli. MeshBasic vs MeshStandard changes it by <1%: the cost is WebGLRenderer itself, not materials.

The 140 kB hard ceiling is not achievable with three.js if measured minified (floor is 3.6x over); if measured as gzip transfer it leaves 10-17 kB for the entire island logic, poster swap, intersection code and assets, and consumes ~70% of the 180 kB page budget.
Hero-typical extras raise it further: GLTFLoader + RoomEnvironment + PMREM = 604 kB min / 153 kB gzip measured; WebGPU entry with one node material = 772 kB min / 212 kB gzip.
No visibility/intersection/reduced-motion awareness: setAnimationLoop keeps rendering until you stop it; nothing checks prefers-reduced-motion or document.hidden.

First render compiles GLSL programs on the main thread (tens of ms desktop, order of 100-300 ms on mid-range phones for a PBR material with shadows/env), which lands exactly where INP is measured unless warmed before reveal.
Continuous rendering at devicePixelRatio 3 on phones is a battery and thermal cost; the library gives no defaults for dpr caps, so budgets must be enforced by our code.
examples/jsm addons are unversioned relative to the API contract (breaking changes each release), hence three-stdlib forks; adds maintenance drag.
patterns_to_steal: Entry-point split ('three' vs 'three/webgpu' vs 'three/tsl' in package.json exports) -> our section library: motion capability tiers as separate entry points so a section imports only the runtime it declares.
WebGPURenderer backend selection with getFallback -> renderer capability ladder for the WebGL island: try tier N, fall back deterministically, record which tier mounted in telemetry.
Build-time headless rendering (three + Playwright) -> art_direction/no_photo_fallback: bake abstract posters and 3-6 s WebM/AV1 loops from a parametrised scene at library time; runtime cost 0 kB JS.
PMREM + RoomEnvironment (no external HDR) -> if a WebGL section ever ships with three.js, lighting must come from generated environments, never remote HDRs.
patterns_to_avoid: three.js as a runtime dependency of any V1 section -> 123-131 kB gzip / 508+ kB min floor breaks the 140 kB section ceiling and eats most of the 180 kB page budget.
WebGPU renderer path -> 212 kB gzip and only useful for effects that would look out of place on a service business site; not for V1.
examples/jsm addons in production without pinning -> API churn every monthly release.
setAnimationLoop without intersection + visibilitychange + reduced-motion gates -> continuous GPU work offscreen.
reusable_patterns: CapabilityEntryPoints: ship separate package entries per rendering capability so consumers pay only for the tier they import.
BackendLadder: try the preferred backend, fall back deterministically, expose which one was chosen.
BakeAtLibraryTime: use the heavy 3D engine offline to produce static/video assets that ship with zero runtime JS.
SelfContainedLighting: generated environment maps (PMREM of a procedural room) instead of downloaded HDRs.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a runtime dependency; use only as a build-time tool. Answering the architect directly: the 140 kB ceiling is not achievable with three.js (measured floor 508 kB min / 123 kB gzip / 100 kB brotli before any scene code), so the <=1 WebGL section must be built on OGL (measured 47 kB min / 14 kB gzip / 12 kB brotli for a lit sphere) or raw WebGL (a fragment-shader plane is <10 kB), lazy-mounted on intersection behind a real rendered poster, with prefers-reduced-motion resolving to the poster only. For most design systems the better move is no WebGL at all: a pre-rendered WebM/AV1 loop (baked with three.js headless) or CSS 3D/SVG, which cost 0 kB JS and decode on the GPU. Reserve live WebGL as a signature move for `technical` and `cinematic` design systems with premium/challenger/luxury positioning; never for local_trust or volume_value.

status_note: active; v9.8.0 pairs with React 19 only (peer react >=19 <19.4, three >=0.156)
core_problem: Expresses a three.js scene graph as React components via a custom react-reconciler, so scene state participates in React state, Suspense and concurrent scheduling instead of imperative mutation.
architecture: packages/fiber/src/core/reconciler.tsx is a react-reconciler host config that maps JSX tags (<mesh>) to `new THREE.Mesh()` via a catalogue built by extend(); web/Canvas.tsx calls extend(THREE) on the whole namespace, measures its container with react-use-measure, creates a root with createRoot(canvas).configure({gl,dpr,frameloop,performance,...}) and renders children inside its own ErrorBoundary + Suspense, with a `fallback` prop for no-WebGL. core/store.ts is a zustand store (RootState) holding gl/scene/camera/size/viewport, `frameloop: 'always'|'demand'|'never'`, `dpr` (number or [min,max] clamped by calculateDpr against window.devicePixelRatio) and a `performance` object {current,min:0.5,max:1,debounce:200,regress()} where regress() drops current to min and a setTimeout restores max after debounce ms. core/loop.ts is one shared requestAnimationFrame loop over all roots: update() runs useFrame subscribers then gl.render, decrements state.internal.frames, and the loop cancels itself when no root has frames left; invalidate(state, frames) sets frames=1 (or 2 when called inside useFrame) and restarts the loop; advance() drives frameloop='never' manually; addEffect/addAfterEffect/addTail are global before/after/idle hooks. core/events.ts does raycast-based pointer events. AI wiring: none.
core_innovation: A React reconciler whose render loop is demand-driven by a per-root frame counter, letting a declarative 3D tree go completely idle when nothing invalidates it.
strengths: frameloop='demand' + invalidate() is a clean idle-by-default model: the rAF loop is cancelled when repeat===0 (loop.ts), so a settled scene costs zero CPU/GPU.

performance.regress() with debounce (store.ts) is a tiny, general 'quality governor' contract: producers call regress(), consumers read performance.current and scale dpr/effects; nothing happens unless a consumer opts in.
dpr=[min,max] clamp (calculateDpr) is the right default for phones with devicePixelRatio 3.
Canvas `fallback` prop and ErrorBoundary wrap give a defined no-WebGL path.
docs/advanced/scaling-performance.mdx documents movement regression, instancing, LOD (<Detailed>), nested Suspense loading: a good checklist for our motion budget rules.
Actively maintained, MIT, large ecosystem.
weaknesses: Measured cost (esbuild, minified, production): a Canvas with one lit icosahedron = 1119 kB min / 309 kB gzip / 248 kB brotli. The total site JS budget is 180 kB; this single island is 1.7x that.

web/Canvas.tsx calls extend(THREE as any) on the full namespace, so three.js cannot be tree-shaken at all in the default path (719 kB min); you would need createRoot + a hand-built catalogue to get back to the ~508 kB three floor.
Requires react + react-dom/client in the island (~45 kB gzip on their own) and a React-19-exact peer range; an Astro island with r3f is the heaviest island type we could ship.

No prefers-reduced-motion handling anywhere in loop.ts/Canvas.tsx; frameloop='always' is the default and keeps rendering offscreen and in background tabs (no IntersectionObserver or visibilitychange gating).
First frame still pays WebGLRenderer construction + shader compile on the main thread (no built-in warm-up; drei's Preload does gl.compile).
Event system raycasts on every pointermove by default; on a marketing page this is wasted main-thread work.
patterns_to_steal: Demand-driven frame counter (loop.ts invalidate/frames/cancelAnimationFrame) -> motion runtime for our single WebGL island: render only when a scroll/intersection/pointer event invalidates; go idle otherwise.
performance.regress()/current/debounce contract (store.ts) -> motion budget: our island exposes one `quality` number that dpr, particle count and effects derive from; scroll/resize call regress().
dpr=[min,max] clamp (calculateDpr) -> renderer config: hard-cap dpr at 1.5 on mobile, 2 on desktop, as a design-system motion token.
Canvas `fallback` + ErrorBoundary -> lazy-mount pattern: the static poster is the fallback and stays in the DOM until the first frame has rendered.
addTail (callback when rendering stops) -> telemetry: record idle/active ratio of the WebGL section as a motion-budget metric.
patterns_to_avoid: Shipping React + r3f as an Astro island -> 309 kB gzip measured minimum breaks the 180 kB total JS budget and the 140 kB section ceiling on its own.
extend(THREE) whole-namespace catalogue -> defeats tree-shaking; any renderer we write must import only the classes it uses.
frameloop='always' default -> continuous rAF at device dpr is the battery drain the architect's motion budget forbids.
Raycast pointer events on the scene -> hover-reactive 3D on a marketing site is an AI-slop tell and costs main thread per pointermove.
reusable_patterns: DemandFrameLoop: a rAF loop that keeps a per-root pending-frame counter, renders while >0, and cancels itself at 0; producers call invalidate().
QualityGovernor: a single normalized `current` in [min,max] that regress() drops and a debounced timer restores; consumers derive dpr/effects from it.
ClampedDpr: dpr resolved as clamp(devicePixelRatio, min, max) from a token, never raw devicePixelRatio.
PosterFallbackSlot: the static poster is the canvas's declared fallback and is only swapped out after the first rendered frame or on GL failure.
adoption_strategy: Adapt — do not ship the library. Re-implement DemandFrameLoop, QualityGovernor and ClampedDpr (together under 150 lines of TypeScript) inside our own vanilla WebGL/OGL island so the <=1 WebGL section is idle-by-default and dpr-capped. Keep r3f only as a reference for the docs/advanced/scaling-performance.mdx checklist when writing motion-budget rules. If a design system ever justifies a React 3D island, it must use createRoot with a minimal catalogue, not <Canvas>, and still cannot meet 140 kB with three.js.

status_note: stalled in public: README says development of 1.0 moved to a private repo 'temporarily'; no public push for 25 months; npm @theatre/core 0.7.x
core_problem: Author high-fidelity keyframe animation in a browser GUI (studio) and play it back deterministically from exported JSON state via a small runtime (core), for DOM, SVG, three.js or anything with numeric props.
architecture: Monorepo packages/: core (52 src files, dep only @theatre/dataverse, a reactive 'prism' system), studio (362 src files, the GUI), react, r3f, theatric, dataverse, saaz (sync/CRDT experiments), sync-server. Data model (packages/core/src/types/private/core.ts and types/public.ts): ProjectState_Historic {sheetsById, revisionHistory: string[], definitionVersion} -> SheetState_Historic {staticOverrides.byObject[objectAddressKey] = SerializableMap, sequence?: {type:'PositionalSequence', length, subUnitsPerUnit, tracksByObject[key] = {trackIdByPropPath[encodedPath] -> trackId, trackData[trackId] = {type:'BasicKeyframedTrack', keyframes: PointableSet<BasicKeyframe>}}}}; BasicKeyframe = {id, value, position, handles:[lx,ly,rx,ry] (bezier), connectedRight, type?}. Prop types (packages/core/src/propTypes/index.ts): t.number(default,{range,nudgeMultiplier,nudgeFn}), t.string, t.boolean, t.rgba, t.stringLiteral, t.compound({...}), t.image, t.file; every config carries `default`, `interpolate(left,right,t)` and `deserializeAndSanitize(json)` (numbers are clamped to range on load). Runtime: getProject(id,{state,assets:{baseUrl}}) -> project.sheet(name) -> sheet.object(key, propsConfig) -> object.value / onValuesChange; SheetObject.getValues() is a dataverse prism that deep-merges defaults + initial + static overrides + sequenced values (interpolationTripleAtPosition per track) and recomputes only what changed. sequences/playbackControllers drive time via rAF (rafDrivers.ts) or an AudioPlaybackController. AI wiring: none.
core_innovation: Animation as versioned, sanitised JSON state (definitionVersion + revisionHistory + per-prop deserializeAndSanitize) authored in a GUI and replayed by a runtime that layers defaults, static overrides and keyframe tracks addressed by object key + encoded prop path.
strengths: State format is a genuine data contract: keyframes keyed by stable ids, tracks addressed by (object address, encoded prop path), bezier handles explicit, and definitionVersion for migrations; exactly the shape a 'motion profile authored at library time' should have.
Prop-type configs bundle default + interpolate + deserializeAndSanitize, so untrusted or stale JSON is clamped/sanitised on load rather than trusted: same philosophy as our Zod contracts.

Layered value resolution (defaults -> initial -> static -> sequenced) separates design-time defaults from per-instance overrides from motion, which maps onto design-system tokens -> section variant -> arrangement motion.
Core runtime is small (30.7 kB gzip) and framework-agnostic; studio is a dev-only dependency and can be stripped from production builds.
Apache-2.0; @theatre/r3f shows how a scene graph exposes props to a sequencer without owning the renderer.
weaknesses: Maintenance: last public commit 2024-08-14; README announces a private 1.0 rewrite that never surfaced. Adopting the runtime means owning a fork.
@theatre/core has sideEffects:true and a global projects singleton (getProject throws if called twice with different config), designed as an app-level singleton rather than an island-scoped module.

Playback is rAF-driven JS (coreTicker/rafDrivers), not CSS/WAAPI: every animated prop costs main-thread work per frame, which conflicts with a <=120 ms main-thread motion budget and near-zero-JS islands.
No prefers-reduced-motion awareness; sequences play regardless.

JSON state is 'any' at the API boundary (IProjectConfig.state?: any) and the historic format has tolerated undocumented shape drift (keyframe.type defaults for older states), so a strict schema must be written by us.
The studio GUI is heavy (362 files, React) and its export is a project-level blob, not per-section motion profiles; sharing profiles across a section library needs our own tooling.
patterns_to_steal: ProjectState_Historic {definitionVersion, revisionHistory, sheetsById} -> motion profiles in the section library: each arrangement's motion is a versioned JSON document with a schema version and revision list, human-authored, reviewed like a playbook.

PropTypeConfig {default, interpolate, deserializeAndSanitize, range} -> Zod schema for motion tokens: every animatable prop declares default, allowed range and an interpolation kind; loading clamps rather than fails.

Track addressing by (objectAddressKey, encoded prop path) -> SiteDefinition motion: keyframe tracks target `sectionId.elementRole.property` paths, never CSS selectors, so the renderer can compile them to CSS keyframes / WAAPI / ScrollTimeline deterministically.

Layered resolution defaults -> static overrides -> sequenced -> assembly: design_system motion defaults, section variant `motion` budget as static override, arrangement signature_move as the sequenced layer; intensity curve computed from this stack.
Studio as dev-only authoring surface -> library-time tooling: a human authors curves in a GUI, exports JSON, a transpiler converts to our schema; the GUI never ships.
patterns_to_avoid: Shipping @theatre/core as the runtime -> unmaintained, singleton-global, rAF-driven JS animation in every island; our playback should compile to CSS/WAAPI with zero runtime dependency.
Project-level monolithic state blob -> sections need per-arrangement motion profiles that compose; keep profiles small and addressable.
Untyped `state?: any` boundary -> violates the typed-JSON (Zod) contract rule; validate on load.
Bezier-handle keyframes for every prop -> over-expressive for a marketing site; restrict interpolation to a named easing set from the design system.
reusable_patterns: VersionedMotionState: animation stored as JSON with definitionVersion and revisionHistory, migrated deterministically on load.
SanitisingPropConfig: each animatable prop carries default + range + interpolate + deserializeAndSanitize; loading clamps invalid values.
PathAddressedTracks: keyframe tracks keyed by object address and encoded prop path rather than DOM selectors.
LayeredValueResolution: final value = defaults + static overrides + sequenced, recomputed incrementally.
AuthorInGuiShipAsData: a dev-only editor produces data; production consumes data through a different, minimal runtime (or a compiler).
adoption_strategy: Adapt — take the data model, not the library. Define a Zod `MotionProfile` schema borrowing definitionVersion/revisionHistory, path-addressed keyframe tracks, per-prop {default, range, easing} with sanitise-on-load, and the defaults->override->sequence layering; store one profile per arrangement in the section library and compile it at build time to CSS @keyframes / WAAPI / ScrollTimeline (and to the WebGL island's uniform timeline for the one allowed 3D section). Optionally use Theatre studio locally as the human authoring GUI with a one-way exporter into our schema, so the stalled runtime never ships. Do not depend on @theatre/core at runtime given the 25-month silence and private-repo 1.0.

status_note: active; semantic-release versioning (10.x), peer @react-three/fiber ^9 / react ^19 / three >=0.159
core_problem: A grab-bag of ~200 ready-made r3f components and hooks (environments, controls, text, performance, loaders) so common three.js recipes are one JSX tag.
architecture: Flat src/core (three-only components) and src/web (DOM-touching components) directories, one file per helper, re-exported from a single index with sideEffects:false and /* @__PURE__ */ annotations so unused helpers tree-shake. Runtime deps are heavy: three-stdlib (ported examples/jsm), troika-three-text (SDF text), three-mesh-bvh, camera-controls, maath, @monogrid/gainmap-js, @mediapipe/tasks-vision, hls.js, detect-gpu, zustand. Relevant helpers read: Float.tsx (a useFrame that sets rotation.x/y/z and position.y from cos/sin of clock time, matrixAutoUpdate=false); PerformanceMonitor.tsx (samples fps over `ms`=250 windows for `iterations`=10, computes refreshrate as max fps, fires onIncline/onDecline when >threshold (0.75) of averages sit above/below bounds(refreshrate) e.g. [40,60], nudges a 0..1 `factor` by `step`, and after `flipflops` oscillations fires onFallback and stops sampling); AdaptiveDpr.tsx (setDpr(performance.current * initialDpr) and optional image-rendering:pixelated); Preload.tsx (gl.compile(scene,camera) plus a throwaway CubeCamera render in a layout effect to force shader compilation before first paint); Environment.tsx + useEnvironment.tsx (preset names map to 1k .hdr files fetched from https://raw.githack.com/pmndrs/drei-assets/<sha>/hdri/, loaded via RGBELoader/EXRLoader/GainMapLoader and PMREM'd); Text.tsx (wraps troika-three-text with suspend-react); web/ScrollControls.tsx (creates its own absolutely-positioned scrolling div over the canvas with sticky inner container, maath easing damping, exposes range()/curve()/visible() offsets). AI wiring: none.
core_innovation: A performance-monitor hysteresis loop (bounded fps averages, step factor, flip-flop fallback) that lets a scene self-tune quality without oscillating.
strengths: PerformanceMonitor is a small, well-designed adaptive-quality algorithm: refresh-rate-aware bounds, threshold voting over N averages, and a flip-flop counter that locks in a fallback baseline instead of ping-ponging.
Preload's gl.compile + cube-camera warm-up is the correct way to move shader compilation off the reveal moment.
AdaptiveDpr shows the minimal consumer of r3f's performance.current: multiply the initial dpr.
sideEffects:false and PURE annotations mean importing one helper does not drag in the whole 1.5 MB package (still drags three + r3f).
Honest docs: performance section explicitly frames these as 'regress quality on movement' tools.
weaknesses: Whole package 1575 kB min / 488 kB gzip (bundlephobia); measured r3f + Float + Environment + AdaptiveDpr + PerformanceMonitor + Preload island = 1177 kB min / 329 kB gzip / 265 kB brotli, i.e. 1.8x our total JS budget.
<Environment preset> fetches ~1-2 MB HDRs from raw.githack.com, a third-party CDN we do not control: unacceptable for a production site (availability, privacy, LCP).
<Text> pulls troika-three-text (+ its worker/SDF generation) for 3D typography, roughly 100 kB+ gzip on top; 3D text is also an obvious slop tell.

ScrollControls replaces native scrolling with its own overflow div: breaks Astro page scroll, Lenis, anchor links, and keyboard/screen-reader scroll semantics; never suitable for a single below-fold section.

Float.tsx is literally the 'floating 3D blob' idiom: sin/cos idle wobble with random phase. It is the most recognisable AI-generated-landing-page signature of 2023-2025 (Spline/r3f glossy floating shapes, orbiting torus knots, sparkles). Nothing in it respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Requires React 19 + r3f; every helper assumes the r3f store (useThree/useFrame) so nothing is reusable in a vanilla island without rewriting.
patterns_to_steal: PerformanceMonitor hysteresis algorithm (bounds from measured refreshrate, 75% vote over 10x250ms windows, step factor, flipflops->onFallback) -> motion runtime: a ~80-line vanilla QualityGovernor driving dpr and particle count in our OGL/raw-WebGL island; telemetry logs the fallback event.

Preload (gl.compile before reveal) -> lazy-mount pattern: mount on intersection with rootMargin, compile and render one frame hidden, then crossfade poster->canvas so the user never sees the shader-compile stall.
AdaptiveDpr (dpr = initialDpr * quality) -> renderer config: dpr is a derived value, never set directly.

detect-gpu dependency idea (GPU tier from a benchmark table) -> eligibility: a client-side tier check that decides whether the WebGL island mounts at all or the poster stays; feed as a predicate input, not a model decision.
patterns_to_avoid: Float / Sparkles / Stars / MeshDistortMaterial / MeshWobbleMaterial idle animations -> anti-slop tier-1 ban: perpetual sin/cos wobble of glossy primitives is the canonical AI-landing-page look and burns battery.
Environment presets from raw.githack.com -> third-party runtime dependency; all assets must be self-hosted through our object storage.
ScrollControls scroll hijacking -> breaks native scroll, Lenis, a11y; scroll-driven motion must read window scroll (or ScrollTimeline) and never own the scroller.
3D <Text> / Text3D -> typography belongs in HTML for SEO, a11y and the FactRegistry's quotable claims; never render copy inside a canvas.
Adopting drei at all inside an Astro island -> forces React + r3f + three (329 kB gzip measured), exceeding both the 140 kB section ceiling and the 180 kB page budget.
reusable_patterns: HysteresisQualityMonitor: fps sampled in fixed windows, decisions made only when a supermajority of window averages cross refresh-rate-derived bounds, with a flip-flop counter that freezes a fallback.
CompileBeforeReveal: force GPU program compilation (gl.compile + one hidden frame) before swapping poster for canvas.
DerivedDpr: effective pixel ratio = clamp(devicePixelRatio) x quality factor, recomputed only when quality changes.
GpuTierGate: a lookup-table GPU tier (detect-gpu style) as an eligibility predicate for mounting heavy visual sections.
adoption_strategy: Ignore — the library cannot be used inside our budget (React + r3f + three are prerequisites) and its signature helpers (Float, Sparkles, Environment presets, 3D Text) are exactly the visual idioms our anti-slop gate should ban. Copy only the PerformanceMonitor algorithm and the Preload compile-before-reveal step into our own vanilla motion runtime; both are under 100 lines and depend on nothing but rAF and a GL context.

license: MIT (wrapper only); @splinetool/runtime and the Spline editor are closed-source SaaS
status_note: active but thin (3 source files); runtime published from a private repo (splinetool/spline) as @splinetool/runtime 2.0.55
core_problem: Drop a scene authored in the Spline SaaS editor into a React page: <Spline scene='https://prod.spline.design/<id>/scene.splinecode' />.
architecture: src/Spline.tsx: a forwardRef component that in useEffect constructs `new Application(canvas, {renderOnDemand, wasmPath})` from @splinetool/runtime, awaits `app.load(sceneUrl)`, wires nine Spline event names (mouseDown, mouseHover, scroll, lookAt, follow, ...) to props, renders `children` only while isLoading (poster slot) and disposes on unmount; src/ParentSize.tsx debounces resize (50 ms). src/next/SplineNext.tsx is a Next.js server component that regex-matches the scene URL, fetches https://<prod|draft>.spline.design/<id>/hash to get a thumbhash + dimensions, decodes it to a data-URI image (decodePreview.ts, thumbhash/blurhash deps) and passes it as the loading placeholder. The runtime itself (not in this repo) is 944 kB min / 263 kB gzip main entry, 368 files / 35.7 MB unpacked including WASM for physics loaded from a `wasmPath` (CDN by default), deps on-change + semver-compare, sideEffects:true. Scenes are hosted on prod.spline.design unless the .splinecode is downloaded and self-hosted (README notes CORS issues). AI wiring: none in the wrapper; Spline's editor has AI generation features server-side.
core_innovation: Server-side thumbhash placeholder fetched from the scene's /hash endpoint so the poster appears at SSR time before the runtime loads.
strengths: renderOnDemand defaults to true (idle when nothing changes).
`children` as a loading slot and SplineNext's thumbhash placeholder are a correct poster-first pattern, generated at build/SSR time.
Tiny, readable wrapper; dispose() on unmount; ErrorBoundary-friendly (throws the load error).
Designers can author in a GUI and export a URL: zero engineering per scene.
weaknesses: Runtime cost: 263.5 kB gzip / 944 kB min for @splinetool/runtime before the scene file (.splinecode is typically hundreds of kB to several MB) and physics WASM: 1.9x the 140 kB section ceiling and 1.5x the whole 180 kB page budget.

Closed source runtime and editor; scene files are a proprietary format; hosting defaults to spline.design (third-party availability, ToS and plan limits govern whether the URL keeps working; self-hosting requires manual download per export).
Peer on react + react-dom: another React island in Astro.

Slop signature: yes. Glossy pastel blobs, iridescent glass shapes, floating abstract orbs with mouse-follow are the recognisable Spline look and are saturated across AI-generated SaaS and agency templates; a local-service client's site with one reads as a template.
No prefers-reduced-motion handling; interactions (lookAt/follow) are pointer-driven by default.
Placeholder is a blurhash, not the real frame: a blurred blob next to sharp typography looks unfinished if the runtime is slow on mobile.
Low bus factor for the wrapper (3 files, last push Mar 2026) and full dependence on a VC-funded SaaS's roadmap.
patterns_to_steal: Build-time placeholder derived from the asset itself (SplineNext /hash -> thumbhash -> data URI) -> asset pipeline: every WebGL/video section carries a poster generated at library time (a real rendered frame, not a blurhash) and stored with the asset_constraints.
`children` rendered only while loading, canvas display:none until loaded -> lazy-mount pattern: poster stays in the DOM until first frame; canvas is hidden, not absent, so layout is stable (no CLS).
renderOnDemand default true -> motion budget default: on-demand rendering is the only allowed mode.
patterns_to_avoid: Spline scenes in any section -> runtime 263 kB gzip + hosted proprietary file; violates budget, self-hosting rule, and reads as an AI template.
Third-party scene hosting on prod.spline.design -> production dependency on a SaaS CDN and its ToS.
Mouse-follow / lookAt interactions -> the 'eyes follow cursor' hero is a slop tell and pointer-costly.
reusable_patterns: AssetDerivedPlaceholder: compute a tiny placeholder (hash or real poster) from the asset at build time and inline it in SSR output.
HiddenUntilFirstFrame: keep the heavy canvas mounted but display:none while a poster occupies the same box.
OnDemandByDefault: renderOnDemand=true as the library default, opt-in to continuous.
adoption_strategy: Ignore — the wrapper is fine but the product it wraps fails every constraint: 263 kB gzip closed-source runtime, proprietary hosted scene files, React peer, and a visual idiom that the anti-slop gate should explicitly ban (tier-1 layout ban on 'floating glossy 3D shapes'). Take only the SSR-placeholder and hidden-until-first-frame ideas for our own poster-first WebGL/video sections.

status_note: active; v6 line adds `theme.zeroRuntime` (ConfigProvider) to skip runtime style generation and import a prebuilt CSS file; cssVar mode also available
core_problem: Enterprise React UI library whose entire visual system is computed from a small set of seed tokens by pluggable derivation algorithms, so a whole light/dark/compact theme can be generated from a handful of inputs.
architecture: Three token tiers with explicit derivation functions (components/theme/). SeedToken (interface/seeds.ts, ~45 keys: colorPrimary/Success/Warning/Error/Info/Link, colorTextBase, colorBgBase, fontFamily, fontSize=14, lineWidth, borderRadius=6, sizeUnit=4, sizeStep=4, controlHeight=32, zIndexBase, motionUnit=0.1, motionBase, 8 easing curves, wireframe, motion:boolean, focusOutline) -> MapToken via an `algorithm` (DerivativeFunc<SeedToken, MapToken>): themes/default/index.ts spreads genColorMapToken + genFontMapToken + genSizeMapToken + genControlHeight + genCommonMapToken. Colour: @ant-design/colors `generate(base)` produces a 10-step palette in HSV (hue rotates ±2° per step, direction depends on hue band 60–240, saturation −0.16/step light, +0.05 dark, value +0.05/−0.15); dark palettes are produced by mixing those steps into a background colour with a darkColorMap table. genColorMapToken maps palette indices to semantic roles (Bg=1, BgHover=2, Border=3, BorderHover=4, Hover=5, base=6, Active=7, TextHover=8, Text=9, TextActive=10). Neutrals: text via alpha of colorTextBase (0.88/0.65/0.45/0.25), fills via alpha (0.15/0.06/0.04/0.02), backgrounds/borders via darken (light) or lighten (dark) of colorBgBase. Type: genFontSizes(base) = base·e^(i/5) rounded to even, lineHeight=(size+8)/size. Size: sizeUnit·(sizeStep±n). Radius: genRadius piecewise table. Motion: motionDurationFast/Mid/Slow = motionBase + motionUnit·{1,2,3}. Dark and compact algorithms are composable (`algorithm: [darkAlgorithm, compactAlgorithm]`), each taking (seed, prevMapToken). MapToken -> AliasToken via util/alias.ts formatToken (developer-facing names: colorTextHeading, paddingContentHorizontal, boxShadowCard, screenXS...; motion:false zeroes all durations). AliasToken -> per-component ComponentToken via prepareComponentToken (e.g. button/style/token.ts computes paddingBlock from controlHeight/lineHeight/lineWidth). useToken.ts runs getComputedToken through @ant-design/cssinjs useCacheToken (hash-salted, optional CSS-var emission with unitless/ignore/preserve lists); genStyleUtils/genStyleHooks generate per-component style sheets from tokens.
core_innovation: Seed → Map → Alias → Component token derivation as composable pure algorithms, so dark and compact modes are functions over seeds (not hand-authored palettes) and a brand hue change regenerates every dependent token.
strengths: The derivation chain is genuinely data-first: a designer owns Seed + Map algorithm, developers own Alias, components own ComponentToken; every layer is a pure function with a typed interface.

@ant-design/colors generate() is a compact, deterministic HSV palette algorithm with hue-band-aware rotation — exactly what `hue_adaptable: true` needs; dark palettes are a table-driven mix into a background colour, not a second hand-made palette.
Algorithms compose: compact = default then size/font/controlHeight re-derived from fontSizeSM and controlHeight−4; dark = default then colour maps re-derived. Composition order is data (an array).
Font-size scale is a formula (base·e^(i/5), even-rounded) with a line-height formula ((size+8)/size), not a lookup table.
motion:boolean and focusOutline:boolean seeds are honoured centrally (formatToken zeroes durations; lineWidthFocus=0) — an example of a global switch modelled as a token.
v6 zeroRuntime + cssVar mode acknowledge that runtime cssinjs is a cost and give a static-CSS escape hatch.
weaknesses: Runtime @ant-design/cssinjs by default (hash-salted style injection, React context); even in zeroRuntime mode the token pipeline is JS at runtime. Not usable inside our JS budget as a library.
Enterprise/admin aesthetics; the component set is irrelevant to marketing sites.

The Map/Alias interfaces are very large (alias.ts 649 lines, maps/colors.ts 644 lines) and many alias values are arbitrary constants (controlPaddingHorizontal: 12, fontWeightStrong: 600) rather than derived — the derivation story is partial.
HSV-based generation (not OKLCH) produces perceptually uneven steps for some hues; the hue-band heuristic (60–240 vs else) is empirical.
genRadius is a piecewise if-ladder — fine, but it shows the limits of encoding design intent as branches instead of a declared scale.
patterns_to_steal: Seed → Map → Alias → Component tiers with a typed DerivativeFunc per tier -> design_system: our YAML design-system files should carry a `seeds` block plus a named `algorithm` (default | dark | compact | custom) so `hue_adaptable: true` systems regenerate palettes from a client's brand hue in code, and the model only selects the design_system_id.

@ant-design/colors generate() (HSV 10-step, hue-band rotation, dark via mix table) -> design_system: port as a pure TS function (~100 lines) behind a `palette_algorithm` id; run once at build; write results as CSS vars. Consider OKLCH variant behind another id.

Palette-index-to-role mapping (Bg=1, Border=3, Hover=5, base=6, Active=7, Text=9) -> design_system: semantic role table as data so a design system can remap roles (e.g. luxury systems using darker 'base' indices).

Composable algorithm array (`[dark, compact]`) each taking (seed, prevMap) -> design_system: conditions like dark mode and density are algorithms applied in order, snapshotted into the Decision Manifest.
genFontSizes base·e^(i/5) + lineHeight=(size+8)/size -> design_system: a type-scale generator parameterised by base and a curve id; expose ratio choice in visual_dna.
motion:false seed zeroing all durations in formatToken -> motion: a single top-level `motion_enabled`/reduced-motion switch that collapses all duration tokens at build time.
patterns_to_avoid: @ant-design/cssinjs runtime style injection and hash-salted classnames -> we emit static CSS; no style runtime in islands.

Component-token tier as hand-computed per-component objects (377-line button token file) -> our section library should reference semantic tokens directly; component tokens only where a rule can derive them.
Alias tier full of magic constants -> keep alias values derived or explicitly declared as `visual_dna` choices; never silent constants.
Letting the model or a runtime touch seeds -> seeds are authored/derived in code; the model selects design_system_id only.
reusable_patterns: SeedMapAliasComponent: four token tiers connected by pure derivative functions with typed inputs/outputs.
HsvPaletteGenerate: 10-step palette from one base colour via per-step hue/saturation/value deltas with a hue-band direction rule; dark palette = mix table into background.
RoleIndexTable: semantic colour roles defined as indices into a generated palette (Bg=1 ... TextActive=10).
ComposableAlgorithms: theme modes (dark, compact) as ordered pure functions (seed, prevMap) -> map.
ExponentialTypeScale: fontSize_i = base·e^(i/5) rounded to even; lineHeight = (size+8)/size.
GlobalSwitchToken: booleans (motion, focusOutline) in the seed tier that collapse dependent tokens centrally.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Port the derivation algorithms (generate(), genColorMapToken role table, genFontSizes, genSizeMapToken, genControlHeight, genCommonMapToken motion durations) into a pure TS `deriveTokens(seed, algorithms[])` module used by the design-system compiler at build time; store seeds and algorithm ids in the YAML design-system files; emit CSS variables per scheme. Ignore antd, cssinjs and the component library entirely.

status_note: active; Material UI v7-era monorepo. Pigment CSS (zero-runtime) lives in a separate repo (mui/pigment-css) and is still documented as 'early alpha' in docs/data/material/experimental-api/pigment-css/pigment-css.md
core_problem: A complete React implementation of Google's Material Design, with a theme object that parameterises palette, typography, spacing, shape, shadows, z-index and motion and lets consumers override every component's styles as data.
architecture: Two layers. @mui/system (packages/mui-system/src) provides the theme kernel: createTheme (breakpoints, spacing via createSpacing(8) unary scale, shape.borderRadius=4, direction, applyStyles), styleFunctionSx, cssContainerQueries, and the CSS-variables machinery (cssVars/cssVarsParser.ts walks the theme object and emits `--prefix-path-to-key` vars + a parallel `vars` object; prepareCssVars.ts assembles per-colour-scheme stylesheets with selector strategies 'media' | 'class' | 'data' | 'data-attr=%s'). @mui/material/styles builds on it: createTheme.ts dispatches to createThemeNoVars.js (legacy palette.mode theme) or createThemeWithVars.js (cssVariables:true; colorSchemes {light,dark,custom} each built by createColorScheme.ts -> createPalette.js; adds *Channel tokens ('12 12 12') so alpha can be applied in CSS via rgba(var(--x-mainChannel)/0.5); nativeColor:true switches to oklch color-mix() and a CSS contrast-color polyfill using --__l clamp math). createPalette.js derives light/dark/contrastText from a single `main` via augmentColor (tonalOffset 0.2 lighten/darken, contrastThreshold 3 with WCAG ratio check). createTypography.js builds 13 variants from (fontSize=14, htmlFontSize=16) with pxToRem and per-variant fontWeight/size/lineHeight/letterSpacing. createTransitions.js exposes easing{easeInOut,easeOut,easeIn,sharp} and duration{shortest..complex, enteringScreen, leavingScreen}; createMotion.js adds motion.reducedMotion 'never'|'system'|'always' consumed by reducedMotion.ts (wraps styles in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)). Components: theme.components.MuiX.{defaultProps, styleOverrides{slot}, variants[{props|predicate, style}]} (styles/variants.ts, styles/components.ts). The runtime is Emotion via createStyled.ts: processStyleVariants() matches each variant's `props` object (or predicate fn) against props+ownerState and appends its style; Button.js itself is authored as base style + variants[] (e.g. props:{variant:'contained'} sets CSS custom props --variant-containedBg) and per-colour variants generated by iterating theme.palette. stringifyTheme.ts serialises the theme to a runtime source for Pigment CSS (theme.toRuntimeSource).
core_innovation: A theme object that is simultaneously a JS data structure and a CSS-variable stylesheet generator (one source, `theme.vars` mirror), with component variants expressed as matchable {props, style} data rather than code.
strengths: cssVarsParser/prepareCssVars: a generic 'nested token object -> CSS custom properties + vars mirror + per-scheme selector stylesheets' pipeline; shouldSkipGeneratingVar lets you exclude non-token keys. Straightforward to re-implement for YAML token files.
Colour-scheme selector strategy is a config enum ('media'|'class'|'data'|custom attr), and applyStyles(scheme, styles) abstracts over runtime vs CSS-vars mode.

Channel tokens (`mainChannel: '25 118 210'`) solve alpha-on-a-variable without JS colour math at runtime; nativeColor mode moves derivation entirely into CSS (color-mix in oklch, contrast-color polyfill).
augmentColor derivation is tiny and deterministic: main -> light/dark via tonalOffset, contrastText via WCAG contrast ratio with a dev-time warning below 3:1.
Variants-as-data: {props: {variant:'contained', color:'primary'} | predicate, style} — matched by exact prop equality; also lets theme authors add brand-new variants without touching components.
motion.reducedMotion as a theme-level tri-state ('never'|'system'|'always') resolved into a media query wrapper — a clean model for a reduced-motion 'condition'.
weaknesses: Runtime CSS-in-JS (Emotion) by default: every styled component serialises styles at render; incompatible with our 180 kB JS budget and Astro islands unless Pigment CSS is used, which is still alpha in a separate repo.
Material Design aesthetics baked into defaults (Roboto, 8dp grid, 25 elevation shadows, uppercase buttons); the components themselves are the opposite of agency-grade marketing design.

Theme object is enormous and untyped in places (palette: Record<string, any>); createThemeWithVars.js is 1000 lines of per-component palette assignment (Alert, AppBar, Chip...) — component-tier tokens are hand-wired, not derived.
Typography derivation is not a ratio scale — sizes are hard-coded Material spec numbers (96/60/48/34/24/20...), scaled only by fontSize/14.
Two parallel theme code paths (NoVars vs WithVars) with subtly different semantics (palette.mode vs colorSchemes) — evidence that bolting CSS vars onto a JS theme late is costly.
patterns_to_steal: cssVarsParser walk (nested token object -> `--ds-<path>` custom properties + `vars` lookup mirror) -> design_system: the compiler from YAML token files to a per-design-system CSS layer; the `vars` mirror gives the renderer type-safe references.

Colour-scheme stylesheet assembly with selectable selector strategy (prepareCssVars.getSelector: ':root', '[data-scheme="dark"]', '@media (prefers-color-scheme)') -> design_system: dark mode as a condition emitted at build time, zero JS.
Channel tokens ('r g b' triplets) alongside colour tokens -> design_system: lets section CSS do rgba(var(--ds-accent-channel)/0.12) for tints/overlays without a runtime colour library.

augmentColor (main -> light/dark/contrastText via tonalOffset + WCAG contrast threshold with hard warning) -> design_system + qa_gate: the seed of a `hue_adaptable` derivation, and a build-time contrast assertion.

Variants-as-data matcher (processStyleVariants: exact-match `props` or predicate, ordered, additive) -> renderer: same shape as our section `arrangements`/`variant × arrangement` selection — a variant is a data row matched against a state object, never a code branch.
motion.reducedMotion tri-state -> motion: a design-system-level flag resolved into `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` wrappers at build time.
patterns_to_avoid: Emotion runtime styled() engine -> violates JS budget and island model; we output static CSS from Astro.

Hand-wired per-component palette blocks in createThemeWithVars.js (Alert.errorColor, Chip.defaultBorder...) -> component-tier tokens should be derived from semantic tokens by rule, not enumerated per component.
Material's fixed typography table and 25-step elevation array -> our type scale must be base+ratio data with a per-design-system `visual_dna`, not a spec transcription.
Dual NoVars/WithVars theme paths -> commit to CSS variables as the only runtime surface from day one.
reusable_patterns: TokenTreeToCssVars: recursively flatten a nested token object into `--prefix-a-b-c` custom properties and a mirror object whose leaves are `var(--prefix-a-b-c)`.
SchemeSelectorStrategy: dark/light/custom scheme emitted under a configurable selector ('media' | 'class' | 'data' | attribute template) so the same tokens serve OS-preference and forced modes.
ChannelToken: store colours as `r g b` triplets next to the hex so alpha is applied in CSS (`rgb(var(--c) / a)`).
AugmentColor: derive {light, dark, contrastText} from one seed with tonalOffset + WCAG contrast threshold and a build-time assertion.
VariantsAsData: an ordered list of {props | predicate, style} rows matched against component state; new variants are added by appending rows.
ReducedMotionTriState: 'never' | 'system' | 'always' at theme level resolved into media-query wrapping at compile time.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not install @mui/material. Re-implement the cssVarsParser/prepareCssVars pipeline (~300 lines) as the compiler from our YAML design-system token files into per-scheme CSS layers, include channel tokens and an augmentColor-style derivation with a build-time contrast assertion in the QA gate, and model reduced motion as a tri-state resolved to media queries. Borrow the {props, style} variant-row shape as the schema for section arrangements.

status_note: active; v3.37 (packages/react). Note: v3 adopts Panda CSS's config API (tokens/semanticTokens/recipes/conditions) but the runtime is still Emotion (@emotion/react peer dep) — it is NOT zero-runtime; a separate packages/panda-preset exports the same theme for real Panda CSS builds.
core_problem: A component system whose styling is fully declarative: tokens, semantic tokens with conditions, and component 'recipes' (variants as data) are all plain objects fed to createSystem(), so a whole theme can be authored, merged and inspected as data.
architecture: packages/react/src/styled-system: config.ts exposes identity creators (defineConfig, defineTokens.<category>, defineSemanticTokens.<category>, defineRecipe, defineSlotRecipe, defineConditions, defineTextStyles, defineLayerStyles, defineAnimationStyles, defineKeyframes). system.ts createSystem(...configs) merges configs, builds a TokenDictionary (token-dictionary.ts: tokens {value} and semantic tokens {value:{base|_light|_dark|...}} are flattened to CSS vars `--chakra-<category>-<path>`; semantic conditions become a cssVarMap keyed by condition, emitted under the resolved selector, e.g. `.dark &` for _dark; `colorPalette` virtual tokens remap `colorPalette.solid` -> `--chakra-colors-color-palette-solid` so one recipe serves every hue), createConditions (conditions.ts: user conditions prefixed `_`, breakpoints merged, sorted after plain props), createUtility, createLayers (@layer reset, base, tokens, recipes), createRecipeFn (cva.ts) and createSlotRecipeFn (sva.ts). A recipe is {className, base, variants{name:{option: styles}}, defaultVariants, compoundVariants[{...selection, css}]}; cva.resolve(props) = base + variant styles for each selected key + compound matches, wrapped in @layer recipes; splitVariantProps separates variant props from DOM props. Slot recipes do the same per named slot. Built-in conditions live in preset-base.ts: _hover (`@media (hover: hover)` + :is(:hover,[data-hover]):not(:disabled)), _focusVisible, _disabled, _open, _checked, group/peer variants, _motionReduce (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`), _dark (`.dark &, .dark .chakra-theme:not(.light) &`), _light, _osDark/_osLight (prefers-color-scheme), _highContrast (forced-colors), _rtl, _print, _landscape. Theme data in packages/react/src/theme: tokens/* (colors, spacing, sizes, radii, durations {fastest 50ms..slowest 500ms}, easings, animations, keyframes), semantic-tokens/colors.ts (bg/fg/border/*.{DEFAULT,subtle,muted,emphasized,inverted,error...} each with _light/_dark refs like `{colors.gray.50}`), text-styles.ts (size -> fontSize+lineHeight+letterSpacing compositions), layer-styles.ts (fill.*, outline.*, indicator.* compositions over colorPalette), motion-styles.ts (animationStyles keyed by data-placement), recipes/* (76) and slot-recipes/*. Components consume recipes via useRecipe/useSlotRecipe hooks with Emotion doing the runtime CSS generation.
core_innovation: Recipes and slot recipes: component styling as a pure data structure (base + variants + compoundVariants + defaultVariants) resolved by a tiny matcher, combined with condition-keyed semantic tokens and a virtual `colorPalette` token that makes one recipe hue-agnostic.
strengths: Everything is a plain object behind an identity function — recipes, tokens, conditions, compositions — so they are trivially serialisable to/from YAML and mergeable (mergeConfigs, cva.merge).
Semantic token conditions ({_light, _dark, _osDark, custom}) are resolved at token-dictionary build time into per-condition CSS-var blocks; the recipe never mentions dark mode.
Virtual `colorPalette` token: `bg: 'colorPalette.solid'` compiles to a var that is re-pointed by setting `colorPalette="teal"` — one variant definition serves every accent hue.

Compositions (textStyle, layerStyle, animationStyle) are named bundles of properties registered as utilities: a small, reusable vocabulary of 'type set', 'surface treatment', 'entrance motion' as data.
Conditions are a single map from name to selector/at-rule, including _motionReduce, _highContrast, _print, _rtl — dark mode, reduced motion and forced colours are literally the same mechanism.
Cascade layers (@layer reset, base, tokens, recipes) give deterministic override order without specificity games.
weaknesses: Runtime Emotion under the hood (peer @emotion/react; @emotion/serialize in deps); recipes are resolved and serialised at render. To get zero-runtime you must switch to Panda CSS with packages/panda-preset — a different build pipeline.
Recipe matcher supports variant/compound selection only; there is no `requires`/gating, no composition metadata, no motion budget — it is purely stylistic.
SaaS/product-UI aesthetics; the 76 recipes are for app components (menu, dialog, table), not marketing sections.
Token references are stringly typed (`{colors.gray.50}`) and resolved late; typos surface only at build/run of the system, not at authoring time (Chakra generates .gen.ts types via CLI to mitigate).
Dark mode via `.dark` class selector default couples tokens to a class-toggling script; media-only mode requires overriding conditions.
patterns_to_steal: Recipe schema {base, variants, defaultVariants, compoundVariants[{selection, css}]} -> renderer/design_system: the exact shape for authoring section-family visual variants as YAML; resolve with a 40-line matcher at build time in Astro and emit static classes.

Semantic tokens with condition-keyed values ({_light, _dark}) compiled to per-condition CSS-var blocks -> design_system: our YAML tokens carry `value: {base, dark, high_contrast}`; the compiler emits `:root` and `[data-scheme=dark]` blocks; sections never branch on mode.

Virtual colorPalette token -> design_system + art_direction: sections reference `accent.*` roles; the design system (or a hue_adaptable derivation) re-points the roles, so arrangements are hue-agnostic.

Conditions map (name -> selector/at-rule) with _motionReduce, _highContrast, _print -> motion + qa_gate: reduced motion and forced-colours are conditions in the same table as dark mode; the anti-slop/QA gate can assert every motion rule has a _motionReduce counterpart.
Compositions (textStyles, layerStyles, animationStyles) -> design_system visual_dna: named bundles ('display', 'eyebrow', 'surface.raised', 'enter.rise') the model selects by id.
Cascade layer order (reset, base, tokens, recipes) -> renderer: adopt @layer to keep design-system CSS, section CSS and island CSS from fighting.
patterns_to_avoid: Runtime recipe resolution through Emotion -> resolve at build time in Astro; ship only static CSS.
Class-based `.dark &` as the default dark condition with a toggling script -> prefer `prefers-color-scheme` media or a server-set data attribute; no client JS for theme.
Chakra's component recipes themselves -> product-UI look; author our own section variants.
Stringly token refs without authoring-time validation -> our YAML must be Zod-validated with token-id enums generated from the token files.
reusable_patterns: RecipeAsData: {base, variants, defaultVariants, compoundVariants} resolved by a matcher; slot recipes extend it with per-part styles.
ConditionKeyedToken: a semantic token whose value is a map from condition (_light/_dark/_highContrast) to a primitive-token reference.
VirtualPaletteToken: role tokens (colorPalette.solid/fg/subtle) re-pointed by a single attribute, making styles hue-agnostic.
ConditionTable: one map from condition name to selector or at-rule covering colour scheme, reduced motion, forced colours, print, rtl.
StyleComposition: named bundles of properties (textStyle/layerStyle/animationStyle) registered as single-value utilities.
LayeredCascade: fixed @layer order reset < base < tokens < recipes.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not install @chakra-ui/react (Emotion runtime, React-only). Copy the data shapes: recipe/slot-recipe schema for section variants, condition-keyed semantic tokens, the virtual colorPalette indirection, compositions as visual_dna vocabulary, and the conditions table including _motionReduce/_highContrast. Implement a build-time resolver (Zod-typed) in the Astro renderer that emits static CSS under @layer.
