status_note: active; react-aria 3.52 / react-aria-components 1.21 / @react-spectrum/s2 1.7. Hooks have been consolidated into packages/react-aria/src/* with @react-aria/* packages as thin re-exports (e.g. @react-aria/button/src/index.ts re-exports from 'react-aria/useButton'). Spectrum 2 style macro depends on @adobe/spectrum-tokens (separate repo) and Parcel macros.
core_problem: Headless, hook-based accessibility and interaction primitives (React Aria) that encode WAI-ARIA patterns, cross-device press/hover/focus semantics, focus management and screen-reader announcements independently of visual design; plus Adobe's own design system (Spectrum) built on them.
architecture: Three tiers. (1) react-aria hooks (packages/react-aria/src): useButton(props, ref) -> {buttonProps, isPressed} composes usePress (unified mouse/touch/pen/keyboard press model with press-start/end/up, virtual click detection, iOS quirks) and useFocusable, and adapts semantics per elementType (button vs a/div/span get role/tabIndex/aria-disabled). useDialog -> {dialogProps, titleProps, contentProps}: focuses dialog on mount with an iOS VoiceOver re-focus workaround, generates aria-labelledby via useSlotId, calls useOverlayFocusContain, dev-warns when no accessible title; deliberately omits aria-modal (Safari iframe bug) and relies on aria-hidden on siblings. FocusScope (focus/FocusScope.tsx, 1100 lines): contain/restoreFocus/autoFocus with a global focus-scope tree, Tab-key trapping, focus manager API. LiveAnnouncer: singleton pair of aria-live polite/assertive regions prepended to body; announce(message, assertiveness, timeout=7000) appends a node and removes it after timeout. Collections (collections/Document.ts, CollectionBuilder.tsx): a fake DOM (BaseNode/ElementNode/Document with insertBefore, dirty tracking) built by rendering children into a hidden portal so item collections are known before the real render (works in SSR); SSRProvider for stable ids. react-stately holds state machines. (2) react-aria-components (packages/react-aria-components/src): components wrap the hooks and expose state as data-* attributes (Button: data-hovered, data-pressed, data-focused, data-focus-visible, data-disabled, data-pending) and render props (utils.tsx useRenderProps: className/style/children may be functions of the state values, plus defaultClassName like 'react-aria-Button' and a `data-rac` marker); slotted contexts (Provider, useContextProps, DEFAULT_SLOT) let compound components communicate. (3) Spectrum 2 (packages/@react-spectrum/s2/style): a build-time 'style macro' (style-macro.ts, run via Parcel macros) compiles a style object into atomic class names (base-62 generated names, one @layer per priority level, conditions resolved as nested at-rules/selectors); spectrum-theme.ts declares the theme: baseColors from @adobe/spectrum-tokens variables.json via colorScale(), each ColorToken carrying {light, dark, forcedColors}; spacing as pxToRem sets; sizing multiplied by `var(--s2-scale)` for touch vs desktop density; fontSize roles ui/heading/title/body ×7; conditions {forcedColors: '@media (forced-colors: active)', touch: '@media not ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))', xs..breakpoints}; runtime.ts merges style strings. The docs macro simulates HCM via variables.
core_innovation: Behaviour and accessibility as composable hooks that return spreadable prop bags, with component state surfaced as data-* attributes and render props so any styling engine — including plain static CSS — can attach to it.
strengths: Best-in-class a11y edge-case handling captured in code (iOS VoiceOver dialog refocus, Safari aria-modal iframe bug, virtual-click detection, Samsung/iPad pointer heuristics for the `touch` condition) — knowledge our QA gate cannot regenerate.
Hooks are UI-agnostic: no styles, no DOM structure imposed; usePress unifies pointer types; FocusScope and LiveAnnouncer are framework-light utilities.

react-aria-components' data-* state attributes (data-pressed, data-focus-visible, data-pending) make interactive state stylable from a static stylesheet — compatible with our 'CSS from tokens, no runtime styling' rule.
Collections built from a hidden fake-DOM render work under SSR — relevant if islands need listboxes/menus.
Spectrum 2 style macro proves a zero-runtime atomic CSS compiler with condition ordering via @layer; ColorToken {light, dark, forcedColors} is a clean tri-condition token shape.
Apache-2.0, Adobe-backed, used by many other component libraries (a de facto standard).
weaknesses: React-only. In Astro each interactive island would need the React runtime (~40 kB gz for react-dom alone) plus react-aria chunks; with a 180 kB total JS budget that is a large slice for a marketing site with few interactive controls.
Component-level weight: react-aria 3.52 is a broad umbrella (i18n, date, number formatting); tree-shaking works but usePress/FocusScope alone are ~2000 lines of source.
Spectrum 2 style macro is Parcel-macro-bound (`with {type:'macro'}`), tied to @adobe/spectrum-tokens and Adobe's visual language; not reusable as a compiler for our tokens without forking.
Spectrum components carry Adobe product-UI aesthetics; irrelevant to marketing design.
Class names are versioned/postfixed (POSTFIX from package.json) and obfuscated, hampering debugging of static output.
patterns_to_steal: State-as-data-attributes contract (data-pressed, data-hovered, data-focus-visible, data-disabled, data-pending) -> renderer + design_system: every island (or even plain Astro components using CSS :has/:focus-visible) exposes the same attribute vocabulary; design-system CSS targets it; a11y a QA rule can assert states exist.

useDialog/FocusScope/LiveAnnouncer behaviours -> renderer islands: adopt react-aria hooks directly in the few React islands that need dialogs, menus or comboboxes; do not reinvent focus containment or live announcements.

`touch` condition (`@media not ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))`) and `--s2-scale` density multiplier -> design_system: density/touch as a condition + a single scale variable, not a second token set.

ColorToken {light, dark, forcedColors} -> design_system: the three-condition colour token shape for YAML (`value: {light, dark, forced_colors}`), with forced-colors mapped to system colour keywords (ButtonText, Highlight...).
Render-props with defaultClassName + slotted contexts -> visual_editor (post-V1): a stable class/data-attr surface the editor can hook into without touching behaviour.
Dev-time assertions (dialog without accessible name warns) -> qa_gate: promote to hard build-time checks in Playwright/axe run.
patterns_to_avoid: Using React Aria Components for non-interactive sections -> zero-JS Astro components; React only where a control genuinely needs it (dialog, accordion, menu, form validation).
Spectrum 2 style macro / @adobe/spectrum-tokens as our token compiler -> Parcel-bound and Adobe-branded; write our own small compiler (see MUI cssVarsParser / Chakra dictionary).
Hidden-portal collection builder for simple lists -> unnecessary complexity for marketing content lists; only for real listbox/menu islands.
Adopting react-stately state machines wholesale -> most site state (nav open, accordion) is fine in native HTML (<details>, popover attribute) with no JS.
reusable_patterns: PropBagHook: behaviour hooks return spreadable DOM prop objects ({buttonProps, isPressed}) so markup and styling stay outside the hook.
StateDataAttributes: interaction state surfaced as data-* attributes for static-CSS styling and testable a11y states.
FocusScopeTree: nested focus scopes with contain/restore/autoFocus tracked in a global tree.
LiveRegionSingleton: two persistent aria-live regions with timed message nodes.
TouchCondition: `@media not ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))` plus a density scale variable.
TriConditionColorToken: {light, dark, forcedColors} per colour token.
adoption_strategy: Adopt (narrowly) + Adapt. Adopt react-aria hooks (useButton, useDialog, FocusScope, LiveAnnouncer, useFocusRing) inside the small set of React islands that need real interactive a11y, budgeting the React runtime once per page. Adapt the data-* state vocabulary, the touch/forced-colors conditions and the tri-condition colour token into the design-system schema. Ignore Spectrum components and the S2 style macro.

status_note: active; token sources have been migrated to W3C DTCG JSON (packages/*/src/dtcg/*.json) with JS/SCSS generated at build; @carbon/motion gained 'motion surfaces' (2026) as composite transition recipes
core_problem: IBM's design system, whose foundation packages (@carbon/themes, @carbon/type, @carbon/layout, @carbon/motion, @carbon/colors) publish the design language as data — four colour themes, a 23-step type scale, spacing/breakpoints, and named easing/duration tokens — consumable from Sass, JS and now DTCG JSON.
architecture: packages/themes: tokens are declared structurally in src/tokens/v11TokenGroup.ts via TokenGroup.create({name, properties:['background'], tokens:[{name:'background-hover', state:'hover'}...]}) — groups know which CSS properties they apply to and which interaction state each token represents; TokenSet/TokenFormat convert names to JS camelCase or SCSS `$kebab-01`. Values now live in src/dtcg/themes.json: each token is `{$type:'color', $description, $extensions:{'carbon.themes': {white:'{gray.10}', g10:'{white.default}', g90:'{gray.80}', g100:'{gray.90}'}}}` — four themes in one file as an extension on the token, with values as references into @carbon/colors (also DTCG, src/dtcg/colors.json). Component tokens (button, tag, notification, status, content-switcher) are separate DTCG files. tools.ts has adjustLightness/adjustAlpha helpers. The README documents 'contextual layer tokens' ($layer, $layer-accent) resolved to numbered tiers 01/02/03 by nesting depth via a <Layer> context. packages/type: scale.ts getTypeSize(n) = size(n-1) + (floor((n-2)/4)+1)·2 yielding 12,14,16,18,20,24,28,32,36,42,48,54,60,68,76,84,92,102,112,122,132,144,156; styles.ts defines type sets as objects {fontSize: rem(scaleNN), fontWeight, lineHeight, letterSpacing} in two families — productive (fixed) and expressive/fluid (with a `breakpoints:{md,lg,xlg,max}` map); fluid.ts converts a breakpoint map into calc() linear interpolation between breakpoints (`calc(min + (max-min) * ((100vw - minVw) / (maxVw - minVw)))`). packages/layout: baseFontSize 16, rem/em/px, breakpoints {sm 320/4col, md 672/8col, lg 1056/16col, xlg 1312, max 1584} with margins, miniUnit 8, spacing01..13, fluidSpacing, container sizes, iconSize. packages/motion: src/dtcg/motion.json declares durations (fast-01 70ms, fast-02 110, moderate-01 150, moderate-02 240, slow-01 400, slow-02 700, each with a usage $description) and easing as `$type: cubicBezier` arrays for standard/entrance/exit × productive/expressive; tokens.ts exports motion(name, mode) -> cubic-bezier string and resolveEasing -> numeric array for JS engines; surfaces.ts + src/dtcg/surfaces.json define 'motion surfaces' — named transition intents (disclosure, contextual, expand, invoke) with `$type:'transition'` DTCG value plus a carbon.motion extension {kind:'reveal'|'shared-element', duration token, enter/exit keyframes as plain CSS pairs, enterEasing/exitEasing {name, mode}, origin:'trigger'}; defineMotionSurface validates custom surfaces at module load.
core_innovation: Motion and typography as validated data: easing curves indexed by (intent × mode), durations with documented intent, and 'motion surfaces' that bundle duration + enter/exit easing + engine-neutral keyframes into a named, validated recipe; plus a multi-theme-in-one-token DTCG encoding.
strengths: DTCG-format sources with `$type`, `$description` and `$extensions` per token — a standards-based, tool-agnostic format; four themes stored as an extension map on each token rather than four files to keep in sync.
TokenGroup metadata (which CSS properties a group is valid for, which state a token represents) is machine-readable — enables lint rules like 'a hover token may only appear under :hover'.
Type scale is a formula (getTypeSize) with productive vs expressive/fluid sets; fluid.ts is a compact, correct linear-interpolation generator between breakpoints.
Motion tokens are two-dimensional (intent: standard/entrance/exit × mode: productive/expressive) with numeric curves available for JS engines; durations carry usage descriptions.
Motion surfaces: a composite, validated, engine-neutral recipe (CSS/WAAPI/View Transitions) — the closest thing in the field to our per-variant `motion` budget as data.
Contextual layer tokens (layer-01/02/03 resolved by nesting depth) are a proven model for 'surface elevation as context'.
weaknesses: Themes are hand-authored per token (white/g10/g90/g100 values enumerated), not derived from seeds — no hue adaptation; changing a brand colour means editing many tokens.
IBM Plex / IBM product aesthetic and 16-column grid; components (packages/react) are enterprise UI, irrelevant here.
Heavy Sass toolchain (@carbon/styles) and generated artefacts (js/generated/*) required before packages even build; DTCG is source but consumption is via generated JS/SCSS.
Motion surfaces are brand new (2026) and small (4 built-ins); shared-element kind relies on a React adapter for layout projection.
Type sets are named by product role (productiveHeading03, expressiveHeading05, display04) with many aliases — a large vocabulary, not a small ratio-driven system.
patterns_to_steal: DTCG token file shape with `$type`, `$description`, `$extensions.<vendor>` -> design_system: author our YAML tokens in DTCG-compatible structure (type, description, extensions for scheme-specific values and visual_dna metadata) so Style Dictionary-class tooling and validators apply.
Multi-scheme values as an extension map on the token (`carbon.themes: {white, g10, g90, g100}`) -> design_system: `schemes: {light, dark, high_contrast}` per semantic token instead of parallel files.
TokenGroup metadata (properties[], state) -> anti_slop + qa_gate: lint that colour tokens are used only on declared properties and state tokens only under matching pseudo-classes.

getTypeSize formula + fluid.ts breakpoint interpolation -> design_system: type scale as base + curve id, with `fluid: {md, lg, max}` maps compiled to calc() (or clamp()) at build; visual_dna exposes 'productive' vs 'expressive' type family.

Motion tokens as (intent × mode) easing + described durations, and motion surfaces {kind, duration, enter, exit, enterEasing, exitEasing} -> motion: section variants declare a `motion.surface` id; the compiler emits CSS with prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks and counts main-thread cost against the budget.
Contextual layer tokens resolved by nesting depth -> renderer: surface/elevation tokens for nested cards/sections resolved by composition depth in the assembly step.
patterns_to_avoid: Hand-enumerated four-theme values -> our hue_adaptable systems must derive dark/high-contrast from seeds (Ant Design pattern) and only override where a designer authored an exception.
Sass-based consumption and generated-artefact build steps -> we compile YAML -> CSS vars in one TS step; no Sass.
The large role-named type-set vocabulary (30+ names) -> keep 6–8 type roles per design system tied to a scale curve.
Carbon React components -> enterprise UI; none appropriate for marketing sites.
reusable_patterns: DtcgTokenFile: tokens as nested JSON with $type/$value/$description/$extensions; references as `{path.to.token}`.
SchemeExtensionMap: per-token map of scheme -> value inside $extensions instead of one file per scheme.
TokenGroupMetadata: groups carry allowed CSS properties and per-token interaction state.
FormulaTypeScale: size(n) = size(n-1) + (floor((n-2)/4)+1)·2 with productive (fixed) and expressive (fluid) sets.
FluidInterpolation: breakpoint font-size map compiled to calc() linear interpolation.
EasingIntentMode: easing tokens indexed by intent (standard/entrance/exit) × mode (productive/expressive), exposed as CSS string and numeric array.
MotionSurface: validated composite recipe {kind, duration, enter, exit, enterEasing, exitEasing} for one transition intent.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not use Carbon packages. Copy the DTCG token file structure (with scheme values as an extension map) as the on-disk format for design-system token files, port fluid.ts and getTypeSize into the type-scale compiler, and model our section `motion` budget after motion surfaces: a small validated set of named surfaces with (intent × mode) easings and described durations, compiled to CSS with reduced-motion fallbacks. Optionally reuse @carbon/motion's easing curves as the default 'productive/expressive' vocabulary.

status_note: active; redirects to OpenHands/OpenHands. IMPORTANT: the OpenHands/OpenHands repo is now 'Agent Canvas' (a TypeScript/React/Electron control center, package @openhands/agent-canvas 1.22.0). The Python agent core (event stream, controller, runtime, microagents) was moved to OpenHands/software-agent-sdk (MIT, ~1.2k stars, pushed 2026-09-23). Legacy V0 Python monolith still readable at tags <= 0.59.0 (openhands/controller/agent_controller.py, stuck.py, openhands/microagent/). This analysis covers the V1 SDK (the live architecture) plus V0 where it differs.
core_problem: Run an LLM coding agent that edits files and runs commands in a sandbox, safely and resumably: an append-only event log as the single source of truth, hard iteration and dollar budgets, loop detection, and a risk-gated confirmation policy for dangerous actions.
architecture: V1 is a uv workspace of four packages: openhands-sdk (core), openhands-tools (terminal, file_editor, browser_use, delegate, task_tracker, workflow), openhands-workspace (Docker/Apptainer/Cloud/RemoteAPI sandboxes) and openhands-agent-server (FastAPI + websocket; conversation_router, event_router, hooks, docker_runtime provisioning/proxy). Data model: openhands/sdk/event/base.py `Event` is a frozen pydantic DiscriminatedUnion with id, timestamp, source and parent_id (events form a tree; sibling branches = alternate histories; `EventLog.path_to_root` and `ConversationState.active_branch()` resolve the live path). Subtypes: ActionEvent/ObservationEvent/MessageEvent/SystemPromptEvent (LLMConvertibleEvent.to_llm_message projects the log into chat messages, merging multi-tool-call batches by llm_response_id), CondensationSummaryEvent, ConversationStateUpdateEvent, AgentErrorEvent, HookExecutionEvent. Persistence (conversation/event_store.py + persistence_const.py): one JSON file per event `events/event-{idx:05d}-{uuid}.json` plus `base_state.json`; EventLog is process-safe via a lock file and a length-marker sidecar; ConversationState auto-persists base_state on every public field change (`__setattr__` hook) and exposes a context manager to batch saves. State machine: `ConversationExecutionStatus` IDLE/RUNNING/PAUSED/WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION/FINISHED/ERROR/STUCK (is_terminal()). Run loop (conversation/impl/local_conversation.py `run()`, ~3k lines): per iteration it checks pause/stuck, invokes agent.step(), runs stop hooks on FINISHED, emits MaxBudgetReached when `max_budget_per_run` (USD, from ConversationStats) is hit and an ERROR event when `max_iteration_per_run` (default 500) is hit. StuckDetector (conversation/stuck_detector.py) scans the last 20 events since the last user message for five patterns: identical action/observation repeats, identical action/error repeats, agent monologue, alternating A-B-A-B patterns, context-window-error loops, with `StuckDetectionThresholds` per pattern; on an action-error streak it first injects a nudge message once, then flips status to STUCK. Confirmation: security/confirmation_policy.py NeverConfirm/AlwaysConfirm/ConfirmRisky(threshold) over SecurityRisk LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/UNKNOWN; risk is predicted per action by a SecurityAnalyzer (llm_analyzer, grayswan, toolshield, defense_in_depth shell AST policy rails) and gates the loop into WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION. Context: context/condenser/* (RollingCondenser, LLMSummarizingCondenser, PipelineCondenser) shrink the View; context/view/properties/* assert invariants (tool_call_matching, batch_atomicity). Critic: critic/base.py CriticBase returns CriticResult(score 0..1) and IterativeRefinementConfig(success_threshold) retries the task with a follow-up prompt. Skills (the successor of microagents, skills/skill.py + trigger.py): markdown with frontmatter loaded as Skill(name, content, trigger) where trigger is KeywordTrigger (whole-token, case-insensitive match against user message), TaskTrigger (slash-command style with inputs) or PathTrigger (gitignore-style globs fired when the agent touches matching files); untriggered skills are always injected. Workspace (workspace/base.py) abstracts execute_command/file_upload/file_download/git_changes/git_diff; DockerWorkspace boots an agent-server image and talks to it over HTTP. There is a TypeScript client (clients/typescript, alpha, remote conversations only) mirroring the server API. Structured final outputs are not first-class: the agent ends via FinishAction(message) or task_outcome presets; there is no response_format/Zod-style schema-validated final result.
core_innovation: A frozen, tree-shaped, file-per-event log is the whole agent state; run status, stuck detection, dollar/iteration budgets and risk-gated confirmation are all pure functions over that log, so any run is replayable and resumable from disk.
strengths: Event log as single source of truth with deterministic replay (events_to_messages is a read-only projection); base_state.json is a derived snapshot, not the truth.
StuckDetector is concrete and cheap: five explicit loop signatures over the last N events with tunable thresholds, plus a 'nudge first, then STUCK' escalation that avoids premature kills.
Two independent hard limits: max_iteration_per_run (step count) and max_budget_per_run (USD from LLM metrics) both terminate with a typed error event, never silently.
Confirmation is a policy object over a risk enum (ConfirmRisky threshold), decoupled from the UI and from the analyzer that predicts risk.
Workspace abstraction cleanly separates 'where commands run' (local/docker/remote/cloud) from the agent loop; the agent-server exposes the same API in every case.
Skills/microagents: knowledge injected only when a whole-token keyword or a file-path glob fires, with version and description in frontmatter and scripts/references/assets side-folders.
weaknesses: Python runtime. Adopting the SDK means a second runtime next to Astro/TS; the TypeScript client is alpha and only drives a remote Python agent-server, so it does not remove the Python dependency.

Built for open-ended coding tasks (500-iteration default, free-form tool use, shell); our pipeline is ~12 deterministic stages with 3-4 constrained model calls, so 90% of the machinery (terminal, file editor, browser tools, condensers, critics, MCP, plugin marketplace) is dead weight.
No schema-validated structured output: the only 'result' is a FinishAction message; you would build the Zod/pydantic validation + retry loop yourself anyway.

Heavy churn: the repo was rebranded (OpenDevin -> OpenHands -> Agent Canvas), the Python core moved repos, V0 tags are frozen; APIs in the SDK are still shifting (deprecation module, legacy skill converters).
local_conversation.py is 3,128 lines with sync and async run loops duplicated; the state machine is spread across the loop rather than being a declarative transition table.
Critic score 0..1 with iterative refinement is exactly the non-reproducible LLM-judge-as-gate pattern we rejected.
patterns_to_steal: Append-only event log with parent_id tree + derived base_state snapshot -> agent_orchestration: persist every pipeline stage transition (StageStarted/StageCompleted/ModelCallRequested/ModelCallReturned/GateFailed) as one JSON row per event in Postgres; the Decision Manifest is then a projection over the log, not a separately maintained document.

ConversationExecutionStatus enum with is_terminal() + explicit FINISHED/ERROR/STUCK/WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION -> agent_orchestration: use the same set for a build run's status column so the QA gate and human review map to WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION, not ad hoc flags.

Dual hard limits (iteration count AND accumulated USD from per-call metrics, each emitting a typed limit-reached event) -> agent_orchestration: every model call records cost; the run aborts with MaxBudgetReached before the copy-generation stage can loop.

StuckDetector's 'identical action/observation repeated k times' and 'nudge once then stop' -> anti_slop / assembly: when beat selection or arrangement selection re-proposes the same rejected id twice, inject the rejection reason once, then fail the stage to fallback archetype (service_clarity) instead of retrying forever.

PathTrigger/KeywordTrigger skills (whole-token keyword match, gitignore globs, frontmatter version) -> niche playbooks: a playbook file gets `triggers:` (niche keywords) and `paths:` (which section families/archetypes it applies to) in YAML frontmatter, and is injected into the creative-direction prompt only when it fires; keep playbooks versioned and human-reviewed exactly as they do with skills.

ConfirmRisky(threshold) policy over a small risk enum -> qa_gate: tag each auto-fix the fixer proposes with LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH (e.g. alt-text edit vs. removing a section) and only pause for human confirmation above the threshold.
patterns_to_avoid: Adopting openhands-sdk or agent-server as the orchestrator -> forces a Python service and Docker agent-server for a pipeline that is mostly TypeScript code with a handful of model calls; the TS client cannot run an agent locally.
CriticBase score-threshold iterative refinement -> this is an LLM judge as a gate (rejected); our gates are Playwright/axe/Lighthouse/regex, LLM judging is warning-only.
LLMSummarizingCondenser / long-horizon memory -> our model calls are short and stateless-by-design (eligible sets are passed in); there is no long conversation to condense.

Free-form tool loop (terminal/file_editor/browser tools) for site building -> the model must select from eligible ids, never write files or run commands; a sandboxed shell for the model contradicts 'constraint not generation'.
Skills marketplace / plugin fetch from GitHub at runtime -> playbooks must be versioned in-repo and human-reviewed; no runtime fetch of behaviour.
reusable_patterns: EventSourcedRunState: every state change is an immutable, typed, parent-linked event; current state and rationale are projections over the log.
DualBudgetGuard: a run is bounded by both a step counter and an accumulated-cost counter, each terminating with a typed event.
LoopSignatureDetector: a fixed window of recent events is scanned for k-fold identical (action, observation) or A-B-A-B signatures; first hit injects a nudge, second hit terminates.
TriggeredKnowledgeInjection: knowledge files declare keyword and path triggers in frontmatter and are added to the prompt only when a trigger fires.
RiskThresholdConfirmation: actions carry a predicted risk level; a policy object decides whether to pause for a human based on a threshold, independent of UI.
WorkspaceBoundary: the agent loop talks to a small execute/upload/download/git interface; local, Docker and remote implementations are interchangeable.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not run the Python SDK; re-implement four small mechanisms in TypeScript: (1) an append-only `run_events` table (id, run_id, parent_id, type, payload jsonb, cost) with a Zod discriminated union of event types, (2) a run status enum copied verbatim (IDLE/RUNNING/PAUSED/WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION/FINISHED/ERROR/STUCK), (3) a budget guard that reads accumulated cost from the log and aborts, (4) a repeat-selection detector for the three constrained model calls. Copy the skills trigger semantics (whole-token keywords + path globs in frontmatter) into the niche-playbook loader. Answer to 'is a full agent framework warranted?': no. Our pipeline is a linear DAG with three or four bounded model calls; OpenHands' value is in the 20% of it that is a durable log + limits, which is ~400 lines of TS, and the other 80% (shell, editor, browser, condensers, critic, MCP) is for open-ended coding agents we do not want.

core_problem: Provide an actor-model runtime (autogen-core: typed message passing, topics/subscriptions, distributed or single-threaded) and, on top of it, an opinionated multi-agent chat layer (autogen-agentchat: teams with turn-taking strategies and composable termination conditions) for LLM agents that talk to each other.
architecture: python/packages/autogen-core/src/autogen_core: `AgentRuntime` Protocol (_agent_runtime.py) with send_message (RPC to an AgentId), publish_message (to a TopicId), register_factory/register_agent_instance; agents are `RoutedAgent` subclasses with @message_handler dispatch by message type; subscriptions map topic types to agent types (TypeSubscription, TypePrefixSubscription); `SingleThreadedAgentRuntime` processes an async queue, a gRPC runtime exists in autogen-ext for distributed use; `InterventionHandler` (_intervention.py) exposes on_send/on_publish/on_response and can return DropMessage, i.e. a runtime-level middleware for confirmation or filtering; `CancellationToken`; `Component` config system (_component_config.py: dump_component/load_component to a versioned ComponentModel with provider path, so a whole team is serializable to JSON and re-loadable). code_executor/ interface with local, docker, docker_jupyter, jupyter and azure executors in autogen-ext. autogen-agentchat: BaseChatAgent/AssistantAgent (tool calling, model_context, memory), UserProxyAgent (input_func for human input), teams in teams/_group_chat: RoundRobinGroupChat, SelectorGroupChat (LLM or custom selector_func picks next speaker), Swarm (handoff messages route control), MagenticOneGroupChat (orchestrator with ledger), and GraphFlow (_graph/_digraph_group_chat.py: DiGraph of DiGraphNode with activation 'all'|'any' and DiGraphEdge with condition; DiGraphBuilder add_node/add_edge/add_conditional_edges/set_entry_point/build; cycles allowed with exit conditions). Termination (conditions/_terminations.py): TerminationCondition is composable with & and | (AndTerminationCondition/OrTerminationCondition); implementations MaxMessage, TextMention, TokenUsage, Timeout, StopMessage, Handoff, External, SourceMatch, TextMessage, FunctionCall, Functional. Teams expose save_state/load_state (Mapping) and pause/resume/reset; state is a dict, not an event log. Also in repo: autogen-studio (web UI), agbench, magentic-one; a .NET implementation under dotnet/. Python and .NET; no TypeScript.
core_innovation: Separating a language-agnostic actor runtime (typed messages, topics, interventions) from the chat-team layer, and making run termination a composable boolean algebra of conditions (max messages & token usage | text mention).
strengths: Composable termination conditions (&, |) over messages, tokens, wall-clock, external signals are a clean, declarative way to express 'stop when'.
InterventionHandler is a runtime-level middleware: every send/publish/response can be inspected, rewritten or dropped without touching agents.
Component serialization (dump_component/load_component with provider + version) makes whole team configurations versioned data.
GraphFlow shows that even a chat-framework converged on explicit DAGs with activation all/any and conditional edges.
Docker/Jupyter code executors with a small CodeExecutor interface.
weaknesses: Maintenance mode, community-managed, no new features; Microsoft directs new work to Microsoft Agent Framework. Building on it means adopting an orphaned API.
Python (and .NET) only; no TypeScript.
Chat-centric: the unit of work is a message in a group conversation, and turn-taking (Selector, Swarm) is decided by an LLM; that is model-narrated orchestration, rejected for us.
State is a dict snapshot per team (save_state/load_state), not an event log; no checkpoint-per-step, no time travel, no cost budget except TokenUsageTermination.
No structured-output validation/retry at the framework level; no stuck detection beyond termination conditions.
Root license CC-BY-4.0 causes tooling confusion (GitHub reports the repo as CC-BY-4.0) even though code is MIT; docs content is CC-BY-4.0, so copying doc text needs attribution.
patterns_to_steal: Composable termination algebra (MaxMessage & TokenUsage | ExternalTermination) -> agent_orchestration: express run limits as a small set of predicate objects combined with and/or (max_model_calls AND max_cost OR owner_cancel), evaluated by code after every stage.

InterventionHandler on_send/on_publish returning DropMessage -> qa_gate / anti_slop: a middleware layer between the model-call wrapper and the assembler that can drop or rewrite any model output that fails tier-1 regex bans before it reaches the state.

ComponentModel (provider, version, config) serialization -> design_system / playbooks: version every configurable object (design system, playbook, archetype) with an explicit schema version and a loader that can migrate past versions (_from_config_past_version).
GraphFlow activation 'all' vs 'any' on nodes -> agent_orchestration: assembly waits for ALL section selections; gap report can fire on ANY gate failure.
patterns_to_avoid: SelectorGroupChat/Swarm/MagenticOne (LLM picks next speaker, ledger-driven orchestrator) -> model-driven control flow contradicts 'code decides, model selects'.
Adopting autogen-core actor runtime -> a Python message bus for a linear TypeScript pipeline; also end-of-life.
Team-level dict save_state as the persistence model -> we want an append-only event log plus per-stage checkpoints for traceability.
reusable_patterns: TerminationAlgebra: stop conditions are objects composed with and/or and evaluated over the run history.
RuntimeIntervention: a middleware hook on every message send/publish that can rewrite or drop it.
VersionedComponentConfig: every pluggable object serializes to {provider, version, config} and can be reloaded and migrated.
ActivationPolicyNode: a DAG node declares whether it fires when all or any of its predecessors complete.
adoption_strategy: Ignore. It is in maintenance mode, Python/.NET only, chat-centric with LLM-selected turn-taking, and offers no durable checkpointing or output validation. Its only transferable ideas (composable termination predicates, a message intervention hook, versioned component configs) are each a few dozen lines in TypeScript and are documented here so the architect can implement them without the dependency. If Microsoft's direction matters to the team, evaluate Microsoft Agent Framework separately, but it is also Python/.NET and not a fit for an Astro/TS pipeline.

status_note: active; now a uv monorepo (lib/crewai, lib/crewai-core, lib/crewai-tools, lib/crewai-files, lib/cli); commercial 'CrewAI AMP/Plus' hooks (plus_api.py, telemetry, a2a) are present in the OSS package.
core_problem: Orchestrate role-playing LLM agents over a list of Tasks (sequential or manager-driven), with structured task outputs, guardrail validation with retries, memory and knowledge retrieval; and, via Flows, wrap those crews in deterministic event-driven Python orchestration with persisted state.
architecture: Core types in lib/crewai/src/crewai: Agent (agent/core.py, 2.2k lines; role/goal/backstory, max_iter, max_rpm, max_execution_time, max_retry_limit, tools, knowledge_sources, memory) executes a Task via agents/crew_agent_executor.py (ReAct-style loop, parser.py for 'Thought/Action/Final Answer', tools_handler, human feedback hook via core/providers/human_input). Task (task.py, 1.5k lines) declares description/expected_output/context/output_json/output_pydantic/response_model/output_file/guardrail(s)/guardrail_max_retries(3)/human_input. Output validation: `_export_output` calls utilities/converter.py `convert_to_model` which tries direct JSON parse, then `handle_partial_json`, then `convert_with_instructions` via InternalInstructor with `max_attempts`; guardrail loop `_invoke_guardrail_function` runs each GuardrailCallable `(TaskOutput) -> (bool, Any)` up to guardrail_max_retries+1 times, and on failure re-executes the agent with the error appended as I18N 'validation_error' context, tracking per-guardrail retry counts; a string guardrail becomes tasks/llm_guardrail.py LLMGuardrail (LiteAgent returning LLMGuardrailResult valid/feedback); tasks/hallucination_guardrail.py scores faithfulness 0-10 against a context with a threshold. Crew (crew.py, 2.6k lines) with Process enum sequential|hierarchical (process.py; consensual is a TODO); hierarchical requires manager_llm or manager_agent and routes every task through the manager; optional `planning=True` runs utilities/planning_handler.CrewPlanner to prepend a plan. Flow (flow/*): decorators @start/@listen/@router with or_()/and_() conditions (flow_wrappers.py, FlowConditionType OR|AND), a pydantic FlowDefinition (flow_definition.py) that also supports a declarative YAML/JSON form with Code/Tool/Crew/Agent/Expression/Script/Each actions and CEL expressions validated at load; runtime (flow/runtime/__init__.py) fires listeners when their trigger sets are satisfied, routers emit string labels that re-arm listeners; state is a dict, a pydantic model or a JSON schema; persistence via flow/persistence (FlowPersistence ABC, SQLite impl: save_state/load_state/save_pending_feedback/load_pending_feedback) and `Flow.from_pending(flow_id)` resumes a flow paused for async human feedback (flow/human_feedback.py, async_feedback/). Checkpoints (state/checkpoint_config.py CheckpointConfig on_events/provider json|sqlite/max_checkpoints/restore_from) snapshot crew execution. Memory (memory/unified_memory.py) is an LLM-scoped store (scope inferred by LLM, LanceDB/Qdrant backends, RecallFlow adaptive depth); Knowledge (knowledge/*) wraps file/CSV/PDF/JSON/Docling sources with an embedder and a storage backend. Tools: BaseTool pydantic args_schema; crewai-tools package plus MCP. Adapters exist for LangGraph and OpenAI Agents SDK agents. Python only; no TypeScript port.
core_innovation: A per-task validation contract: a Task declares a pydantic output schema and a list of pure guardrail callables, and the executor re-runs the agent with the guardrail's error text as feedback until it passes or a bounded retry count is exhausted.
strengths: Guardrail retry loop is explicit, bounded (guardrail_max_retries) and composable (list of callables, per-guardrail counters); the failure message is fed back verbatim to the next attempt.
Structured output has a three-stage fallback (direct parse -> partial JSON repair -> instructor re-ask), each bounded by max_attempts.
Flow gives a deterministic, inspectable DAG (start/listen/router, or_/and_) around LLM steps, with a declarative definition object that can be validated and rendered.
Flow persistence + from_pending is a real, simple human-in-the-loop resume: state and pending feedback are saved, the process can exit, and a later process resumes.
Agent-level limits are complete: max_iter, max_rpm (rate limiter), max_execution_time (timeout), max_retry_limit.
weaknesses: Python only; adopting it means a second runtime and a large dependency tree (litellm, chromadb/lancedb, instructor, docling) for a pipeline whose model calls are a handful of JSON selections.
Role-play prompting (role/goal/backstory, 'You are an expert...') is aspirational prompting by construction, which we have rejected; quality is not enforced by code.
Hierarchical process and planning delegate control to a manager LLM, i.e. model-narrated orchestration, the opposite of our constraint-first principle.
LLMGuardrail and HallucinationGuardrail are LLM-judge gates with numeric thresholds (rejected pattern); only the callable guardrails are deterministic.
Memory infers scope/importance with an LLM on every save; unified memory and Knowledge are RAG machinery we do not need (FactRegistry is typed and curated, not embedded).

Codebase is large and coupled (crew.py 2.6k, agent/core.py 2.2k, task.py 1.5k lines, telemetry and Plus API baked in); frequent breaking changes (deprecated max_retries, response_model vs output_pydantic overlap).
patterns_to_steal: Guardrail contract `(output) -> (ok, resultOrError)` with a bounded retry loop that re-invokes the model with the error text -> creative_direction, beat_selection, arrangement_selection, copy generation: each model call gets a Zod schema plus a list of pure guardrails (ids in eligible set, no banned n-grams, length limits) and at most N re-asks with the concrete violation appended; on exhaustion, fall back deterministically (service_clarity archetype / default arrangement), never accept.

Three-stage structured output coercion (parse -> repair partial JSON -> re-ask with schema instructions), each attempt-bounded -> the shared model-call wrapper; with Zod, stage 1 is safeParse, stage 2 is a tolerant JSON repair, stage 3 is a re-ask including the ZodError issues.

Per-guardrail retry counters and accumulated tool_failures kept across retries -> decision manifest / telemetry: record which guardrail fired, how many times, for which candidate id, so priors promotion can learn which playbooks cause retries.

Flow's declarative definition (FlowDefinition pydantic with validated step names and expressions) -> agent_orchestration: represent our pipeline as a static, validated stage list (Zod) with typed edges rather than code-only wiring, so the Decision Manifest can cite the stage graph.
Flow.from_pending(flow_id) with saved pending-feedback record -> gap_report / human review: pause a build at the gap report, persist a pending record, resume later in a fresh process.
patterns_to_avoid: Crew/Agent role-play with backstory and manager-LLM hierarchical process -> aspirational prompting and model-driven orchestration are both rejected; our orchestration is code.
LLMGuardrail (string guardrail -> LLM validator) and HallucinationGuardrail threshold -> LLM judge as a gate is rejected; keep LLM judging warning-only (anti-slop tier 2).
Unified Memory with LLM-inferred scopes and vector stores -> FactRegistry is typed, provenance-tracked and human-quotable; embedding-based recall would break traceability.
Knowledge sources (Docling/PDF/CSV RAG) for research -> research output must land in FactRegistry with provenance, not in an embedding store queried at generation time.
reusable_patterns: GuardrailRetryLoop: a list of pure predicates over a model output; failures are fed back as feedback and the call is retried at most N times, then a deterministic fallback is taken.
StagedOutputCoercion: parse strictly, then repair, then re-ask with schema errors, each stage bounded.
DeclarativeFlowDefinition: the orchestration graph is data (validated at load) rather than only code, enabling rendering, validation and audit.
PendingFeedbackResume: persist state plus a 'waiting for human' record so a later process can resume via an id.
AgentRateAndTimeLimits: max_iter, requests-per-minute and wall-clock timeout enforced at the executor, independent of prompts.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (pattern only; do not install crewAI). Write a ~150-line TypeScript `constrainedCall<T>(schema: ZodSchema<T>, guardrails: Guardrail<T>[], maxRetries=2)` that mirrors Task._invoke_guardrail_function + convert_to_model: safeParse, repair, re-ask with ZodError issues and guardrail messages, then deterministic fallback; log every attempt as a run event. Ignore Crew/Agent/Process/Memory/Knowledge entirely. Flows are the one orchestration idea worth noting, but LangGraph.js already gives the same start/listen/router semantics with checkpointing in TypeScript, so use that or a hand-rolled state machine instead of porting Flow. Is a full agent framework warranted? No; the guardrail loop is the only piece of crewAI our three constrained calls need.

status_note: active; Python monorepo (libs/langgraph, checkpoint, checkpoint-postgres, checkpoint-sqlite, prebuilt, cli, sdk-py). A first-party TypeScript port exists in langchain-ai/langgraphjs (@langchain/langgraph 1.4.x, MIT, pushed 2026-09-23) exporting StateGraph, Annotation, Send, Command, interrupt, MemorySaver plus checkpoint-postgres/sqlite/redis/mongodb packages.
core_problem: Execute a graph of steps over an explicitly typed state with per-key reducers, checkpoint the state after every superstep so runs are durable, resumable, interruptible for human input, forkable (time travel) and fan-out capable, independent of whether a step is an LLM call or plain code.
architecture: libs/langgraph/langgraph/graph/state.py `StateGraph(state_schema, context_schema, input_schema, output_schema)`: state is a TypedDict/pydantic/dataclass whose keys may be `Annotated[type, reducer]` (reducer signature (a, b) -> c, e.g. operator.add for lists); add_node (function or Runnable, with optional RetryPolicy/CachePolicy/destinations metadata), add_edge, add_conditional_edges(source, path_fn, path_map), add_sequence, compile(checkpointer, interrupt_before/after, store) -> CompiledStateGraph. Runtime is the Pregel model (pregel/main.py): each state key is a channel; a superstep runs all triggered nodes in parallel, collects writes, applies reducers, then persists a checkpoint. Checkpoint (libs/checkpoint/langgraph/checkpoint/base/__init__.py) is a TypedDict {v, id, ts, channel_values, channel_versions, versions_seen, updated_channels}; BaseCheckpointSaver has get_tuple/list/put/put_writes/delete_thread; implementations: MemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver (with a 'shallow' variant that keeps only the latest checkpoint per thread); keyed by thread_id and checkpoint_ns for subgraphs. Durability modes `sync|async|exit` (types.py) decide when checkpoints are written; `recursion_limit` (config, default 25 supersteps) raises GraphRecursionError. Control flow types (types.py): `Send(node, arg)` returned from a conditional edge dispatches N parallel invocations of one node with different inputs (map-reduce, results merged by a reducer); `Command(update=, goto=, resume=, graph=)` lets a node both write state and route, including to the parent graph; `interrupt(value, response_schema=)` raises GraphInterrupt, the checkpoint records the pending interrupt, and `invoke(Command(resume=...))` on the same thread_id re-enters the node with the human's value; `RetryPolicy(initial_interval, backoff_factor, max_attempts, retry_on)` and `CachePolicy(ttl)` are per node. Time travel: get_state, get_state_history (iterates checkpoints), update_state(config, values, as_node) forks a new checkpoint from any prior one; StateSnapshot carries values/next/tasks/interrupts. Subgraphs are compiled graphs used as nodes with their own checkpoint namespace. Streaming modes values/updates/checkpoints/tasks/messages/custom. The JS port mirrors this API (Annotation.Root for state schema, Zod schema support, same Send/Command/interrupt names).
core_innovation: Treating agent execution as Pregel-style supersteps over reducer-typed channels, so that a checkpoint written after every step makes pause, resume, human interrupts, fan-out and forking into properties of the runtime rather than features bolted onto a loop.
strengths: State schema is explicit and typed; reducers make concurrent writes deterministic (append vs overwrite is declared per key).
Checkpoint after every superstep, pluggable saver, and thread_id-based resumption make 'durable pipeline' the default, not extra work.
interrupt()/Command(resume=) is the cleanest human-in-the-loop primitive in the field: the node itself pauses, and the same code path resumes with the answer.
Send fan-out is exactly our per-section parallelism shape (N candidate beats -> N arrangement selections -> merged by reducer).
Time travel (update_state on a past checkpoint) enables re-running from 'arrangement selection' with a different playbook without re-doing research.
Deterministic nodes and LLM nodes are the same thing to the runtime; there is no requirement for an agent loop at all.
Available in TypeScript first-party with Postgres checkpointer; MIT.
weaknesses: Dependency weight: @langchain/langgraph pulls @langchain/core; the checkpoint serde and Runnable abstractions are heavier than our pipeline needs.

recursion_limit defaults to 25 supersteps and counts all nodes; our linear pipeline needs explicit limits per model-call node, which LangGraph does not provide (no per-node cost budget; RetryPolicy is about exceptions, not validation failures).
No stuck detection or cost budget: you must implement both as state keys checked by conditional edges.
Postgres checkpointer stores full channel_values per checkpoint (the 'shallow' saver mitigates); for a SiteDefinition of a few hundred kB this grows fast without pruning.
The JS port lags the Python one in places and its API has churned (Annotation vs Zod schemas, v0 to v1); LangChain's release cadence is a maintenance tax.
Framework semantics (channels, versions_seen, namespaces) are non-trivial to debug when something misbehaves; a hand-rolled 12-stage machine is simpler to reason about.
patterns_to_steal: Explicit state schema with per-key reducers -> agent_orchestration: define PipelineState as a Zod object (facts, eligibility_snapshot, playbook_id, positioning, creative_direction, beats[], arrangements[], site_definition, gate_results[], manifest) where list keys use an append reducer and scalar keys are overwrite-only; the Decision Manifest is derived from the snapshot.

Checkpoint-after-every-node keyed by thread_id + checkpoint_ns -> agent_orchestration: one Postgres row per (run_id, stage) holding the state snapshot; resuming a failed Lighthouse gate restarts at that stage.
interrupt(value) / Command(resume=) -> gap_report and owner-declared positioning: the pipeline literally pauses inside the positioning node until the owner declares; no polling flags.
Send(node, arg) fan-out with reducer merge -> beat_selection/arrangement: dispatch one constrained model call per section family in parallel and merge results by section id.
update_state on a prior checkpoint (time travel) -> telemetry / priors experiments: re-run from creative direction with a promoted prior and diff the resulting SiteDefinition against the original.

Per-node RetryPolicy(retry_on=...) with backoff -> the three model-call nodes and the Playwright/Lighthouse nodes (transient failures) get retry policies; validation failures are handled by the guardrail loop, not RetryPolicy.
patterns_to_avoid: Using the prebuilt ReAct agent (create_react_agent) or tool-calling loops -> our model calls select ids from eligible sets, they never call tools.

Cycles in the graph for 'self-improvement' (generate -> critique -> regenerate loops driven by an LLM judge) -> the fix loop is driven by deterministic gate results, bounded, and never by a model score.
Storing the full SiteDefinition in every checkpoint without pruning -> use shallow checkpoints plus an event log, keep large blobs in object storage referenced by hash.
Letting the graph structure be dynamic (Command(goto=) computed by a model) -> routing must be decided by code from predicate snapshots.
reusable_patterns: ReducerTypedState: each state key declares how concurrent/successive writes merge, making the state machine deterministic under parallelism.
SuperstepCheckpointing: persist a versioned snapshot after every node so any run can be resumed or forked from any step.
InterruptResume: a node can suspend the whole run with a payload and is re-entered with the human's response on the same thread id.
SendFanOut: a conditional edge returns N Send(node, input) objects to run a node N times in parallel, merged by reducers.
TimeTravelFork: writing to a historical checkpoint creates a new branch of execution without mutating history.
RecursionCeiling: a global superstep limit raises a typed error to prevent runaway graphs.
adoption_strategy: Adapt, with Adopt as a legitimate option. Honest sizing: our pipeline is a linear DAG of ~12 deterministic stages with 3 constrained model calls plus copy generation, one owner interrupt (positioning) and one fan-out (per-section selection). A hand-rolled TS state machine (Zod PipelineState, `stages: Stage[]` array, Postgres `run_checkpoints(run_id, stage, state jsonb, version)`, an `await waitForOwner()` implemented as status=WAITING + resume endpoint) is roughly 300-500 lines and has zero framework semantics to debug; that is the recommended V1. If the team prefers not to own resumption/fan-out code, `@langchain/langgraph` + `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` is the only framework in this batch that is TypeScript-native, MIT and matches our shape; use only StateGraph/Annotation/Send/interrupt/Command, never the prebuilt agents. Either way, copy the checkpoint schema (versioned snapshot per superstep with versions_seen) and the interrupt/resume contract exactly. A full agent framework is not warranted; a checkpointed state machine is enough.

status_note: active; redirects to agent0ai/agent-zero. Very high commit velocity; ships as a Docker image with a web UI, plugin system and many integrations (Telegram, WhatsApp, email, TTS/STT).
core_problem: A general-purpose personal agent whose entire behaviour is defined by editable markdown prompt files and Python extension hooks rather than hard-coded logic, running in a Docker container with hierarchical subordinate agents, vector memory and a web UI.
architecture: agent.py (1.6k lines): AgentContext (per chat; holds agent0, log, task, intervention routing) and Agent with the `monologue()` loop: for each iteration it runs extension points (monologue_start, message_loop_start, message_loop_prompts_before/after, before_main_llm_call, response_stream*, reasoning_stream*, message_loop_result, message_loop_end, monologue_end), builds the system prompt from prompt files, streams the model, extracts a JSON tool request (helpers/extract_tools), validates and executes the tool, and appends results to history; `handle_intervention()` is checked between every step so a user message can interrupt any running loop and is broadcast down the subordinate chain. Prompts: prompts/ holds 82 markdown files (agent.system.main.md composes role/specifics/environment/communication/solving/tips via `{{ include "file.md" }}`; fw.*.md are framework messages such as fw.msg_repeat.md, fw.msg_misformat.md, fw.msg_unusable_response_limit.md, fw.intervention.md; agent.system.tool.*.md document each tool). helpers/files.py `read_prompt_file`/`process_includes` resolve a file through an ordered list of directories (agent profile prompts dir first, then base prompts), support `{{include original}}` to pull the lower-priority version of the same file (override-and-extend), and inject kwargs into templates. Agent profiles: agents/<name>/agent.yaml (title, description, context) + agents/<name>/prompts/ overriding only the files they change (developer/, researcher/, hacker/, tiny-local/, agent0/, default/), plus optional per-profile tools/ and extensions/. Extensions: extensions/python/<hook_point>/_NN_name.py, discovered by helpers/extension.py, sorted by numeric prefix, each a class with async execute(); @extension.extensible wraps core methods so plugins can replace them; 30+ hook points including system_prompt (_10_main_prompt, _11_tools_prompt, _13_skills_prompt, _14_project_prompt), message_loop_prompts_after (_60_include_current_datetime, _63_recall_relevant_skills, _65_include_loaded_skills...), tool_execute_before/after, message_loop_result (_20_empty_response counts consecutive unusable responses against settings.max_consecutive_unusable_responses and raises HandledException at the limit; _30_repeat_response detects a response identical to the previous one and injects fw.msg_repeat.md). Plugins: plugins/_<name>/ (40 of them: _memory, _time_travel, _chat_branching, _chat_compaction, _orchestrator, _goal, _tool_access, _context_window, _error_retry, _plugin_validator...) bundle tools+extensions+webui panels; extensions/webui/ mirrors hook points for the front end. Tools: tools/*.py classes with a sidecar .dox.md; call_subordinate.py spawns a child Agent (number+1) with its own profile, parallel.py runs jobs concurrently, skills_tool.py loads SKILL.md folders (skills/), scheduler.py for cron-like tasks. Memory: FAISS via helpers/vector_db.py (plugin _memory), areas main/fragments/solutions/instruments; recall and memorize are extensions run at prompt time and monologue end. Runtime: docker/run (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, fs/ overlay) runs the whole agent + code execution in one container; run_ui.py Flask web UI with websocket. Python only; no structured-output schema enforcement (tool JSON parsed leniently, misformat -> warning prompt).
core_innovation: Behaviour-as-files: the agent has no hard-coded persona or procedure; a layered directory of markdown prompt fragments (with include/override semantics) plus numbered hook-point extension scripts fully define what the agent is, so a 'new agent' is a directory diff.
strengths: Prompt layering with directory precedence and `{{include original}}` gives override-and-extend semantics for behaviour files, diffable and versionable in git.
Hook points with numeric-ordered scripts are a simple, discoverable plugin model (drop a file in a folder); no registry code to edit.
Intervention checked between every loop step: a human can redirect a running agent (and its subordinates) at any time.
Concrete loop-health heuristics: repeated-identical-response detection and a consecutive-unusable-response limit, both configured in settings and expressed as prompt files.
Agent profiles (agent.yaml + prompt overrides) demonstrate cheap specialisation without code.
Skills (SKILL.md folders) recalled by relevance at iteration 0 only, keeping the system prompt small.
weaknesses: Python, Flask, FAISS, Docker-everything; the product is a personal assistant, not a library; there is no importable orchestration core.
No structured-output validation: tool requests are JSON parsed leniently and misformats become a prompt warning; no schema, no retry contract.

No cost budget, no iteration cap in the core loop (only the unusable-response limit and repeat detection), no checkpoints (the _time_travel and _chat_branching plugins branch chat history, not a typed state).
Memory is embedding-based with LLM-written summaries; no provenance.
Behaviour files are free-form prose that the model may or may not follow; correctness is not enforced by code, which is exactly the gap our 'constraint not generation' principle closes.

Extreme velocity and plugin sprawl (40 plugins, integrations for messaging apps) make the core harder to audit; security-review/ folder and _infection_check plugin hint at the attack surface of an agent that runs shell commands.
patterns_to_steal: Ordered-directory prompt resolution with `{{ include "x" }}` and `{{include original}}` -> niche playbooks and copy-generation prompts: a base prompt directory plus per-niche and per-archetype override directories, resolved by precedence, so a playbook overrides only the fragments it changes and can still include the base text; every fragment is a versioned file reviewed in PRs.

Numbered hook-point scripts (`<hook>/_NN_name`) -> anti_slop and qa_gate: implement tier-1 bans and QA checks as ordered files in `gates/anti_slop/_10_regex_bans.ts`, `_20_token_bans.ts`, `_30_layout_bans.ts`, discovered and run in order; adding a rule is adding a file.
Agent profile = agent.yaml + prompt overrides -> page archetypes and positioning: each archetype/positioning pair is a small YAML plus prompt-fragment overrides, not a code branch.

Repeat-response and consecutive-unusable-response counters expressed as settings -> the constrained model calls: identical selection twice or N unparsable outputs terminates the call and triggers the deterministic fallback.
Skill recall only at iteration 0 with a small limit -> creative_direction prompt: inject at most k relevant playbook fragments by keyword match, never the whole library.
patterns_to_avoid: Free-form prose behaviour files as the correctness mechanism -> our behaviour is enforced by predicates, Zod schemas and gates; prompt files only shape the constrained selections.
Hierarchical subordinate agents that delegate via natural language (call_subordinate) -> our fan-out is code-driven per section, not agent-to-agent delegation.
FAISS memory with LLM-written summaries -> FactRegistry with provenance is the memory.
Single container running agent + shell + browser with a web UI -> our model never executes commands; sandboxing is for Playwright/Lighthouse jobs only.
reusable_patterns: LayeredPromptDirectories: prompt fragments resolve through an ordered directory list with include and include-original semantics for override-and-extend.
NumberedHookScripts: extension behaviour is a folder per hook point containing ordered scripts discovered at load time.
ProfileAsOverlay: a named profile is a YAML descriptor plus a sparse overlay of files that override defaults.
InterventionCheckpoint: the loop polls for a human intervention between every step and propagates it to child processes.
UnusableResponseBudget: consecutive unparsable or repeated outputs are counted and terminate the loop at a configured limit.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not run agent-zero; copy two file-system conventions into the Astro/TS repo: (1) a prompt/playbook loader that resolves `{{ include }}` and `{{ include original }}` across ordered directories (base -> niche -> archetype), so playbooks are sparse overlays reviewed as diffs (this is roughly 80 lines of TS plus Zod frontmatter validation), and (2) numbered, folder-discovered gate scripts for the anti-slop and QA tiers. Copy the repeat/unusable counters into the constrained-call wrapper. Everything else (subordinate agents, FAISS memory, Docker-in-one, web UI, plugins) is out of scope. A full agent framework is not warranted; agent-zero is evidence that even open-ended agents end up governed by versioned files plus a handful of loop-health counters.

status_note: dormant; last commit 2025-01-22 (a merged PR), no releases or roadmap activity since; company pivoted to a hosted product. Not archived.
core_problem: A self-hosted platform (FastAPI + Celery + Postgres + Redis + Next.js GUI) to configure, run, schedule and monitor autonomous 'AutoGPT-style' agents with toolkits, marketplace templates and DB-defined workflows.
architecture: superagi/: FastAPI app (main.py, controllers/) with SQLAlchemy models (models/: Agent, AgentConfiguration key/value rows such as 'toolkits', 'permission_type', 'max_iterations', AgentExecution with status enum, AgentExecutionFeed, AgentExecutionPermission, AgentTemplate with marketplace_template_id, Toolkit, Resource, workflows/AgentWorkflowStep). Execution is a Celery worker (worker.py, jobs/) that runs one step per tick through superagi/agent/*: agent_iteration_step_handler.py builds the prompt (agent_prompt_builder.py, prompts/*.txt), calls the LLM, parses the reply with output_parser.py (AgentSchemaOutputParser: regex-extract a JSON block via helper/json_cleaner.JsonCleaner, ast.literal_eval fallback) and dispatches a tool via tool_executor.py; agent_tool_step_handler.py runs a fixed tool step; agent_workflow_step_wait_handler.py implements WAIT_STEP. Workflows are database graphs: AgentWorkflowStep rows have step_type TRIGGER|NORMAL, action_type TOOL|ITERATION_WORKFLOW|LLM|WAIT_STEP and a next_steps JSONB list of {step_id, step_response} edges; fetch_next_step picks the edge whose step_response matches the LLM's answer ('YES'/'NO'/'COMPLETE'); workflow_seed.py hard-codes the shipped workflows (e.g. build_sales_workflow with 11 steps). Human-in-the-loop: AgentConfiguration permission_type 'RESTRICTED' makes output_handler.py return WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION for non-excluded tools, and the execution stays in that status until a permission row is approved via controllers/agent_execution_permission.py. Tools (tools/*): BaseTool pydantic with args_schema and create_function_schema, grouped in toolkits (github, slack, jira, email, google_search, webscraper, image_generation, code...). resource_manager/: file_manager for uploads plus llama-index summaries (resource_summary.py) stored as vector docs. vector_store/ and vector_embeddings/ for knowledge search. GUI is a Next.js app in gui/ (package.json at root is for the GUI). Python 3.9-era code, LangChain 0.0.x pinned.
core_innovation: Modelling an agent's workflow as database rows with LLM-response-conditioned edges (next_steps JSONB keyed by 'YES'/'NO'/'COMPLETE'), so non-developers can compose branching agent workflows and share them as marketplace templates.
strengths: Execution status is a first-class DB enum (RUNNING, PAUSED, WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION, WAIT_STEP, COMPLETED...) and the worker is stateless per tick, so runs survive worker restarts.
Permission gating is a data setting (permission_type RESTRICTED) that pauses the execution row rather than a prompt instruction.
Workflow graph with response-conditioned edges is a genuinely declarative, inspectable control flow for its era.
Toolkits declare pydantic argument schemas, so tool calls are schema-checked.
weaknesses: Dormant since January 2025; pinned to ancient LangChain/OpenAI SDKs; Python 3.9 era; security-sensitive stack (Celery, Redis, Docker-compose) with no maintenance.
AutoGPT-style loop: the LLM emits free-form JSON 'thoughts/command' that is regex-cleaned; no schema-validated structured outputs, no retry on validation failure.
Workflow edges are selected by string-matching the LLM's answer ('YES'/'NO'), i.e. model-narrated control flow.
No stuck detection, no cost budget (only max_iterations config key), no checkpoint/time travel; feeds are append-only logs for display, not for replay.
Heavy infrastructure (Postgres + Redis + Celery + Next.js + optional local-LLM containers) for what is a single-agent loop.
Python and a separate React GUI; nothing reusable in our TypeScript stack.
patterns_to_steal: Execution status enum in the database including WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION and WAIT_STEP, with a stateless worker that advances one step per tick -> agent_orchestration: model our build run as a Postgres row with a status column and a worker that processes 'one stage per job', so owner input (positioning, gap report) is a status, not an in-memory await.
permission_type as a per-run data setting rather than prompt text -> qa_gate: a run-level 'auto_fix_policy' column (none | low_risk | all) decides which QA fixes apply without confirmation.
patterns_to_avoid: LLM-answer-string-matched workflow edges ('YES'/'NO') -> routing must come from predicate snapshots computed in code.
Regex JSON extraction (JsonCleaner) as the output contract -> use native structured outputs + Zod safeParse with bounded re-ask.
Marketplace templates fetched at runtime from a vendor URL -> playbooks are in-repo, versioned, human-reviewed.
Resource summaries via llama-index vector store as the agent's knowledge -> FactRegistry with provenance, not embeddings.
reusable_patterns: PersistedExecutionStatus: run state lives in a DB row with an explicit enum including human-wait states; workers are stateless.
DataDrivenPermissionGate: whether an action needs approval is a stored setting evaluated by code, not an instruction to the model.
adoption_strategy: Ignore. Dormant, Python, AutoGPT-era loop with regex-parsed outputs and LLM-string-matched branching; nothing here beats LangGraph or OpenHands on the mechanisms we need. The one salvageable idea, a DB-persisted execution status enum with WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION advanced by a stateless worker, is trivial to implement with our Postgres and is already implied by the OpenHands/LangGraph recommendations.

status_note: active; v0.13.10; Python >=3.11; talks to Chromium directly over CDP via the in-house cdp-use client (Playwright dependency removed); commercial cloud (browser-use.com) funds it and the codebase carries cloud/telemetry hooks (posthog, browser_use/sync, browser_use/cloud_events)
core_problem: Let an LLM complete open-ended tasks in a real browser by repeatedly serializing the page into a compact indexed list of interactive elements, asking the model for a structured batch of actions, executing them, and looping until a `done` action.
architecture: Python package browser_use/. browser/ owns a CDP session (cdp-use==1.4.5) with watchdogs (popups, downloads, crashes). dom/service.py (DomService.get_dom_tree) issues DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot (with REQUIRED_COMPUTED_STYLES), DOM.getDocument and Accessibility.getFullAXTree per frame, merges them into EnhancedDOMTreeNode (dom/views.py: bounds, computed styles, ax_node, has_js_click_listener, frame_id, backend_node_id) with iframe offset translation, max_iframes/max_iframe_depth limits and optional cross-origin iframe recursion. dom/serializer/serializer.py (DOMTreeSerializer.serialize_accessible_elements) runs: _create_simplified_tree (ClickableElementDetector.is_interactive heuristics in clickable_elements.py: js click listeners, tag/role/aria props, label/span wrappers of form controls, search-class heuristics), PaintOrderRemover (drops nodes covered by later paint), _optimize_tree, _apply_bounding_box_filtering (99% containment threshold collapses children of a/button/combobox), then _assign_interactive_indices_and_mark_new_nodes producing a selector_map {index -> node} and a text tree where interactive nodes render as `[12]<button ...>` with a `*` prefix when new since the last step; SVG collapsed, |SHADOW(open)|, |scroll element|, |IFRAME| markers, compound_components for sliders/selects. agent/service.py Agent.run/step builds messages via agent/prompts.py (AgentMessagePrompt with <browser_state>: url, tabs, stats, elements text, page_info, pending network requests) plus a screenshot (use_vision True|False|'auto'; auto exposes a `screenshot` tool the model calls on demand; llm_screenshot_size resize). The LLM must return AgentOutput (agent/views.py: thinking, evaluation_previous_goal, memory, next_goal, current_plan_item, plan_update, action: list[ActionModel]); ActionModel is a pydantic model synthesized at runtime by tools/registry/service.py create_action_model() from decorated functions in tools/service.py (search, navigate, go_back, wait, input, upload_file, switch, close, extract, search_page, find_elements, scroll, send_keys, find_text, screenshot, save_as_pdf, dropdown_options, select_dropdown, write_file, replace_file, read_file, evaluate, done, click), with domain filters and sensitive_data placeholder substitution. Flash mode strips thinking fields. ActionLoopDetector/PageFingerprint (url + element_count + sha256 of dom text) inject soft 'you are looping' hints. agent/judge.py runs an LLM judge over the trace + up to 10 screenshots. AgentHistoryList persists every step (DOMInteractedElement with element_hash, xpath, ax_name); Agent.rerun_history replays saved actions with _update_action_indices cascading matches EXACT hash -> STABLE hash (dynamic classes stripped) -> XPATH -> AX_NAME -> ATTRIBUTE, optionally re-running an LLM for extract steps. browser_use/mcp/server.py exposes browser_navigate/click/type/get_state/extract_content/get_html/screenshot/scroll/go_back/list_tabs as MCP tools. 37 runtime deps including every LLM SDK.
core_innovation: A CDP-level DOM+AX+paint-order fusion that yields a numbered, diff-marked clickable-element index small enough for an LLM to act on without vision, plus runtime-synthesized pydantic action schemas that constrain the model's output.
strengths: The serializer is the best-documented example of turning a live page into an LLM-sized, index-addressable state: paint-order occlusion removal, bbox containment collapse, `*` new-element markers, scroll and shadow/iframe markers, compound-component summaries.

Structured output contract: AgentOutput/ActionModel are pydantic schemas built from the tool registry, so the model can only emit registered actions with typed params; action registration is a decorator with domain allowlists.
Replay with cascading element matching (hash -> stable hash -> xpath -> ax name -> attribute) is a serious attempt at deterministic re-execution of an LLM-discovered path.
PageFingerprint + ActionLoopDetector are cheap, model-free stagnation detectors.
use_vision='auto' makes screenshots an on-demand tool rather than a per-step cost.
MCP server and judge module make it easy to bolt an 'act like a user, report friction' pass onto any site.
MIT, extremely active (116k stars, pushes weekly).
weaknesses: Python 3.11+ runtime with 37 dependencies including openai/anthropic/google-genai/groq/ollama SDKs, posthog telemetry and pyobjc; embedding in an Astro/TS pipeline means a sidecar process and a second toolchain.

Every step is an inference call over a full page serialization (often 5-20k tokens) plus optional screenshot; a 15-step 'book an appointment' run costs dollars and minutes, and the loop is non-deterministic across runs and models.

Clickability is heuristic (class-name search indicators like 'magnify', 'glass'; label/span wrapper rules) and tuned for arbitrary third-party sites; on our own generated markup we already know the interactive elements from the SiteDefinition.
Replay is best-effort: rerun_history has skip_failures, max_retries and re-invokes an LLM for extract steps, so it is not a deterministic gate.
The judge (agent/judge.py) is an LLM scoring a trace with screenshots, exactly the non-reproducible 'design critic' pattern we rejected.
Rapid API churn (0.x versions; Playwright removed in favour of cdp-use; flash_mode, judge, variable detection added recently); pinning is mandatory and upgrades are breaking.
Bypasses Playwright entirely, so none of its artifacts (trace.zip, reporter JSON, snapshots) integrate with the gate's evidence model.
patterns_to_steal: Indexed interactive-element serialization with new-element markers → agent_orchestration (optional explorer pass): if we ever run an LLM friction pass on a generated site, serialize from the SiteDefinition + Playwright ARIA snapshot in the same shape (`[n]<role name>` with `*` for changed nodes) rather than shipping raw DOM.

Runtime-synthesized action schema from a registry (create_action_model) → agent_orchestration: build the Zod schema for any model-facing selection step from the eligible set at runtime (eligible design_system_ids, arrangement ids) so the model cannot name an option code did not permit.
PageFingerprint (url + element count + text hash) → qa_gate: fingerprint each generated page's DOM text to detect 'identical section across pages' and to dedupe crawl results in the research stage.

Cascading element re-identification (exact hash -> stable hash -> xpath -> accessible name) → qa_gate replay: when a human-authored friction script must survive regeneration, resolve targets by data-slot/aria name first, xpath last.

Domain-scoped actions and sensitive_data placeholders → research: any crawler-side action registry should carry allowed_domains so a fact-ingestion agent physically cannot navigate outside the target list.
patterns_to_avoid: LLM judge over screenshots as pass/fail (agent/judge.py) → non-reproducible score; we already rejected design-critic gating. At most a warning-only tier-2 note.
Per-step full-page inference loop as a gate → cost, latency and non-determinism violate 'deterministic gate'; the gate is Playwright assertions, the agent loop is optional exploration.

Adopting the Python runtime as a pipeline dependency → second toolchain, telemetry hooks (posthog), heavy dep tree; if an explorer pass is wanted, Playwright MCP or Stagehand tool-calling in TS covers it.
Heuristic clickable detection on our own output → we own the markup; interactive elements are declared in SiteDefinition and verifiable via ARIA roles, no guessing needed.
reusable_patterns: IndexedElementState: page state for a model is a numbered list of interactive nodes with role, name, bounds-derived visibility and a changed-since-last-step marker.
RegistrySynthesizedSchema: the output schema handed to a model is generated at call time from the currently permitted action/option set.
PaintOrderOcclusionFilter: drop DOM nodes fully covered by later-painted nodes before serialization.
CascadingElementReidentification: replay resolves an element via a strict-to-loose ladder of identity keys.
SoftLoopDetector: hash actions and page fingerprints in a rolling window; inject a hint rather than blocking.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for the gate; optionally Adapt one idea. Do not add browser-use to the pipeline: it is a Python, LLM-per-step, non-deterministic agent whose judge is the rejected critic pattern, and its accessibility/DOM work duplicates what Playwright's ARIA snapshot and our own SiteDefinition already give us. If an 'act like a user, book an appointment, report friction' pass is wanted, run it in TypeScript with Playwright MCP or Stagehand tool-calling as a warning-only Gap Report input. The one mechanism worth re-implementing in Zod is registry-synthesized output schemas for model selection steps.
