status_note: active; v1.64.0-next on main; monorepo also ships @playwright/mcp (microsoft/playwright-mcp, 37.5k stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-09-18) and @playwright/cli as agent-facing front-ends
core_problem: Drive Chromium/Firefox/WebKit through one API with auto-waiting locators, and run tests in isolated contexts with a runner that carries fixtures, a project (device) matrix, retrying web-first assertions, pixel and ARIA snapshot comparison, tracing and pluggable reporters.
architecture: Monorepo under packages/*: playwright-core (server/ drivers over CDP/Juggler/WebKit protocol; server/screenshotter.ts does in-page prep: inject stylePath CSS, hide caret, disable/sync animations, mask locators with #F0F, then captures until two consecutive screenshots match), injected/ (scripts evaluated in the page: ariaSnapshot.ts builds the ARIA tree, ariaSnapshotDistiller.ts is a babel-style visitor chain that removes/unwraps nodes without losing refs), isomorphic/ariaSnapshot.ts (YAML-ish template parser: role, quoted-exact or /regex/ name, [level=], [checked], /url:, /children: equal|contain|deep-equal), playwright (the test runner: common/config.ts + configLoader.ts define TestConfig/TestProject/use options and snapshotPathTemplate; common/fixtures.ts + poolBuilder.ts implement test.extend() dependency-injected fixtures; runner/dispatcher.ts + processHost.ts run workers; matchers/toMatchSnapshot.ts implements both toMatchSnapshot and toHaveScreenshot with expected/actual/previous/diff file quartet, updateSnapshots modes all|changed|missing|none, maxDiffPixels and maxDiffPixelRatio combined via min(), comparator pixelmatch (threshold default 0.2) or ssim-cie94 from utils/comparators.ts; matchers/toMatchAriaSnapshot.ts diffs against a .aria.yml or inline template), reporters/ (json.ts, html.ts, blob.ts for sharded merge, junit, github, perfetto; all implement types/testReporter.d.ts Reporter with TestResult{status, errors, attachments[], steps[], annotations[]}), trace-viewer and html-reporter (web UIs reading trace.zip actions + DOM snapshots + network + console). Extension points: fixtures (worker- and test-scoped), projects with dependencies, custom reporters, expect.extend, page.route/context.route for network stubbing, page.emulateMedia for media features, page.on('console'|'pageerror'|'requestfailed'). @axe-core/playwright is a separate deque package that injects axe into the page and exposes AxeBuilder.withTags/include/exclude/disableRules/analyze(). Playwright MCP exposes browser_snapshot (accessibility tree with refs), browser_click(ref), browser_console_messages, browser_network_requests, opt-in --caps=testing browser_verify_* assertions, --caps=vision coordinate mode, --save-trace.
core_innovation: Web-first, auto-retrying assertions over an accessibility-tree model of the page, plus a snapshot/trace pipeline that turns every check into reproducible artifacts (PNG quartet, ARIA YAML, trace.zip) rather than opinions.
strengths: Deterministic gate primitives already exist: toHaveScreenshot (pixelmatch/ssim with numeric thresholds), toMatchAriaSnapshot (structural a11y assertion with regex and partial matching), page.route (block third-party / assert zero external requests), emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce', colorScheme, forcedColors}), keyboard.press('Tab') + toBeFocused for tab order, page.on('console'/'pageerror') for zero-console-error checks.

Project matrix: projects[] with devices['Pixel 5'|'iPhone 12'|'Desktop Chrome'] and per-project use{} gives one spec file x N viewports/browsers with snapshot names templated by {projectName}/{platform}; project dependencies model setup-before-gate.

Screenshot stabilization is engineered, not ad hoc: stylePath injection, caret hide, animations disabled, masks, and capture-until-two-consecutive-identical; diff artifacts (expected/actual/previous/diff) attach to the report.

Reporter model is data-first: JSON reporter and the Reporter interface expose per-test status/errors/attachments/steps/annotations, which is exactly what a 60+ check gate report needs to be assembled from; blob reporter + merge-reports handles sharded runs.
trace.zip captures actions, DOM snapshots, network and console; it is the evidence bundle for a Gap Report or a fix loop.

Playwright MCP (accessibility snapshot with element refs, no vision needed) gives an LLM a token-cheap way to explore a generated site; --caps=testing adds verify_* tools; Apache-2.0 and Microsoft-maintained.
Apache-2.0, huge ecosystem, weekly releases, first-party TypeScript types; matches our Astro/TS stack with zero runtime bridge.
weaknesses: Visual snapshots are platform-specific (fonts/rendering differ per OS/browser); baselines must be generated in the same container image as the gate or maxDiffPixelRatio has to be loosened until it means little.

Snapshots default to a previous-build baseline model (test-file-snapshots dir, --update-snapshots); nothing in the runner understands 'reference render per arrangement', so that layer is ours to build via snapshotPathTemplate and a custom fixture.

toHaveScreenshot is for full or clipped page pixels; it cannot express layout intent (approx_vh, focal_weight, density). Those need DOM-measurement assertions we write with locator.boundingBox() and page.evaluate.
ARIA snapshot format is Playwright-specific YAML, not a standard; it drifts across versions (distiller plugins change verbosity), so pin the version and regenerate reference snapshots on upgrade.
axe integration is third-party (@axe-core/playwright, MPL-2.0 for axe-core); axe only catches ~30-40% of WCAG issues automatically, so an axe-clean page is a floor not a certificate.

The runner is opinionated (worker processes, its own expect, config discovery); embedding it programmatically inside an agent pipeline means shelling out to `playwright test --reporter=json` and parsing, not calling a library function.
Monorepo is 240 MB; browser binaries add ~1 GB per browser; CI images must pre-bake mcr.microsoft.com/playwright to keep gate runs fast.
patterns_to_steal: Project matrix (projects[] x devices[]) → qa_gate: one gate spec, projects = {desktop-chrome, mobile-safari(iPhone 12), tablet, reduced-motion(use: {reducedMotion:'reduce'}), dark(colorScheme:'dark')}; snapshotPathTemplate = '{testDir}/__refs__/{arg}/{projectName}{ext}'.

Reference-per-arrangement baselines → qa_gate + section library: at library authoring time render each arrangement (variant x arrangement x design_system_id) with fixture content and commit the PNG + .aria.yml as the reference; the gate compares the generated section against that reference with maxDiffPixelRatio tuned per arrangement (stored on the arrangement YAML as visual_tolerance) and masks for content slots (mask: [locator('[data-slot]')]).

toMatchAriaSnapshot with partial templates → qa_gate + anti_slop: each section variant carries an a11y template (heading level, landmark roles, link count, /url patterns) authored once; the generated page must contain it (/children: contain), which asserts structure without pixels.

expect/attachments/steps data model → decision manifest + gap report: run with reporter=[['json',{outputFile}],['html',{open:'never'}]], map every gate check to a test.step() so the JSON has 60+ named steps with status and attachments; the Gap Report is derived from failed steps, never narrated.

page.route + page.on('console'|'pageerror'|'requestfailed') → qa_gate: assert zero console errors, zero failed requests, zero requests to non-allowlisted origins (the 180 kB JS budget is enforced by summing response sizes of script requests via page.on('response')).

emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) + toHaveScreenshot → motion: the static poster fallback must be pixel-identical to the reference under reduced motion; also assert no element has running animations via page.evaluate(() => document.getAnimations().length).

Fixtures (test.extend) → qa_gate: a `site` fixture that boots the Astro preview server (webServer config), a `axe` fixture that pre-configures AxeBuilder.withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa']).exclude('[data-known-issue]'), a `refs` fixture that resolves the reference render path per arrangement id.

Playwright MCP accessibility snapshot → agent_orchestration (optional, warning-only): let a model explore the generated site via browser_snapshot/browser_click and emit friction notes; never let it gate, only feed the Gap Report as 'model observation'.
patterns_to_avoid: Previous-build snapshot baselines (--update-snapshots after each build) → for generated sites every build is new, so the baseline must be the library-time reference render, not the last output; otherwise the gate rubber-stamps drift.
Loosening maxDiffPixelRatio globally to cope with font/OS differences → destroys the meaning of the check; instead pin the gate to one container image and generate references in the same image.
Full-page toHaveScreenshot as the only visual check → a single ratio hides which section broke; compare per-section locators with per-arrangement tolerances.
Vision-mode MCP (--caps=vision, coordinate clicks) → non-deterministic and token-heavy; accessibility snapshot mode only.
Using the trace viewer or HTML report as the artifact of record → they are for humans; the JSON reporter output (or a custom Reporter) is the machine artifact the Decision Manifest consumes.
reusable_patterns: DeviceProjectMatrix: one spec, N projects each with a devices[] preset plus media emulation; snapshot names templated by project so references are per-device.
ReferenceRenderBaseline: visual regression baseline is a canonical render produced when the section library was authored, keyed by (arrangement_id, design_system_id, project), not the previous build.
StabilizedCapture: before pixel capture inject CSS, hide caret, disable animations, mask dynamic slots, capture until two consecutive frames match.
StructuralA11yTemplate: an authored partial ARIA-tree template per section variant asserted with contain semantics, decoupling structure checks from pixels.
StepAsCheck: every gate check is a named test.step with attachments so the reporter JSON is the gate report; failures map 1:1 to Gap Report lines.
NetworkAllowlistGate: page.route blocks and records every request; the gate asserts origin allowlist, zero failures, and byte budgets from response sizes.
adoption_strategy: Adopt. Use @playwright/test directly as the Launch QA gate runtime: a single gate.spec.ts with projects for desktop/mobile/tablet/reduced-motion/dark, fixtures for the Astro preview server and AxeBuilder, per-section toHaveScreenshot against library-time reference renders (snapshotPathTemplate keyed on arrangement id and project), toMatchAriaSnapshot against per-variant structural templates, page.route/console/pageerror listeners for network and console cleanliness, and JSON reporter output parsed into the Decision Manifest and Gap Report. Pin the Playwright version and run the gate in the official mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image so references and actuals share fonts. Treat Playwright MCP as an optional warning-only explorer for the agentic 'act like a user' pass, never as a gate.
evidence: packages/playwright/src/matchers/toMatchSnapshot.ts (SnapshotHelper: expectedPath/actualPath/previousPath/diffPath, updateSnapshots modes, maxDiffPixels validation, toHaveScreenshot options animations/caret/scale/stylePath/mask/maskColor/omitBackground/fullPage/clip, _expectScreenshot loop)

status_note: active; v0.9.3; Python >=3.10; single-maintainer-led project with a large contributor base; ships a FastAPI Docker server (deploy/docker) with browser pool, Redis job queue, JWT auth, MCP bridge and Prometheus metrics
core_problem: Fetch web pages with a real browser (or plain HTTP), strip them to LLM-ready markdown or schema-extracted JSON, and crawl outward with pluggable strategies, filters and scorers, all behind a single async API and a Docker REST service.
architecture: crawl4ai/async_webcrawler.py AsyncWebCrawler.arun(url, config) orchestrates: optional robots check (RobotsParser, only when CrawlerRunConfig.check_robots_txt=True; default False), cache lookup (async_database.py SQLite; cache_context.CacheMode ENABLED/DISABLED/READ_ONLY/WRITE_ONLY/BYPASS, default BYPASS; cache_validator.py revalidates via ETag/If-None-Match and a head_fingerprint), fetch via async_crawler_strategy.py (AsyncPlaywrightCrawlerStrategy over playwright/patchright with browser_manager.py pools, enable_stealth via playwright-stealth, use_undetected mode, proxy_strategy rotation, user_agent_generator, virtual scroll, js_code hooks, capture_network_requests/capture_console_messages, screenshot/pdf/mhtml) or AsyncHTTPCrawlerStrategy, then content_scraping_strategy.py (LXMLWebScrapingStrategy: cleaned_html, links{internal,external}, media, metadata, tables), markdown_generation_strategy.py (DefaultMarkdownGenerator over html2text with content_source raw_html|cleaned_html|fit_html; convert_links_to_citations produces markdown_with_citations + references_markdown; an optional content_filter produces fit_html/fit_markdown), content_filter_strategy.py (PruningContentFilter: per-block score from text density, link density, tag weights with fixed or dynamic threshold default 0.48; BM25ContentFilter: rank-bm25 against user_query or page metadata; LLMContentFilter), and extraction_strategy.py (JsonCssExtractionStrategy / JsonXPathExtractionStrategy / JsonLxmlExtractionStrategy over a schema {baseSelector, fields:[{name, selector, type: text|attribute|html|nested|list|nested_list|computed|regex}]} with schema validation feedback when baseSelector matches 0 elements and a generate_schema() LLM helper; LLMExtractionStrategy chunks markdown/html by token threshold and calls litellm with a pydantic schema or block instruction, accumulating usages; RegexExtractionStrategy; CosineStrategy). Results are models.CrawlResult (url, html, cleaned_html, fit_html, markdown.{raw,fit,with_citations,references}, links, media, tables, metadata, extracted_content, screenshot, pdf, response_headers, status_code, redirected_url, ssl_certificate, network_requests, console_messages, head_fingerprint, cached_at, cache_status hit|hit_validated|hit_fallback|miss). deep_crawling/: BFSDeepCrawlStrategy, DFSDeepCrawlStrategy, BestFirstCrawlingStrategy with FilterChain (URLPatternFilter, DomainFilter, ContentTypeFilter, ContentRelevanceFilter, SEOFilter) and scorers (KeywordRelevanceScorer, PathDepthScorer, ContentTypeScorer, FreshnessScorer, DomainAuthorityScorer, CompositeScorer); async_dispatcher.py runs arun_many with memory-adaptive concurrency; async_url_seeder.py discovers URLs from sitemaps (robots -> sitemap chain) and Common Crawl index with lastmod-aware caching; adaptive_crawler.py stops when information-foraging coverage saturates; domain_mapper.py builds site maps; link_preview.py scores links. async_configs.py holds BrowserConfig, CrawlerRunConfig (~120 params), LLMConfig, SeedingConfig; a Provenance TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED enum plus UNTRUSTED_ALLOWED_TYPES restricts what a network request body may deserialize on the Docker server (no LLM strategies, proxies, deep-crawl or seeding from untrusted callers). deploy/docker/server.py exposes /crawl, /crawl/stream, /md, /html, /screenshot, /pdf, /execute_js, /llm/{url}, /ask, /schema, /artifacts, /monitor, with crawler_pool.py (permanent/hot/cold browsers), work_queue.py + Redis, webhook.py, mcp_bridge.py, and llm_broker.py.
core_innovation: A crawl result object that carries the page in several parallel, provenance-preserving forms (raw html, cleaned html, fit markdown with citation references, schema-extracted JSON, network/console/ssl evidence) so downstream code can choose the strictest form it needs.
strengths: Deterministic, LLM-free extraction path exists end to end: JsonCssExtractionStrategy with a JSON schema, PruningContentFilter/BM25ContentFilter for fit markdown, and markdown_with_citations that keeps a numbered references list of source URLs, which is exactly what a FactRegistry with `external` provenance needs.

CrawlResult keeps evidence: status_code, response_headers, redirected_url, ssl_certificate, cached_at, cache_status, head_fingerprint; a fact can be stamped with url + fetched_at + http status without extra plumbing.

Deep crawl is a composable pipeline (strategy x FilterChain x scorer) with hard budgets (max_depth, max_pages, DomainFilter) so a competitor-site sample for a niche playbook can be bounded and reproducible.
URL seeding from sitemaps/Common Crawl with lastmod caching gives cheap, polite discovery before any browser is opened; HTTP crawler strategy avoids a browser entirely for static pages.

Docker server is a real service: browser pool, Redis job queue, JWT, Prometheus, and a Provenance/UNTRUSTED allowlist that blocks LLM/proxy/deep-crawl configs from network callers, a good security posture for a sidecar.
Apache-2.0, 84k stars, weekly pushes, extensive docs and CHANGELOG.
weaknesses: Python 3.10+ runtime with 34 deps (playwright, patchright, playwright-stealth, nltk, numpy, lxml, unclecode-litellm fork, shapely/alphashape) and its own browser install; in an Astro/TS pipeline it must run as the Docker sidecar over REST, adding an ops surface.

Anti-bot posture is aggressive by default design (patchright, undetected mode, enable_stealth, user-agent spoofing, magic mode, remove_consent_popups) and robots.txt is opt-in (check_robots_txt=False); using these against competitor sites or Google SERPs is a ToS and reputational risk for an agency product. Google search results scraping violates Google's ToS; GBP data should come from the Places API, not scraping.

LLMExtractionStrategy and generate_schema() are convenience paths that can hallucinate fields; nothing in the library marks which extracted values are literal DOM text versus model output, so provenance must be enforced by us (use only JsonCss/XPath/Regex strategies for facts).

PruningContentFilter and BM25 are heuristic; 'fit markdown' can silently drop the paragraph that held the fact (thresholds 0.48 fixed / dynamic), so facts must be extracted from cleaned_html or raw_html with selectors, not from fit_markdown.
Very large, fast-moving surface (CrawlerRunConfig ~120 params, 2.5k-line config module, adaptive crawler, domain mapper, hub) with breaking minor releases; pin versions and wrap a small facade.
Cache is a local SQLite keyed on URL; no built-in notion of 'fact-level' freshness beyond ETag/head fingerprint, so fetched_at semantics and re-verification cadence are ours to define.
The README's attribution request (badge/text) is not part of the Apache-2.0 grant but is a community expectation; harmless but note it.
patterns_to_steal: CrawlResult multi-form record with evidence fields → fact_registry: define FactSource {url, final_url (redirected_url), status_code, fetched_at (cached_at), etag/head_fingerprint, content_hash, extraction: 'css'|'xpath'|'regex'} and require every `external` Fact to reference one; no FactSource, no Fact.

markdown_with_citations + references_markdown → fact_registry + research: keep the numbered citation map so every quoted claim in a niche playbook draft links back to the exact source URL; quotable=false unless the DOM text is captured verbatim.

JsonCssExtractionStrategy schema {baseSelector, fields[]} with validation feedback → research: author per-source-type extraction schemas (registry pages, association directories, competitor service pages) as versioned YAML in the playbook repo; a schema that matches 0 base elements fails loudly and never returns fabricated fields.

Deep crawl = strategy x FilterChain x scorers with max_depth/max_pages/DomainFilter → research: the competitor-sample job for a niche playbook is a BestFirst crawl bounded to N pages per domain with KeywordRelevanceScorer on service terms, recorded with its config hash so the sample is reproducible for drift review.
Sitemap/Common Crawl seeding with lastmod caching → research drift review: re-check competitor sitemaps by lastmod before re-crawling; drift review only refetches pages whose lastmod or ETag changed.

Provenance TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED config allowlist → agent_orchestration: any config the model or a network caller can produce is deserialized through an allowlist that cannot enable LLM strategies, proxies or unbounded crawls; the same idea applies to model-emitted SiteDefinition patches.
CacheMode + ETag revalidation → fact_registry freshness: store etag/head_fingerprint with each FactSource and revalidate with If-None-Match on a schedule; a 304 renews fetched_at without re-parsing.
patterns_to_avoid: Stealth/undetected/patchright/user-agent spoofing and remove_consent_popups against third-party sites → ToS and ethics exposure for a commercial agency; run with check_robots_txt=True, honest UA, rate limits (mean_delay/max_range), and never bypass bot detection.

Scraping Google SERPs or Google Business Profile pages for 'SERP sampling' or GBP facts → violates Google ToS; use official APIs (Custom Search JSON API, Places API) or licensed SERP providers and record the API as the FactSource.

LLMExtractionStrategy / LLMContentFilter / generate_schema for facts → model-produced values are not provenance-safe; allowed only for exploratory summaries flagged non-quotable and never written to the FactRegistry as `external` facts.
Using fit_markdown as the fact source → pruning can drop the sentence containing the number; extract from cleaned_html via selectors and store the verbatim snippet.

Crawling competitor sites to clone layouts/tokens → explicitly rejected website-cloner pipeline; Crawl4AI is for text facts, positioning language and service inventories only, never screenshots-to-design.
Adopting the whole Docker service surface (/llm, /ask, MCP bridge, hooks) → keep a narrow facade: /crawl with JsonCss schemas and /md with citations; disable LLM endpoints in config.yml.
reusable_patterns: EvidenceBearingFetchRecord: every fetch yields one record carrying the content in multiple fidelities plus transport evidence (status, headers, redirect, tls, timestamps, hashes).
CitationPreservingMarkdown: convert links to numbered citations and keep a references block so derived text retains source URLs.
SchemaSelectorExtraction: declarative {baseSelector, fields[{selector,type}]} extraction that fails loudly on zero matches instead of inventing values.
BoundedBestFirstCrawl: frontier ordered by composable scorers, pruned by a filter chain, capped by depth/pages/domain.
UntrustedConfigAllowlist: deserialize externally supplied configuration only through a strict type/field allowlist with clamped values.
LastmodGatedRecrawl: recrawl only URLs whose sitemap lastmod or ETag changed.
adoption_strategy: Adopt as a research-stage sidecar only, behind a thin TS facade. Run the official Docker image with LLM endpoints disabled, call POST /crawl with CrawlerRunConfig {cache_mode: ENABLED, check_robots_txt: true, mean_delay/max_range for politeness, no stealth, JsonCssExtractionStrategy schemas versioned in the playbook repo, DefaultMarkdownGenerator with citations} and map each CrawlResult into a FactSource record (url, redirected_url, status_code, fetched_at, etag/head_fingerprint, verbatim snippet) before any Fact is created with provenance kind `external`. Use BestFirst deep crawl with DomainFilter and page caps for competitor sampling and sitemap lastmod seeding for drift review. Do not use it for SERP or GBP scraping (use APIs) and never for design/token extraction. Python runtime is acceptable only because it is isolated in a container with a REST contract.

status_note: active; v4.0.0 monorepo (pnpm/turbo) with TS, Python and Go SDKs generated from one Zod protocol; v4 removed agent() and local caching in favour of Browserbase-hosted server-side cache; the runtime is a Chrome-extension service worker ('understudy') driven over JSON-RPC, so it no longer sits on top of Playwright
core_problem: Give scripts three natural-language primitives over a real browser (act, extract, observe) that resolve to concrete selectors and schema-validated data, so LLM judgement is spent only where a page needs it and everything else stays plain code.
architecture: packages/protocol: schemas.ts (Zod) is the single source of truth; schema-registry.ts binds schemas to JSON-RPC methods (StagehandMethods) and notifications; build-json-rpc-schema.ts emits stagehand.v4.json from which Python models and Go structs are generated. ActionSchema = {selector (css or xpath=...), description, method?, arguments?[]} is the interchange type: observe() returns Action[], act() accepts a string instruction or an Action. packages/extension is the runtime: understudy/ reimplements a Playwright-like Page/Frame/Locator over raw CDP (cdp.ts, frameRegistry.ts, executionContextRegistry.ts, locator.ts, deepLocator.ts for shadow/iframe piercing, networkManager.ts, lifecycleWatcher.ts, domainPolicy.ts); understudy/a11y/snapshot/ builds the model-facing page state: a11yTree.ts calls Accessibility.getFullAXTree per frame, decorateRoles (scrollable and file-input markers, tagName for generic nodes), buildHierarchicalTree prunes structural roles (generic/none/inlinetextbox) and redundant static text, treeFormatUtils.formatTreeLine renders `[ordinal-backendNodeId] role: name [checked]` lines, injectSubtrees nests iframe outlines, diffCombinedTrees returns only new lines; domTree.ts walks DOM.getDocument to produce xpathMap {encodedId -> absolute xpath}, tagNameMap and scrollableMap; capture.ts merges everything into page.snapshot() -> {formattedTree, xpathMap}. services/observeService.ts sends the outline to the model and maps returned element ids back through xpathMap into Action[] with `xpath=` selectors; services/actService.ts: act(string) -> waitForDomNetworkQuiet -> withCache -> runActPipeline (observe-style inference -> takeDeterministicAction via performUnderstudyMethod on a Playwright-style locator method) with selfHealAction re-observing when the cached/derived selector fails; act(Action) skips inference entirely. services/extractService.ts sends outline (+ optional viewport screenshot) with a Zod schema and validates the response; extract cache keys exclude screenshot pixels. services/cacheService.ts: withCache ships the raw CDP a11y tree(s) + instruction/options to the Browserbase API which hashes DOM shape and URL, stores in Redis, and returns Action[] on a hit; replayCachedActions executes them with no LLM and any failure falls through to the inference pipeline (which is the self-heal path). llm/ wraps Vercel AI SDK providers; PageCDPEvent notifications forward Runtime.consoleAPICalled. packages/sdk-ts is a thin JSON-RPC client; packages/evals holds a task/dataset eval harness; packages/integrations ships adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Mastra, Vercel AI, CrewAI. Docs v4/migrations/v3.mdx explains agent() removal: 'code mode' (a coding assistant writes a Stagehand script once) or 'tool calling' (expose page.goto/snapshot/locator.click/... as narrow tools; page.snapshot() anchors the loop).
core_innovation: observe() turns a natural-language intent into a concrete, replayable Action (selector + method + args) so the LLM run happens once and subsequent runs are deterministic locator calls, with a DOM-shape-keyed cache and self-heal fallback around that boundary.
strengths: Exactly the 'LLM explores, deterministic asserts' split: observe() yields Actions with real xpath selectors that can be committed to a repo and replayed with act(Action) without any model call.
Zod-first everywhere: protocol schemas, extract() output schema, LLM response schemas; TypeScript native, so it slots into our TS/Zod stack with no bridge.

Accessibility-tree page model with structural pruning, iframe injection and diff-of-new-lines is compact and model-agnostic (no vision required); page.snapshot() returns formattedTree + xpathMap which is directly reusable as a serialization format.

Cache is keyed on DOM shape + instruction + options and deliberately excludes model config, so switching models does not invalidate; replay failure automatically re-enters inference (self-heal) rather than hard-failing.
v4 philosophy statement ('use page.locator() wherever a selector is stable, spend a model call only where the page needs judgement') matches the constraint-not-generation principle.
MIT; three SDKs generated from one schema; active daily commits; evals package shows they measure act/extract accuracy on datasets.
weaknesses: v4 caching is server-side only and requires a Browserbase session + API key; with a local browser `cache` is a no-op, so 'deterministic replay after first LLM run' has to be built ourselves by persisting observe() Actions (the primitives exist, the local cache does not).

The runtime is a Chrome-extension service worker driven via JSON-RPC and its own CDP Page/Locator reimplementation, not Playwright; it produces no trace.zip, no reporter JSON, no toHaveScreenshot; it cannot be a fixture inside @playwright/test and Firefox/WebKit are out.
agent() (including CUA mode) was removed in v4; 'act like a user and report friction' must be a tool-calling loop we own.

Selectors are absolute xpaths from domTree.ts; on regenerated markup they are brittle by construction, so replay on a new build will self-heal (= LLM call) frequently unless we key Actions on data-slot/aria attributes instead.
Heavy monorepo (190 MB, MDX docs, Go/Python SDKs); v2->v3->v4 API churn within 18 months; the v4 docs still carry migration TODOs.
Vendor gravity: the best features (cache, hosted browsers, session persistence) route through Browserbase's paid API.
patterns_to_steal: observe() -> Action[] then act(Action) → qa_gate (friction scripts): author user-journey scripts in natural language once, resolve them to Action[] at library authoring time against the reference render of each arrangement, commit the Actions (rewritten to data-slot/aria selectors), and replay them deterministically in the gate; only on failure re-run observe as a warning-only diagnostic.

Cache key = hash(DOM shape) + instruction + options, model excluded → agent_orchestration: every model selection step (creative direction, arrangement pick) is memoized on the hash of its eligible-set snapshot + positioning + playbook version so re-runs are byte-identical and model upgrades do not silently change priors.

page.snapshot() {formattedTree, xpathMap} with structural pruning and diffCombinedTrees → agent_orchestration (explorer pass): if an LLM explorer runs on the generated site, feed it the pruned a11y outline and only the new lines after each action, not screenshots.

Protocol package pattern (Zod schemas -> JSON schema -> generated clients) → SiteDefinition contract: keep the Zod SiteDefinition as the single source of truth and generate the JSON Schema consumed by the renderer/editor/validators from it, as stagehand.v4.json is generated from schemas.ts.

Self-heal as fallback, not default (selfHeal flag, replay throws to re-enter inference) → qa_gate: deterministic replay first; inference only on explicit failure and always recorded as a distinct outcome in the report.
patterns_to_avoid: Absolute-xpath Actions as durable selectors → on generated sites the DOM shape changes per arrangement; use stable data-slot / role+name selectors so replay is deterministic across builds.
Depending on Browserbase server-side cache for determinism → vendor lock and network dependency in the gate; persist Actions locally in the section library instead.
Replacing Playwright with the understudy runtime → loses toHaveScreenshot, ARIA snapshots, reporters, tracing, multi-browser; Stagehand is a companion for exploration, not the gate runtime.
extract() with screenshots for facts → screenshot-assisted extraction is non-deterministic and cannot cite a source string; FactRegistry entries must come from DOM text with a URL and fetched_at.
reusable_patterns: ObserveThenReplay: natural-language intent is resolved once into concrete selector+method+args records that are executed without a model thereafter.
DomShapeKeyedMemo: memoize model outputs on a hash of the structural input (a11y tree / eligible set) plus instruction, excluding model identity.
SelfHealFallback: deterministic replay is the primary path; inference is entered only when replay throws, and the outcome is labelled.
PrunedA11yOutline: model-facing page state is the CDP accessibility tree with structural roles unwrapped, ids encoded as frameOrdinal-backendNodeId, and iframes injected inline.
SchemaFirstProtocol: one Zod schema catalog generates the wire JSON schema and all client types.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not embed the Stagehand runtime in the gate (it is not Playwright and its cache is hosted). Take the observe()->Action->act(Action) contract and the DOM-shape-keyed memo pattern and implement them in our Playwright/TS stack: an authoring-time script `resolveJourney(intent, referenceRenderUrl)` that uses an LLM once (via Playwright MCP-style a11y snapshot or Stagehand's TS SDK against a local browser) to produce Action[] pinned to data-slot/aria selectors, stored beside the arrangement in the section library; the gate replays those Actions with plain Playwright locators as named test.steps. Optionally use the Stagehand TS SDK with localBrowser.launch() for the warning-only 'user friction' explorer pass via tool calling, since it is MIT and pure TS.

license: MIT (Expat) for the Community Edition; any code under an `ee/` directory is under the separate Enterprise license (packages/core/admin/ee/LICENSE). EE terms also apply if you hold a Strapi Cloud account.
status_note: active (v5.54.0 on develop); EE features (SSO, audit logs, review workflows, content releases) gated by license file/registry (packages/core/core/src/ee/license.ts).
core_problem: A Node (Koa + Knex) headless CMS where content types are JSON schema files on disk (src/api/*/content-types/*/schema.json) plus reusable `components`, generating DB tables, REST/GraphQL APIs, a React admin, draft/publish and a plugin system.
architecture: packages/core/core is the runtime (Strapi.ts container, loaders for apis/components/plugins/policies/middlewares, registries, services). Content-type definitions are validated with yup (packages/core/core/src/domain/content-type/validator.ts: info.singularName/pluralName kebab-case, attributes, lifecycles, actions) and typed in packages/core/types/src/schema: Struct.ContentTypeSchema/ComponentSchema with `attributes` as a union of Attribute definitions (string, text, richtext, blocks, json, enumeration, relation, media, component, dynamiczone, uid...). `component` attribute = {type:'component', component: UID.Component, repeatable?} whose value is the component entry (or array). `dynamiczone` = {type:'dynamiczone', components: UID.Component[], min/max, required} whose value is `Array<Data.Component<UID> & {__component: UID}>` (packages/core/types/src/schema/attribute/definitions/dynamic-zone.ts) — the typed block list, discriminated by `__component`; components are declared once under src/components/<category>/<name>.json and reused across zones; dynamic zones cannot be nested inside components. `blocks` is a separate rich-text JSON attribute with a fixed node grammar (paragraph/heading/list/quote/code/image) (definitions/blocks.ts). Document Service API (v5): strapi.documents(uid).findMany/findFirst/findOne/create/update/delete/count/clone and, when draftAndPublish is enabled, publish/unpublish/discardDraft (packages/core/types/src/modules/documents/service-instance.ts); implemented as per-content-type repositories wrapped by a middleware manager (`strapi.documents.use((ctx,next))` with ctx{uid, action, params, contentType}) (packages/core/core/src/services/document-service/index.ts, middleware.ts). Draft & publish: draft and published rows are separate entries sharing a documentId; the `status` param defaults to draft and is translated to a `publishedAt` $null/$notNull lookup (document-service/draft-and-publish.ts); components are deep-cloned per status (components.ts). Plugins: server (register/bootstrap/routes/controllers/services/content-types) + admin (React) halves; core plugins content-manager, content-type-builder (edits schema.json via API), upload, i18n, users-permissions, graphql, documentation. EE: packages/core/core/src/ee/license.ts reads a license file, verifies against a registry, and unlocks features (sso, audit-logs, review-workflows, content-releases). Also packages/core/core/src/ai.ts and mcp.ts entry points, and an OpenAPI package.
core_innovation: Filesystem JSON content-type schemas with reusable components and dynamic zones (typed polymorphic block lists discriminated by __component), edited visually by the Content-Type Builder and exposed through a middleware-wrapped Document Service with separate draft/published entries.
strengths: dynamiczone is a well-understood typed block list: allowed component UIDs are explicit, min/max enforced, value rows carry `__component`; components are single-sourced JSON reused across content types (similar to Payload's config.blocks references).
Document Service middlewares (`strapi.documents.use`) give one interception point per action for cross-cutting rules, typed by uid/action/params.
Draft and published as separate entries sharing documentId keeps the published row untouched while drafts evolve; discardDraft restores from published.
Schema validation of content types with yup at load time and kebab-case naming rules; generated TS types for schemas (Public.ContentTypeSchemas registry).
Large ecosystem, MIT core, OpenAPI generation, GraphQL plugin, data-transfer package for export/import between environments.
weaknesses: Content types live as JSON files edited by the admin at dev time (Content-Type Builder writes schema.json and restarts the server); they are not TypeScript/Zod and cannot express predicates, cross-field allow-lists, or context-dependent component filtering (no analogue of Payload's blocks filterOptions).
dynamiczone cannot be nested (no dynamic zone inside a component) and components cannot be filtered per position; arrangement/slot/fact binding would have to be flat components with string fields.
Heavy runtime: Koa server + full React admin + Knex; multi-tenancy is absent (one Strapi = one project; agencies run one instance per client or filter by relation).
EE split: workflows/releases/audit are licensed; ee/ code is under a different license and must not be copied.
Versioning is draft/published only (plus Content History in EE/Cloud); no full revision history in CE.
Lifecycle hooks are per content type (beforeCreate etc.) with less path context than Payload field hooks.
patterns_to_steal: `__component` discriminator + components single-sourced in a category/name namespace -> name section variants as `family/variant` ids (e.g. proof/logo_wall_v2) in the section library and reference them from SiteDefinition.sections[].variant_id (section library / assembly).

Document Service middleware chain typed by (uid, action, params) -> a single `store.use()` interception layer in our Drizzle repository for audit logging and invariant enforcement on every write (fact_registry / cms).

Separate draft and published entries sharing a documentId, status resolved to a publishedAt null/notNull lookup -> sites table with published_version_id pointer + draft rows; reads default to published unless status=draft is requested (versions).

Load-time yup validation of content-type files with strict naming rules -> load-time Zod validation of every playbook and section-library YAML with a strict id grammar; fail the build on violations (niche playbook / section library).
patterns_to_avoid: Filesystem JSON schemas mutated by an admin UI at runtime -> our contract is code-only Zod; schema changes are PRs.
Flat dynamic zone without contextual allow-lists -> insufficient for `requires`/`design_compat` gating; keep eligibility in the predicate layer.
Strapi's `blocks` rich-text grammar for section copy -> we bind slots to facts, not free rich text.
Copying anything under ee/ directories -> different license.
reusable_patterns: DiscriminatedComponentList: array of component rows each tagged with a component UID from an explicit allow-list with min/max.
SingleSourcedComponents: reusable sub-schemas declared once in a namespaced registry and referenced by id.
ActionMiddlewareChain: every data-service action passes through registered (ctx, next) middlewares typed by entity and action.
DualEntryDraftPublish: draft and published are distinct rows sharing a document id; reads pick by status.
StrictSchemaLoadValidation: schema files validated with naming rules at boot; invalid definitions fail startup.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a runtime — Strapi's schema.json + Koa + React admin is a heavier, less typed alternative to Payload with no advantage for an Astro/Zod pipeline; its dynamiczone is strictly less expressive than Payload's blocks (no nesting, no contextual filterOptions) and far less than a Zod discriminated union. Reuse only the ideas: `__component`-style variant ids, a middleware chain on the repository, the dual-entry draft/published read model, and strict boot-time validation of authored schema files.

status_note: active (ghost 6.65.1-rc.0; Node 22/24); monorepo with ghost/core (Express app), admin (Ember + React apps), and many @tryghost/* packages.
core_problem: An opinionated, batteries-included publishing platform: posts/pages with a Lexical content model rendered to HTML, Handlebars themes driven by routes.yaml, members, paid tiers (Stripe), newsletters/email delivery, comments, ActivityPub, and a read-only Content API for headless use.
architecture: ghost/core/core/server is an Express monolith over Bookshelf/Knex (MySQL 8 in prod, SQLite dev) with a hand-maintained table schema (server/data/schema/schema.js: posts has mobiledoc, lexical, html, plaintext, status, visibility, type, custom_template, canonical_url, newsletter_id...). Content model: posts store Lexical JSON (`lexical` column); server/lib/lexical.js renders it to the cached `html` column via @tryghost/kg-lexical-html-renderer with DEFAULT_NODES from @tryghost/kg-default-nodes (cards: image, gallery, bookmark, html, callout, product, signup, email CTA...), with render options for image transforms and feature flags; `validate()` renders with a throwing error handler to reject malformed docs; server/lib/mobiledoc.js keeps the legacy Mobiledoc card factory and @tryghost/kg-converters migrates mobiledoc->lexical. API layer: server/api/endpoints/* framework-style descriptors (docName, browse/read/edit with option allow-lists, permissions, cache keys) — posts-public.js is the Content API for posts (options include/filter/fields/formats/limit/order/page; formats html|plaintext; read by id|slug|uuid) served under web/api/endpoints/content. Frontend: routes.yaml (default: collections `/` permalink `/{slug}/` template index; taxonomies tag/author) parsed by services/route-settings and turned by frontend/services/routing/router-manager.js into StaticRoutesRouter, CollectionRouter, TaxonomyRouter, StaticPagesRouter, PreviewRouter registered in a registry; rendering via frontend/services/rendering (renderer, templates, format-response) through the theme-engine (express-hbs instance, helpers under frontend/helpers, partials). Themes are Handlebars packages validated by gscan (server/services/themes/validate.js: gscan.check/checkZip against the Ghost major version; `canActivate = !results.hasFatalErrors`; warnings hidden in production). Members/newsletters/tiers/offers/stripe/email-service/email-analytics/link-tracking/comments/recommendations/activitypub are services under server/services; scheduling via post-scheduling + jobs-service; the url service maintains resource URLs for the routing layer.
core_innovation: A vertically integrated publisher: one content model (Lexical -> cached HTML) fanned out to web (routes.yaml + Handlebars), email newsletters, RSS and a Content API, with memberships and payments built in.
strengths: Lexical JSON as canonical content with pre-rendered `html`/`plaintext` columns: render once on write, serve static HTML — good for a near-zero-JS blog surface.

routes.yaml is a small declarative routing DSL (collections with permalink/filter/template, taxonomies, static routes with data bindings) compiled into router classes — a clean separation of URL structure from templates.
gscan theme validation with fatal-error gating before activation is a mature 'gate before ship' precedent for template packages, including version-targeted rule sets.
Content API is stable, cacheable, key-based read-only access with include/filter/fields/formats — trivially consumable by Astro at build time.
Complete newsletter/member stack (Stripe tiers, offers, email batching, analytics, link tracking, suppression lists) that would take years to rebuild; MIT.
weaknesses: Monolith: Express + Bookshelf + MySQL + its own admin (Ember/React) + Handlebars themes; not embeddable as a library, runs as a separate service per site or a Ghost(Pro) account.
Multi-tenancy absent: one Ghost instance = one site (Ghost(Pro) runs many instances); an agency would run N containers or pay per site.
Content model is post/page-centric with card-based rich text; no typed section/block schema, no design-system tokens, no fact provenance — irrelevant to SiteDefinition.
Themes are Handlebars, which would fight an Astro renderer; the visual identity of a client site would then be split across two template systems.
Very large codebase and release cadence (weekly minors) — operational burden for a blog add-on.
patterns_to_steal: Render-on-write: store canonical structured content and a pre-rendered html/plaintext alongside -> cache rendered section HTML fragments per SiteDefinition version for instant preview diffs and Lighthouse-stable output (renderer).

gscan-style versioned rule sets with fatal vs warning classes and `canActivate = !hasFatalErrors` -> the Launch QA gate and anti-slop tier 1 should be a versioned rule pack with fatal/warning severity and an explicit activation predicate (qa_gate / anti_slop).

routes.yaml declarative collections/taxonomies with permalink and filter -> page archetype to route mapping declared in the playbook (e.g. /services/{slug}/ bound to service facts) rather than hard-coded in the renderer (renderer / playbook).

Content API consumption pattern (key-based read-only, formats=html, filter/include) -> if a client needs a blog/newsletter, run Ghost as an external service and pull posts into Astro at build time via the Content API; keep it out of SiteDefinition (cms add-on).
patterns_to_avoid: Embedding Ghost into the agency runtime -> monolithic service, MySQL, own admin; only ever integrate over its Content API.
Handlebars themes for client sites -> conflicts with the Astro renderer and the design-system token model.
Card-based rich text (Lexical cards) as the page model -> free-form content with no fact binding or arrangement grammar.
reusable_patterns: RenderOnWriteCache: canonical structured content plus pre-rendered html/plaintext columns updated on save.
VersionedFatalWarningRulePack: validator rule sets keyed to a target version with fatal errors blocking activation and warnings advisory.
DeclarativeRouteMap: YAML collections/taxonomies/static routes with permalink and filter compiled into routers.
ReadOnlyContentAPI: key-scoped public read API with include/filter/fields/formats for static-site consumption.
adoption_strategy: Ignore for V1 and for the core architecture; it does not touch SiteDefinition, facts, design systems or the pipeline. Post-V1, if a client needs a blog or newsletter, the cheapest quality path is Ghost as an external managed service (Ghost(Pro) or a container) consumed by Astro at build time through the Content API, with the newsletter/member surface left entirely to Ghost — rather than rebuilding email delivery. Take two ideas now: gscan's fatal/warning versioned rule pack shape for our QA and anti-slop gates, and render-on-write caching of section HTML.

status_note: active; main branch is 4.0.0-canary.36 (3.x stable). Next.js-native admin, new @payloadcms/tanstack-start adapter in 4.0 canary; Local API runs framework-free (getPayload).
core_problem: A config-as-code TypeScript backend/CMS: you declare collections/globals/fields in buildConfig() and get a DB schema (Drizzle Postgres/SQLite or Mongo), REST/GraphQL/Local API, generated TS types + JSON schema, versions/drafts, access control, hooks and a React admin panel for free.
architecture: Root Config (packages/payload/src/config/types.ts: collections, globals, blocks, db adapter, editor, plugins[], jobs, kv, typescript, admin.livePreview) is sanitized into SanitizedConfig with flattenedFields per collection. Fields (packages/payload/src/fields/config/types.ts) are a discriminated union on `type` (text, number, select, relationship, upload, array, group, tabs, row, collapsible, json, richText, blocks, join, point...). Every data field carries FieldBase: access{create,read,update}, validate(value, opts), hooks{beforeValidate,beforeChange,afterChange,afterRead,beforeDuplicate}, jsonSchema[] transformers, localized, index/unique, admin.condition. `blocks` fields hold Block[] (slug, fields, interfaceName, admin.images/group, jsx import/export for Lexical/Markdown) or slugs referencing config.blocks; each stored row carries blockType (=slug) + blockName; filterOptions({siblingData,data,req}) restricts which block slugs are allowed per context and is re-validated on save (fields/validations.ts `blocks`). Hook pipeline per operation: beforeOperation -> beforeValidate (field hooks + type coercion in fields/hooks/beforeValidate/promise.ts) -> validate -> beforeChange -> DB -> afterChange -> afterRead; field hooks receive path/schemaPath/blockData/siblingData/previousValue/operation. Versions (packages/payload/src/versions/*): a shadow `_slug_versions` collection stores {parent, version:<full doc>, autosave, _status, createdAt}; drafts inject `_status: draft|published`, `draft:true` writes only to the versions table, maxPerDoc/enforceMaxVersions, schedulePublish jobs, autosave debounced ~800ms updates the latest autosave version in place. Access control = per-collection/per-field functions returning boolean or a Where query. Live preview (packages/live-preview/src): admin iframes the frontend and posts `{type:'payload-live-preview', collectionSlug|globalSlug, data, locale}`; the frontend's subscribe()/handleMessage() calls mergeData() which POSTs the unsaved form data to `/api/<collection>/<id>` with header `X-Payload-HTTP-Method-Override: GET` to get relationships populated, caches previousData, and re-renders; server-side variant uses isDocumentEvent() -> router.refresh(). Plugins are `(config) => config` functions (definePlugin with slug/order/options) that push collections/fields: plugin-seo injects a `meta` group (title/description/image/preview with generate fns), plugin-redirects a `redirects` collection (from, to{type,reference|url}), plugin-form-builder `forms`+`form-submissions` with a blocks field of form-field blocks, plugin-multi-tenant adds a `tenant` relationship to listed collections, baseListFilter by selected tenant, filterOptions on relationships, and a collection hook rejecting writes to tenants the user is not assigned (userHasAccessToAllTenants override). Types: `payload generate:types` emits payload-types.ts from JSON schema (json-schema-to-typescript) with a per-block top-level interface; `declare module 'payload' { interface GeneratedTypes }` gives a typed Local API (payload.find({collection:'pages'})). The official examples/astro shows getPayload({config}) + payload.find() called directly in an .astro frontmatter with the Payload config imported from a sibling workspace package; the admin UI still requires a Next.js (or TanStack Start, 4.0 canary) host.
core_innovation: A single TypeScript config is simultaneously the DB schema, the API, the generated types/JSON schema, the validation/hook pipeline and the admin UI, with typed block unions (blockType) and full-document versioning as first-class primitives.
strengths: blocks field = typed discriminated union (blockType) with per-block generated TS interface and JSON schema; block definitions can be centralized in config.blocks and referenced by slug everywhere (including inside Lexical richText).
BlocksField.filterOptions({siblingData,data,req}) => allowed slugs, re-validated on save: a schema-level 'which sections are eligible here' gate that mirrors our compat filter.

Field hooks/validate receive blockData, siblingData, path, schemaPath, previousValue and operation, so an invariant can be expressed exactly at the field where it lives and return a string error that becomes a ValidationError.

Versions model is simple and correct: full-document snapshots in `_slug_versions` with parent/autosave/_status, drafts written only to the versions table, published doc immutable until explicit `_status: published`, maxPerDoc retention, scheduled publish via the jobs queue.
Live preview protocol is framework-agnostic (window.postMessage + ready/subscribe/unsubscribe + mergeData populate round-trip); Astro would only need a tiny client island to implement it.

Local API works outside Next (getPayload({config}) in scripts/Astro frontmatter); MIT; Postgres via Drizzle; plugin-multi-tenant is a complete, small reference implementation of tenant isolation (field + list filter + write-enforcement hook).
Generated types + `jsonSchema` transformers let you emit a JSON schema for LLM tool calling directly from the content model (used by plugin-mcp).
weaknesses: Next-native by design: the admin panel, custom field components (PayloadComponent paths), server functions and RSC utilities live in @payloadcms/next / @payloadcms/ui; the TanStack Start adapter is 4.0 canary. With Astro you host a second app (Next) just for the admin/editor, or consume Payload as a headless backend from Astro over Local API/REST.

Relational storage of blocks/arrays: on Postgres each block type and array becomes its own table with _order/_path/_locale columns (packages/drizzle). A deep SiteDefinition (sections[] -> arrangement -> slots[] -> fact refs) becomes dozens of tables and a migration each time the section library changes; the `json` field escapes this but then you lose the admin UI value.

Hooks run at the CMS write boundary inside Payload's request lifecycle; our invariants (fact provenance, rights != unknown, quotable-only) must run in the deterministic pipeline before assembly anyway, so Payload hooks would be a second, duplicated enforcement point.

4.0 canary on main means API churn (definePlugin, blocks references, versions defaults changed recently); 1164 open issues; large dependency surface (React 19, Next, Lexical) for what is, in V1, a store with no human editor.

Per-document versioning is document-scoped: no cross-collection 'site snapshot' (site + design system + facts at one point in time) and no pinning of external artifact versions; that has to be modelled by hand either way.

Live preview merges unsaved form data via a server round-trip per keystroke (mergeData POST) and requires depth to match the initial fetch; it is optimized for Payload's relationship population, not for re-running a deterministic assembly pipeline.
patterns_to_steal: blockType-discriminated block rows + per-block interfaceName -> SiteDefinition.sections[] as a Zod discriminatedUnion('family') with generated JSON schema handed to the model as the only vocabulary it may select from (Creative Direction / Beat selection).

BlocksField.filterOptions re-evaluated on every data change and re-validated on save -> Compat filter: eligible section families/arrangements computed from the predicate snapshot, and a save-time re-check that rejects any section not in the eligible set (Eligibility + Assembly).

Field hook pipeline order (beforeValidate coercion -> validate -> beforeChange -> afterChange) with FieldHookArgs{path, schemaPath, blockData, siblingData, previousValue, operation} -> a tiny in-house `applyInvariants(siteDef, ctx)` runner where each invariant is registered against a schemaPath (e.g. sections[].slots[].fact_id must resolve to a FactRegistry entry with quotable=true and rights!=unknown) and returns path-addressed errors (FactRegistry + QA gate).

`_slug_versions` snapshot table {parent, version(full doc), autosave, _status, createdAt} + `draft:true` writes-only-to-versions + explicit publish -> site_versions table storing the whole SiteDefinition JSON per save with status draft|published, published row immutable; pin design_system@version and playbook@version inside the snapshot so old sites never auto-migrate (versions + pinning).

Live preview postMessage protocol (ready -> subscribe -> {type, data} events -> mergeData -> re-render; isDocumentEvent -> refresh for SSR) -> post-V1 editor: the editor posts a draft SiteDefinition into an Astro-rendered iframe; an Astro SSR endpoint renders from the posted JSON so the renderer stays the single source of truth (visual_editor).

plugin-multi-tenant mechanics (tenant relationship on every collection, baseListFilter by selected tenant, relationship filterOptions scoped to tenant, collection hook rejecting writes to non-member tenants, cleanupAfterTenantDelete) -> site_id column on every table + Drizzle query helpers + one write guard (multi-tenancy for the agency store).

plugin-seo `meta` group with generateTitle/generateDescription/generateURL callbacks and plugin-redirects from/to{reference|url} schema -> SEO slot and redirects table in SiteDefinition; keep generation deterministic (derived from facts), not model-written (renderer/cms).
`jsonSchema` field transformers + generate:types -> single Zod source producing both TS types and the JSON schema for the model's constrained tool call (agent_orchestration).
patterns_to_avoid: Running Payload as the primary store in V1 -> requires a Next host for an admin we cut from V1, relational block tables that churn with the section library, and 4.0 canary churn; store SiteDefinition as validated JSONB instead.
Modelling sections as Payload blocks with free-form text/richText fields editable by humans -> our slots must bind to FactRegistry ids, not free text; free text is where unquotable claims leak in.
Lexical richText as the content model for section copy -> heavy JS/editor surface and unconstrained markup; use fact-bound slots with limited inline marks.
Client-side live preview with mergeData populate round-trips per keystroke -> our preview should re-run assembly + the anti-slop gate server-side on a debounced draft, not merge partial form state.
Letting plugin-seo generate* callbacks call an LLM for meta text -> violates 'model only selects'; derive meta from positioning + facts deterministically.
reusable_patterns: TypedBlockUnion: a list field whose rows are a discriminated union on a `blockType` slug, each variant with its own schema and generated interface.
ContextualAllowList: a per-field function computing which union variants are permitted from sibling/parent data, re-validated at write time.
PathAddressedFieldHooks: validators/hooks registered on schema paths receiving (value, siblingData, blockData, path, previousValue, operation) and returning path-scoped errors.
ShadowVersionTable: full-document snapshots in a parallel table with parent/status/autosave flags; drafts never touch the published row.
PostMessagePreviewBus: iframe preview protocol of ready/subscribe/document-event messages with the frontend re-rendering from pushed draft data.
TenantGuardTriplet: tenant field + list filter + write-enforcement hook as the minimal multi-tenancy kit.
adoption_strategy: Adapt — do not adopt Payload as the V1 store; use plain Postgres + Drizzle + Zod with a `sites` table holding the SiteDefinition as JSONB, a `site_versions` shadow table copied from Payload's versions model (full snapshot, parent, status draft|published, autosave flag, pinned design_system@version/playbook@version inside the snapshot), a `facts` table (FactRegistry) with provenance/quotable/rights columns, and a small path-addressed invariant runner modelled on Payload's field-hook pipeline. Keep Payload's conventions (blockType discriminator, per-variant interface names, JSON schema generated from the same Zod source) so that, post-V1, the visual editor can either be built on Payload (its live-preview bus and admin are exactly the cut features) or remain custom without a data migration. Trade-off stated honestly: Payload would give drafts/autosave/versions/access/admin/live-preview for free and its Local API demonstrably works inside Astro frontmatter, but it costs a second Next/TanStack host, relational block tables that churn with every section-library change, duplicated invariant enforcement at the CMS boundary, and 4.0-canary API drift — in V1 (no human editor, the deterministic pipeline writes the doc) those costs buy nothing; revisit at the editor milestone.

license: MSCL-1.0-GPL (Monospace Sustainable Core License 1.0, derived from the Fair Core License; converts to GPL-3.0 four years after each release). NOT BSL 1.1 anymore: the LICENSE file is copyright 2026 Monospace Inc. README: free for orgs under $5M revenue and 50 employees via an 'Open Innovation Grant' license key; a key-less 'Free Core Tier' exists with entitlement limits enforced in code.
status_note: active (api 39.2.0); license changed from BSL 1.1 to MSCL 1.0 with runtime license-key entitlement checks (api/src/license/*).
core_problem: Wrap any existing SQL database with a metadata layer (collections/fields/relations tables) and get instant REST/GraphQL APIs, a Vue admin app, permissions, event-driven Flows and an extension system — data-model-first rather than code-first.
architecture: Express + Knex API (api/src). Schema = introspected SQL tables (@directus/schema, packages/schema) overlaid with `directus_collections`/`directus_fields`/`directus_relations` metadata: Field = {collection, field, type, schema: Column|null, meta: FieldMeta|null} where FieldMeta carries interface, display, options, conditions, validation (a Filter AST), validation_message, special[], readonly/required (packages/types/src/fields.ts); CollectionMeta has singleton, versioning, autosave_revision_interval, archive_field, preview_url, status active|inactive (packages/types/src/collection.ts). Queries compile to an AST (database/get-ast-from-query) then to Knex (database/run-ast). Events: an Emitter with emitFilter (mutating, awaited chain), emitAction (fire-and-forget) and emitInit (api/src/emitter.ts). Flows (api/src/flows.ts FlowManager): Flow{trigger: event|schedule|operation|webhook|manual, options, operation} where operations form a graph of Operation{type, options, resolve: Operation|null, reject: Operation|null}; executeOperation runs each operation and follows resolve or reject; data is keyed ($trigger, $last, operation keys) and templated into options; built-in operations under api/src/operations: condition (Filter AST validated with joi via validatePayload), transform, request, exec (isolated-vm sandbox), item-create/read/update/delete, mail, notification, log, sleep, throw-error, trigger. Extensions (packages/types/src/extensions): app types interfaces/displays/layouts/modules/panels/themes, API types hooks (register.filter/action/init/schedule/embed), endpoints, operations; bundles; loaded by api/src/extensions/manager.ts with a sandbox option. Content Versions (packages/types/src/versions.ts, api/src/services/versions.ts): ContentVersion{key, collection, item, hash, delta} stores a delta branch per item; save() merges deltas and writes revisions; promote() applies the delta to the main item; a hash of the main item detects staleness (`outdated`). Visual editing (packages/visual-editing): a frontend script parses `data-directus` attributes into EditConfig{collection,item,fields,mode}, draws overlays, and talks to the admin iframe via postMessage actions (connect, checkFieldAccess, edit, navigation, addToContext / confirm, activateElements, saved, highlightElement). License entitlements (api/src/license/entitlements/lib): countActiveCollections, countActiveFlows, seats, sso-enabled, custom-permission-rules-enabled, custom-llms-enabled; compute-license-status returns active|grace|locked and resolveCollections/resolveFlows set items to inactive when over the limit.
core_innovation: Treat the existing SQL schema as the source of truth and layer editable metadata, permissions and an operation-graph automation engine (Flows with resolve/reject edges) on top, instead of generating the database from code.
strengths: Data-model-first: any Postgres schema we own (sites, facts, versions) could be administered without a code schema; introspection means zero lock-in of the DB shape.

Flows' operation graph with explicit resolve/reject successors and keyed data ($trigger/$last) is a clean, inspectable automation DSL; the `condition` operation reuses the same Filter AST as permissions and validation.
Content versions as deltas with a main-item hash for staleness detection and explicit promote(): a lighter model than full snapshots when documents are large.
Visual-editing SDK is decoupled from the admin: attribute-encoded EditConfig on DOM nodes + a postMessage bus, framework-agnostic (would work in Astro).
FieldMeta.validation as a Filter AST + validation_message: declarative, storable, UI-editable validation rules.
Multi-storage drivers, Redis/memory stores, websocket subscriptions, MCP OAuth service, isolated-vm sandbox for untrusted extension code.
weaknesses: License: MSCL 1.0 is source-available, not OSI open source; 'Competing Use' excludes offering Directus itself as a hosted product; license-key entitlements are enforced at runtime (collections/flows/seats counted; over-limit -> 'locked' and collections switched to inactive). An agency store with many tenant collections or per-client flows can hit Free Core Tier limits; the $5M/50-employee grant requires applying for a key.

Multi-tenancy is not first-class: isolation is by policies/permissions with filter rules per role; no tenant field/list-filter kit like Payload's plugin; per-tenant collections would explode the licensed collection count.

SQL-first model fights a document-shaped SiteDefinition: nested sections/arrangements/slots must be either a JSON column (opaque to Directus' interfaces/validation) or normalized into relational many-to-any junction tables that the 'builder' interface uses — its analogue of typed block lists, far weaker than Zod/Payload blocks (no per-block schema generation, no allow-list per context).
Heavy runtime: Express+Knex API plus a Vue 3 admin SPA, Redis for multi-instance; extension authoring is Vue-specific for app extensions.
Flows are stored in DB rows, edited in a canvas UI, not code-reviewable YAML; `exec` operations run arbitrary JS in isolated-vm — the opposite of our authored, versioned playbooks.
Validation is a Filter AST, not a type system: cannot express cross-entity invariants like 'slot fact must be quotable' without hook extensions in JS.
patterns_to_steal: Operation graph with resolve/reject edges and keyed data ($trigger, $last, <opKey>) -> the agency pipeline runner: each stage (eligibility, creative direction, assembly, anti-slop, launch QA) is an operation with a reject edge to a Gap Report / retry stage; the graph is data (YAML), inspectable, and produces the Decision Manifest trace (agent_orchestration).
Content-version delta + main-item hash + promote() -> owner edits post-V1 stored as deltas against a pinned published SiteDefinition; staleness detected by hash before promote (versions + pinning).

Attribute-encoded EditConfig (`data-directus="collection:item:fields"`) + overlay manager + postMessage bus -> `data-slot="sections[i].slots.headline"` emitted by the Astro renderer so a post-V1 editor can click-to-edit without the renderer knowing about the editor (visual_editor).

Filter-AST validation stored on field metadata with validation_message -> store per-slot constraints (max chars, allowed marks, required fact kinds) as data in the section library YAML rather than code (section library / anti_slop tier 1).
emitFilter (awaited, mutating chain) vs emitAction (side effects) distinction -> gates are filters (can reject/transform), telemetry are actions (never block) (qa_gate / telemetry).
patterns_to_avoid: Running Directus as the agency store -> MSCL license-key entitlements and Competing-Use ambiguity for a hosted multi-tenant product; runtime lock-out risk when collections/flows exceed the tier.
DB-stored, canvas-edited Flows with `exec` JS -> our playbooks must be authored YAML, versioned and human-reviewed; no runtime-editable automation.
Many-to-any 'builder' junction tables as the block list -> loses typed variants and allow-lists; SiteDefinition stays a Zod-validated JSON document.
Introspection-driven metadata (schema defined in the DB, not code) -> our contract must be code (Zod) shared by AI, renderer and editor.
reusable_patterns: ResolveRejectOperationGraph: automation as a graph of operations each with success and failure successors, data keyed by operation key.
DeltaVersionBranch: named version = delta over a main item plus a hash of main for conflict detection, promoted explicitly.
AttributeEncodedEditTarget: DOM attributes carrying collection/item/fields so an overlay editor can attach to any rendered page.
FilterOrAction: two event kinds — awaited filters that may mutate/reject, fire-and-forget actions that only observe.
MetadataOverIntrospectedSchema: editable meta tables layered on an introspected SQL schema.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a store or runtime — the 2026 MSCL license (source-available, license-key entitlements that lock collections/flows when over the free tier, Competing-Use clause) is a poor fit for a multi-tenant agency platform, and its SQL-first metadata model does not express a typed, allow-listed section contract. Take three patterns only: the resolve/reject operation graph as the shape of our YAML pipeline runner, delta+hash versioning for post-V1 owner edits, and attribute-encoded edit targets emitted by the Astro renderer for the future editor.

status_note: active but low-velocity: @keystone-6/core 8.1.0 on Prisma 7 / Next 16 / React 19; releases 2026-08-18, 08-20, 08-31; maintained by Thinkmill; 141 open issues, small community.
core_problem: Schema-as-code CMS: define lists with typed field functions, access control and hooks in TypeScript; Keystone prints a Prisma schema, generates a GraphQL API with @graphql-ts, and serves a Next.js admin UI.
architecture: packages/core/src/schema.ts exports config({db, lists, session, ui}), list({fields, access, hooks, ui, db, graphql, isSingleton}), group(), action(). Fields are functions (text(), relationship(), select(), json(), image()...) returning FieldTypeFunc that declare a Prisma column kind and GraphQL input/output (types/next-fields.ts). initialise-lists.ts resolves lists into an InitialisedList graph; prisma-schema-printer.ts emits schema.prisma from lists; graphql.ts builds the schema; lib/core/mutations,queries implement resolvers. Access control (types/config/access-control.ts) is three-tier: operation (boolean per query/create/update/delete), filter (returns boolean or a `where` filter merged into the query), item (per-item boolean with inputData/item), plus field-level read/create/update. Hooks (types/config/hooks.ts, lib/core/hooks.ts): resolveInput (transform input) -> validate (receives addValidationError(msg), can be split per create/update/delete) -> beforeOperation -> afterOperation, at list and field level; errors accumulate into a GraphQL validation error. Context (types/context.ts) exposes context.db.<List>.findMany/createOne (typed, bypasses GraphQL) and context.query (GraphQL-shaped) with sudo(). The document field (packages/fields-document) is a Slate editor storing Slate JSON with componentBlocks (component({schema: fields.object/array/conditional/child/relationship/form, preview})) and a separate `structure` field (structure.ts) that stores an arbitrary typed JSON tree described by a ComponentSchema, validated with assertValidComponentSchema and given generated GraphQL input/output types — effectively a runtime schema DSL for typed JSON columns. Rendering is via @keystone-6/document-renderer (React). Admin UI is Next.js + @keystar/ui (react-aria).
core_innovation: Lists-as-code that print a Prisma schema and derive a fully typed GraphQL API, with a three-tier (operation/filter/item) access model and a `structure` field that turns a declarative component schema into a validated JSON column with generated GraphQL types.
strengths: Closest to our approach among the CMSs: the schema is plain TypeScript functions, Prisma is the migration/ORM layer, and context.db gives a typed data API without GraphQL.

Three-tier access model (operation boolean, filter-as-where, item predicate) is a clean generalization that maps directly onto row-level tenant isolation (filter returns {site: {id: {equals: tenant}}}).
validate hook with addValidationError accumulates multiple errors per operation instead of throwing on the first; hooks split by create/update/delete.

`structure` field: a declarative ComponentSchema (object/array/conditional/form/relationship) produces a validated JSON column plus GraphQL input/output types — a proof that a Zod-like runtime schema can drive storage, validation and API without per-block tables.
MIT, small surface, Postgres/SQLite/MySQL via Prisma, already on Prisma 7.
weaknesses: Momentum: ~10k stars, releases cluster around a few weeks, Thinkmill-driven; ecosystem is thin (few plugins, no SEO/redirects/multi-tenant packages, no versions/drafts, no live preview, no jobs).
No versioning or draft/publish primitives at all — would have to be built (which we must do anyway).
Admin UI and document field are React/Next-bound (Next 16 peer); the document field is Slate (custom editor stack), heavier to reuse than Lexical-based ones.
GraphQL-first API adds a schema layer we do not need for a deterministic pipeline; context.db exists but the mental model is GraphQL.
Prisma as ORM vs our Drizzle choice: adopting Keystone means adopting Prisma's migration workflow and client generation.
patterns_to_steal: Three-tier access (operation / filter-as-where / item) -> Drizzle query helpers: `scopeToSite(query, siteId)` filter layer + per-row predicate for owner-editable fields; the same predicate language as Eligibility can express access (multi-tenancy / cms).

validate hook with addValidationError accumulation split by operation -> the SiteDefinition invariant runner collects all violations (unquotable fact, rights unknown, missing requires) and returns them together for the Gap Report instead of failing on the first (fact_registry / qa_gate / gap report).

structure field ComponentSchema (object/array/conditional/relationship) validated at boot with assertValidComponentSchema -> validate the section library YAML against the Zod schema at boot and fail fast; keep SiteDefinition as one validated JSON column rather than normalized tables (renderer / section library).
prisma-schema-printer: derive the DB schema from the code schema, never the reverse -> Drizzle schema derived from the same TS module that exports the Zod contracts (cms).
patterns_to_avoid: Adopting Keystone as the runtime -> brings Prisma + GraphQL + Next admin for zero versioning/draft features; we would build the important parts ourselves anyway.
Slate document field with componentBlocks as section content -> free rich text with embedded components again invites unquotable copy; sections bind to facts.
GraphQL as the internal pipeline API -> unnecessary indirection for deterministic code calling a typed repository.
reusable_patterns: ThreeTierAccess: operation boolean, filter-as-where, item predicate, plus field-level read/write.
AccumulatingValidateHook: validators call addValidationError and the operation fails with the full list.
SchemaDrivenJsonColumn: a declarative component schema validated at boot that types, validates and exposes a JSON column.
CodeSchemaPrintsDbSchema: TS list definitions are the single source from which the ORM schema is printed.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a runtime (low momentum, no versions/drafts/live preview, Prisma+GraphQL+Next stack) but adapt three mechanisms into the plain Postgres+Drizzle+Zod design: the three-tier access model for site scoping, the accumulating validate hook for the invariant runner and Gap Report, and the `structure` field's schema-driven JSON column as the justification for storing SiteDefinition as one validated JSONB document. Its schema-as-code is indeed closer to our Zod approach than Payload's field-object config, but that closeness is an argument for writing our own thin layer, not for adopting Keystone.
