status_note: active; v13.5.0; Google-maintained, monthly releases; lighthouse-ci (@lhci/cli) is a sibling repo GoogleChrome/lighthouse-ci also active
core_problem: Loads a page in Chrome under emulated device/network conditions, collects raw artifacts (trace, devtools log, DOM snapshots, axe results) and runs ~180 declarative audits that each produce a 0-1 score plus structured details, aggregated into weighted category scores (performance, accessibility, best-practices, seo, and since v13 an 'agentic-browsing' category).
architecture: Three-layer pipeline declared entirely in core/config/default-config.js: (1) artifacts: [{id, gatherer}] where each gatherer extends core/gather/base-gatherer.js (BaseGatherer with meta.supportedModes and lifecycle hooks startInstrumentation/startSensitiveInstrumentation/stopSensitiveInstrumentation/stopInstrumentation/getArtifact(passContext)); e.g. the Accessibility gatherer (core/gather/gatherers/accessibility.js) injects axe-core into an isolated world, runs axe.run with runOnly tags ['wcag2a','wcag2aa'], resultTypes ['violations','inapplicable'], an explicit per-rule enable/disable map, and re-maps nodes through getNodeDetails to {lhId, devtoolsNodePath, selector, boundingRect, snippet, nodeLabel}. (2) audits: string paths to classes extending core/audits/audit.js; each declares static meta {id, title, failureTitle, description, requiredArtifacts, scoreDisplayMode, supportedModes, guidanceLevel} and static audit(artifacts, context) returning a Product {score 0-1|null, numericValue+numericUnit, displayValue, details, metricSavings, notApplicable, errorMessage, warnings}. Audit.SCORING_MODES = numeric|binary|metricSavings|manual|informative|notApplicable|error; generateAuditResult() clamps score to 2 decimals, swaps in failureTitle when score < 0.9, quantizes metricSavings (50 ms / 0.001 CLS). Details helpers produce typed tables: makeTableDetails/makeOpportunityDetails/makeListDetails/makeChecklistDetails/makeSnippetDetails/makeNodeItem/makeSourceLocation. AxeAudit (core/audits/accessibility/axe-audit.js) is the generic adapter: inapplicable -> notApplicable, incomplete with .error -> error result, informative audits treat incomplete as failures, score = Number(rule === undefined), details table of failing nodes + debugdata {impact, tags}. ManualAudit (core/audits/manual/manual-audit.js) is a fixed scoreDisplayMode 'manual' checklist item (10 a11y manual audits e.g. logical-tab-order, focus-traps, visual-order-follows-dom, managed-focus, interactive-element-affordance; seo/manual/structured-data). (3) categories: {auditRefs: [{id, weight, group, acronym}]} scored by core/scoring.js ReportScoring.arithmeticMean (weighted mean; notApplicable/informative/manual forced to weight 0; null if any weighted audit is null). Perf weights FCP 10 / LCP 25 / TBT 30 / CLS 25 / SI 10 / INP 0; a11y weights mirror axe impact (critical 10, serious 7, moderate 3, minor 1); SEO is-crawlable 93/23 and the rest 1. Settings in core/config/constants.js: formFactor mobile, throttling mobileSlow4G via 'simulate' (Lantern), Moto G Power 412x823 DPR 1.75 (desktop 1350x940), maxWaitForLoad 45 s, network/CPU quiet 1 s. Config extension: {extends:'lighthouse:default', settings:{onlyCategories|onlyAudits|skipAudits}, artifacts, audits, groups, categories}; plugins (lighthouse-plugin-*) may add audits + one category but not gatherers. User flows: startFlow(page) -> flow.navigate(url|fn) / startTimespan()+endTimespan() / snapshot(); categories declare supportedModes; createFlowResult() yields steps[] of LHRs. Output LHR (types/lhr/lhr.d.ts): audits: Record<id, Result>, categories, categoryGroups, configSettings, runWarnings, runtimeError, environment.benchmarkIndex, timing, entities, fullPageScreenshot.nodes (lhId -> rect).
core_innovation: A fully declarative audit plugin model (artifact -> audit -> normalized score + typed details -> weighted category) where the config is data, so any check can be added, removed or re-weighted without touching the runtime.
strengths: Config-as-data: default-config.js is the whole contract; adding a check is one class + one auditRefs entry; removal is skipAudits; weighting is a number. Directly matches our 'constraint not generation' principle.

Clean scoring vocabulary: scoreDisplayMode binary/numeric/metricSavings/manual/informative/notApplicable/error is exactly the state machine a gate needs (pass, graded, needs-human, info-only, n/a, error) and it is enforced in generateAuditResult, not left to each audit.

Typed details (table/opportunity/list/checklist/snippet/node/source-location/debugdata) plus fullPageScreenshot.nodes let a report point at the failing element with selector, snippet and bounding rect - reusable for our client-facing gate report.
Manual audits are first-class citizens with weight 0: the report shows what a human still has to verify instead of silently omitting it.
Three run modes (navigation/timespan/snapshot) via startFlow let us audit post-interaction state (e.g. after opening a menu or submitting a form) with the same audit set.

LHCI turns any audit into an eslint-style assertion (level | [level, {minScore, maxLength, maxNumericValue, aggregationMethod}]), supports category assertions, resource-summary:<type>:size|count budgets, user-timings:<mark>, assertMatrix per URL pattern, and picks a representative run (closest to median FCP+TTI) across numberOfRuns.

Explicit variability doc: median of 5 runs is twice as stable as 1; computeMedianRun exported from core/lib/median-run.js; simulate throttling minimizes variance; never run concurrent Lighthouse on one machine.
Apache-2.0; ships as ESM node library, CLI, and DevTools panel; the axe bundle inside is pinned and reviewed by the Lighthouse team (rule enable/disable list is opinionated and documented inline).
weaknesses: Performance metric scores (FCP/LCP/TBT/CLS/SI) are inherently non-deterministic; only medians over 3-5 runs are gate-safe and that costs ~30 s per run per page. Simulated throttling also diverges from real devices.

Only ~60 of the 105 axe rules run (wcag2a/wcag2aa tags plus a hand-picked list of best-practice rules); region, page-has-heading-one, landmark-* uniqueness, nested-interactive, no-autoplay-audio, frame-tested and all wcag21/wcag22 rules except target-size are not run. Running axe directly is still required.
Per-page tool with no crawling or site-wide checks (no duplicate titles, no broken-link crawl, no canonical consistency across pages); seo/canonical only validates the tag on the audited page.

LHCI's presets/all.js still lists removed audits (uses-responsive-images, offscreen-images, uses-http2, first-meaningful-paint) alongside the new *-insight audits, so a preset cannot be trusted as a definitive audit inventory; unknown ids only produce a warning.
Heavy runtime (Chrome + trace processing, ~4.5 MB JS), needs 2 dedicated cores and quiet hardware; not suitable for serverless CI runners per its own docs.
Plugins cannot add gatherers; custom DOM data needs a full custom config, which loses semver stability.
Audit ids and details schemas change between majors (v12 opportunities -> v13 insights); an LHR consumer must be version-pinned.
patterns_to_steal: Audit class contract {meta:{id,title,failureTitle,description,requiredArtifacts,scoreDisplayMode}, audit(artifacts,ctx)->Product} -> qa_gate: define GateCheck as a Zod-typed object with the same fields so our 60+ checks (placeholder scan, canonical, schema.org, tab order) share one shape with imported Lighthouse/axe results.

Artifact/audit split -> qa_gate: gather once per page (Playwright DOM snapshot, axe JSON, LHR, crawl graph, console log, form-submit trace) into a typed ArtifactBundle; every check is a pure function over the bundle, which makes checks unit-testable with fixture bundles.

scoreDisplayMode enum (binary|numeric|manual|informative|notApplicable|error) + weight-0 semantics -> qa_gate GateReport: use it verbatim so 'needs human' and 'not applicable' are explicit rows, never missing rows.

Category auditRefs with weights + arithmeticMean that returns null when any weighted audit errored -> qa_gate: our gate should fail closed (null score => not shippable) instead of averaging over errors.

LHCI assertion grammar {auditId: [level, {minScore|maxLength|maxNumericValue, aggregationMethod}]} plus assertMatrix by URL pattern and resource-summary:script:size -> qa_gate config: our budget file is a superset of lighthouserc assertions; script size 180 kB budget becomes resource-summary:script:size maxNumericValue 184320.

numberOfRuns + median-run selection (representative-runs.js: run minimizing squared distance to median FCP and TTI) -> qa_gate: run perf 3x on the hero page and homepage, assert on median-run; gate deterministic audits on run 1 only.

Node detail item {lhId, selector, boundingRect, snippet, nodeLabel} + fullPageScreenshot.nodes -> qa_gate report: store one full-page screenshot per page and reference rects, so the client report can highlight failures without re-rendering.

Manual audits as explicit checklist items -> qa_gate: our human/visual checks (focus visibility, reduced motion, meaningful alt, art-direction grade) are emitted as scoreDisplayMode 'manual' with a reviewer field, so the Decision Manifest records who signed off.
User flow snapshot mode -> qa_gate: after Playwright submits the contact form and lands on the thank-you page, run a snapshot-mode Lighthouse (a11y + seo) on that state.
Insight audits with metricSavings quantization (50 ms / 0.001 CLS) -> telemetry: quantize before storing so priors promotion is not driven by noise.
patterns_to_avoid: Gating on category performance score (e.g. minScore 0.9) -> the score is a log-normal blend of noisy metrics; gate on deterministic proxies (resource-summary sizes, unsized-images, render-blocking, non-composited-animations, dom-size, total-byte-weight) and only warn on metric medians.

Extending Lighthouse via custom gatherers for our proprietary checks (placeholder scan, schema.org, form e2e) -> ties us to Lighthouse's Chrome-driver lifecycle and major-version churn; run those in Playwright and merge at the GateReport level instead.

Using 'lighthouse:all'/'lighthouse:recommended' presets as-is -> they reference stale audit ids and mark noisy audits (bootup-time, mainthread-work-breakdown) as errors; author our own explicit assertion list.

Treating the accessibility category score as WCAG conformance -> Lighthouse runs a subset of axe and cannot see the ~40% of WCAG that needs a human; our gate must keep the a11y manual checklist separate and required.
The new agentic-browsing category (WebMCP, llms.txt, ARD) -> immature and weight-1 fraction scoring; ignore for V1 beyond emitting llms.txt if cheap.
reusable_patterns: ArtifactAuditSplit: gather raw evidence once per page into a typed bundle; every check is a pure function of the bundle, so checks are testable against fixtures and never touch the browser.

ScoreDisplayModeEnum: every check result carries one of binary|numeric|manual|informative|notApplicable|error, and aggregation treats manual/informative/notApplicable as weight 0 and error as poisoning the aggregate.
ConfigAsWeightedAuditRefs: category = list of {id, weight, group}; adding/removing/re-weighting checks is data, not code.
EslintStyleAssertionGrammar: check id -> level | [level, {threshold options, aggregationMethod}] with URL-pattern matrices; one file expresses the whole gate policy.
RepresentativeRunSelection: run N times, choose the run nearest the multi-metric median, assert on that run only.
NodeEvidenceItem: failing element = {selector, snippet, boundingRect, screenshot ref} so reports can highlight without re-rendering.
adoption_strategy: Adopt as a runner and Adapt its plugin model as the template for the whole gate. Run Lighthouse via the Node API (or @lhci/cli collect) against the built Astro output served locally, mobile + desktop, with our own explicit assertion list (not a preset): a11y/seo/best-practice audits at error minScore 1; resource-summary:script:size <= 184320 bytes, resource-summary:font:count <= 2, dom-size, unsized-images, non-composited-animations, render-blocking-insight maxLength 0; metric medians (numberOfRuns 3, aggregationMethod median-run) as warnings only. Parse the LHR JSON directly into our GateReport rather than consuming LHCI's server. Copy the Audit meta/Product/scoreDisplayMode contract into a Zod GateCheck type and implement our non-Lighthouse checks (axe full ruleset, placeholder scan, canonical/title uniqueness, schema.org, link crawl, form e2e, reduced-motion, tab order, LCP element identity) as audits over a Playwright-gathered ArtifactBundle.
evidence: core/config/default-config.js (artifacts list with gatherer ids, full audits list incl. accessibility/manual/*, seo/manual/structured-data, insights/*, agentic/*; groups; categories with weights: FCP 10/LCP 25/TBT 30/CLS 25/SI 10, a11y impact weights, seo is-crawlable 93/23, agentic-browsing categoryScoreDisplayMode fraction)

core/config/constants.js (defaultSettings: formFactor mobile, throttling mobileSlow4G, throttlingMethod simulate, Moto G Power 412x823 DPR 1.75, desktop 1350x940, maxWaitForLoad 45000, quiet thresholds 1000)

core/audits/audit.js (SCORING_MODES, meta contract, generateAuditResult, _normalizeAuditScore, _quantizeMetricSavings with METRIC_SAVINGS_PRECISION, makeTableDetails/makeOpportunityDetails/makeNodeItem/makeSnippetDetails/makeChecklistDetails)
core/gather/base-gatherer.js (lifecycle methods, meta.supportedModes)

core/gather/gatherers/accessibility.js (axe.run with runOnly wcag2a/wcag2aa, resultTypes violations+inapplicable, explicit rules enable/disable map, createAxeRuleResultArtifact, relatedNodes cap 3, getNodeDetails)
core/audits/accessibility/axe-audit.js (notApplicable/incomplete-error/informative handling, score = Number(rule === undefined), debugdata impact/tags)
core/audits/manual/manual-audit.js and core/audits/accessibility/manual/logical-tab-order.js (scoreDisplayMode manual, weight 0 in category)
core/scoring.js (ReportScoring.arithmeticMean, weight forced 0 for notApplicable/informative/manual, null propagation)
types/lhr/lhr.d.ts and types/lhr/audit-result.d.ts (LHR shape, fullPageScreenshot.nodes, Result fields incl. metricSavings, scoringOptions p10/median, guidanceLevel)
docs/configuration.md, docs/plugins.md (extends lighthouse:default, onlyCategories/onlyAudits/skipAudits, plugin capability table: plugins cannot add gatherers)

docs/user-flows.md (startFlow, navigate/startTimespan/snapshot, createFlowResult, supportedModes), docs/throttling.md (simulate/devtools/packet-level, cpuSlowdownMultiplier 4x, benchmarkIndex), docs/variability.md (sources table, median of 5 twice as stable, computeMedianRun, no concurrent runs)

lighthouse-ci: docs/configuration.md assert section (levels off/warn/error, minScore/maxLength/maxNumericValue, aggregationMethod median/optimistic/pessimistic/median-run, categories:<id>, resource-summary:<type>:size|count, user-timings:<name>, assertMatrix matchingUrlPattern, budgetsFile), packages/utils/src/presets/all.js and recommended.js, packages/utils/src/assertions.js (AUDIT_TYPE_VALUE_GETTERS, default minScore 0.9 when unspecified in getStandardAssertionResults), packages/utils/src/representative-runs.js (closest to median FCP+interactive), packages/utils/src/budgets-converter.js (budget.json path -> regex, KB -> bytes)

status_note: active; v4.13.0; Deque-maintained with ACT-rule alignment; companion repo dequelabs/axe-core-npm (MPL-2.0) ships @axe-core/playwright, @axe-core/puppeteer, @axe-core/cli, @axe-core/react, @axe-core/reporter-earl
core_problem: Runs a declarative set of ~105 accessibility rules inside the page (including iframes and shadow DOM) and classifies every matched element into violations, passes, incomplete (needs review) or inapplicable, with impact, WCAG/ACT tags and per-check messages, so automated WCAG testing is consistent across tools and browsers.
architecture: Rule = JSON spec in lib/rules/<id>.json: {id, impact (minor|moderate|serious|critical), selector (CSS), matches (named matcher fn id, e.g. 'color-contrast-matches'), excludeHidden, enabled, pageLevel, reviewOnFail, preload, tags [...], actIds [...], metadata {description, help}, any/all/none (check ids)}. lib/core/base/rule.js materializes it (Rule constructor assigns selector default '*', any/all/none arrays, tags, actIds, createExecutionContext(matches)). Check = lib/checks/<cat>/<id>.json {id, evaluate: '<id>-evaluate', options, metadata {impact, messages {pass, fail, incomplete}}} with the evaluate function in <id>-evaluate.js; e.g. checks/color/color-contrast.json carries options (contrastRatio normal 4.5 / large 3, boldValue 700, largeTextPt 18, shadowOutlineEmMax) and 16 distinct incomplete reasons (bgImage, bgGradient, imgNode, bgOverlap, complexTextShadows, fgAlpha, pseudoContent, outsideViewport, shortTextContent, equalRatio...). Rule semantics: any = at least one check passes, all = all pass, none = none pass; a check returning undefined puts the node in 'incomplete'. Tags (doc/API.md): wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag2aaa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa, best-practice, wcag### (success criterion e.g. wcag111), ACT, section508(.x.y), TTv5/TT#, EN-301-549/EN-9.x, RGAAv4, experimental (disabled by default), cat.* (aria, color, forms, keyboard, language, name-role-value, parsing, semantics, sensory-and-visual-cues, structure, tables, text-alternatives, time-and-media). doc/rule-descriptions.md inventory: 60 WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2 WCAG 2.1 (autocomplete-valid, avoid-inline-spacing), 1 WCAG 2.2 (target-size), 27 best-practice (landmark-*, region, page-has-heading-one, heading-order, skip-link, tabindex, meta-viewport-large, empty-heading...), 3 AAA (color-contrast-enhanced, identical-links-same-purpose, meta-refresh-no-exceptions), 7 experimental (p-as-heading, focus-order-semantics, hidden-content, label-content-name-mismatch, css-orientation-lock, table-fake-caption, td-has-header), 5 deprecated. API: axe.run(context, options) where context = selector | {include, exclude} | {fromFrames, fromShadowDom}, options = {runOnly: {type:'tag'|'rule', values} , rules: {id: {enabled}}, reporter: v1|v2|raw|raw-env|no-passes|na (lib/core/reporters), resultTypes ['violations',...] (only limits expensive selector generation), selectors, ancestry, xpath, absolutePaths, iframes, elementRef, frameWaitTime 60000, preload (cssom), performanceTimer, pingWaitTime}. axe.configure({rules, checks, branding, reporter, locale, noHtml, allowedOrigins}) adds custom rules/checks at runtime. Results: {url, timestamp, testEngine, testEnvironment, testRunner, toolOptions, violations|passes|incomplete|inapplicable: [{id, impact, tags, description, help, helpUrl, nodes: [{html, impact, target (selector array per frame/shadow level), failureSummary, any, all, none: [{id, impact, message, data, relatedNodes}]}]}]}. Multi-frame via axe.runPartial/finishRun and frameMessenger. @axe-core/playwright: new AxeBuilder({page}).include(sel).exclude(sel).withTags([...]).withRules([...]).disableRules([...]).options({...}).setLegacyMode().analyze() -> AxeResults; injects axe into every frame and uses runPartial/finishRun.
core_innovation: A rule/check algebra (any/all/none over small named checks, each with pass/fail/incomplete messages) that yields a three-way outcome per element, making 'needs human review' a first-class machine result rather than a false pass.
strengths: Deterministic for a given DOM + viewport + loaded fonts; no timing or network dependence, so results are gate-safe on run 1.
The incomplete bucket with per-check reason codes tells us exactly which human checks remain (e.g. color-contrast bgImage/bgGradient -> 'contrast on photo/gradient' manual check).
Tag-driven selection (runOnly wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21aa/wcag22aa/best-practice) plus rules enable map lets policy be a data file; axe.getRules(tags) enumerates the active set for the report.
Rich per-node evidence: target selectors through iframes/shadow DOM, html snippet, failureSummary, check data (fg/bg color, ratio, font size), relatedNodes.
Custom rules/checks can be registered with axe.configure without forking; ACT rule ids let us cite W3C test rules in the Decision Manifest.
MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: using or bundling unmodified is fine for a closed SaaS; only modified axe source files must be published.

Runs 27 best-practice and 3 wcag21/22 rules that Lighthouse skips (region, page-has-heading-one, landmark uniqueness, nested-interactive, avoid-inline-spacing, no-autoplay-audio) - covering structural rules our section library must satisfy.
EARL JSON-LD reporter exists (@axe-core/reporter-earl) for a standards-based interchange format; v2 reporter gives compact nodes.
weaknesses: Coverage ceiling: Deque's own claim is ~57% of WCAG issues by volume; everything requiring judgement (meaningful alt, focus visibility, reading order, reduced motion, link purpose, captions quality, keyboard operability of custom widgets) is either incomplete or entirely absent (no focus-visible rule, no prefers-reduced-motion rule, no reading-order rule).

color-contrast goes incomplete on any text over images, gradients, overlapping elements or alpha foregrounds - exactly the hero-over-photo pattern our art direction produces, so the gate needs a separate sampled-pixel contrast check.

Results are viewport- and state-dependent (target-size, color-contrast, hidden content): must run at mobile and desktop viewports and after fonts and lazy content load, and again after opening menus/dialogs.
Experimental rules (p-as-heading, focus-order-semantics, label-content-name-mismatch) are disabled by default and produce false positives; enabling them needs a review policy.
Rule set changes between minors (deprecations: duplicate-id, audio-caption, aria-roledescription); pin the version and snapshot getRules() output into the gate config.
Repository is ~31 MB of HTML fixtures (languages.json shows 31 MB HTML) - fine to depend on, awkward to vendor.
No site-level or navigation-level reasoning (no crawl, no per-route sampling, no cross-page consistency).
patterns_to_steal: Rule spec {selector, matches, any/all/none checks, tags, impact, metadata} -> qa_gate: express our own DOM checks (placeholder text, duplicate h1, empty section, link text 'click here', CTA present) in the same JSON grammar and register them via axe.configure so they run in-page with axe's selector/iframe machinery and appear in the same result shape.

Three-way outcome per element (violation | pass | incomplete) with incomplete reason codes -> qa_gate GateReport: 'needs_review' status with reason enum; map color-contrast incomplete reasons to specific human checks (bgImage/bgGradient -> visual contrast check on hero photos).
Impact enum critical/serious/moderate/minor -> qa_gate severity and Lighthouse weight mapping (10/7/3/1) - reuse to weight our own checks consistently.

Tags as policy surface (runOnly by tag + rules override) -> qa_gate config: a11y_policy: {tags: ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21aa','wcag22aa','best-practice'], disable: ['frame-tested'], enable_experimental: ['p-as-heading']} snapshotted into the Decision Manifest.
target selector arrays per frame/shadow level -> qa_gate evidence: store target[] verbatim; Playwright can re-locate the element for screenshots via page.frameLocator/locator chains.
axe.getRules(tags) enumeration -> gate report: print the exact rule list executed with version, so the client report and Decision Manifest state what was checked, not just what failed.

Check options as data (contrastRatio expected 4.5/3, largeTextPt 18) -> design_system: validate design-system token pairs (text/background combos in visual_dna) against the same thresholds at build time, before any page is rendered.
patterns_to_avoid: Treating zero violations as WCAG-AA conformance in client-facing copy -> ~43% of criteria are not automatable; the gate must require the manual checklist and word the report as 'automated checks passed'.

Running only Lighthouse's embedded axe -> it runs a subset (wcag2a/aa + hand-picked best-practice) and drops incomplete nodes; run @axe-core/playwright directly with the full tag set and keep incomplete.
Enabling all experimental rules as errors -> known false positives (p-as-heading, focus-order-semantics); run them as warnings/informative only.

Writing a large corpus of custom axe rules for non-a11y checks -> rules run in-page with no access to network, crawl graph, or build artifacts; keep site-level checks (canonical uniqueness, 404s, schema.org) in the Node-side gate.
reusable_patterns: AnyAllNoneCheckAlgebra: a rule is a selector plus small named checks composed with any/all/none; a check that cannot decide returns undefined and the element becomes 'needs review' instead of pass.
IncompleteReasonCodes: every non-decidable outcome carries a stable reason id (bgImage, fgAlpha, outsideViewport...) that a downstream process maps to a specific human task.
TagPolicySelection: rule activation is a set algebra over standards tags plus per-rule overrides, snapshotted for reproducibility.
FrameAwareTargetPath: element identity is an array of selectors, one per iframe/shadow boundary, so evidence survives re-location in another tool.
RuntimeRuleRegistration: a host can add rules/checks via configure() without forking the engine.
adoption_strategy: Adopt @axe-core/playwright (pinned axe-core version) inside the Playwright crawl step of the Launch QA gate: run AxeBuilder.withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa','wcag22aa','best-practice']) on every crawled page at mobile and desktop viewports, after fonts settle, and again in snapshot states (nav open, form error state, thank-you page). Treat violations of impact serious/critical as gate failures, moderate/minor as warnings, and emit every incomplete node as a needs_review row with its reason code mapped to our manual checklist. Register 6-10 house rules via axe.configure (placeholder text patterns, single h1, non-empty sections, generic link text) so they ride on the same engine and result shape. Keep the pixel-sampling contrast check for text over images/gradients, the focus-visible tab walk, and the prefers-reduced-motion check as separate Playwright checks, since axe has no rules for them.
evidence: lib/rules/color-contrast.json, lib/rules/image-alt.json, lib/rules/focus-order-semantics.json (rule spec fields: id, impact, selector, matches, excludeHidden, tags, actIds, metadata, any/all/none; experimental tag)
lib/core/base/rule.js (Rule constructor: selector default '*', any/all/none, tags, actIds, enabled, pageLevel, reviewOnFail, preload, createExecutionContext(matches))
lib/checks/color/color-contrast.json (check options contrastRatio 4.5/3, boldValue 700, largeTextPt 18; messages pass/fail/incomplete with 16 incomplete reason keys)
doc/rule-descriptions.md (auto-generated inventory: 60 WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2 WCAG 2.1, 1 WCAG 2.2, 27 best-practice, 3 AAA, 7 experimental, 5 deprecated; issue type failure vs needs review per rule)

doc/API.md sections: Axe-core Tags table, axe.run Options Parameter table (runOnly, rules, reporter, resultTypes, selectors, ancestry, xpath, iframes, elementRef, frameWaitTime, preload, performanceTimer, pingWaitTime), Results Object (passes/violations/incomplete/inapplicable, node fields target/any/all/none/relatedNodes), axe.configure, axe.runPartial/finishRun

lib/core/reporters listing (v1, v2, raw, raw-env, no-passes, na) and lib/checks category directories (aria, color, forms, generic, keyboard, label, landmarks, language, lists, media, mobile, navigation, parsing, shared, tables, visibility; 121 check JSON files)

dequelabs/axe-core-npm packages/playwright/src/index.ts (AxeBuilder include/exclude/options/withRules/withTags/disableRules/setLegacyMode/analyze), packages/reporter-earl/README.md (EARL 1.0 JSON-LD reporter), packages listing (cli, playwright, puppeteer, react, reporter-earl, webdriverio, webdriverjs)

status_note: active; v0.18.1 (pre-1.0, single maintainer harlan-zw); pnpm monorepo packages/{core,cli,client,server,unlighthouse,unlighthouse-ci} plus Nuxt/Vite/Webpack integrations
core_problem: Runs Lighthouse across an entire site instead of one URL: discovers routes (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, framework route definitions, HTML link crawl), collapses dynamic routes into groups and samples a few per group, runs Lighthouse in a Puppeteer cluster with per-route caching and median-of-N sampling, and renders a live/static comparison dashboard with a CI mode that fails on category score budgets.
architecture: packages/core/src/constants.ts defaultConfig: scanner {maxRoutes 200, skipJavascript true, samples 1, throttle true, crawler true, dynamicSampling 8, sitemap true, robotsTxt true, device 'mobile', customSampling {}, ignoreI18nPages true, include/exclude}, puppeteerClusterOptions {concurrency Cluster.CONCURRENCY_BROWSER, maxConcurrency cpus/2, retryLimit 3, retryDelay 2000, timeout 5 min, workerCreationDelay 500}, lighthouseOptions {onlyCategories: performance, accessibility, best-practices, seo}, cache true, outputPath .unlighthouse, ci {budget, reporter, buildStatic}. resolveConfig.ts merges user unlighthouse.config.ts (c12 + defu). Discovery (discovery/routes.ts resolveReportableRoutes): explicit urls (disables sitemap/robots/crawler/sampling) OR site root + robots.txt (parseRobotsTxt: sitemaps + disallow groups merged into exclude) + sitemap.xml via sitemapper (>=50 sitemap URLs on non-localhost disables the crawler) + route definitions discovered from a pages dir (discovery/routeDefinitions.ts globs *.vue/*.md up to depth 5, util/createRoutes builds Nuxt-style paths) + crawler (hook 'discovered-internal-links' queues internal links found by the HTML task; if home page yields no links with skipJavascript it flips to JS execution and disables cache). Route normalisation (router/util.ts normaliseRoute): id = hash(path); definition assigned by (a) scanner.customSampling regex map, (b) provider.mockRouter (router/mockRouter.ts builds regexparam matchers from framework route definitions), or (c) a runtime heuristic that names the route from path segments treating the last segment as dynamic. Sampling: groupBy(route.definition.name) then lodash sampleSize(group, dynamicSampling) - random selection, capped by maxRoutes in worker.queueRoute. Worker (puppeteer/worker.ts): puppeteer-cluster with routeReports Map<id, UnlighthouseRouteReport>; each route runs two tasks in sequence with status waiting|in-progress|completed|failed|ignore|failed-retry: inspectHtmlTask (puppeteer/tasks/html.ts extractHtmlPayload -> processHtml via ultrahtml: title, meta description, og:title/description/image, favicon, hreflang x-default (i18n skip), internal/external link lists) and runLighthouseTask (puppeteer/tasks/lighthouse.ts: reads cached lighthouse.json if present; otherwise spawns process/lighthouse.ts as a child process per sample that calls lighthouse(url, {port, output ['html','json'], ...lighthouseOptions}) against the cluster's Chrome; for samples > 1 uses lighthouse/core/lib/median-run.js computeMedianRun and regenerates artifacts from the median run; strips base64 screenshots for client stability). Hooks (hookable): site-changed, resolved-config, worker-finished, route-definitions-provided, visited-client, task-added/started/complete, discovered-internal-links, puppeteer:before-goto, authenticate. Server (h3 + ws) broadcasts route reports to the Vue client; client columns (constants.ts DefaultColumns) map tabs to LHR keys, e.g. report.audits.largest-contentful-paint sortKey numericValue, report.audits.color-contrast sortKey length:details.items, report.computed.ariaIssues, seo.internalLinks/externalLinks/description/og.image, and an overview screenshot timeline from screenshot-thumbnails. CI (packages/cli/src/ci.ts): --budget N or per-category map; ciBudget.ts isScoreBelowBudget(score*100 < budget) per route per category; exit 1 on any breach; reporters jsonSimple/jsonExpanded/csv/csvExpanded/lighthouseServer; --build-static emits the client as a static site.
core_innovation: Route-pattern deduplication with per-group random sampling so a 10,000-page site is audited by scanning ~8 pages per template, combined with a per-route two-task pipeline (cheap HTML extraction feeding crawl + SEO columns, expensive Lighthouse feeding scores) in a browser cluster.
strengths: Discovery ladder (explicit urls > robots/sitemap > framework route files > link crawl) with sensible auto-fallbacks; each stage is a small isolated module.

Route grouping by definition name (framework router or path heuristic) with customSampling regex overrides is the right unit for a template-driven site: our archetype x arrangement pages map 1:1 to groups.
Two-task design: the HTML task is cheap (no JS by default) and yields crawl edges plus SEO meta in one pass, so link discovery and meta extraction do not wait on Lighthouse.
Per-route disk cache keyed by path with cache-busting on config change, plus retry states, make re-runs incremental.
samples > 1 with computeMedianRun reuses Lighthouse's own median selection instead of inventing one.
Hookable lifecycle (task-added/started/complete, puppeteer:before-goto, authenticate) allows injecting auth, cookies, or extra checks without forking.

Client UI: a per-route table with category tabs, sortable metric columns bound to LHR keys, screenshot timeline, grouping by route definition, drill-in to the full Lighthouse HTML - a proven layout for a whole-site gate report.
MIT, TypeScript, small core (~50 files).
weaknesses: CI budget is category-score-only (score*100 < budget) - exactly the noisy signal LHCI warns against; no per-audit assertions, no maxLength/maxNumericValue, no aggregation method, no URL-pattern matrix.
Sampling uses lodash sampleSize (random): different pages each run, so results are not reproducible and a regression on an unsampled page is missed; no seed or deterministic 'first N by priority'.

Puppeteer + puppeteer-cluster, not Playwright; adds a second driver and Chrome management; cluster concurrency also contradicts Lighthouse's advice against concurrent runs on one machine (perf metrics degrade).

Lighthouse-only: no direct axe run (inherits Lighthouse's wcag2a/aa subset), no link-status checking (links are discovered but 404s are not asserted), no placeholder/schema/form checks; SEO columns are display-only, not asserted.
Pre-1.0 with breaking config changes; single maintainer; client still shows deprecated FID column; i18n pages skipped by default (ignoreI18nPages) which would hide localized routes.
Route heuristic (last path segment = dynamic) mis-groups shallow static sites (e.g. /services/roofing vs /services/gutters are the same group and may be sampled away).
Default skipJavascript true for the HTML task can miss client-rendered links; flips only if the home page has zero links.
patterns_to_steal: Discovery ladder (explicit urls > sitemap/robots > route definitions > crawl) -> qa_gate: for our own Astro build we know every route from the SiteDefinition, so use 'explicit urls' from the build manifest as source of truth and run the crawl only to find links that point outside the manifest (404/orphan detection).

Route grouping by definition + per-group sampling -> qa_gate: group pages by page_archetype x arrangement_id from the SiteDefinition; run the expensive Lighthouse perf triple on one representative per group (chosen deterministically: highest-priority beat, not random) and run cheap deterministic checks on every page.

Two-task per route (cheap HTML extraction feeding crawl/SEO, expensive Lighthouse) with status enum waiting|in-progress|completed|failed|ignore|failed-retry -> qa_gate scheduler: Playwright pass 1 (DOM, axe, links, meta, console, placeholders) on all pages; Lighthouse pass 2 on sampled pages; GateReport keeps per-task status.
Per-route cache keyed by path + config hash -> qa_gate: cache per (page hash, gate config version) so the fix loop only re-audits pages whose HTML changed.

Client column model {label, key: 'report.audits.<id>', sortKey: 'numericValue' | 'length:details.items', tooltip} -> client-facing gate report: define report columns as data bound to GateReport paths; group rows by archetype; screenshot strip per page.
Hook names (task-complete, puppeteer:before-goto, authenticate) -> qa_gate: expose the same hook points so archetype-specific pre-steps (cookie banner dismiss, nav open) plug in.

processHtml SEO extraction (title, description, og:*, favicon, hreflang x-default, internal/external links) -> qa_gate structure checks: extend into asserted checks: duplicate titles/descriptions across site, og:image present and 1200x630, favicon 200, hreflang reciprocity.
patterns_to_avoid: Category-score budgets as the CI gate -> non-deterministic; use per-audit assertions and resource budgets (LHCI grammar) and treat category scores as reporting only.
Random route sampling -> non-reproducible; select representatives deterministically from the SiteDefinition and record which pages were sampled in the Decision Manifest.
Running Lighthouse concurrently in a cluster on one machine -> distorts perf metrics; run perf audits serially (or one per isolated worker) and parallelize only the deterministic Playwright checks.
Framework page-dir route discovery and mockRouter -> irrelevant for us; our route list comes from the typed SiteDefinition, not from globbing files.
Depending on the package itself -> Puppeteer-based, pre-1.0, Lighthouse-only; the crawl/sample/cluster ideas are ~300 lines to reimplement over Playwright.
reusable_patterns: DiscoveryLadder: ordered route sources with automatic fallback and cross-source dedupe by normalized path id.
TemplateGroupSampling: normalize each URL to a template/definition key and audit only k representatives per key for expensive checks while running cheap checks on all.
CheapThenExpensiveTaskPair: a fast extraction task that feeds discovery and metadata precedes the slow measurement task, with independent status per task.
MedianOfSamplesPerRoute: N runs per route collapsed with the engine's own median-run selection before reporting.
DataBoundReportColumns: report UI columns declared as {key path, sortKey, label, tooltip} over the result JSON, not hand-written per metric.
adoption_strategy: Adapt, do not adopt. Reimplement whole-site gating in our Playwright-based gate: pages come from the SiteDefinition build manifest (not crawling), grouped by archetype x arrangement; every page gets the deterministic pass (axe full tags, DOM/structure/placeholder/meta/schema/link-status/console checks, mobile + desktop); one deterministic representative per group gets Lighthouse 3x serial with LHCI-style per-audit assertions and resource-summary budgets, asserted on the median run. Copy the task-status enum, per-route cache keyed by (page hash, gate version), the hookable pre-goto/authenticate points, and the client's route-table-with-category-tabs layout for the client-facing report. Keep unlighthouse in mind only as an ad-hoc research tool for auditing competitor sites (its crawl + dashboard is convenient for that).

status_note: active; v10.0.0 (Puppeteer 25, axe-core ~4.13, @pa11y/html_codesniffer 2.6 fork); sibling pa11y/pa11y-ci (LGPL-3.0, 633 stars, pushed 2026-09-13) provides sitemap/URL-list batch runs
core_problem: A Puppeteer-driven CLI and Node API that loads a URL, optionally performs a scripted list of pre-test actions, injects one or more in-page accessibility engines (HTML_CodeSniffer by default, axe optional), and normalizes their output into a single flat issue list with error/warning/notice levels, a threshold and exit code for CI.
architecture: lib/pa11y.js orchestrates a fixed sequence: option.parseArguments (defaults: standard WCAG2AA, runners ['htmlcs'], timeout 60000, viewport 1280x1024, includeNotices/includeWarnings false, levelCapWhenNeedsReview 'error', wait 0) -> setBrowser (puppeteer.launch(chromeLaunchConfig) or a caller-supplied browser/page) -> setPage (viewport, userAgent, console forwarding) -> interceptRequests (only if headers/method/postData) -> gotoUrl (waitUntil networkidle2, or ignoreUrl to audit an already-navigated page) -> runActionsList -> injectRunners (lib/runner.js + each runner's scripts via page.evaluate) -> wait -> runPa11yWithOptions -> saveScreenCapture. lib/runner.js is the in-page aggregator exposed as window.__pa11y: runs each named runner, filters issues by rootElement / hideElements / ignore (codes or types), and maps each to {code, type error|warning|notice, typeCode 1|2|3, message, context (outerHTML truncated to 250 chars, innerHTML to 31), selector (id-anchored 'tag:nth-child' path), runner, runnerExtras}. Runners are plugins {scripts: [paths injected], run(options, pa11y), supports: semver}: lib/runners/htmlcs.js calls HTMLCS.process(standard, document) with standard WCAG2A|WCAG2AA|WCAG2AAA and optional extra sniff 'rules', mapping HTMLCS type 1/2/3 to error/warning/notice; lib/runners/axe.js calls axe.run(rootElement||document, {runOnly: {type:'tags', values:['wcag2a','wcag21a', +'wcag2aa','wcag21aa' unless WCAG2A, 'best-practice']}, rules: enable/disable map derived from pa11y rules/ignore}) and maps impact critical|serious -> error, moderate -> warning, minor -> notice; crucially it emits axe 'incomplete' results as issues with runnerExtras.needsFurtherReview = true, capped to levelCapWhenNeedsReview. lib/action.js is a regex-matched DSL run before testing: 'navigate to <url>', 'click element <sel>', 'set field <sel> to <val>', 'clear field', 'check|uncheck field', 'screen capture <file>', 'wait for url|path|fragment|host to (not) be <x>', 'wait for element <sel> to be added|removed|visible|hidden', 'wait for element <sel> to emit <event>'. Reporters (lib/reporters): cli, csv, tsv, json, html (mustache template). CLI (bin/pa11y.js): --runner, --standard, --threshold N (exit 2 if issues > N), --level, --level-cap-when-needs-review, --ignore, --add-rule, --root-element, --hide-elements, --config JSON. pa11y-ci: lib/pa11y-ci.js runs an async queue (concurrency default 1, useIncognitoBrowserContext true) over 'urls' (each a string or {url, ...overrides, threshold}) or a --sitemap (recurses sitemapindex, --sitemap-find/--sitemap-replace to rewrite hosts, --sitemap-exclude regex), cycles reporters through beforeAll/begin/results/error/afterAll, and exits 2 when errors >= threshold.
core_innovation: Runner abstraction that normalizes heterogeneous a11y engines into one issue schema, plus a plain-English pre-test action DSL so page state can be set up without writing browser code.
strengths: Dual engines: HTML_CodeSniffer catches some WCAG techniques axe does not express (and WCAG2AAA sniffs), giving a cheap second opinion on the same DOM.

Needs-review policy is explicit: axe incomplete results are surfaced as issues (needsFurtherReview true) and their level is capped by levelCapWhenNeedsReview, so 'unknown' is never silently dropped - the same fail-closed posture our gate wants.
Issue schema is tiny and stable (code/type/message/context/selector/runner) and identical across engines; trivially mapped into a GateReport.
Action DSL is human-readable and validatable (pa11y.isValidAction), suitable for authoring per-archetype pre-conditions in YAML.
pa11y-ci provides sitemap-driven batch runs with per-URL threshold overrides and a minimal reporter lifecycle contract.
Accepts an external Puppeteer browser/page (browser + page + ignoreUrl), so it can run on a page another script already navigated.
weaknesses: LGPL-3.0-only: acceptable for unmodified use as a CLI or npm dependency in a closed SaaS (LGPL section 4 applies to combined works; dynamic linking/consumption via npm is customary), but any modification to pa11y's own source must be published, and some enterprise clients flag LGPL in dependency audits. Nothing here is worth that friction.
Puppeteer, not Playwright: a second browser driver and Chrome download in our stack, with its own lifecycle, for a job Playwright + @axe-core/playwright already does.

HTML_CodeSniffer is a legacy engine (pa11y's own fork, minor updates), noisy notices, and its WCAG 2.1 mapping is partial; its unique value versus axe is small for modern semantic HTML that our section library controls.

Flattens axe's rich result: any/all/none check data, relatedNodes, tags and helpUrl are lost or squashed into message text; impact->level mapping discards 'incomplete' as a distinct status (only a boolean in runnerExtras).
Selector generation (id-anchored nth-child path) is weaker than axe's own target arrays and does not traverse iframes or shadow DOM.
Per-page tool; pa11y-ci has no route sampling, no dedupe, no cross-page checks, and threshold is a plain count rather than severity-weighted.
Runs with a desktop 1280x1024 viewport by default; no built-in multi-viewport runs, no throttling, no performance or SEO checks.
patterns_to_steal: Needs-review cap (levelCapWhenNeedsReview) -> qa_gate: policy knob that decides whether axe 'incomplete' nodes fail, warn or inform, defaulting to fail (error) for launch.

Action DSL grammar ('click element X', 'wait for element X to be visible', 'set field X to Y') -> qa_gate: author per page-archetype pre-test steps (open mobile nav, submit contact form, dismiss cookie banner) in YAML and compile them to Playwright calls; validate at load time like pa11y.isValidAction.
Runner plugin contract {scripts, run, supports} -> qa_gate: our in-page checks (placeholder scan, h1 count, generic link text) as runners that share the axe/HTMLCS injection path and result schema.
Uniform issue row {code, type, message, context, selector, runner} -> GateReport row baseline; add status (fail|warn|needs_review|pass|n/a), impact, tags, target[] and screenshot ref on top.
pa11y-ci urls entry as string | {url, overrides, threshold} -> qa_gate config: per-page overrides for pages with legitimately different rules (legal pages, thank-you page).
patterns_to_avoid: Adding pa11y as a dependency -> duplicates Playwright with Puppeteer, drags in LGPL, and loses axe result fidelity; run @axe-core/playwright directly.
HTML_CodeSniffer as a gate engine -> unmaintained mapping and noisy notices would create non-actionable failures; at most run it informative-only in research to spot gaps in our section library.
Count-based threshold ('permit N issues') -> we gate on severity classes and specific check ids, never on totals; a single critical is a fail, ten minors are warnings.
Default desktop-only viewport -> our checks must run at mobile 412x823 (Lighthouse's Moto G emulation) and desktop 1350x940 so target-size and contrast are evaluated where users see them.
reusable_patterns: NeedsReviewSeverityCap: undecidable machine results are surfaced as issues with a configurable maximum severity, defaulting to fail-closed.
PlainEnglishActionDSL: regex-matched imperative sentences compiled to browser actions, validated before the run.
EngineRunnerPlugin: {scripts, run(options), supports} lets multiple in-page engines share injection, filtering and output schema.
PerUrlThresholdOverride: batch config where each URL can override defaults and its own pass threshold.
adoption_strategy: Ignore as a dependency; Adapt two small patterns. Given Playwright + @axe-core/playwright are already in the stack, pa11y is redundant: its axe runner is a thin wrapper that loses data, and HTML_CodeSniffer adds little for semantic HTML we author ourselves. Take (1) the needs-review severity cap as a gate policy setting and (2) the action-sentence DSL for authoring pre-test steps per archetype in YAML, implemented over Playwright. Do not vendor its code (LGPL); the patterns are trivial to re-implement (~100 lines).
evidence: lib/pa11y.js (runPa11yTest sequence setBrowser/setPage/interceptRequests/gotoUrl/runActionsList/injectRunners/wait/runPa11yWithOptions/saveScreenCapture; pa11y.defaults incl. standard WCAG2AA, runners ['htmlcs'], timeout 60000, levelCapWhenNeedsReview 'error'; allowedStandards WCAG2A/AA/AAA)

lib/runner.js (window.__pa11y run(): runners map, processIssues with rootElement/hideElements/ignore filters, issue shape code/type/typeCode/message/context/selector/runner/runnerExtras, getElementContext 250/31 char truncation, id-anchored selector builder)

lib/runners/axe.js (runOnly tags wcag2a/wcag21a/wcag2aa/wcag21aa/best-practice; impact->level map critical/serious=error moderate=warning minor=notice; incomplete emitted with needsFurtherReview=true and capped by levelCapWhenNeedsReview; supports '^10.0.0')
lib/runners/htmlcs.js (HTMLCS.process(standard, document), extra sniff rules pushed into HTMLCS_<standard>.sniffs[0].include, type 1/2/3 mapping)
lib/action.js (action regexes: navigate-url, click-element, set-field-value, clear-field-value, check-field, screen-capture, wait-for-url, wait-for-element-state, wait-for-element-event)

lib/reporters/{cli,csv,tsv,json,html}.js, package.json (v10.0.0, LGPL-3.0-only, deps puppeteer ^25.9, axe-core ~4.13, @pa11y/html_codesniffer ^2.6)
README.md CLI options (--runner, --standard, --threshold, --level-cap-when-needs-review, --add-rule, --ignore, --root-element, --hide-elements)

pa11y/pa11y-ci README.md and lib/pa11y-ci.js, bin/pa11y-ci.js (urls/defaults config, concurrency queue, useIncognitoBrowserContext, --sitemap with sitemapindex recursion, --sitemap-find/--sitemap-replace/--sitemap-exclude, reporters beforeAll/begin/results/error/afterAll, exit 2 when errors >= threshold)

status_note: active; Vercel Labs; not on the original repo list but cited in implementation-strategy.md
core_problem: Let an LLM generate a UI reliably by constraining it to a developer-defined component catalogue, validating the JSON it emits against a Zod schema, and rendering it progressively as it streams.
architecture: Monorepo. @json-render/core holds the schema builder (packages/core/src/schema.ts: defineCatalog(schema, {components: {Name: {props: zod, description}}, actions})), which derives three things from one catalogue: catalog.prompt() (system prompt listing allowed components/props/rules), catalog.jsonSchema({strict:true}) (strict JSON Schema for provider structured-output APIs; records collapsed because additionalProperties must be false), and catalog.validate(spec) (Zod). The spec is a FLAT document: {root: key, elements: {key: {type, props, children[], slots{}, visible?, on?, repeat?}}, state} rather than a nested tree, so that streaming RFC 6902 JSON Patch lines (/root first, then /elements/... and /state/...) can fill the UI progressively. spec-validator.ts performs structural checks with machine-readable codes (missing_root, missing_child, orphaned_element, visible_in_props, repeat_state_mismatch...). visibility.ts defines declarative conditions ({$state, eq|gt|...}, $and/$or, $item/$index for repeats) validated by strict Zod. edit-modes.ts supports three edit wire formats for refinement (RFC 6902 patch, RFC 7396 merge, unified diff) with per-mode prompt instructions. state-store.ts plus adapters (redux/zustand/jotai/xstate). directives.ts ($format, $math, $t...). Renderers per target: react, vue, svelte, solid, react-native, next (routes/layouts/SSR), remotion (video), react-pdf, react-email, ink, image (Satori), react-three-fiber. @json-render/shadcn ships 36 catalogue-ready shadcn components. @json-render/codegen turns a spec into source code. Devtools with stream taps.
core_innovation: One catalogue definition compiles to prompt + strict JSON Schema + validator simultaneously, so the thing the model is told, the thing the API enforces, and the thing the runtime checks can never drift apart.
strengths: Single source of truth: catalogue -> prompt(), jsonSchema(strict), validate(), zodSchema(). This is exactly the 'model chooses within what code permits' principle, productionised.
Flat elements map keyed by id enables streaming, patch-based edits and stable references; better for undo/redo and visual editing than a nested tree.
Structured error codes from spec validation give a deterministic repair loop (re-prompt with the specific code) instead of 'try again'.
Three edit modes (patch/merge/diff) for refinement of an existing spec: a mature answer to 'how does the model edit, not regenerate'.
Declarative visibility/conditions and directives keep logic in data, not model-written code.
Renderer-agnostic: the same spec drives web, email, PDF, OG-image, video; relevant for producing client deliverables (proposal PDF, OG images) from the same SiteDefinition.
Apache-2.0, actively maintained by Vercel Labs, TypeScript-native, Zod-native: zero runtime mismatch with our stack.
weaknesses: Designed for app UIs (dashboards, forms) with generic layout primitives (Stack, Card, Grid); it has no notion of section families, composition, rhythm, art direction, asset constraints or eligibility. Using its shadcn catalogue would produce exactly the generic output we exist to avoid.

The renderer packages are client-runtime oriented (React/Vue/Svelte). There is no Astro renderer; our output must be static HTML with islands, so we would use only core at build time and write our own Astro emitter.

The model still emits the whole spec (which components, which props). In our pipeline the model must only pick ids from pre-computed eligible sets; json-render's prompt() would need heavy customisation to express 'choose from these 4 variants for beat 3' rather than 'compose freely from the catalogue'.
Strict JSON Schema mode cannot express record/map types; our slot bindings and fact queries are maps, so we would flatten them.
Streaming progressive render is irrelevant for a build pipeline that renders after all gates pass; the complexity (patch stream, state store) is dead weight for us.
patterns_to_steal: Catalogue-compiles-to-{prompt, strict JSON schema, validator} -> our three constrained decision calls (creative direction, beat selection, arrangement): generate the enum-constrained schema per build from the eligible set, so the model literally cannot name an ineligible id.

Flat elements map with stable ids -> SiteDefinition sections and slots keyed by stable instance ids (section_instance_id already exists in the telemetry contract); makes manifests, patches and the post-V1 editor trivial.
Machine-readable validation codes -> our assembly/anti-slop violations should be typed codes (no_focal_moment, rhythm_profile_breach) that drive substitution-based repair, not prose.
Edit modes (RFC 6902 patch) for refinement -> the client-facing 'change this section' flow post-launch: model emits patches against SiteDefinition, gates re-run on the patched doc.
@json-render/image (Satori) -> OG image generation from SiteDefinition data; react-pdf -> gate report / proposal PDF from the same source.
patterns_to_avoid: Free composition from a generic catalogue (Stack/Card/Grid) -> this is the 'Hero 1/2/3' problem; the model must select whole authored arrangements, never compose primitives.
Streaming spec with live state store -> unnecessary for a build-then-gate pipeline; adds client JS against a 180 kB budget.
Model-authored visible/state logic in marketing sites -> interactive state belongs in authored islands, not model-emitted conditions.
reusable_patterns: SchemaTriad: one typed catalogue definition emits prompt, JSON Schema and runtime validator so they cannot drift.
FlatIdDocument: documents as {root, elements: Record<id, node>} rather than nested trees, enabling patches, stable refs and streaming.
TypedValidationCodes: structural validation returns machine codes that feed an automated repair loop.
PatchRefinement: edits to an existing document are expressed as RFC 6902/7396 operations chosen by the model, never full regeneration.
MultiTargetRender: the same spec renders to web, PDF, email, OG image via target-specific renderers.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Do not adopt the renderers or the shadcn catalogue. Take @json-render/core's SchemaTriad idea and re-implement it thinly (a few hundred lines of Zod + JSON-schema generation) around our own SiteDefinition, so each constrained model call receives a per-build strict schema whose enums are exactly the eligible ids. Consider directly depending on @json-render/core only if its defineCatalog proves flexible enough to express per-beat enum sets; otherwise the pattern is more valuable than the package. Evaluate @json-render/image for OG images.
evidence: packages/core/src/schema.ts: Catalog interface with prompt(), jsonSchema({strict}), validate(), zodSchema()
packages/core/src/spec-validator.ts: SpecIssue codes missing_root, missing_child, orphaned_element, visible_in_props, repeat_state_mismatch
packages/core/src/visibility.ts: declarative $state/$item/$index conditions with strict Zod
packages/core/src/edit-modes.ts: patch (RFC 6902) / merge (RFC 7396) / diff edit modes with prompt instructions
packages/core/src/prompt.ts: buildUserPrompt with refinement mode and streaming instruction

status_note: alpha v0.1, Windows-only, single maintainer; cited in implementation-strategy.md
core_problem: AI web tools edit code blind and say 'done' when nothing rendered changed. Loupe closes the loop: point at an element on the live render, the agent edits source, and the change is verified against the real render before it reports success.
architecture: Windows desktop app pairing an AI chat with a live design canvas. Build modes: Solo (one pass), Studio (Director -> Builder -> Reviewer with a clarify gate), experimental Swarm (planner maps site, parallel page builders, reviewer) and Loop (iterate a page against a quality bar). Grounding comes from baseline/library/: references/<n>/ (~1,300 analyses of real sites, each with extracted design tokens), recipes/ (DESIGN.md-style distilled palettes/type/composition/motion per source), techniques/ (how-tos: WebGL cross-fade, stacked-blur glass, perf tiers, sticky-pin responsive, GSAP choreography), snippets/ (lifted code from magic-ui, aceternity, shadcn, three.js examples, own builds), standards/ (design-standards precedence arbiter + verification playbook), INDEX.md (searchable tagged index). The library README documents a harvest pipeline: fetch page + assets via Playwright -> screenshots -> distill into recipe/techniques -> index. The element picker sends exact selectors + source files to the agent; a verify step diffs the real render. Canvas edits persist as CSS; one undo/redo stack spans AI and hand edits; /assemble compiles canvas arrangement into clean semantic HTML/CSS; a token panel stays in sync with the site's real CSS. BYOK engines: Claude, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI, or subscription CLIs.
core_innovation: Verify-the-render: an agent edit is not 'done' until the change is confirmed against the actual rendered DOM/pixels, with the element picker giving the agent exact selectors instead of a description.
strengths: Verify-the-render loop is the right instinct and maps directly to our visual validation stage: never trust a code edit, trust the render.
Library structure (references / recipes / techniques / snippets / standards / INDEX) is a clean taxonomy for a design knowledge base; standards/ as a precedence arbiter is the interesting part.
Director -> Builder -> Reviewer with a clarify gate for vague briefs: a small, sane agent topology.
Unified undo/redo across AI and hand edits, and /assemble (canvas -> clean code) show the visual editor and the code output can stay in one model.
Design-token panel bound to the site's real CSS: tokens as the editable surface, not raw CSS.
weaknesses: The ~1,300 reference analyses with extracted tokens are derivative of real commercial sites' trade dress; using them to generate sites sold to clients is a legal posture we explicitly rejected.
Fills image slots with AI-generated photos, which directly violates our non-overridable never: ai_generated_person / ai_generated_premises rule.
Snippets lifted from magic-ui/aceternity/three.js examples are the canonical slop vocabulary (beams, sparkles, orbiting circles).
Loop mode iterates against a quality bar judged by a model: the non-reproducible LLM critic we rejected.
Alpha, Windows-only, 13 stars, one maintainer; not a dependency.
Generation is free-form code editing; no typed site contract, no eligibility, no fact grounding.
patterns_to_steal: Verify-the-render -> QA gate step: after any repair/substitution, re-render and assert the expected section/arrangement actually appears (DOM marker per section_instance_id + screenshot diff against the arrangement's library-time reference render).
Element picker -> post-V1 editor: selection resolves to a section_instance_id + slot, not a CSS selector; edits become SiteDefinition patches.

Library taxonomy (references/recipes/techniques/standards/INDEX) -> the shape of our authored library docs: each variant has a recipe (signature_move, negative_example), techniques are reusable implementation notes, standards are the precedence rules.
Clarify gate before building on a vague brief -> our intake refuses to start creative direction until positioning is declared and blocking facts exist (already in Gap Report blocking).
patterns_to_avoid: Harvested-site token corpus as generation grounding -> trade-dress risk and homogenisation; use hand-authored design systems.
AI-generated imagery for slots -> hard-banned by art direction rules.
Model-judged quality loop as a gate -> not reproducible; our loop iterates only against deterministic gate failures.
Snippet library from effect-component sites -> slop vocabulary.
reusable_patterns: VerifyTheRender: an edit is complete only when the rendered output is checked, not when the code is written.
SelectorGroundedEdit: the editing agent receives exact structural references (ids/selectors + files), never a description.

status_note: active, single-maintainer, tiny audience; cited in implementation-strategy.md
core_problem: Turn a short brief into a complete, SEO/GEO-ready, accessible Astro website by orchestrating an AI coding assistant (Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity) through a fixed sequence of skills, with quality gates, on a house stack of Astro -> GitHub -> Cloudflare Pages.
architecture: No runtime code of its own: the product is ~30 SKILL.md files under skills/ (ai-seo, business-listings-setup, copywriting, customer-research, image, independent-review, internal-link-audit, keystatic-setup, new-website, og-images, schema-markup, search-console-*, seo-audit, site-architecture, website-content-guide, website-design-system, website-motion, website-positioning, website-positioning-check, website-qa, website-review, website-seo-geo, website-testimonials, astro-i18n-setup...). new-website is the orchestrator: insights -> positioning -> content -> SEO/GEO -> design -> QA -> review -> launch. Skills carry references/ (playbooks, e.g. ai-seo/references/platform-ranking-factors.md, content-patterns.md) and evals/evals.json. Templates for the Astro scaffold live in skills/new-website/templates/. Repo tooling enforces hygiene: scripts/check_skill_budgets.sh (token budget per skill), check_model_agnostic.sh (skills must not depend on one vendor), check_template_coverage.sh, check_clean.sh; docs/reviews/ holds dozens of dated independent-review diffs, an audit trail of the suite reviewing its own changes. Sites are version-stamped with the suite version.
core_innovation: The whole agency process is encoded as versioned, budgeted, model-agnostic skill files with an independent-review skill that reviews the suite's own changes: process-as-code rather than app-as-code.
strengths: Pipeline shape matches ours almost exactly (positioning before design, QA and review as explicit stages, launch as a stage); validates the sequence.
Skill token budgets enforced by CI (check_skill_budgets.sh): a concrete answer to prompt bloat.
independent-review skill and docs/reviews/ trail: every change to the process gets a written review; maps to our 'drift review is a diff, not a write' rule.
Version stamping of built sites: the same idea as pinning library@commit in the manifest.
website-positioning-check exists as a separate skill from website-positioning: verification split from authoring.
Astro house stack independently chosen; keystatic-setup shows a git-backed CMS path for client edits without a database.
Search Console / business listings skills: post-launch measurement and local-SEO setup are treated as part of building the site.
weaknesses: Everything is prose instructions to a model; nothing is deterministic code. Quality depends entirely on the model following the SKILL.md; there is no gate that can fail a build.
No fact registry, no grounding leash: content is whatever the model writes from the brief.
No design library; 'design' is a skill describing principles, so output is model-invented layout, precisely the slop path.
4 stars, one maintainer; not a dependency, only a reference.
Positioning is elicited conversationally rather than declared as a typed value with honesty constraints.
patterns_to_steal: Stage list and ordering (insights -> positioning -> content -> SEO/GEO -> design -> QA -> review -> launch) -> confirms our selection pipeline; add their post-launch stages (search console, listings) to our launch checklist.
Skill/asset token budgets enforced in CI -> apply to playbooks, design systems and prompts: a playbook YAML over N tokens fails CI.
Model-agnostic check -> our three constrained calls should be tested against at least two providers so the pipeline is not vendor-shaped.
Dated review documents for every process change -> our /_proposed/<asset>@<date>.yml drift-review outputs should keep a review log alongside.
Version-stamp the site with library/playbook/design-system versions in a meta tag or build manifest served alongside the site.
patterns_to_avoid: Process-as-prose only -> cannot gate; our invariants must be code.
Conversational design decisions -> model invents layouts; we select authored arrangements.
Content generated without a fact registry -> unverifiable claims.
reusable_patterns: ProcessAsVersionedSkills: an agency workflow encoded as versioned instruction files with CI hygiene checks.
BudgetedPrompts: per-asset token ceilings enforced in CI.
SelfReviewTrail: every change to process assets produces a dated independent review artifact.
VersionStampedOutput: built sites record which process version built them.
adoption_strategy: Adapt. Take the stage ordering as confirmation, the CI hygiene scripts as a pattern for our YAML assets, and the post-launch SEO stages as checklist items. Do not adopt the skills themselves; they are prose where we need code.
